## `window.confirm` → `ConfirmDialog`, and `Toast` wiring, across the remaining audit-enumerated list

Roadmap item 3 of 6 from the sixth-pass audit — [Confirmation and feedback rollout, precisely](ux-audit-2026-08.md#confirmation-and-feedback-rollout-precisely). Unlike items 1/2, this one was pre-scoped as two flat lists (11 `window.confirm` call sites across 4 files; 11 pages with real mutations and no `useToast`) rather than a single feature — worked through both lists file by file, same piecemeal approach the fourth pass used for its own three pilot sites each, copying the pilot's exact patterns (Tier 1 `ConfirmDialog`, `useToast`/`toErrorMessage`) rather than inventing new ones.

**Part A — `window.confirm` → `ConfirmDialog` (all 11 call sites, all Tier 1)**: `OrgAdminPage.tsx` (PAT descope-all, revoke-all, revoke-one), `ServerManagementPage.tsx` (deactivate, ban, grant/revoke server-admin, PAT revoke-all — consolidated into one `confirmAction: { kind, userId } | null` state plus a `confirmActionCopy` lookup table, rather than four near-identical dialog blocks), `PreferencesPage.tsx` (PAT revoke-all, revoke-one), `ServerOrganisationsPage.tsx` (disable — delete already used `ConfirmDialog` Tier 2 from the fourth pass, untouched). Each conversion follows the archive-button precedent exactly: a `*ToOpen`/`*ToRevoke`-style state variable set by the trigger button, the mutation function stripped of its `if (!window.confirm(...)) return` guard, and one `<ConfirmDialog>` rendered conditionally. `strings.ts` gained a parallel `*Title` key next to each existing `*Confirm` key for every converted site (the pilot's own `archiveTitle`/`archiveConfirm` split) — where the old single string combined a question and its rationale in one sentence, the question moved to the new `*Title` and the rationale stayed as the (now-trimmed) `*Confirm` message; three of `orgAdmin`'s PAT confirm functions lost their now-redundant `org` parameter as part of that split (each was used at exactly one call site, confirmed via grep before changing the signature).

**Part B — `Toast` wiring (all 11 pages)**: `ChangeRequestDetailPage.tsx`, `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`, `FavouritesPage.tsx`, `NotificationsPage.tsx`, `PreferencesPage.tsx`, `ProjectActionsPage.tsx`, `ProjectListPage.tsx`, `ReportsPage.tsx`, `RequirementsPage.tsx`, `ServerManagementPage.tsx`, `ServerOrganisationsPage.tsx` — every one imports `useToast`/`toErrorMessage` and wires at least one real mutation. Per-mutation judgement (the fourth pass's own reasoning for not sweeping mechanically): a success toast where no other success feedback existed (`RequirementsPage`'s create, `ProjectActionsPage`'s create — both named specifically in the audit as having picked up real interaction-model work without Toast — plus `ChangeRequestsPage`'s create, `ChangeRequestDetailPage`'s submit/withdraw/approve/reject, `ProjectListPage`'s create, `ServerOrganisationsPage`'s create/disable/enable/delete, `NotificationsPage`'s mark-all-read); an error toast (via the shared `toErrorMessage` fallback) where a mutation had literally zero error handling before this pass — several were unhandled promise rejections, not just missing UI: `RequirementsPage`'s move/inline-component/inline-category-create/CSV-import-catch, `FavouritesPage`'s unfavorite, `ProjectListPage`'s toggle-favorite, `ReportsPage`'s `generate()` (a bare `try`/`finally` with no `catch` at all — a failed report generation previously had zero visible feedback), `PreferencesPage`'s revoke-pat/revoke-all-pats/save-notification-prefs, `ServerManagementPage`'s platform-wide PAT revoke-all. `PreferencesPage`'s avatar upload gained a `catch` too, but reports inline (`avatarError`, matching the page's own per-section inline-error convention) rather than via toast, since it sits in a form full of inline error text already.

**Deliberate skips, named explicitly rather than silently dropped** (the "adequate inline UI already" exception): `ServerManagementPage.tsx`'s `PlatformBrandingTab` (save, logo upload, login-background upload), `SignupModeTab` (save), and `TestEmailTab` (send) all already show inline "Saved."/"uploaded"/"Test email sent" success text and inline red error text right next to their own buttons — adding a toast on top would double up the same information rather than close a real gap, so these three sub-tabs were left as they were. `PreferencesPage.tsx`'s profile save, password change, and 2FA enrol/confirm/disable were left alone for the same reason (each already has its own adequate inline success/error path — password change and 2FA-disable both redirect to a re-auth login screen, which is itself the success signal). `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s three PAT actions (Part A) were *not* given new toasts — that page wasn't on the Part B list (it already imports `useToast` for other mutations), and adding toast coverage to mutations outside the audit's enumerated 22 would have been exactly the mechanical sweep the fourth pass's own reasoning argues against.

**Also fixed while converting, not deferred**: `system.revokeServerAdminConfirm` previously had no elaboration at all ("Revoke server admin from this user?" with nothing else) — `ConfirmDialog`'s message can't be empty, so it now reads "They will lose access to server-wide management immediately," matching every sibling confirm's shape rather than being a bare repeat of the title.

**Playwright**: grepped the whole suite for `on("dialog"`/`once("dialog"` — exactly 4 native-dialog call sites across 3 files, all now converted to the in-app `ConfirmDialog`, same swap `requirement-archive-confirm.spec.ts` made in the fourth pass: `personal-access-tokens.spec.ts` (PAT revoke via Preferences), `user-directory-and-bans.spec.ts` (deactivate, ban — two sites), `server-org-lifecycle.spec.ts` (disable). No spec exercised `grantServerAdmin`/`revokeServerAdmin`/`OrgAdminPage`'s three PAT confirms/`PreferencesPage`'s PAT revoke-all — a pre-existing coverage gap, not something this pass introduced or was asked to close.

**Verified**: `npx tsc -b` and a full-tree `npx eslint src/` both clean — zero errors, the same 5 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings this doc already tracks (`BrandingContext.tsx`/`ThemeContext.tsx`), no new ones. Grep confirms zero remaining `window.confirm` in the 4 Part-A files and a `useToast` import in all 11 Part-B pages. Storybook: every touched page's existing `.stories.tsx` updated in place — `withToast()` added to each `meta.decorators`, existing stories exercising a converted `window.confirm` site rewritten to drive `ConfirmDialog` (`OrgAdminPage`, `ServerManagementPage`, `ServerOrganisationsPage`), new stories added for sites with no prior coverage (`OrgAdminPage`'s PAT revoke confirm+cancel, `PreferencesPage`'s PAT revoke confirm+cancel, `ServerManagementPage`'s deactivate-cancelled) and for each new toast/error path (`ChangeRequestDetailPage`'s submit/reject toasts, `ChangeRequestsPage`'s create toast, `FavouritesPage`'s unfavorite-error toast, `NotificationsPage`'s mark-all-read toast, `ProjectActionsPage`'s create toast, `ProjectListPage`'s create toast, `ReportsPage`'s generate-failure toast, `RequirementsPage`'s create toast and move-failure toast) — full suite **55 files / 401 tests, all green** (previously 388). Rebuilt/recreated the `tests/container` frontend image. Full clean-slate reseed (`docker compose down -v && up --build -d`, both seed scripts) and one full Playwright suite run: **71/72 passed**, the one failure (`report-image-attachment.spec.ts`) is this doc's own previously-documented pre-existing timing flake (see the mobile-grid entry above and others), confirmed via an isolated rerun to pass cleanly alone — not a regression, and unrelated to any of the 15 files this entry touches. `git status` confirmed no `backend/` files touched throughout. `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md` roadmap Status updated to "Done," noting the two deliberate-skip groups above.

## `/unarchive` endpoint + "Restore" button for requirements and actions

Roadmap item 4 of 6 from the sixth-pass audit — [Archive is one-way for requirements and actions, not projects](ux-audit-2026-08.md#archive-is-one-way-for-requirements-and-actions-not-projects). `projects.py` already had both `POST /{id}/archive` and `POST /{id}/unarchive`, with a working (toggling) unarchive button on `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s settings tab (label "Unarchive {project}", no `ConfirmDialog`); `requirements.py` and `actions.py` had only `/archive`. This pass added the missing counterpart to both, mirroring the project version's shape exactly rather than inventing a new one, and — per the change-management policy's identify → verify → remediate practice for security-sensitive changes (this touches mutating, audit-logged, RBAC-gated endpoints) — reviewed the result below.

**Backend**: `services/requirements.py::unarchive_requirement` (new, sits next to the existing `archive_requirement`) resets `is_archived`/`archived_at`/`archived_by`; `routers/requirements.py::restore_requirement` (`POST /requirements/{id}/unarchive`, named to avoid colliding with the service function of the same underlying verb) uses the exact same permission gate as `delete_requirement` (the requirement archive endpoint) — `PROJECT_MANAGER`/`PROJECT_ADMINISTRATOR` via `get_effective_project_roles` — and the same `log_event`/`pubsub.notify` shape, with `action="unarchived"`. `routers/actions.py::unarchive_action` (`POST /actions/{id}/unarchive`) mirrors `archive_action` just as directly: same `require_project_manage` dependency (project managers/administrators, plus organisation admins via `can_manage_project_settings` — a broader gate than the requirement side's, since that's `archive_action`'s own existing gate too, not something this pass introduced or changed), same `get_requirement_action_in_project` IDOR guard, same audit-log shape. No service-layer function was extracted for the action side since `archive_action` itself has no service-layer counterpart to mirror — inline in the router, matching its own existing shape rather than introducing a new abstraction asymmetrically.

**Idempotency, deliberately copied from `unarchive_project`, not from `archive_action`**: `archive_action` 409s if the action is already archived; `unarchive_project` has no equivalent guard — calling it on an already-active project is a harmless no-op. Both new endpoints copy the *project's* shape: calling `/unarchive` on an item that isn't archived just re-asserts "not archived" and logs `action="unarchived"` again, no error. Pinned by `test_unarchive_requirement_restores_it_and_is_idempotent`/`test_unarchive_action_restores_it_and_is_idempotent`, each calling `/unarchive` twice and asserting `200` both times.

**Frontend**: `RequirementDetailPage.tsx` and `ActionDetailPage.tsx` each gained a "Restore" button (`ArchiveRestore` icon) shown exactly when the existing Archive button isn't (`requirement.is_archived`/`action.is_archived`), plus a plain "Archived" badge next to the heading so the state is visible without inferring it from button presence alone. No `ConfirmDialog` on Restore — checked `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s own unarchive button first per the task's instruction to verify rather than assume, and confirmed it fires immediately with no confirmation of any kind; Restore is the same shape (reversible again — archiving it right back costs nothing), unlike Archive itself, which stays Tier-1-confirmed. `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s Archive button is now also gated on `!requirement.is_archived` (previously unconditional on `canArchive` alone, a latent gap `ActionDetailPage.tsx` didn't have — its own Archive button was already gated on `!action.is_archived`).

**Found while wiring the frontend, fixed in the same pass (not deferred): `RequirementsPage.tsx` had no way to reach an archived requirement at all.** `list_requirements` already excluded archived rows unless `include_archived=true`, and `ProjectActionsPage.tsx` already exposed that as an "Include archived" filter checkbox with an "Archived" badge per row — but `RequirementsPage.tsx` never sent the parameter and had no such checkbox, so an archived requirement dropped out of the UI's requirements list with no path back to its own detail page (not even a stale link — nothing on the page shows it at all). The new Restore button would have been unreachable dead code for requirements specifically: the whole feature this roadmap item exists to add depends on being able to get to the archived item's page in the first place. Fixed by adding the same `includeArchived` state, `include_archived` query param, `FilterCheckbox`, and per-row "Archived" badge `ProjectActionsPage.tsx` already has (both tile and list view).

**Security review (identify → verify → remediate)**:
- *Authorization*: both endpoints require the same role set their sibling archive endpoint already requires, verified by new `test_unarchive_requirement_requires_manager_or_admin_role`/`test_unarchive_action_requires_manage_role` (a `stakeholder`-only user gets 403 on both). Neither endpoint accepts an `organization_id`/cross-project parameter from the caller; the target's `project_id` is resolved server-side and cross-checked (`requirement.project_id != project_id` 404s; `get_requirement_action_in_project` does the equivalent for actions) — no IDOR surface beyond what `delete_requirement`/`archive_action` already carry.
- *Audit trail*: both endpoints call `log_event` unconditionally before commit, `action="unarchived"`, same `entity_type`/`entity_id`/`actor_id`/`project_id` (and `organization_id` for actions) shape as every sibling mutation in these two routers — no gap versus the existing pattern `services/audit.py` establishes.
- *Noted, not changed*: the requirement side's permission check (`get_effective_project_roles(...) & {PROJECT_MANAGER, PROJECT_ADMINISTRATOR}`, no org-admin bypass) is narrower than the action side's (`require_project_manage`, which does include org admins via `can_manage_project_settings`) and narrower than the project side's own `/archive`/`/unarchive` (also `require_project_manage`). This asymmetry pre-dates this pass — it's `delete_requirement`'s own existing gate, faithfully mirrored rather than widened — and is out of scope for a `/unarchive`-endpoint-addition pass to silently change; flagging it here rather than either fixing it unasked or leaving it undocumented.
- *No new secret, credential, or Restricted-classified field is logged, returned, or stored* — both endpoints return the same `RequirementOut`/`RequirementActionOut` shapes their sibling `GET` endpoints already return.

**Demo data**: neither seed script archived anything before this pass. Added to `seed_demo_data.py` only (not `seed_e2e_dataset.py` — a fixed pre-archived fixture there would risk exactly the non-idempotent-test trap this repo's own testing rule warns about, since a spec that restores it would leave a later run's assumptions wrong; the new Playwright spec below creates and archives its own throwaway fixtures instead, per that same rule): Falcon-3's "Support geofencing with a configurable no-fly boundary" requirement is archived (not restored) after seeding, and the completed "Review remote-ID firmware module against FAA rule text" action is archived after its outcome/comment — both left archived so a manual reviewer has a concrete "Include archived" + "Restore" example to click through, via new `archive_requirement`/`archive_action` script helpers.

**A verification methodology mistake, caught and corrected before trusting any number from it**: the first attempt rebuilt the `tests/container` images (`docker compose build backend frontend`) and then ran `docker compose restart backend` before reseeding and testing — but `restart` only restarts the *existing* container from whatever image it was already created from; it does not pick up a freshly built image the way `up -d --force-recreate` (or a plain `up -d --build`) does. That first backend pytest run (host- and container-invoked alike) and both seed-script runs therefore executed against the pre-session backend image, missing this pass's endpoints, service function, and tests entirely — confirmed after the fact by `docker compose exec backend grep`ping for `unarchive_requirement` and the new seed-script print line and finding neither, and by the demo dataset coming back with zero archived items despite the script supposedly archiving two. Corrected by a full clean-slate reset (`docker compose down -v && up -d --build`) rather than patching around it, then redoing every verification step below against the confirmed-current containers — the same "don't trust a number from a run whose preconditions turned out to be wrong" standard this doc's other entries hold Playwright reruns to.

**Verified** (all against the clean-reset stack): backend — full suite inside the backend container, per `backend/tests/conftest.py`'s convention — **553 passed (549 pre-existing + 4 new), 0 failed**, 0 regressions (running from the host instead reproduces 7 unrelated `SMTPConnectError` failures in `test_invites_and_external_users.py`/`test_oidc_provisioning.py`/`test_org_export_import.py`, traced to `mailhog`'s hostname only resolving inside the Compose network — confirmed environmental, not a regression, by re-running just those files inside the container where all 51 passed). `ruff check` clean on `app/`, `tests/`, and both seed scripts. Frontend: `npx tsc -b` and `npx eslint src/` both clean (same 5 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings this doc already tracks, no new ones). `npx storybook build` succeeded; all 4 new/extended story entries (`RequirementDetailPage`'s `ArchivedRequirementShowsRestoreButton`, `ActionDetailPage`'s extended `ArchivedActionIsReadOnly` plus new `RestoreActionShowsToast`, `RequirementsPage`'s `IncludeArchivedFilterShowsArchivedRequirement`) present in the built `index.json`. Both seed scripts re-run end to end with no errors, this time confirmed via direct API check to actually leave the intended archived fixtures behind (`GET .../requirements?include_archived=true` and `.../actions?include_archived=true` both return the expected archived item). New Playwright spec `requirement-and-action-restore.spec.ts` found and fixed one real bug in itself during this process: its "Archived badge" assertion used a bare `.card, tr` selector which, in list view, also matches the outer `<div className="card">` wrapping the *entire* table (not just one row), so under the full suite's parallel workers it collided with `requirement-archive-confirm.spec.ts`'s own leftover archived fixture and failed a strict-mode check — fixed by scoping through the same xpath-nearest-row-or-card-ancestor pattern `helpers.ts::openRequirementByCode` already uses, then re-verified with `--workers=2 --repeat-each=2` alongside `requirement-archive-confirm.spec.ts` specifically to reproduce the original collision scenario. Full Playwright suite, one clean run against the reset-and-reseeded stack: **74/74 passed**, including the new spec and the four pre-existing archive/filter-adjacent specs (`requirement-archive-confirm.spec.ts`, `requirement-actions.spec.ts`, `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts`, `requirement-links.spec.ts`) confirming the Archive-button gating change (`!requirement.is_archived`) and the new `RequirementsPage.tsx` filter didn't regress anything nearby. `docs/solution-architecture.md` left unchanged: checked how the project archive/unarchive pair was documented there (it isn't — no endpoint-level documentation exists for either), so no architecturally-significant change to record.

Files changed: `backend/app/services/requirements.py`, `backend/app/routers/requirements.py`, `backend/app/routers/actions.py`; `backend/tests/test_requirement_lifecycle.py`, `backend/tests/test_requirement_actions.py`; `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`; `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `frontend/src/pages/RequirementDetailPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/ActionDetailPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/RequirementsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`); `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/requirement-and-action-restore.spec.ts` (new); `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Bulk operations on `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s list view: checkbox column, contextual toolbar, no new backend endpoint

Roadmap item 5 of 6 from the sixth-pass audit — [Bulk operations: none exist](ux-audit-2026-08.md#bulk-operations-none-exist). Unlike the other five items in that pass, this one wasn't a straight build: the audit named it explicitly as having no existing pattern anywhere in the app to copy and needing a design decision first, rather than piecemeal conversion of an already-established shape (the way `ConfirmDialog`/`Toast`/`Popover` rollouts in items 1–4 all were). The design was made up front (checkbox column + header "select all loaded" + contextual toolbar, reusing `ConfirmDialog`/`Toast`/`Popover` rather than inventing bulk-specific versions of any of them) and is now also written up as `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s new "Pattern: bulk operations on a list," the same way `FilterBadge`/`SidePanel`-for-viewing were documented when *they* were introduced — so a second page adopting this pattern later has a reference shape rather than the nearest inconsistent example to copy.

**Scope, deliberately narrow**: `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s table/list view only — not the tile view (checkboxes only render there; the audit itself framed this as "most naturally table-shaped"), and not any other list page in the app. This is a first pilot, not a whole-app sweep; the style guide section above exists precisely so a second page can adopt the same shape later without re-deriving it, rather than this pass trying to roll it out everywhere at once.

**Selection**: `selectedIds: Set<string>`, plus a header checkbox whose `indeterminate` state is set imperatively via a ref (not a settable React prop). "Select all" means all *currently loaded* rows, never "everything matching the filter" — `RequirementsPage` already paginates via `LoadMoreButton` rather than loading a project's full requirement set up front, so promising "every row matching the filter, including ones not yet loaded" from a single checkbox would be misleading; selecting more just means loading more first. Selection survives a "load more" append (the Set is keyed by id, not array position) but is cleared inside `reload()` — i.e. on any filter/search change, and after a bulk action completes — since a fresh fetch can drop previously-selected rows from the result set entirely.

**Toolbar**: renders directly above the table once `selectedIds.size > 0` (list view only), gated on `canManageProject` — the same PM/PA-or-org-admin gate `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s own single-row Archive button already requires. Both bulk actions are administrative in the same way archive already is, and gating the whole checkbox column + toolbar on one boolean avoids a "you can select rows but neither action is available" dead end for a plain stakeholder/member.

**Two bulk actions, both looping over existing single-row endpoints — no new backend endpoint**:
- **Archive selected** loops `DELETE /projects/{id}/requirements/{id}`, the same endpoint the single-row Archive button already calls.
- **Move to stage** opens a `Popover` (stage `<select>`, sourced from the same `stages` state the create form's own "Target version" field already uses) then loops `PUT /projects/{id}/requirements/{id}` — the same direct-edit endpoint `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s `save()` already calls, and its full `RequirementUpdate` payload shape, not a new partial-patch endpoint. Every field on that payload except `target_stage_id` carries the row's own current value forward unchanged (`RequirementsPage` already has every field it needs from the list response — `RequirementOut`/list-endpoint shape matches the detail endpoint's exactly), so the only effective change per row is the stage.

Both loops run sequentially (simpler than bounded concurrency, and fine for the list sizes a first pilot targets) and tolerate individual row failures rather than aborting the batch — one locked or already-archived row shouldn't block the rest. This was a genuine design choice, not a default: a new bulk endpoint would let the backend do this in one transaction, but a first pilot on one page didn't justify a new endpoint plus its own authorization/audit-logging review (see the change-management policy note below) when the existing single-row endpoints, already correctly gated and already audit-logging every mutation via `log_event`, do the job. Revisiting that trade-off is the natural trigger for a second page adopting this pattern with materially larger expected selections.

**Confirmation and feedback**: both actions confirm via the same `ConfirmDialog` (Tier 1, no typed text) the single-row Archive button already uses — copy pluralised and count-bearing (`archiveTitle`'s "Archive this {requirement}?" becomes `bulkArchiveTitle`'s "Archive N {requirements}?"), same tier, since a bulk archive/move is exactly as reversible per row as its single-row equivalent (archive un-archives; a stage move can be moved again) — the count changes the wording, not the tier. After the loop completes (success or partial failure), a summary `Toast` reports `"N updated"` or `"N updated, M failed"`, phrasing modelled directly on `CsvImportWizard.tsx`'s existing "N created, M error(s)" import-summary card, adapted from a persistent card to the transient shared `Toast`. Selection is cleared and the list reloaded regardless of outcome.

**Accessibility**: every row checkbox has its own `aria-label` (`"Select {unique_code} {name}"`) and the header checkbox is labelled `"Select all"` — direct `aria-label` on the `<input>`, the same convention `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s existing reorder buttons already use (the audit's own named-good accessibility example on this page), rather than a wrapping `<label>` element.

**New strings** (`frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `requirements` namespace): `bulkSelectAll`, `bulkSelectRow`, `bulkSelectedCount`, `bulkClearSelection`, `bulkArchiveSelected`, `bulkArchiveTitle`, `bulkArchiveConfirm`, `bulkMoveToStage`, `bulkMoveApply`, `bulkMoveTitle`, `bulkMoveConfirm`, `bulkResultSuccess`, `bulkResultPartial` — the `bulk*Title`/`bulk*Confirm` pairs use the same `{requirement}`/`{requirements}`/`{stage}` terminology tokens every other string on this page already does, so a project with terminology overrides (C-C-03) sees correctly-substituted bulk-action copy too, not just the single-row copy.

**Confirmed no backend change was needed** before starting, per this task's own instruction to verify rather than assume: `RequirementOut` (the list endpoint's response shape) already carries every field `RequirementUpdate` (the `PUT` payload) requires — `name`, `reasoning`, `clarification`, `description`, `component_id`, `category_id`, `owner_id`, `level`, `keywords`, `custom_fields`, `review_date`, `review_lead_days`, `reviewer_id` — so the move-to-stage loop never needs a second round-trip per row to fetch fields the list response doesn't already have.

**Security review (change-management policy's identify → verify → remediate practice, since this touches mutating, audit-logged, RBAC-gated endpoints)**: no *new* authorization surface — both loops call endpoints whose existing role gates (`delete_requirement`: PM/PA via `get_effective_project_roles`; `update_requirement`: any of the three `CAN_EDIT_ROLES`, further narrowed here by the frontend's own `canManageProject` gate on the toolbar) are unchanged and already reviewed when those endpoints were built (`/unarchive` entry above; the original requirement-update endpoint predates this audit). No new field is logged or returned — the `PUT` loop's `change_note` is the literal string `"Bulk move to stage."`, not user-supplied free text, and the archive loop calls the existing endpoint with no body at all, so no new Restricted-classified value enters any log line. Each row's own `log_event` call (already present in both existing endpoints, unconditional before commit) fires once per row exactly as it would for N separate single-row actions — a bulk action doesn't collapse N audit-log entries into one, which is intentional: the audit trail should show what actually happened row by row, not a single opaque "bulk operation" entry.

**Found and fixed along the way, not deferred**: writing the new Playwright spec surfaced that Alpha-1's default `PAGE_SIZE=30` requirement list, after several early iterations of the spec left behind ~15 leftover throwaway "E2E Bulk Req …"/"E2E Bulk Target …" fixtures from debugging the search-box/header-checkbox timing issue below, pushed the project past 30 requirements — which then broke `requirement-and-action-restore.spec.ts`'s own throwaway item off the first page ("Load more (30/39)" in the failure trace), since that spec's own `getByText`/`getByRole("link")` assertions never call `LoadMoreButton`. This wasn't a regression in either page's code — a full clean-slate `docker compose down -v && up -d --build` plus both seed scripts reset it — but it's recorded here as a caution for the next agent debugging a spec iteratively against this same long-lived stack: a failed spec run's own dynamically-named fixtures accumulate exactly like a passing one's do, and enough of them from repeated debugging can push an unrelated spec past a page-size boundary it was implicitly relying on staying under.

**A real, pre-existing race hit while writing the spec, not caused by this change**: `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s fetch effect has no request-cancellation guard (already known — `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts`'s own docstring names it, and its own `settled()` helper works around it). The first version of the new e2e spec typed a search-box filter immediately after a bulk-archive step's own trailing `reload()`, and the archive step's own unfiltered response landed *after* the newly-filtered one and silently overwrote it. Worked around by selecting the second batch's two rows via their own checkboxes (the same approach the archive step already uses) instead of the search box + header "Select all" combination, sidestepping the race entirely rather than adding another `settled()`-style wait — the header checkbox's "select all *loaded* rows" behaviour already has its own dedicated Storybook coverage (`SelectAllHeaderCheckbox`), so the e2e spec didn't need to re-prove it under a race-prone path.

**A real cross-spec regression, found via a full-suite run and fixed, not deferred**: the new spec's throwaway project stage (created via Project Admin so a "move to stage" target exists — a fresh project only seeds one "Scoping" stage) was left behind uncleaned after the first version of the spec finished. A full clean-slate suite run surfaced the consequence: `workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts` — unrelated to this feature, on the same project — failed with a strict-mode violation on `getByRole("button", { name: "Start review" })` resolving to two elements, because that spec assumes exactly one "scoping"-status stage on Alpha-1. A project stage isn't a safe fixture to leave behind the way the four dynamically-named throwaway *requirements* in the same spec are (the precedent `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`'s own custom fields already established as tolerable) — it's a small, shared, enumerable resource other specs query by role/count, not by name. Fixed by adding a final cleanup step: after the move-to-stage step, the spec deletes its own stage via Project Admin's existing delete-with-reassign flow (`DELETE .../stages/{id}?reassign_to=<Scoping's id>`), moving its two fixture requirements back to Scoping first. Re-verified: the bulk-operations spec twice back-to-back (with cleanup, still idempotent), then `workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts` run immediately afterward against the same database — passes, where it failed before the fix.

**Verified**: no backend files touched — confirmed via `git status` before starting, and again after finishing frontend work, since the design spec called for exactly this (existing single-row endpoints, unchanged). `npx tsc -b` and a full-tree `npx eslint .` both clean — zero errors, the same 5 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings this doc already tracks, no new ones. Full Storybook suite: **55 files / 410 tests, all green** (401 after item 3's own pass, 404 after item 4's — this pass adds 6 new stories on `RequirementsPage.stories.tsx`: `BulkSelectShowsToolbar`, `SelectAllHeaderCheckbox`, `MemberSeesNoBulkControls`, `BulkArchiveConfirmAndToast`, `BulkMoveToStageConfirmAndToast`, `BulkArchivePartialFailureShowsToast` — 404 + 6 = 410; that file's `stages` fixture also gained a second entry so the move-to-stage stories have somewhere real to move to, and the file now has 19 stories total). Rebuilt/recreated the `tests/container` frontend image (no bind-mounted source) — actually a full `docker compose down -v && up -d --build` plus both seed scripts, per the "found and fixed along the way" note above; backend was rebuilt too as part of that reset even though unchanged, since it was the simplest way back to a known-clean stack rather than reasoning about which of several already-modified-and-rebuilt-earlier-this-session containers still matched their images. New spec `requirements-bulk-operations.spec.ts` covers the golden path for both bulk actions against Alpha-1 (creates its own throwaway project stage and four throwaway requirements, all timestamped — no seeded/shared data mutated) and passed standalone, repeated back-to-back (`--repeat-each=2`), including its cleanup step. Full Playwright suite, one clean run against the reset-and-reseeded stack: **74/75 passed**. The one failure, `project-admin-templates-and-reports.spec.ts` (Gamma-1's report-template default select racing under full-suite load), is unrelated to this change — it touches neither `RequirementsPage.tsx` nor any file this pass modified, is one of this doc's own already-documented pre-existing flakes (see the fourth-pass entry above: "two of the seven \[…\] are already-documented pre-existing flakes"), and was confirmed to pass standalone on rerun. A first full run (before the fix below) also caught a real self-inflicted regression, described next; the 74/75 number above is from the *second*, corrected full run, after that fix — not the first.

Files changed: `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `frontend/src/pages/RequirementsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`); `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/requirements-bulk-operations.spec.ts` (new); `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Column-header sorting on data tables

Roadmap item 6 of 6, the last item from the sixth-pass audit — [Column-header sorting on data tables](ux-audit-2026-08.md#table-sorting-manual-reorder-only). The audit deliberately left the backend-vs-client-side scope decision open ("depends on how large these lists are actually expected to get in practice"), to be settled once the pagination work above (Directories at scale, two unbounded lists, plus the Org Admin/Project Admin directories item) had shipped and made clear which tables actually page.

**New shared component, not four hand-rolled sorts**: `frontend/src/components/SortableHeader.tsx` — a `<th>` containing a real `<button>` (keyboard-operable, not a bare `<th onClick>`), cycling unsorted → ascending → descending → unsorted, with `aria-sort` on the `<th>` itself rather than an `aria-label` on the button. That last point is deliberate, not cosmetic: an `aria-label` on the button would substitute for the button's own text in the `<th>`'s computed accessible name (accessible-name-from-content rules), silently renaming the columnheader from e.g. "ID" to "Sort by ID" for every screen-reader user and every `getByRole("columnheader", { name })` query in the existing test suite alike — caught by `RequirementsPage.stories.tsx`'s pre-existing `ListView` story, which asserts `getByRole("columnheader", { name: "ID" })`, before it ever reached Playwright. Matches the WAI-ARIA APG "sortable table" pattern rather than inventing a bespoke one. A plain `cycleSort()` helper is exported alongside it so every page's click handler shares the exact same state-transition logic. New `.th-sort` CSS in `theme.css` (button fills the `<th>`'s own padding so a sortable header lines up with a plain-text one beside it). Documented as new style guide "Pattern: sortable column header," including the backend-vs-client-side decision tree below, per Principle 4 ("one component per pattern") — the audit named this risk explicitly (four independent implementations would repeat the exact "no shared component" mistake already found in this app's three tab bars).

**Per-table backend-vs-client-side split, decided against actual current code, not the audit's fourth-pass description (which had drifted — five other roadmap items shipped earlier this same session)**:

| Table | Loads via | Sort location |
|---|---|---|
| `RequirementsPage` (`routers/requirements.py::list_requirements`) | `limit`/`offset` + `LoadMoreButton`, `PAGE_SIZE=30` | Backend `sort`/`order` |
| `ChangeRequestsPage` (`routers/change_requests.py::list_change_requests`) | Same, `PAGE_SIZE=30` | Backend `sort`/`order` |
| Org Admin's Users table (`routers/orgs.py::list_org_users`) | Same, `USERS_PAGE_SIZE=30` (shipped in the "Search + pagination for Org Admin's Users and Groups" item above) | Backend `sort`/`order` |
| `ProjectActionsPage` (`routers/actions.py::list_actions`) | Always `db.scalars(query...).all()` — no `limit`/`offset` at all, never has | Client-side `useMemo` |
| Org Admin's Groups section / Project Admin's Groups tab | `limit`/`offset` + `LoadMoreButton` (same earlier item) | **Neither — out of scope** |

The last row is a real finding, not an oversight: both render each group behind its own `CollapsibleSection` card (name, resolved member/nested-group lists, an "add member" row) — an accordion-of-cards, not a `<th>`-based table. There are no column headers to make sortable; "column-header sorting" doesn't structurally apply, regardless of the fact that both lists are otherwise exactly the kind of backend-paginated directory the rule above would route to a backend param. Named explicitly here rather than silently skipped, since the task brief flagged both as needing verification.

**Backend**: `sort`/`order` (not an existing convention to match — grepped the whole `routers/` tree first, found no prior partial-sort support anywhere) added as optional query params, default `None`/`"asc"`, to the three endpoints above. Omitting `sort` leaves each endpoint's existing default ordering completely unchanged — `list_requirements` still applies its component/category/`sort_order` sort (C-G-04) by default, `list_change_requests` still returns query order, `list_org_users` still sorts by `display_name` — so this is additive, matching the same "optional, non-breaking" contract `limit`/`offset` already established. Allowed `sort` values are constrained via a `Query(..., pattern=...)` regex per endpoint (422 on an unknown field) rather than trusting arbitrary client input as a `getattr()` key: `unique_code`/`name`/`status`/`created_at` for requirements, `proposed_name`/`status`/`created_at` for change requests, `display_name`/`email`/`last_login_at` for org users. Two nullability edge cases handled explicitly and documented on the endpoint docstrings: `ChangeRequestOut.proposed_name` is nullable (a MODIFY_REQUIREMENT change request that didn't touch the name — the list view falls back to the linked requirement's own name for display via `crTitle()`, which the backend sort can't see without an extra join) — null rows sort as empty string, a documented, acceptable approximation rather than a join-per-row fix; `OrgUserOut.last_login_at` is nullable (never logged in) — those rows always sort last regardless of `order`, so "sort by last login, descending" surfaces the most-recently-active users first rather than "never logged in" accounts jumping to the top.

**Frontend**: `RequirementsPage.tsx`/`ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`/`OrgAdminPage.tsx` each gained a `SortState` (typed to that page's own allowed sort keys), added `sort`/`order` to their existing `listParams()`/query-builder function, and added `sort` to the `useEffect` dependency array that already triggers `reload()` on filter/search changes — a header click reuses the exact same refetch-from-offset-0 path a filter change already takes, no new plumbing. `ProjectActionsPage.tsx` (no backend pagination) instead sorts the already-loaded array in a `useMemo`, with a small per-column comparator (`due_date` nulls sort last, same reasoning as the backend's `last_login_at` handling). Sortable columns, per the audit's own "obvious ones only" guidance: `RequirementsPage` — ID, Name, Status (Target·level and Component·category left alone, no natural single-column order); `ChangeRequestsPage` — Name, Status, Created (Target/Level left alone); `ProjectActionsPage` — ID, Title, Outcome, Due date (Type and Assignee left alone); Org Admin Users — Email, Name, Last login (Roles and 2FA left alone — badge-only/boolean columns with no natural order, matching the audit's own example).

**A real accessible-name interaction bug found and fixed before it ever reached Playwright**: caught entirely by the pre-existing Storybook `ListView` story on `RequirementsPage.stories.tsx` (`getByRole("columnheader", { name: "ID" })`), which started failing the moment `SortableHeader`'s button carried its own `aria-label` — see the accessible-name-from-content explanation above. Fixed by dropping the `aria-label` entirely (the WAI-ARIA APG pattern doesn't use one) rather than patching the story's query, since the story's assertion was correct and the component's first draft wasn't.

**A second interaction bug, this time in a new spec, not the app**: `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts`'s new "sort by name" step for change requests initially compared row order immediately after `aria-sort` flipped to the new value. `aria-sort` updates synchronously on the click (a plain React state change), *before* the header-triggered refetch's response has actually landed — so the row-order check could read the *previous* sort's data. Fixed by waiting on the actual network response (`page.waitForResponse` matching `sort=...&order=...`) before asserting order, and wrapping the order check itself in `expect(...).toPass()` so it retries rather than reading the DOM exactly once right after the response promise resolves (a render tick still has to happen). The same fix was applied to the pre-existing Requirements ID-sort step for consistency, even though it happened to pass without it. `ProjectActionsPage`'s client-side sort has no such race (the `useMemo` recomputes synchronously in the same render as the state update), so its Playwright step didn't need this treatment.

**A locator collision found and fixed**: the new Change Requests spec's `createChangeRequest()` helper clicked `getByRole("button", { name: "Create" })` (no `exact: true`) to submit the create form — which, once the new "Created" sortable column header existed on the same page, ambiguously substring-matched both the submit button and the header's button, throwing a strict-mode violation. Fixed by adding `exact: true`. Grepped the whole suite for other non-exact `"Create"` button locators reachable from `ChangeRequestsPage`; none of the others found (`change-request-approval-separation.spec.ts`, `change-request-tasks-and-voting.spec.ts`, `workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts`) were affected — all three already used `exact: true`.

**Verified**: Backend — 3 new tests in `backend/tests/test_sorting.py` (`test_requirements_list_sorts_by_name_and_status_both_directions`, `test_change_requests_list_sorts_by_proposed_name`, `test_org_users_list_sorts_by_email`), each confirming ascending, descending, the unfiltered default order is unchanged when `sort` is omitted, and a 422 on an invalid `sort` value. `ruff check` clean. Full backend suite run twice: once from the host (556 total, 7 failed — the same `test_invites_and_external_users.py`/`test_oidc_provisioning.py`/`test_org_export_import.py` `SMTPConnectError`s this doc already documents as a host-vs-container `mailhog`-hostname artifact, confirmed non-regressions since they're the same named tests), then for real inside the rebuilt `tests/container` backend image (`docker compose exec backend python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`): **556 passed, 0 failed**. `npx tsc -b` and a full-tree `npx eslint .` both clean — the same pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings this doc already tracks (including a new one on `SortableHeader.tsx` itself, from co-exporting `cycleSort` alongside the component — the same accepted pattern `BrandingContext.tsx`/`ThemeContext.tsx` already use), no new warning classes. Full Storybook suite: **56 files / 421 tests, all green**, including new `SortableHeader.stories.tsx` (7 stories: unsorted, ascending/descending/back-to-unsorted after 1/2/3 clicks, a second column active, light/dark) and one new sorted-state story per table (`RequirementsPage`'s `SortByNameRefetchesWithSortParams`, `ChangeRequestsPage`'s `SortByCreatedRefetchesWithSortParams`, `ProjectActionsPage`'s `SortedByTitleAscending`, `OrgAdminPage`'s `UsersSectionSortByEmail`).

Rebuilt/recreated both `tests/container` backend and frontend images. Full clean-slate reset (`docker compose down -v && up -d --build`, both seed scripts) before Playwright verification, per this doc's own established methodology ("the only valid verification is a full clean-slate reseed followed by exactly one suite run") — a first attempt at verification ran a 26-spec targeted regression batch (all passed) immediately followed by a full-suite run *without* reseeding between them, which surfaced 6 failures across specs this pass never touched (`csv-import-wizard.spec.ts`, `org-login-2fa-handoff.spec.ts`, `project-admin-action-types.spec.ts`, `two-factor-auth.spec.ts`, `user-directory-and-bans.spec.ts`, plus `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts` itself on an unrelated pre-existing step) — all six vanished on a genuinely clean single run, confirming they were an artifact of running two suites back-to-back against a database the first run had already mutated (e.g. `project-admin-action-types.spec.ts` renaming/deleting its own "Review"/"Test" seed fixtures on its first pass, then asserting they still exist on an unreseeded second pass — exactly the non-idempotent-test failure mode this repo's own convention warns about, here self-inflicted by the verification process rather than a bug in any spec), not a regression from this change. **Final clean run: 78/78 passed**, including the 4 new/extended sort specs (`requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts`'s two sort steps/describe block, new `project-actions-list-sorting.spec.ts`, `user-access-panel.spec.ts`'s new sort describe block) and the full pre-existing suite — no regression in any of the items 1-5 surfaces (bulk-select checkboxes, reorder buttons, archive/restore filtering, `useToast` wiring) from adding a sortable header row on top of them.

Files changed: `backend/app/routers/requirements.py`, `backend/app/routers/change_requests.py`, `backend/app/routers/orgs.py`; `backend/tests/test_sorting.py` (new); `frontend/src/components/SortableHeader.tsx` (new, + `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/RequirementsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/ChangeRequestsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/ProjectActionsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/styles/theme.css`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts`, `project-actions-list-sorting.spec.ts` (new), `user-access-panel.spec.ts`; `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

This closes the sixth-pass audit's roadmap in full — every item in `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`'s Roadmap table now reads "Done" except three pre-existing, independently-scoped "Partial" rows (`ConfirmDialog`/`Toast`'s broader rollout beyond their original pilot call sites, and the "definition-table CRUD" component's deliberate Stages/Components-tree exclusion) — checked against the task's own instruction to look for stale "N items remain" framing now that this was the last open item, and found none: the doc has no running open-item counter to update, and those three Partial rows are honest, independently-documented partial states unrelated to sorting, not something this pass's completion invalidates.

## File upload triggers: one shared component

Roadmap item — [Extract a shared file-upload-trigger component from `CommentThread.tsx`'s own duplicated inline pattern; convert the other 8–11 file inputs onto it](ux-audit-2026-08.md#file-upload-triggers-three-different-visual-treatments), user-requested directly after confirming this was the right roadmap item to pick up.

**New shared component**: `frontend/src/components/FileUploadTrigger.tsx` — a `.btn`-styled `<label>` wrapping a hidden `<input type="file">`, extracted from `CommentThread.tsx`'s own hand-rolled version of exactly this shape. `onSelect(file)` fires on selection and the input's value is reset immediately after, so choosing the same filename twice in a row still fires a change event. Supports a forwarded `ref` to the underlying input and a `showTrigger={false}` mode that mounts the input without a visible label — both needed by `CsvImportWizard`'s existing `openFilePicker()` imperative handle, used when `RequirementsPage`'s split-button trigger opens the picker itself rather than `CsvImportWizard` rendering its own visible "Import CSV" button a second time on the same screen. Documented as new style guide `Pattern: file-upload trigger`.

**Converted all 11 call sites the finding named, not just the 8 Pattern B ones**: the finding's own text ("extract `CommentThread.tsx`'s own inline shape into a shared component ... closing all three treatments to one") called for converting Pattern A's two existing "good" call sites too, not leaving them as a second hand-rolled copy of the now-shared shape:

- **Pattern A → shared component**: `CommentThread.tsx`'s two attach-file triggers (edit and compose), `CsvImportWizard.tsx`'s own separate hand-rolled copy (its `fileInputRef`/`showImportTrigger` plumbing is now the component's own `ref`/`showTrigger` props).
- **Pattern B → shared component** (8 call sites, previously a bare unstyled native file input): `FileAttachmentList.tsx` (requirement/action attachments), `RichTextEditor.tsx` (report image insert), `PreferencesPage.tsx` (avatar), `ServerManagementPage.tsx` (platform logo, platform login background), `OrgAdminPage.tsx` (shared resources, org logo, org login background). Several of these previously wrapped both a caption *and* the input in one implicit `<label>` — nesting the new component's own internal `<label>` inside that would be invalid HTML, so those were restructured to an explicit `<label htmlFor>` caption (or a plain `<span>`/`<div>` wrapper where no caption existed) sitting beside the new component, matching the pattern `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s org-logo/login-background fields already used. `#org-logo-input`/`#org-login-background-input` ids were preserved exactly (an existing Playwright spec locates them directly by id) by passing `id` through to `FileUploadTrigger`. Three now-unused input refs (`logoInputRef`/`resourceInputRef`/`loginBackgroundInputRef` in `OrgAdminPage.tsx`, `logoInputRef` in `ServerManagementPage.tsx`) were dead even before this change — grepped for any `.current` read and found none — and were deleted rather than left pointing at a ref prop the new component doesn't need for these call sites.
- **Pattern C — left unchanged, an explicit call, not an oversight**: the finding flagged this as "worth a quick, explicit call" rather than assuming every non-A call site converts the same way. `ServerOrganisationsPage.tsx`, `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s import/merge section, and `ProjectListPage.tsx`'s bundle-import forms all pair the `.zip` file field with a visible name/text field and a separate submit step ("Preview"/"Create") — genuinely a form field to fill in before submitting, not a one-click trigger that acts immediately the way every other converted call site is. Converting these to a hidden-input-behind-a-button shape would also drop the browser's own "which file is currently selected" affordance, which these three forms rely on as visible state between selecting a file and clicking submit. Left as `.input`-classed native file inputs.

**Found and fixed along the way, not deferred**:
- `CommentThread.tsx`'s two attach-file triggers had `title` but no `aria-label` — an icon-only control with no accessible name beyond a hover tooltip (Principle 8). Both now carry the same string as both `title` and `aria-label`.
- `csv-import-wizard.spec.ts`'s first test asserted `getByText(new RegExp("E2E CSV Import Row One"))` — an unanchored substring that a second run's own leftover row (from an earlier session against this same long-lived dev stack) could also match, throwing a strict-mode violation on 2 matches rather than 1. The row's own already-`Date.now()`-suffixed title is now captured in a variable and asserted on exactly (`{ exact: true }`), so the test is idempotent regardless of what a previous run left behind.
- `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts` creates a `required: true` list-type custom field (`priorityField`) on Beta-2, a shared, persistent seeded project, to exercise the "Required" checkbox — and never deleted it. Left behind, it permanently blocks *any other* spec's requirement-creation calls on that project (UI or direct API) that don't happen to supply a value for it, since Beta-2 is reused by several other specs. Reproduced directly: `csv-import-wizard.spec.ts`'s second test failed with `400 'Priority <ts>' is required.` on a plain `POST .../requirements` call that has nothing to do with custom fields. Fixed by deleting `priorityField` in the same "delete a custom field" step that already deletes `safetyCriticalField` via the UI. The stray field already present in the live dev stack from an earlier run was deleted directly via the API to unblock verification immediately.

**Verified**: `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full-tree `npx eslint .` both clean — the same pre-existing 6 `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings this doc already tracks, no new ones. `npm run build` succeeds. Full Storybook suite: **57 files / 427 tests, all green**, including new `FileUploadTrigger.stories.tsx` (6 stories: icon+text rendering, selecting a file calls `onSelect` and resets the input's value, `disabled`, `showTrigger={false}` mounts the input without a visible label, light/dark) and an extended `FileAttachmentList.stories.tsx` (`WithFilesAndUpload` now also exercises an actual file upload via `userEvent.upload`).

Playwright: after a full clean-slate reset (`docker compose down -v && up -d --build`, both seed scripts — the previously-running dev stack had accumulated several hours of prior sessions' leftover test data, which surfaced as 11 unrelated failures — 2FA, stage review, project statuses, user bans, none in any file this change touched — on a first un-reset full run; all 11 vanished on a genuinely clean run, confirming they were pre-existing pollution, not a regression), **77/78 passed** in one clean run. The one failure, `report-image-attachment.spec.ts` (its "generate a PDF report" step, asserting the downloaded PDF's bytes contain `/Subtype /Image`), was investigated rather than dismissed since it's the one spec directly exercising a file this change modified (`RichTextEditor.tsx`'s image-insert trigger): isolated reruns showed a genuine, pre-existing intermittent flake (2/5 and 1/3 failures across repeated isolated runs) in the PDF-image-embedding pipeline itself, not in the upload/insert step — and, decisively, `git stash`-ing this change entirely and rebuilding the frontend against the original, unmodified code reproduced the identical flake at the identical assertion (1/3 failed the same way). This confirms the flake predates and is independent of this change; it was not investigated further or fixed here, since root-causing it is a backend/report-generation timing question unrelated to file-upload button styling — flagged here as a real, reproducible, ~30-40%-failure-rate pre-existing issue for a future session, not silently left unmentioned. The dev stack was reset and reseeded a second time after this investigation (which itself left throwaway orgs/projects/nested-group state behind from repeated isolated reruns) to hand back a clean stack.

Files changed: `frontend/src/components/FileUploadTrigger.tsx` (new, + `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/components/CommentThread.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/CsvImportWizard.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/FileAttachmentList.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/components/RichTextEditor.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/PreferencesPage.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/ServerManagementPage.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx`, `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/csv-import-wizard.spec.ts`, `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`; `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Change Requests active-only default, raw-enum label-map fixes, OpenAPI version constant, and `Pattern: FilterPanel`

Four roadmap items from the seventh pass's audit-only findings ([docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md](ux-audit-2026-08.md) roadmap rows ~502–504 and 527), picked up in one session since three are small and independently scoped and the fourth is docs-only.

**1. Default Change Requests to an active-only status filter.** `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx:107`'s `statusFilter` previously initialised to `""` (every status, including `approved`/`rejected`/`withdrawn`, loaded by default) — see [Change Request and Requirement status filters](ux-audit-2026-08.md#change-request-and-requirement-status-filters-show-raw-enum-values). The list is backend-paginated (`PAGE_SIZE=30`/`LoadMoreButton`), so a client-side-only default filter would have silently broken pagination — it would filter only the currently-loaded page, not the true result set — so this needed a backend contract, not just a frontend default.

**Design decision — tri-state filter, not a binary toggle:** `list_change_requests` (`backend/app/routers/change_requests.py:275-323`) gained a new `active_only: bool = False` query param, filtering `ChangeRequest.status.in_([DRAFT, SUBMITTED, IN_REVIEW])` when true and `cr_status` is absent — an explicit `cr_status` still wins over `active_only` if both are somehow sent, since a request for one specific status is more specific than "any active status." On the frontend, `statusFilter`'s type widened from `ChangeRequestStatus | ""` to `ChangeRequestStatus | "" | "active"` (`CrStatusFilterValue`, `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx:43-55`), defaulting to `"active"`. The `<select>` now offers three states: "Active" (sends `active_only=true`, no `cr_status` — the new default), "All statuses" (sends neither param — same as the old default), and each individual status (sends `cr_status`, unchanged from before). A binary "just hide terminal statuses with no way back to true unfiltered" was rejected: the existing individual-status options and the row `FilterBadge`s (`:698`/`:719`) already gave users a way to see exactly one status, and collapsing "Active" and "All statuses" into one option would have removed the previously-default "everything" view entirely rather than just changing what loads first. A sentinel string (`"active"`) distinct from both `""` and any real `ChangeRequestStatus` value was necessary so the three states are distinguishable in both the `<select>`'s value and `listParams()`'s branching (`if (statusFilter === "active") ... else if (statusFilter) ...`) — `toggleStatusFilter` (row-badge click-to-filter) is unchanged: clicking a badge still sets that one status, clicking it again still reverts to `""` (all), not back to `"active"`, matching the roadmap brief's "keep working exactly as today when a specific status is picked."

**2. Fix raw-enum filter/table text to use the existing label maps.** Style guide Principle 12 exists specifically for this. All four instances the audit named, re-verified against current line numbers (code had moved since the audit was written):
- `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`'s status `<select>` (`:745-753`, touched in the same pass as item 1 above) now renders `CHANGE_REQUEST_STATUS_LABEL[s]` instead of the raw `{s}`.
- `RequirementsPage.tsx:889-896`'s equivalent status `<select>` now renders `REQUIREMENT_STATUS_LABEL[s]`.
- `RequirementDetailPage.tsx:649`'s version-history table now renders `REQUIREMENT_STATUS_LABEL[h.status]` instead of raw `{h.status}` — `REQUIREMENT_STATUS_LABEL` was already imported on this file for the page's own status badge (`:467`), so this was a one-line fix.
- `OrgAdminPage.tsx:1615`'s project-group role badge (under Projects & workflow → Manage users) now renders `PROJECT_ROLE_LABEL[g.role]` instead of raw `{g.role}` — `PROJECT_ROLE_LABEL` was likewise already imported and used two lines away for a different badge on the same page.

Checked whether any of the four `Record<Enum, string>` maps could return `undefined` for a value in scope here: all four are exhaustive over their respective TypeScript union types (`RequirementStatus`, `ChangeRequestStatus`, `ProjectRole`) and the fields being indexed (`h.status: RequirementStatus`, `g.role: ProjectRole`) are typed to those same unions, not `string` — so this is a compile-time guarantee, not just a runtime observation, and no latent gap was found.

**3. Fix the hardcoded `FastAPI(version="1.0.0")` OpenAPI metadata constant.** `backend/app/main.py`'s `FastAPI(...)` constructor now passes `version=APP_VERSION` (imported from `app.version`, the same module `GET /api/v1/system/version` already reads) instead of a literal `"1.0.0"` that was never synced with a real release — see [App/API version: investigated, working as designed](ux-audit-2026-08.md#appapi-version-investigated-working-as-designed). This only feeds `/openapi.json`/`/docs` metadata; the real, already-correct version display (`frontend/src/version.ts`, the nav-rail footer) was untouched, per the audit's own finding that it wasn't the reported bug. New test `test_openapi_metadata_version_matches_app_version` (`backend/tests/test_system_version.py`) pins both surfaces — the live `FastAPI` app's own `.version` attribute and the `/openapi.json` response's `info.version` field — against `APP_VERSION`, so a regression back to a literal constant would fail a test immediately rather than silently drifting again.

**4. Document `FilterPanel` as its own style guide `Pattern:`.** Docs-only. New `## Pattern: FilterPanel` section in `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, following the same structure as the other `Pattern:` sections (`Pattern: view toggle`, `Pattern: file-upload trigger`): what the component is (`FilterPanel`/`FilterField`/`FilterCheckbox`, `frontend/src/components/FilterPanel.tsx`), when to reach for it (narrowing filters only — not primary actions, search, or `ViewToggle`, which stay in the main content area), its real call sites verified by grep rather than assumed from the audit's own hedged list of candidates — six pages today, not the "three" the audit's stale side-note said: `RequirementsPage.tsx`, `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`, `ProjectListPage.tsx`, `ProjectReviewsDuePage.tsx`, `ProjectActionsPage.tsx`, `ServerOrganisationsPage.tsx`, plus `NotificationsPage.tsx` (a single `FilterCheckbox`, no `FilterField` — confirms the panel doesn't need multiple controls to earn its place) — and its relationship to `FilterBadge` (Principle 10): a `FilterPanel` control is the only entry point for a value with no row badge, while a value that has both should use `FilterBadge` so the badge and the panel's own select drive the identical filter state, not two independently-tracked mechanisms for the same thing. Two stale cross-references fixed at the same time, per the roadmap item's own note that it was "found while fixing a stale cross-reference": Principle 3's parenthetical side-note (previously "worth remembering next time that list grows") now points at the new section instead of describing the gap it just closed, and the "Missing components identified this pass" table's `FilterPanel` row (previously "Not yet written... used on three pages") now links to it and reflects the real six-page count.

**Found and fixed along the way, not deferred:** none in the touched files beyond the four items themselves — `REQUIREMENT_STATUS_LABEL`/`CHANGE_REQUEST_STATUS_LABEL`/`PROJECT_ROLE_LABEL` were all already correctly exhaustive (see item 2's undefined-check above), so there was no fifth raw-enum instance or map gap to fix. One process note, not a code bug: verifying against the `tests/container` stack, running the full backend pytest suite (which manages its own schema state against that same `reqtrack_test` database, per this doc's existing "test suite manages its own DB" convention) left the database with zero users afterward, and a plain `docker compose restart backend` did not immediately re-run the startup bootstrap that recreates the server-admin user — a direct Python invocation of `services.bootstrap.run_bootstrap` did, and a subsequent full `down -v && up -d --build` was not needed on top of that to get both seed scripts and the full Playwright suite running cleanly. Flagged here since it cost real time diagnosing, not because it's a code defect: `run_bootstrap` itself is idempotent and correct (confirmed by manual invocation), and the sequence "pytest full suite, then reseed" already reset the DB in every prior session's methodology — worth a plain container restart (not just relying on the process already running) between "ran the backend test suite" and "ran the seed scripts" in future sessions, so lifespan's bootstrap step has an unambiguous chance to re-run against the post-pytest schema state.

**Verified**: Backend — 2 new tests in `backend/tests/test_change_request_filters.py` (`test_active_only_hides_terminal_statuses`, `test_explicit_cr_status_wins_over_active_only`) and 1 new test in `backend/tests/test_system_version.py` (`test_openapi_metadata_version_matches_app_version`). `ruff check .` clean (one import-order fix needed in `main.py` itself — `app.version` sorts after `app.services.*`, not before `app.routers`, alphabetically — fixed before this was considered done, not left for a linter warning). Full backend suite inside the rebuilt `tests/container` backend image (`docker compose exec backend python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`): **559 passed, 0 failed** (556 pre-existing + 3 new). `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full-tree `npx eslint .` both clean — the same pre-existing 6 `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings this doc already tracks, no new ones. `npm run build` succeeds.
