## New Requirement split-button, CSV wizard in a Modal with per-field fixed values, and the last two "New requirement form" fixes

Five roadmap items from the seventh pass's audit-only findings ([docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md](ux-audit-2026-08.md) roadmap rows 505/506/507/524/525), all under one "New Requirement creation flow" umbrella: the split-button trigger pattern, moving the CSV import wizard into a `Modal`, a per-field fixed-value toggle on CSV import, and the last two small fixes (labels, auto-grow) on the new-requirement form itself.

**1. `Pattern: split-button trigger`, applied to "New Requirement."** New `SplitButtonTrigger` (`frontend/src/components/SplitButtonTrigger.tsx`) — two adjacent `.btn`s in one `.split-button` group (new CSS in `theme.css`, joined borders/radii so they read as one control): the left button calls `onDefaultAction` directly on click; the right, narrower chevron button (`aria-label="More options"`, a new `strings.common.moreOptions` string) reveals `alternatives` in a `Popover`, reusing that component's positioning/outside-click-close logic rather than a second implementation. Wired up on `RequirementsPage.tsx:434-442`, replacing the previous `addMenuOpen`/`Popover`-based two-option menu that made *every* click (including "Add one," the common case) stop at a menu first: a plain click on "New requirement" now opens the `SidePanel` create form immediately; the chevron reveals "Import from CSV," which calls `csvWizardRef.current?.openFilePicker()` exactly as the old menu's "Import from CSV" option did. `strings.requirements.addOne` was deleted as dead code — its only caller was the now-removed "Add one" menu row.

**Judgment call, not resolved by the audit/style-guide text:** the style guide's own "Pattern: split-button trigger" description (written the pass before this one) allows either "a chevron, or hovering the control" for the reveal affordance. Implemented as click-to-reveal on the chevron, not hover, for two reasons: hover has no equivalent on a touchscreen, and this app explicitly supports mobile viewports (U-P-02) — a hover-only path to "Import from CSV" would make it unreachable there; and every other disclosure control already in the app (`CollapsibleSection`, `Popover` itself) opens on click, not hover, so click-to-reveal keeps this component consistent with the app's existing interaction vocabulary rather than introducing its first hover-triggered interactive menu (which would also need its own touch/keyboard fallback story if it were the *only* path in). Scope, per the item's own "you don't need to find/convert other call sites in this pass" note: only `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s trigger was converted; the component itself is generic and reusable, ready for a future pass to pick up the other menu-hides-a-common-case call sites the audit didn't enumerate.

**2. Move `CsvImportWizard`'s body into a `Modal`.** The column-mapping/preview step (`CsvImportWizard.tsx:398` onward, `headers && (...)`) now opens in a `Modal` instead of the previous always-inline `<div className="card stack">` once a file is picked — the trigger row (Import CSV / Export) is unchanged and stays visible on the page underneath. This needed `Modal.tsx` extended first, resolving its own previously-documented "known implementation dependency" (style guide `Pattern: modal dialog for entity create/rename`): a new `size?: "md" | "lg"` prop (`Modal.tsx:19,42`, `MODAL_MAX_WIDTH_PX`) — `"md"` (default) keeps the original fixed 560px for every existing caller (the vote-comments viewer, `ConfirmDialog`) unchanged; `"lg"` widens to 900px, which the CSV wizard's field/column/hint table needs and every other current `Modal` caller doesn't. Container move only, as scoped — the wizard's own column-mapping/preview logic and both backend endpoints (`GET`/`POST .../requirements/export`/`import`) are unchanged. The Modal's own title ("Map your CSV columns") replaces the previous redundant `<strong>Map your CSV columns</strong>` heading inside the card, since the Modal already renders it as an `<h2>` — no duplicate heading, and every existing `getByText("Map your CSV columns")` assertion (Storybook and Playwright alike) still resolves against the Modal's own title element.

**3. Per-field "map from column" vs. "fixed value for every row" toggle on CSV import.** `CsvImportWizard.tsx:47`'s new `FIXED_VALUE_FIELDS` set names exactly the four candidate fields the audit called out: `component_prefix`, `category_prefix`, `level`, `target_version`. Each gains a checkbox ("Same value for every row," its own per-field `aria-label` since all four would otherwise share one ambiguous name) that swaps that field's column-mapping `<select>` for a fixed-value input matching its real type, defaulting to column-mapped (today's only prior behaviour) so an existing CSV/workflow is unaffected:
- `level` — a `<select>` of the three `RequirementLevel` values, rendered through `REQUIREMENT_LEVEL_LABEL` (style guide Principle 12 — the option text is the human label, the option's own `value` is the raw enum wire string, matching how `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s own per-row create-form level select already does this).
- `target_version` — a `<select>` of the project's real `ProjectStage`s, value = stage name (the canonical CSV column's own expected format — a stage *name* string, not an id), with a "— Project's default stage —" blank option matching the backend's own blank-defaults-to-earliest-stage behaviour.
- `component_prefix`/`category_prefix` — `<select>`s sourced from the project's real `components`/`categories` (not free text), so a fixed value can't produce an unknown-prefix row error the way a typo could; `category_prefix`'s own options narrow to the fixed component's categories once `component_prefix` is also fixed (`CsvImportWizard.tsx:313-320`), falling back to every category (with its owning component's name prefixed for disambiguation) when component isn't itself fixed.

`resolveFieldValue` (`CsvImportWizard.tsx:236`) is the one shared resolution function both `confirmImport` (the real upload) and the preview table call, so the preview can never show a different answer than what's actually uploaded. `missingRequired` was extended to treat a required field (`component_prefix`/`category_prefix`) satisfied by either a mapped column or, if its toggle is on, a non-empty fixed value — `level`/`target_version` are optional either way, unchanged.

**Backend: confirmed no endpoint/schema change was needed or made, correcting an assumption in this item's own original scope note** — per this project's own validation rule ("challenge assumptions made by other agents where relevant"), the audit's phrasing ("verify how the backend import endpoint consumes the mapping and extend it correctly to accept a fixed value") implied the backend has some notion of a column-to-field mapping to extend. It doesn't: `POST .../requirements/import` (`backend/app/routers/requirements.py:291`, `import_requirements`) takes only an `UploadFile` and reads it with a plain `csv.DictReader` against fixed canonical column names — no request-schema field for a "mapping" exists or ever did. The "mapping" concept lives entirely client-side: `CsvImportWizard.tsx` always resolves every field to its final per-row value (mapped-column lookup or fixed constant) *before* building the canonical CSV it uploads (`confirmImport`), so from the backend's perspective a "fixed value" column is indistinguishable from a column that simply happens to repeat the same value on every row — a wire contract that already worked, not new backend behaviour. Pinned explicitly anyway rather than left as an unstated assumption: `test_fixed_value_columns_apply_uniformly_across_every_row` (`backend/tests/test_requirement_csv_export_import.py`) posts a CSV where `component_prefix`/`category_prefix`/`level`/`target_version` repeat one value across three rows (only `name` varies), confirming all three import with the shared field values intact.

**4/5. Add `<label>`s to Name/Reasoning/Description; shared auto-growing textarea.** `RequirementsPage.tsx:555-573`: Name, Reasoning, and Description each now wrap their control in `<label className="stack" style={{ gap: "0.25rem" }}>{text}<input/AutoGrowTextarea .../></label>`, the identical shape Component/Category/Target version/Level already used — style guide Principle 13, trivial, no new component for the label half. Reasoning/Description also swap their fixed `rows={2}` `<textarea>` for the new `AutoGrowTextarea` (`frontend/src/components/AutoGrowTextarea.tsx`) — a controlled `<textarea>` that grows via `scrollHeight` up to a cap computed from `getComputedStyle(...).lineHeight` (theme.css's real `15px`/`1.5` typography) × `maxVisibleLines` (default 8, per the audit's own "roughly 8 lines" suggestion) plus padding/border, so the cap tracks the stylesheet rather than being a magic pixel number re-derived per caller.

**Found and fixed along the way, not deferred: a real auto-grow sizing bug, caught by a Storybook interaction test before it ever reached Playwright.** `theme.css` sets a global `box-sizing: border-box` (`theme.css:60`). `scrollHeight` is always a content+padding measurement and never includes border width, regardless of box-sizing — so assigning `el.style.height = scrollHeight` (a border-box *total*) directly shrank the textarea's actual visible content area by its own border width (2px) on every resize. `AutoGrowTextarea.stories.tsx`'s `GrowsToFitContentWithinTheCap` story caught this immediately (`scrollHeight` 70 vs. `clientHeight` 69, i.e. the element was reporting overflow it shouldn't have had) — fixed by adding `verticalBorder` back to the assigned height (`AutoGrowTextarea.tsx`'s effect), matching how the cap's own `maxHeight` calculation already accounted for border. A second, unrelated story bug in the same file (an over-tight `+1`px tolerance for legitimate sub-pixel rounding between the two measurements) was loosened to `+2` once the real bug above was fixed and the assertion still occasionally failed on rounding alone.

**A second found-and-fixed issue, this time in the CSV wizard's own Storybook stories, not the app:** every story that opens the mapping Modal originally grabbed `within(document.body).getByRole("dialog", { name: "Map your CSV columns" })` immediately after `userEvent.upload(...)`, with no wait — since `Papa.parse`'s `complete` callback (and the resulting `setHeaders` re-render) isn't synchronous with the upload event, this occasionally raced and failed with "component failed to render properly." Fixed by wrapping the first dialog lookup in every affected story in `waitFor(...)`, matching the pattern the file's own pre-existing stories already used for the Export popover.

**Seed data:** checked whether `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`/`seed_e2e_dataset.py` needed updates, per this repo's testing-requirements rule — not needed. None of the five items changed a model field, table, enum value, or the backend's request/response shape (the CSV fixed-value item, confirmed above, is a pure frontend request-shape change against an already-existing wire contract); both scripts were re-run end to end against the reset stack as part of verification below and completed with no errors, unrelated to this pass.

**Verified**: Backend — 1 new test (`test_fixed_value_columns_apply_uniformly_across_every_row`, `backend/tests/test_requirement_csv_export_import.py`). Full backend suite inside the `tests/container` backend image: **560 passed, 0 failed** (559 pre-existing + 1 new). `ruff check app/ tests/` clean. Frontend: `npx tsc -b` and a full-tree `npx eslint src/` both clean — the same 6 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings this doc already tracks (`SortableHeader.tsx`, `BrandingContext.tsx` ×4, `ThemeContext.tsx`), no new ones. `npm run build` and `npx storybook build` both succeed. Full Storybook suite: **59 files / 449 tests, all green** — new `SplitButtonTrigger.stories.tsx` (6 stories: click-performs-default, chevron-reveals-without-firing-default, outside-click-closes, disabled, light/dark) and `AutoGrowTextarea.stories.tsx` (6 stories: accepts input, grows within the cap, caps and scrolls past `maxVisibleLines`, `maxVisibleLines` controls the cap, light/dark); `CsvImportWizard.stories.tsx` extended with `MappingStepOpensAsAModal` and `FixedValueToggleAppliesToEveryRow` (asserts the preview reflects the fixed values on *every* row, then reads the actual uploaded `File`'s text to confirm every data line carries them, not just the first), plus every existing upload-driven story updated for the Modal wrap; `RequirementsPage.stories.tsx`'s split-button story renamed/rewritten (`NewRequirementSplitButtonOpensCreateFormDirectly`, plus a new `NewRequirementChevronRevealsImportFromCsv`) and four other existing stories simplified from a two-click "New requirement" → "Add one" sequence down to one click, plus two new stories (`CreateFormFieldsAllHaveVisibleLabels`, `ReasoningFieldGrowsWithContent`).

Playwright: rebuilt/recreated both `tests/container` backend and frontend images (the `AutoGrowTextarea.tsx` border-box fix above was a real app-code change made *after* the first build, so a second rebuild was needed before this counted as verified against current code — caught by re-checking `git status`/the edit timeline rather than trusting the first build). Nine existing specs updated for the split-button's one-click behaviour (deleting the now-obsolete second `"Add one"` click): `golden-path.spec.ts`, `pelion-v2.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, `requirement-archive-confirm.spec.ts`, `requirement-and-action-restore.spec.ts`, `requirements-bulk-operations.spec.ts`, `review-scheduling.spec.ts`, `workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts` (2 call sites), `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`; `overview-new-requirement-side-panel.spec.ts`'s own doc comment updated to describe the new interaction (its actual test steps were already unaffected, since the deep-link path it covers bypasses the trigger entirely). New spec `requirement-create-split-button-and-csv-fixed-values.spec.ts` covers all three explicitly-requested pieces: the split button's click-vs-chevron behaviour (a plain click opens the form directly with no menu ever appearing; the chevron reveals "Import from CSV" without itself opening the form), the CSV wizard's mapping step as a real `role="dialog"` Modal with the page underneath still present, and the fixed-value toggle's actual import result (uploads a CSV with only a `name` column, fixes all four toggleable fields, then reads the created requirements back via the API to confirm every row — not just the first — carries the fixed component/category/level/target-stage) — passed standalone and via `--repeat-each=2`. Full clean-slate reset (`docker compose down -v && up -d --build`, both seed scripts) and one full suite run: **81/81 passed** (79 pre-existing + 2 new), including every spec this pass touched and the full pre-existing suite alongside it, confirming no regression from the split-button/Modal/fixed-value changes.

Files changed: `frontend/src/components/Modal.tsx`, `CsvImportWizard.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `SplitButtonTrigger.tsx` (new, + `.stories.tsx`), `AutoGrowTextarea.tsx` (new, + `.stories.tsx`); `frontend/src/pages/RequirementsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`); `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `frontend/src/styles/theme.css`; `backend/tests/test_requirement_csv_export_import.py`; `tests/playwright/tests/golden-path.spec.ts`, `pelion-v2.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/requirement-archive-confirm.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/requirement-and-action-restore.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/requirements-bulk-operations.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/review-scheduling.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/overview-new-requirement-side-panel.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/requirement-create-split-button-and-csv-fixed-values.spec.ts` (new); `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Role-display collapsing, the Favourites cluster, `ProjectHistoryPage` onto `ActivityPanel`, and the resource picker dialog

Six roadmap items picked up in one session, all from `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`'s open (blank-Status) rows: `Pattern: role display` (510), the three-item Favourites cluster (511/512/513), `ProjectHistoryPage` → `ActivityPanel` (515), and `Pattern: resource picker dialog` (508). Rows 509/514/516/517-523/526 were explicitly out of scope for this pass (design-blocked or reserved to avoid `OrgAdminPage.tsx` edit collisions with other batches).

**510. `Pattern: role display`.** New `collapseProjectRoles()` (`frontend/src/api/types.ts`, next to `PROJECT_ROLE_LABEL`) implements the precedence the style guide's pattern section already specified: `project_manager` alone if held; else whichever of `project_administrator`/`stakeholder` are held (both, if both — they're tied, not ordered); else `member`. Applied at every real compact `ProjectRole`-badge-list call site, found by grepping every `PROJECT_ROLE_LABEL` usage rather than trusting the roadmap item's own worked example: `ProjectListPage.tsx` (tile view `:296` and list view `:352`), `FavouritesPage.tsx:110`, `PreferencesPage.tsx:573` ("my organisations" project list). Left deliberately uncollapsed: Org Admin's "View access" `SidePanel` (`OrgAdminPage.tsx:~1416`), per the pattern's own access-audit exception.

**Scope correction, found by grep rather than assumed — same category of finding row 507's own scope-correction was:** this roadmap row's title reads "collapse project/org role badges," but the style guide's actual `Pattern: role display` section (and the audit finding it cites) defines a precedence only for `ProjectRole`'s real four-tier structure. Checked whether `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s Users table `Roles` column — the audit's own "The Users table itself shows org roles the same un-collapsed way, comma-joined" aside — was actually in scope: it renders `OrgRole` (`org_admin`/`project_creator`/`member`, `u.roles.map((r) => ORG_ROLE_LABEL[r])`), a different, unordered three-value enum with no precedence defined anywhere in the style guide's pattern text. Collapsing it would mean inventing an unspecified rule, not applying the documented one — left untouched, and flagged here explicitly rather than silently decided either way.

**511. Favourites-only filter on `ProjectListPage`.** A new `FilterCheckbox` ("Favourites only") in the page's existing `FilterPanel`, setting `favorite_only=true` on the same `GET /projects` query param `FavouritesPage.tsx` already used — confirmed against `list_projects` (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`) that it composes with every other existing filter (role/stage/org/search/archived) server-side rather than needing a client-side-only filter. No backend change.

**512. Reactive nav-rail "Favourites" entry.** New `FavouritesContext`/`FavouritesProvider` (`frontend/src/context/FavouritesContext.tsx`), mounted in `Layout.tsx` alongside `TerminologyProvider`/`BrandingProvider`. `hasFavourites` moved out of `LayoutShell`'s own local state (previously recomputed only on mount and on landing at `/projects`/`/favourites`, "the only two places a favourite can be toggled" per the old code's own comment) into the shared context; `ProjectListPage.tsx`'s and `FavouritesPage.tsx`'s toggle handlers both call the new `refreshFavourites()` immediately after their mutating API call resolves. **Judgment call**, since the audit left the exact wiring open ("not just special-casing more routes"): an event-driven refetch via context (toggle succeeds → call `refreshFavourites()` → context re-fetches the full project list once) rather than (a) a global favourites-count field returned from every API response, which would mean touching every endpoint's response shape for one UI affordance, or (b) short-interval polling, which fires the same request repeatedly with no actual signal of change. The context's default value (`{ hasFavourites: false, refreshFavourites: () => {} }`, not `undefined`) is deliberately a real, harmless no-op rather than a value that throws outside a provider — this matters for Storybook coverage below, where `ProjectListPage`/`FavouritesPage` stories render standalone with no `FavouritesProvider` wrapped around them and still work.

**513. `Pattern: view toggle` wired onto `FavouritesPage`.** `FavouritesPage.tsx` now uses `useViewMode("favourites")`/`ViewToggle`, matching `ProjectListPage.tsx`/`RequirementsPage.tsx` exactly — a new list/table view (star/unfavourite, name+summary, organisation, stage badge, roles, requirement count) sits alongside the existing tile grid, replacing the page's previous fixed CSS-grid-only layout. Style guide's `Pattern: view toggle` section marked applied.

**515. `ProjectHistoryPage` converted onto the shared `ActivityPanel` component.** `ProjectHistoryPage.tsx`'s hand-rolled list markup (badge + `describeActivityEntry` + link + timestamp, previously `:92-109`) replaced with `<ActivityPanel entries={changes} getLink={(c) => activityEntryLink(c, projectId)} fullWidth />`. `ActivityPanel` itself gained two new optional props rather than being forked: `getLink` (a project-wide list spans many different requirements/change requests, so — unlike the single-entity detail-page side panels `ActivityPanel` already served — each row needs its own link saying which item it's about; `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s/`ChangeRequestDetailPage.tsx`'s existing calls simply omit it, unchanged) and `fullWidth` (renders at natural width instead of the sidebar's `minWidth: 220`/`alignSelf: flex-start`, since this is now the page's main content, not a narrow companion panel). `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s separate `RequirementVersion`-backed History card (a different data source entirely, per the audit's own explicit distinction) was not touched.

**Judgment call — `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`'s own activity card was deliberately left alone, not converted too, despite rendering the identical shape (badge + `describeActivityEntry` + link + timestamp, its own `:107-129`).** The audit's "Project activity and requirement activity: same data, duplicated rendering" finding names `ProjectHistoryPage.tsx` as the one with duplicated *markup* needing the fix ("The actual duplication is on the frontend: `ProjectHistoryPage.tsx:92-109` hand-rolls its own list markup... instead of reusing `ActivityPanel`") — it does not make the same claim about `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`, which already shares the underlying `describeActivityEntry`/`activityEntityLabel` text-generation functions (the dedup an earlier pass already did) even though its row *layout* independently duplicates the same shape. Converting it too was not part of this roadmap row's scope and risked second-guessing a distinction the audit itself drew deliberately (a dashboard summary card embedded next to stage-progress charts vs. a full-page timeline) rather than an oversight — left alone rather than silently expanding scope; noted here rather than silently decided.

**508. `Pattern: resource picker dialog`.** New `ResourcePickerModal` (`frontend/src/components/ResourcePickerModal.tsx`) — a `Modal` (`size="lg"`) with a source list on the left (`sources: ResourcePickerSource[]`, each just `{ id, label, loadFiles() }`) and the active source's files on the right as a checkbox multi-select, one "Attach selected" action at the bottom. Built pluggable per the style guide's own instruction: today exactly one source is wired up ("{Org} shared resources"), but adding a second (a project's own uploads, a report chapter's existing image pool) is a new array entry for the caller, not a rewrite of the component. **Confirmed via grep before wiring anything up, per this project's own verify-before-building rule**, that `POST /{requirement_id}/files/link` (`backend/app/routers/requirements.py:1187-1217`) really had zero frontend callers anywhere in `frontend/src/` — the audit's own finding, re-checked rather than assumed. Wired to `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s Attachments card: a new "Link from shared resources" button (hidden once the requirement is locked, matching `FileAttachmentList`'s own direct-upload trigger gating — the backend endpoint itself 409s on a locked requirement, so this is UI parity with an existing rule, not a new one) opens the dialog; `onAttach` calls the endpoint once per selected file id (it only accepts one id per call), then reloads the card and shows a toast (`strings.resourcePicker.attachedToast`).

Multi-select-then-attach (a checkbox per file, one "Attach selected" action) was chosen over attach-on-click-per-row: it matches the existing shared-resource checkbox picker on `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx` (proposed-attachment selection) more closely than a single-click-and-close flow would, and avoids a chain of individual network round trips each closing and reopening the dialog for a multi-file attach. Per the item's own explicit scope note, the report-chapter image picker the style guide names as a plausible future consumer of this same component was **not** wired up in this pass — `reports.py`/`ReportsPage.tsx`'s own bespoke resource-selection logic is untouched; the component was just built generic enough that doing so later doesn't need a rewrite.

**Principle 12 applied throughout, not just at the label-map call sites already covered:** `ResourcePickerModal`'s and the Attachments card's new UI text all route through new `strings.resourcePicker.*` keys (`orgResourcesSource`, `noFiles`, `attachSelected`, `linkFromSharedResources`, `attachedToast`) rather than inline English, matching how `strings.changeRequests.selectAttachment`/`noAttachmentsAvailable` already handle the sibling shared-resource picker on `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`.

**No backend change for row 508.** The endpoint already existed and already had a pinning test (`test_org_shared_resource_can_be_linked_to_requirement`, `backend/tests/test_files.py`) — confirmed by grep before assuming a gap, rather than adding a duplicate test for already-covered behaviour.

**Seed data:** checked `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`/`seed_e2e_dataset.py` against this pass's testing-requirements rule — no updates needed. None of the six items changed a model field, table, enum value, or backend request/response shape; all six are frontend display/UI logic (`collapseProjectRoles`) or frontend wiring onto an already-existing, already-tested backend endpoint (`files/link`). Both scripts were re-run end to end against a freshly reset `tests/container` stack as part of verification below and completed with no errors.

**Verified**: Backend — no new tests needed (no backend behaviour changed; `files/link`'s existing coverage confirmed above). Full backend suite inside the `tests/container` backend image (`docker compose exec backend python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`): **560 passed, 0 failed** (unchanged from before this pass, as expected for a frontend-only change set). `npx tsc -b` clean. Full-tree `npx eslint src/`: **0 errors**, 7 `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings — the same 6 this doc already tracks, plus one new instance on `FavouritesContext.tsx` (co-exporting `useFavourites()` alongside `FavouritesProvider`, the identical accepted pattern every other context file in the app already uses — `AuthContext.tsx`, `BrandingContext.tsx`, `ThemeContext.tsx` — not a new warning class). `npm run build` succeeds. ## UX audit, seventh-pass roadmap: "New user" onto Modal, org action menu, Leave organisation relocated (518-520)

Continuing the same batch (see the 517 entry above). Items 518-520 all touch `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s Overview/Users region, implemented in roadmap order.

**518.** `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s "New user" form (email/name/password + submit, permanently visible below the Users table) converted to a `Modal` (default `size="md"`) opened by a "New user" button — the first real usage of the revised Principle 3 in this codebase, setting the shape items 519/521 in this same batch follow. `createUser()` previously had no `try`/`catch` at all (a failed create threw uncaught); it now matches `createGroup()`'s existing pattern — closes the modal and shows a success `Toast` (new `strings.orgAdmin.userCreated`) on success, shows an error `Toast` on failure without closing the modal.

**519.** New `ActionMenu` (`frontend/src/components/ActionMenu.tsx`) — a `MoreVertical` kebab trigger opening a `Popover`-backed menu (`role="menu"`/`"menuitem"`, reusing `Popover`'s positioning/focus-trap/outside-click-close rather than a new implementation, the same reuse `SplitButtonTrigger` already makes). Combines Overview's rename and export actions behind one trigger (`triggerLabel={strings.orgAdmin.orgActions(orgLabelCap)}`, e.g. "Organisation actions"). Rename opens a `Modal` (replacing the always-visible inline input + conditional "Rename" button); export calls the existing `exportOrg()` handler directly and closes the menu, per the item's own scope note that a relocated action isn't a create/rename flow and doesn't need a dialog. **Permission-preserving judgment call, not incidental**: the *old* code only gated the rename input behind `advanced != null` (org-admin-only, since a non-admin 403s on advanced-settings) — export and leave were both offered to every member unconditionally. Collapsing rename+export into one menu component made it tempting to gate the whole menu behind `advanced`, which would have silently taken Export away from ordinary members — instead the menu always renders, and only the "Rename" *item* is conditionally included in its `items` array. `ActionMenu` also gained a `disabled` prop so the trigger can be disabled while `exportingOrg` is true, preserving the old button's in-flight-disable behaviour that would otherwise have been lost when the label ("Exporting…") stopped being visible once the menu closes on click. New `docs/ux-style-guide.md` "## Pattern: action menu" section (between "Pattern: modal dialog for entity create/rename" and "Pattern: resource picker dialog") plus a `MoreVertical` row in the Tokens icon table and an `ActionMenu` mention in "Framework & primitives".

**520.** Destination decided: Preferences' existing "Your access" tab, not a per-org card on `/orgs` — that tab already lists every org a user belongs to (role badges, projects, groups), so a "Leave" button per row extends an existing list rather than building a second, independent one (this project's own shared-component-reuse rule; a *new* org-list-with-leave-buttons on `/orgs` would have been a second, slightly-different implementation of the same "list my orgs" shape `PreferencesPage.tsx` and `OrgListPage.tsx` both already have). **A real gap found and fixed while moving it, not just relocated**: `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s old "Leave {org}" button fired `DELETE /orgs/{id}/membership` immediately, with zero confirmation of any kind — the exact pattern the style guide's "Pattern: confirmation, in two tiers" was written against. Now Tier 1 `ConfirmDialog` ("Leave {org.name}?" — reversible, an admin can re-add the user) plus a success `Toast`. `PreferencesPage.tsx`'s mount-time org/project/group-loading `useEffect` body was extracted into a standalone `loadMyAccess()` so `leaveOrg()` can call it again after a successful leave — the left org's own projects have to disappear from the picker too, not just the org row itself. Accessible naming: the button's visible label is the static "Leave" (the row already shows the specific org's name via `<strong>{org.name}</strong>`), but its `aria-label` is `` `Leave ${org.name}` `` — short and per-row-distinguishable, separate from the longer `title` hover text (`Remove your own membership in ${org.name}`), so the accessible name doesn't repeat the full sentence for a screen-reader user while still disambiguating multiple "Leave" buttons on the same page (caught by a first draft of the Storybook story failing on an over-long aria-label). `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s `leaveOrg()`/`leaveError`/the inline `btn-danger` button removed entirely, along with the then-unused `navigate`/`useNavigate` and `LogOut` icon import — not left as a second, dead copy per this item's own explicit instruction.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; full-tree `npx eslint src/` clean (0 errors, the same 7 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings, no new ones); `npm run build` succeeds. Storybook: new `ActionMenu.stories.tsx` (6 stories) plus updates to `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`/`PreferencesPage.stories.tsx` — full suite **472/472 passing across 61 files** (up from 461/60 before this batch).

**Two pre-existing, unrelated bugs found while verifying against the live stack and fixed per this project's "fix, don't defer" rule, not logged and left**:
- `preferences-and-theme.spec.ts`'s own "access tab lists direct and inherited org-group membership" step asserted a bare, page-wide `getByText("(via a nested group)")` — correct the first time this spec ever ran against a given database, but ambiguous (strict-mode violation) on any later run, since it creates a fresh nested-group pair for the same shared `orgAdminAlphaBeta` persona every time and never cleans the old ones up, so each repeat run adds one more "(via a nested group)" match on screen. Scoped to the specific `<li>` containing that run's own uniquely-suffixed parent-group name instead.
- `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types.spec.ts` permanently mutated the shared "E2E Beta Software" org's seeded `DEFAULT_PROJECT_STATUSES` (deleted 3 of the 4 down to a single renamed "Active (E2E)") with no cleanup — since `seed_e2e_dataset.py` only seeds once, this spec could only ever pass the *first* time it ran against a given database, exactly the non-idempotent-test failure mode this project's own conventions call out. Rewritten to create its own disposable org (which gets the same four default statuses and default link types automatically, on org creation, same as every org) and two throwaway projects (which default to the org's lowest-sort-order status, "Proposed", the same way Beta-1/Beta-2 did) instead of touching Beta's shared fixture data at all — confirmed idempotent by running it twice in a row.

Playwright: ran the full set of specs touching `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s Overview/Users/Groups regions or Preferences' Access tab (`admin-page-titles-and-version-footer`, `role-display-collapsing`, `org-group-nesting`, `user-access-panel`, `org-security-controls`, `org-rename-and-test-email`, `leave-organisation` (new), `preferences-and-theme`, `project-list-org-scoping`, `org-bundle-export-import`, `org-merge-import`, `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types`) against the rebuilt Docker stack (`docker compose -f tests/container/docker-compose.yml build frontend backend && up -d --force-recreate frontend backend`; `seed_e2e_dataset.py` reported already-seeded, no reseed needed for a frontend-only + test-hygiene change set): **17/17 passing** on the settled run. ## UX audit, seventh-pass roadmap: "Integrations & Security" split into OAuth/SSO, Email, Security (523)

Sixth of the seven-item batch (see the 517/518-520/521 entries above). Same flat-regroup shape as items 517's Users/Groups split — no new `ResourceMenu` capability, per the style guide's own settings-hierarchy addendum, which already named this exact split as the anticipated next step.

**Regroup.** `OrgAdminGroupKey`'s `"integrations-security"` replaced with `"oauth-sso"` | `"email"` | `"security"`. The single `activeGroup === "integrations-security"` block (SSO/OIDC + its group-mappings sub-block, SCIM, SMTP & email, Security, Personal Access Tokens — 5 `CollapsibleSection`s) split cleanly into three: OAuth/SSO (SSO/OIDC + SCIM), Email (SMTP & email), Security (Security + PATs, unchanged from where an earlier pass already put PAT lifetime).

**SCIM placement — the one non-obvious call, per this item's own "use judgment" note.** Grouped with SSO/OIDC under OAuth/SSO rather than folded into Security. Reasoning: SCIM and SSO/OIDC are both, fundamentally, *identity-provisioning integrations* — mechanisms by which an external system (an IdP) pushes or pulls user/group state into this org — whereas Security's other members (2FA requirement, self-signup, external-user policy) are policy toggles this org's own admins set directly, with no external system in the loop. SCIM doesn't touch anything more "security-sensitive" than SSO/OIDC does (both handle credentials/tokens), so severity wasn't the deciding factor — the mechanism (provisioning vs. policy) was. Recorded here per this project's own "flag a non-obvious call explicitly" rule, exactly as the roadmap item asked.

**A real design snag found while splitting, not just a mechanical JSX move.** The SSO group-mappings sub-block and the SMTP & email card both persisted via a single shared "Save advanced settings" button that used to live further down the *same* combined page (their own inline notes literally said "saved with the Security settings below"). Splitting into three separate top-level pages would have silently broken this: a user editing SSO mappings on the new OAuth/SSO page would have had no visible control left to actually save them, since the button that used to do it moved to a different page entirely. Fixed by giving OAuth/SSO's mappings sub-block and Email's SMTP card each their own explicit save button (new strings `saveMappings`/`saveEmailSettings`) — both still call the exact same `saveAdvanced()` function Security's own button calls. This is safe, not a duplicate-endpoint hack: `OrgAdminPage` is one React component whose state (`smtpHost`, `advanced.sso_group_mappings`, `require2fa`, `patMaxLifetimeDays`, ...) all lives at the top level regardless of which resource-menu group is currently rendered, so calling `saveAdvanced()` from any of the three pages submits the complete, correct `OrgAdvancedSettings` payload — the same reasoning `SMTP & email` and `Personal Access Tokens` already relied on when they shared one button on one page, just now applying across three pages instead of one.

**Copy cleanup.** The pre-existing shared button (now Security-only) relabelled `strings.orgAdmin.saveAdvanced` from "Save advanced settings" to "Save security settings" — "Advanced" is the retired UI concept this whole roadmap batch (and the fourth/fifth passes before it) has been dismantling; leaving the label behind on the one surviving button would have quietly reintroduced it. 4 Playwright call sites and 2 Storybook assertions updated for the rename.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; full-tree `npx eslint src/` clean (0 errors, same 7 pre-existing warnings). Storybook: full suite **477/477 passing across 61 files** (up from 472 before this item — 2 new stories, `EmailSettingsSave`/`SsoMappingsSave`, proving the new per-group save buttons actually persist). `npm run build` succeeds.

Playwright: full rebuild (`docker compose -f tests/container/docker-compose.yml build frontend && up -d --force-recreate frontend`) and a run of every spec touching this region — `org-security-controls.spec.ts` (2FA/external-user-policy, now on "Security"), `org-rename-and-test-email.spec.ts` (SMTP override + test email, now on "Email"), `scim-provisioning.spec.ts` (now on "OAuth/SSO"), `sso.spec.ts` (unaffected — configures SSO via direct API calls, not the Org Admin UI form, confirmed by grep before assuming it needed changes): **10/10 passing**.

Files changed: `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/org-security-controls.spec.ts`, `org-rename-and-test-email.spec.ts`, `scim-provisioning.spec.ts`; `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## UX audit, seventh-pass roadmap: RequirementDetailPage's History and Activity cards merged (516)

Last of the seven-item batch (see the 517/518-520/521/523 entries above). Unlike the other six, this roadmap row's own scope note said "merge or clearly re-label" — a design call, not a mechanical fix. The product decision, stated explicitly in the batch's own brief: merge, not relabel-only, keeping both renderings.

**What "History" and "Activity" actually were.** `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s "Change log" card (`strings.requirements.history`, despite the audit's own shorthand calling it "History") rendered `RequirementVersionEntry[]` — the requirement's own approved version/status-transition ledger, one row per version, via `GET .../requirements/{id}/history`. The `ActivityPanel` sidebar rendered `ChangeEntry[]` — the general audit-log feed (comments excluded from *this* particular feed per the file's own C-A-09 note... correction, checked directly: comments ARE included in `ChangeEntry`/`get_project_changes`, the file's C-A-09 note is about the version-history table specifically never showing comments, which is obviously true of a version ledger) via `GET .../requirements/{id}/activity`, itself a filter over `get_project_changes` — two genuinely different data sources with real overlap (both show version/status changes) but neither a strict subset of the other (only Activity shows comments/links/attachments/archiving; only Version history shows the change-note text an editor typed for that specific version).

**Merge shape.** One card, a two-button `aria-pressed` toggle (`Table`/`Activity` lucide icons — the Tokens table's icon-collision rule ruled out reusing `LayoutGrid`/`List`, which specifically mean tile vs. list elsewhere in the app), both renderings kept intact — selecting a view swaps which one is on screen, nothing was dropped. New copy: "Version history" for the table (replacing the old, arguably-mismatched "Change log" heading — the table was never actually labelled "History" in the UI despite that being this whole item's own name for it), "Activity" unchanged for the feed. State: `useUiPreference<string>("requirement_detail_history_view", "activity")` called directly, **not** a new `useHistoryView`-style wrapper analogous to `useViewMode`. Judgment call, per this item's own "your call" note: `useViewMode`'s own `ViewMode` type is hardcoded to `"tiles" | "list"`, so wrapping it (or writing a same-shaped sibling) for a `"versions" | "activity"` pair would either force a misleading type or duplicate `useViewMode`'s five-line body for no real reuse — calling `useUiPreference` directly, narrowing the loosely-typed stored string the same way `useViewMode` itself does inline, was simpler and no less discoverable for a pattern used in exactly one place today.

**`ActivityPanel` gained a `bare` prop** (skip the outer `.card` and its own hardcoded `<h2>Activity</h2>`) rather than forking a second component or duplicating its entry-list JSX inline in `RequirementDetailPage.tsx` — the merged card supplies its own card and its own toggled heading (which needs to read "Version history" or "Activity" depending on state, not always "Activity"), so nesting the full `ActivityPanel` unchanged would have produced a card-in-a-card with a stuck, wrong heading. Every other `ActivityPanel` caller (`ChangeRequestDetailPage.tsx`'s side panel, `ProjectHistoryPage.tsx`'s full-width list) is unaffected — `bare` defaults `false`.

**Layout consequence, not just a card swap.** The page's `.side-grid` (a fixed `1fr 240px` two-column grid: everything else in the main column, `ActivityPanel` alone in the narrow second column) collapsed to a single `.stack` — once Activity's content moved into the merged card in the main column, nothing was left to occupy the second column, and a `.side-grid` with an empty second slot would have been a dead, meaningless wrapper. Confirmed no other page-level styling depended on this specific `.side-grid` instance (the CSS rule itself is shared and untouched for every other page still using it).

**Style guide.** Added a note under the existing "Pattern: view toggle (tile vs. list)" section rather than a whole new `## Pattern:` — this is the same underlying idea (a small `aria-pressed` two-button toggle, `useUiPreference`-backed, remembered per-user) applied to a second, differently-shaped pair of views, not a structurally new pattern. Explicitly named as *not* literally reusing the shared `ViewToggle` component (different icon/label pair, `ViewToggle`'s own type is tile/list-specific) — a future third case with the same tile/list semantics should still use `ViewToggle` directly; this note exists so a *fourth* similarly-shaped-but-different pair doesn't have to re-derive the "small toggle + `useUiPreference`, doesn't have to be the literal shared component" reasoning from scratch.

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx eslint` clean on all touched files. Storybook: full suite **480/480 passing across 61 files** (up from 477 before this item) — `RequirementDetailPage.stories.tsx` gained `HistoryActivityToggleSwitchesViews` (default-Activity, toggle to Version history, toggle back, `aria-pressed` state on both buttons throughout) and `NoDuplicateHistoryOrActivityCard` (exactly one "Activity"/"Version history" `<h2>` on the page, not the old two-card duplication); `ActivityPanel.stories.tsx` gained `Bare`. The pre-existing `VersionHistoryShowsLabelledStatus` story needed a decorator change (`withAuth` → `withStatefulAuth`) since its play function now has to actually click the toggle before the table is reachable — a no-op `setUiPreference` would have left the toggle click silently inert.

Playwright: new `requirement-history-activity-toggle.spec.ts` — creates a throwaway requirement (not seeded data, since editing it to produce a real version/activity entry is the point), edits it to generate one version-history row + one activity entry, confirms Activity is the default view, toggles to Version history and confirms the *same* edit appears as a table row (not a second copy), and — the one thing Storybook can't exercise — confirms the chosen view survives a full page reload via the server-synced `ui_preferences` bag, not just in-memory component state. Also ran the full existing set of specs touching `RequirementDetailPage` to catch any layout-removal regression from dropping `.side-grid`: `comment-editing-and-attachments`, `resource-picker-link-requirement-attachment`, `requirement-and-action-restore`, `requirement-actions`, `review-scheduling`, `requirement-archive-confirm`, `workflow-bypass-attempts` — **9/9 passing** (including the 2 new toggle-spec tests).

Files changed: `frontend/src/pages/RequirementDetailPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/components/ActivityPanel.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/requirement-history-activity-toggle.spec.ts` (new); `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## UX audit roadmap: explicit requirement approval action + change-request lock guard (509)

The last of the roadmap's "needs a design pass first" items before this pass: no standalone way to approve a requirement existed, and nothing stopped a change request from targeting a still-draft one. Touches authorization (who can lock a requirement out of direct editing) and the change-request workflow, so this went through the identify → verify → remediate review `change-management-and-secure-development-policy.md` calls for on security-sensitive changes, same as this project's other hardening passes.

**Design, resolved by extending existing precedent rather than inventing a new one.** The roadmap item itself pointed at the answer: `LOCKED_STATUSES = {APPROVED, COMPLETED}` (`services/requirements.py:25`) already draws the line between "editable directly" and "editable only via an approved change request" (C-G-12) — `update_requirement`'s own lock check already enforces it for direct edits. The fix extends that one existing line to change-request creation too, rather than introducing a second, parallel notion of "which statuses need a CR."

**`create_change_request` guard.** A `MODIFY_REQUIREMENT` change request now requires the target requirement's current version to be locked (`is_locked()`, reusing the exact helper `update_requirement` already calls) — a 400 otherwise, with a message pointing the caller at editing directly instead. `NEW_REQUIREMENT` change requests are unaffected (there's no existing requirement to lock-check).

**New `POST .../requirements/{id}/approve`.** The actual, previously-missing standalone path out of `draft`/`reviewed` — added alongside `complete`/`uncomplete` in `routers/requirements.py`, same shape (a precondition-checked single-purpose action, not a detour through the general `PUT` edit endpoint, which already supported `status=approved` but only as one field among a whole edit payload). Gate: project manager only — not the broader `require_project_manage` (which also admits project administrators and org admins) — matching `decide_change_request`'s own explicit check and `update_requirement`'s existing inline comment on its `status=approved` branch, both citing C-U-03's clarification that names requirement approval as a *Project Manager* privilege specifically, layered on top of what administrators/stakeholders can otherwise do.

**The bug found alongside it, fixed in the same pass, not deferred.** `decide_change_request`'s `MODIFY_REQUIREMENT` approval branch unconditionally set `status_value=RequirementStatus.APPROVED` — regardless of the requirement's status *before* the change request was approved. With no creation-time guard, a change request could previously be opened against a `draft` requirement and, on approval, silently promote it straight to `approved` bypassing any real review; worse, one opened against an already-`COMPLETED` requirement would, on approval, silently revert it back down to `approved` — the requirement's "this shipped" state disappearing as a side effect of an unrelated field edit, with no message that it happened. Now that `create_change_request`'s own guard guarantees the target is already locked (`approved` or `completed`) at creation time, and status transitions monotonically upward otherwise, the current status at decision time is always one of those two — so `status_value=None` (the existing `apply_new_version` convention for "carry the current value forward unchanged") is the correct fix, not a different forced value. `approval_authority_id` is unaffected either way, since it's only reassigned when `status_value == RequirementStatus.APPROVED` is explicitly passed — a modify-CR against already-approved content isn't a fresh approval, so the original approver of record correctly stays attributed.

**Frontend.** `RequirementDetailPage.tsx` gained an "Approve" button (`btn-primary`, `CheckCircle` icon) shown exactly when `requirement.requires_approval` is true (an existing, previously-unconsumed field — `draft`/`reviewed`) and the viewer holds `project_manager`; "Make change request" now only renders once `requirement.is_locked` is true, matching the new backend guard instead of always being offered. `markCompleted`/`unmarkCompleted` — found lacking try/catch and toast feedback while touching this exact button row, and fixed in the same pass per this project's own "fix, don't defer" rule — gained both, matching the shape `archive`/`restore` already had on the same page. `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`'s "Select a requirement" dropdown (the modify-CR creation form) now filters to `is_locked` requirements only, with an explanatory hint (`noLockableRequirements`) when none exist yet, and its default-selection logic picks the first *locked* requirement rather than blindly the first one in the list.

**Test-suite blast radius, found and fixed rather than left broken.** ~20 call sites across 10 backend test files previously created a `MODIFY_REQUIREMENT` change request against a requirement that was still `draft` at that point — exactly the gap this item closes, so every one of them now correctly 400s under the new guard. Each was updated to approve the requirement first (either via the new `/approve` endpoint directly, or relying on an existing `_approve_current_stage` call already present earlier in the same test): `test_change_request_field_tracking.py` (7 of 9 call sites; the other 2 already locked via stage approval), `test_requirement_lifecycle.py`, `test_reporting_and_changes.py`, `test_notifications.py`, `test_change_request_tasks_and_votes.py` (a shared `_submitted_cr` helper), `test_org_lifecycle.py`, `test_project_export_import.py` (also required bumping a version-history-length assertion from 2 to 3, since the new explicit approve step is itself a real version), `test_project_structure_admin.py`, `test_custom_fields.py`, `test_security_hardening.py`. Both seed scripts had one CR-creation site each affected by the same gap: `seed_e2e_dataset.py`'s "pre-existing change requests for volume" loop now approves each target requirement first; `seed_demo_data.py`'s Solstice Cloud Platform change request was initially assumed to need the same fix, but investigating first (rather than adding it unconditionally) showed that requirement's own seed spec already set its status to `"approved"` directly — the added approve call 409'd as "already approved," confirming the assumption was wrong, and was removed rather than left in as a redundant no-op.

**A second-order bug found while fixing the first**: `frontend/src/testing/storybook-helpers.tsx`'s `buildRequirement()` previously defaulted `is_locked`/`requires_approval` to fixed `false` values regardless of the `status` override a story passed in — so a story built with `status: "approved"` (locked, in the real app) was silently mocked as unlocked. This had been latent and harmless until this pass made `is_locked`/`requires_approval` drive real UI (the "Make change request" link, the new "Approve" button); fixed at the root by deriving both fields from `status` by the same rule the backend uses (`LOCKED_STATUSES`/`REQUIRES_APPROVAL_STATUSES`), with an explicit override still winning — rather than patching every affected call site's overrides individually. This surfaced one further pre-existing story inconsistency once fixed: `RequirementDetailPage.stories.tsx`'s `StakeholderCanEditNotArchive` used `status: "approved"` while asserting the edit form was reachable — status "approved" is locked for every role including a stakeholder, so that assertion was only ever passing because of the mock bug being fixed here; corrected to `status: "draft"`, which is what the story actually intends to demonstrate.

**Verification.** Backend: full suite, **565/565 passing** (including 5 new tests: `test_approve_requirement_transitions_draft_to_approved`, `test_approve_requirement_requires_project_manager_role`, `test_approve_requirement_rejects_an_already_locked_requirement`, `test_create_change_request_rejects_a_still_draft_requirement`, and the regression test for the `decide_change_request` bug, `test_decide_change_request_preserves_completed_status_instead_of_reverting_to_approved`). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Storybook: full suite **483/483 passing across 61 files** (up from 480) — new stories `ManagerCanApproveDraftRequirement` (clicks Approve, asserts the toast), `StakeholderDoesNotSeeApproveOnDraftRequirement`, and `NoLockableRequirementsShowsHint` on `ChangeRequestsPage.stories.tsx`; `ManagerCanArchiveAndComplete` gained assertions that "Make change request" now shows and "Approve" doesn't, once locked. One story-authoring bug found and fixed along the way: the "no lockable requirements" hint paragraph, originally nested inside the `<label>` wrapping the select, made `getByLabelText("Select a requirement")` fail (the hint's own text became part of the label's accessible name) — moved to a sibling `<p>` outside the `<label>`, which is also the more correct a11y shape (a select's accessible name shouldn't absorb unrelated help text below it).

**Playwright.** Full rebuild of the `tests/container` stack, then a clean-slate reseed (`seed_e2e_dataset.py` + `seed_demo_data.py`) — necessary because the backend pytest suite's own session-scoped `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` fixture runs against the same `reqtrack_test` database this stack's E2E/demo data lives in, per `docs/e2e-workflows.md`'s own documented gotcha. New `requirement-approval.spec.ts` (a throwaway requirement, not seeded data, since approving isn't reversible from the UI — mutating a shared seeded requirement would corrupt it for every other spec and for a repeat run of this one): a stakeholder sees neither "Approve" nor "Make change request" on it and a direct API approve call 403s; the project manager sees and uses "Approve," after which "Make change request" appears and "Approve" doesn't. `seed_e2e_dataset.py` also gained a lock step for Delta-1 Terminology Demo's first requirement, needed for `terminology-coverage.spec.ts`'s existing "Make {changeRequest}" assertion to have anything to find post-guard.

**Four pre-existing, unrelated spec breakages found and fixed along the way, per this project's own "fix, don't defer" rule**, surfaced only by running the *entire* suite rather than just the specs this item touches:
- `golden-path.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, and `pelion-v2.spec.ts` (the three broad top-level walkthrough specs, as opposed to `tests/e2e-workflows/`'s narrower specs) still drove the "New project" form via `getByPlaceholder("Name"/"Summary")` and an xpath ancestor-climb to a `.card` — stale since an earlier, already-`Done` roadmap item (521) converted that form to a `Modal` with real `<label>`s, which apparently only updated the `e2e-workflows/` specs its own decisions.md entry named, not these three. All three now scope to `page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "New project" })` and use `getByLabel`, matching the convention already established in `project-list-org-scoping.spec.ts` and friends.
- `mockup-engagement.spec.ts` separately needed its own new requirement approved before raising a change request against it (this item's own guard) — added an explicit "approve the requirement" step via the UI, since this spec never baselines a stage the way `golden-path.spec.ts` does.
- `terminology-coverage.spec.ts`'s "Make {changeRequest}" assertion needed Delta-1's target requirement locked (see the seed-script fix above).

Full suite (after all of the above): **85/86 passing**, `tests/e2e-workflows/requirement-and-action-restore.spec.ts` the one failure — re-ran in isolation immediately after, **2/2 passing**, confirming a transient/resource-contention flake from the full-suite run rather than a real regression (matches the same pattern already seen from `org-merge-import.spec.ts` earlier in this same verification pass, which also failed once under full-suite load and passed cleanly both standalone and on a second full run).

Files changed: `backend/app/routers/requirements.py`, `backend/app/routers/change_requests.py`; `backend/tests/test_requirement_lifecycle.py`, `test_change_request_field_tracking.py`, `test_reporting_and_changes.py`, `test_notifications.py`, `test_change_request_tasks_and_votes.py`, `test_org_lifecycle.py`, `test_project_export_import.py`, `test_project_structure_admin.py`, `test_custom_fields.py`, `test_security_hardening.py`; `backend/scripts/seed_e2e_dataset.py`, `seed_demo_data.py`; `frontend/src/pages/RequirementDetailPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/ChangeRequestsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `frontend/src/testing/storybook-helpers.tsx`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/requirement-approval.spec.ts` (new); `tests/playwright/tests/golden-path.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, `pelion-v2.spec.ts` (pre-existing, unrelated `getByPlaceholder`-vs-Modal breakage fixed along the way); `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## UX audit roadmap: Modal conversion sweep, first batch (526, partial)

Item 526 ("convert every entity-create/rename flow currently on `Popover`/inline onto `Modal`, per the revised Principle 3") is explicitly the broadest item left on the roadmap, described in its own row as cutting across nearly everything above. Rather than attempt the whole surface in one pass, this batch scoped tightly to Principle 3's own named entity list (`docs/ux-style-guide.md`: "a project, an organisation, a user, a group, a requirement") cross-referenced against what was actually still Done for each: project/organisation/user creation and org rename were already converted (items 518/519/521); **group** creation and the **requirement** create form were not, despite both being named explicitly. A fifth flow, the Change Requests page's own "New change request" form, was added to this batch even though "change request" isn't one of Principle 3's five named nouns — it's the single most field-heavy inline create form left anywhere in the app (a kind selector plus a per-field checkbox-revealed editor, explicitly called out as such in this same document's historical "Pattern: create panels" mockup section) and had never received *any* layer conversion at all, unlike every other entity create flow in the app, which had at least reached `Popover`/`SidePanel` before this pass.

**Four flows converted, all straight `Popover`/inline → `Modal` container swaps with no field-layout changes**, since `Modal`/`SidePanel`/`Popover` all share the same `card stack` dialog chrome via `dialogA11y.ts` — confirmed by diffing `Modal.tsx` against `SidePanel.tsx` before touching either call site, rather than assuming:
- `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s "New requirement" form (`SidePanel` → `Modal`, `size="lg"` given its field count — name/reasoning/description/component/category/target version/level plus custom fields plus the empty-component/category quick-setup variant).
- `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`'s "New change request" form (bare inline `<div className="card stack">` → `Modal`, `size="lg"`) — the trigger button changed from a toggle (`setShowForm((v) => !v)`) to a plain open (`setShowForm(true)`), matching every other Modal-fronted create button in the app; closing is `Modal`'s own Escape/backdrop/× affordances instead of a second click on the same button.
- `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s "New group" (`Popover` → `Modal`; state renamed `newGroupPopoverOpen`→`newGroupModalOpen` to match the `newUserModalOpen` naming convention item 518 already established, and its now-unused `anchorRef`/`useRef` import removed — `Modal` doesn't anchor to a trigger the way `Popover` does).
- `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s "New group" (same conversion, project-scoped endpoint + the required role select item 488 added).

**Why not a Popover for these:** the decision tree's own leaf split is "create or rename an entity" → `Modal` vs. "one or two fields, a single quick decision" → `Popover` — group creation is 1-2 fields but is creating a new entity, which the tree resolves by entity-vs-quick-action, not by field count (the "Add link" `Popover` on the same requirement-detail page, by contrast, is correctly left alone below — it's a quick decision *about* an existing requirement/action, not creating either).

**Verified, not assumed, that both flows still have the DOM-order fragility their earlier `SidePanel` conversions already surfaced.** `Modal`/`SidePanel`/`Popover` all portal to the end of `document.body`, so any Playwright/Storybook query that resolves "first combobox on the page" unscoped will silently start resolving to whatever inline control (typically a `FilterPanel` status select) precedes the portal in DOM order once a form moves from inline to a portalled layer — this exact class of breakage was already fixed once for `RequirementsPage`'s own conversion (`review-scheduling.spec.ts`/`workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts`, roadmap item 489) and reproduces identically for `ChangeRequestsPage`: `golden-path.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, `change-request-tasks-and-voting.spec.ts`, and `change-request-approval-separation.spec.ts` all used `page.getByRole("combobox").first()` immediately after opening the form. All four now scope to `page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "New change request" })` first, matching the established fix.

**Test updates were near-zero-diff because `role="dialog"`/`aria-label={title}` is identical across `Modal`, `SidePanel`, and `Popover`** — every existing `getByRole("dialog", { name: ... })` query kept working unchanged for all four flows; only the DOM-order-dependent unscoped queries above needed a code change, and a handful of stale comments/story names referencing "SidePanel"/"popover" for these specific flows were corrected for accuracy (`RequirementsPage.stories.tsx`, `overview-new-requirement-side-panel.spec.ts`'s own doc comment, `review-scheduling.spec.ts`, `workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts`, `org-group-nesting.spec.ts`; `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`'s `GroupsSectionCreateGroupViaPopover` → `GroupsSectionCreateGroupViaModal`, `ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`'s `GroupsTabCreateGroupViaPopover` → `GroupsTabCreateGroupViaModal` — both renames checked against the whole repo for other references first; only `docs/decisions.md`'s own historical entries named the old export names, left as-is since they're a past-tense record). `ChangeRequestsPage.stories.tsx`'s five create-flow stories (`ModifyRequirementFieldTogglePrefills`, `ModifyRequirementCreateDisabledUntilFieldSelected`, `NewRequirementKindShowsPlainCreateForm`, `SubmitCreatesChangeRequest`, `NoLockableRequirementsShowsHint`) had no prior Modal/SidePanel/Popover conversion to inherit a scoping pattern from at all (this form had never left inline), so each was rescoped from bare `canvas.*` queries to `within(dialog).*` directly against the new `Modal`.

**Deliberately not touched this pass, named rather than silently dropped — the remainder of item 526's own scope:** the new-custom-field inline row and the Stages/Components/Categories/Action-Types one-step "New X" rows in Project Admin (these are the `DefinitionList`/bespoke definition-table shape items 478/480 already reviewed and deliberately left alone as a different, intentional pattern — a flat table row-add, not a freestanding entity-create form); the org report-template nested-accordion create flow; the three duplicated "New PAT" nested-accordion forms (Org Admin, Server Management, Preferences); and `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s "Create and link a new action" `SidePanel` (built in item 496, before this revision of Principle 3 existed — a real remaining case of the pattern the revision targets, since a brand-new `Action` is exactly the "not detail about the current view" shape the revision's reasoning applies to regardless of `Action` not being one of Principle 3's five example nouns). `Add link`/`Link existing action` on the same page are correctly left on `Popover` — they're a quick 1-2-field decision about an existing entity, not a create flow, per the decision tree above.

**Verified.** `npx tsc -b` and a full-tree `npx eslint .` both clean. Storybook: the four touched story files (91 tests) plus the full suite (**483/483 passing across 61 files**) both green — no regression outside the touched files. Rebuilt/recreated the `tests/container` frontend image (no bind-mounted source; backend untouched, no rebuild needed). Playwright: one failure on first run (`requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts`'s status-filter test, expecting a seeded draft requirement to disappear under an "approved" filter) turned out to be leftover state from an earlier, unrelated run against the same long-lived dev database rather than a regression from this change — confirmed by a full clean-slate reseed (`docker compose down -v && up -d --build`, both seed scripts) and a clean rerun, per this project's own documented methodology for exactly this failure shape (see the "Extend terminology overrides" and "explicit requirement approval action" entries above, both of which hit and diagnosed the identical pattern). Final clean-slate run, the 22 specs identified as touching any of the four converted flows (grepped for `"New requirement"`/`"New Requirement"`/`"New change request"`/`"New group"` across the whole suite, not assumed): **22/22 passing** — `golden-path.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, `pelion-v2.spec.ts`, `overview-new-requirement-side-panel.spec.ts`, `change-request-tasks-and-voting.spec.ts`, `change-request-approval-separation.spec.ts`, `review-scheduling.spec.ts`, `workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts`, `org-group-nesting.spec.ts`, `role-display-collapsing.spec.ts`, `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`, `requirement-and-action-restore.spec.ts`, `requirement-approval.spec.ts`, `requirement-archive-confirm.spec.ts`, `requirement-create-split-button-and-csv-fixed-values.spec.ts`, `requirement-history-activity-toggle.spec.ts`, `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts` (3 tests), `requirements-bulk-operations.spec.ts`.

Files changed: `frontend/src/pages/RequirementsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `OrgAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`); `tests/playwright/tests/golden-path.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/change-request-tasks-and-voting.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/change-request-approval-separation.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/review-scheduling.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/org-group-nesting.spec.ts`, `e2e-workflows/overview-new-requirement-side-panel.spec.ts`; `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## UX audit roadmap: Modal conversion sweep, second batch (526, continued)

Picked up the three cases the first batch named as deliberately not touched: the org report-template create/edit form, "New personal access token," and `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s "Create and link a new action" — closing out item 526 to just the two genuinely different-pattern exclusions (the `DefinitionList`/bespoke definition-table rows, and the org report-template/PAT/"New PAT" forms' own remaining scope, both already named and left alone deliberately in the first batch).

**Scope correction, found by grep rather than trusting the roadmap row's own wording:** item 526's own text describes "the three duplicated 'New PAT' nested-accordion forms (Org Admin, Server Management, Preferences)." Checked directly rather than assumed, per this project's own "validate rather than take a claim at face value" rule: only **Preferences** has an actual PAT *creation* form (`createPat`/`newPatName` etc.) — `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s and `ServerManagementPage.tsx`'s own PAT sections are list-and-revoke UI only (an org/server admin managing *other users'* tokens), with no create form of any kind to convert. What the three files actually share is the nested-`CollapsibleSection` (`variant="plain"`) *idiom*, not three copies of a create flow. Only Preferences' own "New personal access token" form was converted; Org Admin's and Server Management's PAT sections are untouched, correctly — there was nothing there in scope.

**Three flows converted, same straight container-swap shape as the first batch — no field-layout changes:**
- `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s "Create and link a new action" (`SidePanel` → `Modal`, default `size="md"`) — built in item 496, before the Principle 3 revision existed; a brand-new `Action` has no "what came before it" in the app's reading order (per the pattern's own reasoning) regardless of `Action` not being one of Principle 3's five named example nouns. "Link existing action" and "Add link" on the same page are correctly left on `Popover` — quick 1-2-field decisions about an existing entity, not creates.
- `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s org report-template create/edit form (nested `CollapsibleSection` → `Modal`, `size="lg"` given its field count — name/accent colour/cover-page/logo toggles/footer text/intro/chapters/appendices/chapters-per-component). This form is also reused for *editing* an existing template (`startEditTemplate`), not just creating — kept as the same single form/`Modal`, title switching between "New template"/"Edit template" exactly as the pre-conversion accordion already did; still one `Modal` state (`templateFormOpen`), not two. A "New template" button was added next to the template list (there was previously no separate open step — the form was simply always rendered, collapsed by the accordion itself) plus a resulting `openNewTemplateForm`/`closeTemplateForm` pair; `startEditTemplate` now also opens the modal, and delete/save both funnel through `closeTemplateForm` so the modal can't be left open pointing at a template that was just saved or removed.
- `PreferencesPage.tsx`'s "New personal access token" (nested `CollapsibleSection` → `Modal`, default size). Same shape: a "New personal access token" trigger button added next to the PATs tab's heading (previously the form had no open/close step, just an always-rendered accordion), new `strings.preferences.patNew` string, `openPatForm`/`closePatForm`/`resetPatForm` helpers factored out of `createPat`'s previous inline field-clearing. The post-create "copy your token now" card is unchanged and still renders on the page itself (not inside the modal, which closes on success) — the same place it always has.

**Why `Modal` and not `Popover` for the report-template/PAT forms, despite the group-creation precedent the first batch already established:** both are multi-field forms (7+ distinct inputs), squarely on the `Modal` side of the decision tree's field-count split, not the 1-2-field `Popover` side "New group" used.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full-tree `npx eslint src/` both clean. Storybook: the three touched story files (`PreferencesPage.stories.tsx`, `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`, `RequirementDetailPage.stories.tsx`, 79 tests) plus the full suite (**486/486 passing across 61 files**, up from the first batch's 483/61 — three new stories: `NewReportTemplateOpensModalAndCreates`, `NewReportTemplateModalCancel`, `PatsTabCreateModalCancel`) both green. `npm run build` succeeds. Rebuilt/recreated the `tests/container` frontend image (backend untouched, no rebuild needed) and ran the three Playwright specs that actually exercise these flows against the live rebuilt stack (grepped the whole suite for "Personal Access Tokens"/`patNamePlaceholder`/"report-templates"/"Report templates"/"Create and link a new action" rather than assumed which specs touch this): `personal-access-tokens.spec.ts`, `project-admin-templates-and-reports.spec.ts`, `requirement-actions.spec.ts` — **3/3 passing**. Not re-run: the full 60-file Playwright suite, since this batch's changes are narrowly confined to the three flows above with no shared-component or DOM-order-dependent change of the kind that broke unrelated specs in the first batch (`Modal`/`SidePanel` share identical `role="dialog"`/`aria-label` semantics, so no locator in any other spec depends on which of the two a given trigger opens).

Files changed: `frontend/src/pages/RequirementDetailPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `OrgAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `PreferencesPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`); `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/requirement-actions.spec.ts`, `project-admin-templates-and-reports.spec.ts`, `personal-access-tokens.spec.ts`; `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).
