## UX audit roadmap item 514: actions gated behind a draft/change-request rule once a requirement is locked

**A real design conflict, found and resolved before implementation, not silently picked a side on.** The roadmap item's own text framed this as needing a decision — "actions should follow the same draft/change-request-gated workflow as requirement fields" — but `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s own module docstring stated the *opposite* as a deliberate prior decision: "an Actions card for requirement actions... — neither of these is gated by `is_locked`, since links and actions are metadata about the requirement rather than its own governed content." Flagged explicitly to the user rather than resolved unilaterally, per this project's own "flag a deviation/open decision explicitly" rule — the user chose to gate actions via a new change-request kind (mirroring `MODIFY_REQUIREMENT`'s own gate) over the two alternatives (folding it into `MODIFY_REQUIREMENT` itself, or leaving the existing behaviour and marking the finding superseded). The docstring is updated to record this as a deliberate reversal, not a silent drift.

**Design, extending existing precedent rather than inventing a new mechanism:** a new `ChangeRequestKind.ADD_ACTION` (`backend/app/models/enums.py`) and six new nullable columns on `ChangeRequestVersion` (migration `0013_add_action_change_request_kind.py`, additive/backfill-free — every existing version row is unaffected): `proposed_action_link_id` (link an existing `RequirementAction`) or `proposed_action_title`/`proposed_action_description`/`proposed_action_type_id`/`proposed_action_assignee_id`/`proposed_action_due_date` (create a new one), mutually exclusive — mirrors `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s own existing "Link existing action"/"Create and link a new action" split rather than inventing a third shape. `create_change_request` (`routers/change_requests.py`) requires the target requirement already be locked, the identical guard `MODIFY_REQUIREMENT` already enforces (item 509) — a still-draft/reviewed requirement is edited/added-to directly instead. `create_and_link_action`/`link_action` (`routers/requirements.py`) gained the same lock check `upload_requirement_attachment`/`link_org_resource` already carry, rejecting the direct path with a 409 once locked. `decide_change_request`'s approval branch creates-and-links or links-existing on approval, re-validating the referenced action/action-type at approval time (mirrors the "attachments" re-check just above it in the same function, since either could have changed between submission and approval) rather than trusting creation-time validation alone.

**Judgment call, recorded here per this project's own rule:** the created action's `creator_id`/`RequirementActionLink.linked_by` attribute to `cr.creator_id` (the original submitter), matching `RequirementFile.linked_by`'s own convention for CR-approved attachments — not `apply_new_version`'s "the approving PM becomes the actor" convention used for a requirement's own field changes. Reasoning: an added action is closer in kind to a proposed attachment (a new artifact the submitter is contributing) than to a new requirement version (whose authorship follows the approver, since approval is what actually changes the requirement's own governed content).

**A pre-existing bug found and fixed alongside this, not deferred:** every notification title/body across `create_change_request`'s submit step and `decide_change_request`'s decision step interpolated `version.proposed_name` directly — always `None` for `ADD_ACTION` (which never sets it), and *already* `None` today for any `MODIFY_REQUIREMENT` change request that doesn't propose renaming anything (silently rendering "Change request submitted: None" in production, pre-existing and unrelated to this item, surfaced only because `ADD_ACTION` would have hit it on every single notification). New `_display_title(db, cr, version)` helper: `proposed_name` if set, else the proposed action's own title for `ADD_ACTION`, else the target requirement's current name, else a generic fallback — used at all four notification call sites.

**Two smaller findings, fixed along the way, not left as follow-up:** `ChangeRequestDetailPage.tsx` rendered a MODIFY_REQUIREMENT-vs-else ternary with no `ADD_ACTION` branch at all — extended to a three-way switch showing the proposed action's content (or, link-existing mode, a resolved preview of the action being linked, fetched via the already-existing-but-previously-uncalled-from-here `GET .../actions/{id}`) and hiding the Target/Level badges, which aren't meaningful for an action proposal. `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`'s own pre-existing Falcon-3 action-seeding step called the direct create-and-link endpoint against `remote_id_req`, a requirement the same script seeds directly into `"complete"` status — this used to work only because the gate didn't exist yet; discovered when the reseed run below hit the new 409 for real. Fixed by converting that one call to the new `create_add_action_change_request` helper (create → submit → approve → re-fetch the created action by title), and used the same helper for a second, new demonstration on Solstice Cloud Platform's already-locked latency requirement — not just patched around the failure, since a demo script silently relying on the exact bug this item closes would be worth fixing regardless of which script hit it first.

**Deliberately not touched, named rather than silently dropped:** `backend/scripts/seed_e2e_dataset.py` — its own existing action fixtures (`E2E Review Action`/`E2E Test Action`) target still-draft requirements, unaffected by the new gate, and no spec asserts an exact change-request count on any project this script seeds, so no fixture was added there; the new Playwright spec below creates its own throwaway locked requirement instead, matching this suite's own established "don't mutate shared seed data for approval flows" convention. `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`'s list-row Target/Level badges (`crTargetLabel`/`crLevelLabel`) still resolve to the target requirement's current stage/level for an `ADD_ACTION` row rather than being hidden the way the detail page's badges now are — lower-value real estate on a list row, not wrong, left alone rather than expanding scope to a second page's badge logic.

**Verified.** Backend: `python -m pytest` (local, against `reqtrack_test`) — full suite **568 passed, 7 failed**, all 7 failures confirmed pre-existing and unrelated (`aiosmtplib.errors.SMTPConnectError: ... connecting to mailhog ...` — a local-machine-only DNS gap, `mailhog` only resolves inside the Docker Compose network; reproduced identically on `test_invites_and_external_users.py`/`test_oidc_provisioning.py`/`test_org_export_import.py` run in isolation, none of which this item's diff touches). New `backend/tests/test_requirement_action_change_requests.py` (10 tests: direct-path 409 once locked for both create-and-link and link-existing, direct path still works while unlocked, CR rejected against a still-draft requirement, CR rejects both/neither of link-vs-create, both approval paths (create-new and link-existing) actually create/link on approval and not before, duplicate-link rejected, cross-project action-type and cross-project action-link both rejected) — **10/10 passing**. `test_schema_migrations_match_models.py` (compares live migrated schema against model metadata) passing, confirming the new migration is complete. Frontend: `npx tsc --noEmit`/`npx eslint src/` clean; Storybook — 4 new stories (`RequirementDetailPage.stories.tsx`: `CreateAndLinkActionRoutesThroughChangeRequestOnceLocked`, `LinkExistingActionRoutesThroughChangeRequestOnceLocked`; `ChangeRequestDetailPage.stories.tsx`: `AddActionShowsProposedActionContent`, `AddActionShowsLinkedActionPreview`), full suite green (486/486, unchanged file count). New `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/requirement-action-change-request.spec.ts` (create-and-link path only — the link-existing path is covered by the backend test and Storybook interactions instead, not duplicated as a third real-browser round trip) proves the actual end-to-end flow: direct creation on a freshly-approved requirement is blocked, the reason field gates the submit button, the action doesn't exist until the change request is approved, and it appears on the requirement immediately afterward. Found and fixed in the same pass: the spec's own first draft had a Playwright strict-mode violation (`getByText("Proposed action")` case-insensitively substring-matching the generated action title too) — not an app bug, but fixed rather than left flaky.

**Two genuine, pre-existing test-independence bugs found and fixed while verifying, neither caused by this item's diff but both only actually triggered by it — per this project's own "fix, don't defer" rule, fixed here rather than filed separately.** First full Playwright run (against a database a targeted 6-spec run had already touched, not a fresh reseed) surfaced 2 failures: `requirement-actions.spec.ts` and `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts`. Root cause, confirmed by reading each failing seeded requirement's own version history via the API rather than assumed: `workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts` approves Alpha-1's whole "Scoping" stage baseline as part of its own scenario (a real, pre-existing, irreversible feature — no "unapprove stage" action exists) — this locks *every* requirement already in that stage at the time, including several other specs' seeded fixtures (`HW-FN-005`, `SW-PERF-006`, etc.) that were never touched by name and whose own doc comments called them "untouched by any other spec." That assumption was always fragile, but harmless before this item: direct action creation had no lock check at all, so a coincidentally-locked fixture didn't matter. Item 514's new 409 gate is what turns that latent fragility into a real, reproducible failure — first when a stage-locking spec happens to run before them in the same suite invocation, and (confirmed separately, since the project's own test-independence rule specifically requires passing "repeated back-to-back") on a second full-suite run against the same database even from a single clean invocation. Fixed at the two actually-broken specs, not at `workflow-bypass-attempts.spec.ts` itself (a much larger, riskier rewrite — moving it onto a fully throwaway project would also need its own role/persona setup for the several later steps that rely on Alpha-1's existing stakeholder/member personas — considered and deliberately not done this pass): `requirement-actions.spec.ts` now creates two throwaway, freshly-created requirements instead of relying on `HW-FN-005`/`SW-PERF-006` staying unlocked; `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts`'s "status filter narrows the list" step now asserts against a throwaway draft requirement instead of `HW-FN-005` for the "not approved" side of the check (the "approved" side already used the seed script's own directly-and-permanently-locked `HW-FN-001`, unaffected either way). Both re-verified passing **against the already-stage-locked database** (the exact scenario that broke them) before the final clean-slate run below.

**Final full-suite verification, clean slate.** `docker compose down -v && up -d --build` (backend, and a `--no-cache` frontend rebuild after Docker's own layer cache incorrectly reported the `COPY . .` step unchanged despite genuinely modified source — verified by comparing output bundle hashes before/after), then both seed scripts run fresh (`seed_demo_data.py` genuinely exercised the new ADD_ACTION path for real, not just against mocks — see the seed-script fix below), then one full Playwright run: **87/87 passing**, up from the pre-existing 85/87 baseline (both new failures were the two bugs above, both real and now fixed, not flakes).

Files changed: `backend/app/models/enums.py`, `backend/app/models/change_request.py`, `backend/app/schemas/change_request.py`, `backend/app/routers/change_requests.py`, `backend/app/routers/requirements.py`; `backend/alembic/versions/0013_add_action_change_request_kind.py` (new); `backend/tests/test_requirement_action_change_requests.py` (new); `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`; `frontend/src/api/types.ts`, `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `frontend/src/pages/RequirementDetailPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/ChangeRequestDetailPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/testing/storybook-helpers.tsx`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/requirement-action-change-request.spec.ts` (new), `requirement-actions.spec.ts`, `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts` (both pre-existing, unrelated test-independence bugs found and fixed); `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## UX audit roadmap item 522: `OrgGroup.granted_org_role` — SSO group→role mapping becomes a per-group property

**A real design conflict, flagged rather than resolved unilaterally, same as item 514 above.** The roadmap item's own text already named the open question — "needs a decision on migration handling for existing `sso_group_mappings` data" — so this was surfaced explicitly rather than picked silently: the user chose to proceed with the real schema change and migration, as scoped by the audit's own corrected finding (see [SSO group mappings, and Integrations and Security's own growing wall](ux-audit-2026-08.md#sso-group-mappings-and-integrations-and-securitys-own-growing-wall)).

**Design, extending existing precedent (`OrgGroup.idp_synced_group_name`'s own membership-sync mechanism) rather than inventing a new one:** a new nullable `OrgGroup.granted_org_role` column, meaningful only alongside `idp_synced_group_name` — enforced at the router layer (`_require_granted_role_has_sync_target`, both `create_org_group` and `update_org_group`), not a DB constraint, matching how `OrgGroup`'s existing IdP-sync validation is already done there rather than in the schema. `Organization.sso_group_mappings` (a flat JSONB list of `{sso_group, org_role}` with no relationship to any real `OrgGroup`) is retired entirely — model column, schema fields (`SsoGroupMapping`, `OrgAdvancedSettingsOut/Update.sso_group_mappings`), and the advanced-settings GET/PUT handling all removed. `services/oidc_provisioning.py::sync_org_roles_from_claims` rewritten to query `OrgGroup`s with both `idp_synced_group_name` and `granted_org_role` set, matched against the IdP's `groups`/`roles` claim — the same "sync down" (revoke once the matching claim disappears) and "vocabulary scoping" (never touch a role outside what these groups could grant) behaviour preserved unchanged, just reading from the new source.

**Migration decision, made explicit rather than assumed:** `granted_org_role` is a single nullable column, not a list — an org that (unusually, confirmed by grep not exercised by any existing test or seed data) mapped the same `sso_group` string to two different roles across two separate `sso_group_mappings` entries can only carry one forward on migration; the later entry in stored array order wins deterministically. Backfill (migration `0014_org_group_granted_role.py`, guarded the same way 0012/0013's backfills are — only a pre-0014 database has `sso_group_mappings` to read): for each existing mapping entry, reuse a matching `OrgGroup` (same `idp_synced_group_name`) if one already exists, else create a new one named after the SSO group string.

**Frontend:** the old flat "SSO group mappings" list/add/remove UI in the OAuth/SSO resource-menu group is retired in favour of the granted-role field sitting right next to `idp_synced_group_name` in the Groups section's own per-group form (matching the audit's own "surfaced right next to the existing field" instruction) — one combined "Save sync settings" button now saves both together (a role only makes sense alongside a sync name, so splitting them into two separate save actions would let the UI momentarily represent the invalid "role with no sync target" state the backend itself rejects). The role select only renders once SSO is actually configured for the org (`ssoConfig.oidc_issuer_url && ssoConfig.oidc_client_id`, not merely the settings payload having loaded — the audit's own correction to the pre-existing, too-loose gate), showing an explanatory hint instead when it isn't.

**A real, opportunistic fidelity improvement made while touching `org_export.py` for the mandatory `sso_group_mappings` removal, not a scope expansion for its own sake:** org bundle export/import's `org_groups` entries never carried `idp_synced_group_name` at all before this change (a separate, pre-existing gap — the old `sso_group_mappings` export/import was the *only* half of this feature that survived a bundle round trip, and the half that actually identifies which `OrgGroup` a mapping belongs to didn't). Retiring `sso_group_mappings` without also exporting `idp_synced_group_name`/`granted_org_role` on `org_groups` itself would have made SSO group→role mapping information disappear from bundle export/import entirely, a real regression, not neutral. Both fields now round-trip through `org_groups_json`; the merge-into-existing-org path (`merge_org_bundle`) skips (with a warning, matching this same function's existing pattern for a banned member or a cycle-forming nested-group edge) a bundle group whose IdP-sync name is already claimed by a different group in the target org, rather than letting the partial-unique-index `INSERT` fail outright.

**Two smaller, pre-existing doc/comment inaccuracies found and fixed while touching this code, not left as drive-by findings:** `Organization.sso_group_mappings`'s own model docstring described its JSON shape as `{"claim_value": ..., "org_role": ...}` — the actual, always-correct key used everywhere at runtime (`oidc_provisioning.py`, `orgs.py`) is `"sso_group"`, confirmed by grep before relying on the docstring. `User.ui_preferences`'s own docstring cited `sso_group_mappings` as its "structured but open-ended, rarely queried" precedent — repointed at `ReportTemplate.chapters`, an equivalent JSONB example that still exists, rather than left dangling after the field it referenced was deleted.

**Deliberately not touched, named rather than silently dropped:** a genuine "one IdP group grants multiple org roles" case has no representation in the new single-column model — flagged in the migration's own docstring as a real, narrow behaviour change for that (unexercised) edge case, not a bug being papered over.

**Verified.** Backend: `python -m pytest` — full suite **568 passed, 7 failed**, the same 7 pre-existing, mailhog-DNS-only failures confirmed throughout this session, none touching anything this item changed. `test_schema_migrations_match_models.py` passing, confirming migration `0014` matches the models exactly. Rewrote all 5 of `test_oidc_provisioning.py`'s `sync_org_roles_from_claims` tests onto the new `OrgGroup`-based fixture (mirroring `sync_org_groups_from_claims`'s own existing test pattern) — grant/no-match/sync-down/vocabulary-scoping/no-claim-at-all behaviour all still pass unchanged. Cleaned up 5 other test files' now-dead `"sso_group_mappings": []` payload keys and one real assertion rewrite (`test_engagement.py`'s advanced-settings roundtrip test). Frontend: `npx tsc --noEmit`/`npx eslint .` clean; Storybook — `SsoMappingsSave` replaced with `GroupsSectionSaveIdpSyncAndGrantedRole` (asserts the combined PATCH) and a new `GroupsSectionGrantedRoleHiddenWithoutSso` (the visibility-gate case) — both new stories plus the existing OrgAdminPage/ProjectAdminPage suites (58 tests) green.

**Full clean-slate Playwright verification, including the real Keycloak SSO flow this item's own core logic runs through.** `docker compose down -v && up -d --build` (+ a `--no-cache` frontend rebuild — Docker's layer cache incorrectly reported `COPY . .` unchanged a second time this session despite genuinely modified source; always verify by comparing output bundle hashes, don't trust the cache-hit alone), both seed scripts, then Playwright. `sso.spec.ts` (`tests/e2e-workflows/sso.spec.ts:61`, the group→role setup step) rewritten from a raw `PUT .../advanced-settings` with `sso_group_mappings` to a `POST .../groups` with `idp_synced_group_name`/`granted_org_role` together — the real authorization-code flow against the actual Keycloak instance in `tests/container` then provisions the role through the new mechanism for real, not against a mock. A first run (against a database a prior *targeted, non-reseeded* 6-spec batch had already touched, not this item's own fault) surfaced two failures in *other* specs entirely unrelated to this item's diff — both investigated, confirmed genuine and pre-existing, and fixed rather than deferred, per this project's own rule:
- `requirement-actions.spec.ts` and `requirements-and-cr-filters.spec.ts` (already covered under item 514's own entry above, discovered in that item's verification pass) — not re-caused here, just re-confirmed still fixed.
- `ProjectHistoryPage.tsx`'s date-range filter had no request-cancellation guard: an out-of-order `/changes` response could resolve after a newer one and silently overwrite it (`project-history.spec.ts`'s "filtering to a future date range" step, ~25% flaky in isolation before the fix, 0/9 flaky after). Fixed with a `requestGeneration` ref bumped on every `reload()` (a real filter/project change, not a `LoadMoreButton` append) — a response is only applied if it's still answering the latest generation by the time it resolves. No existing `AbortController`/cancellation pattern existed anywhere in the codebase to reuse; this is the first one, scoped to this one page rather than introduced as a new cross-app pattern in the same pass.
- `project-admin-templates-and-reports.spec.ts`'s "select it as Gamma-1's default report template" step called `page.reload()` immediately after clicking "Save settings" with no wait for the save's own `PUT .../report-config` to land — confirmed the backend persists correctly via a direct API call, so this was a pure test-side race (the same shape `preferences-and-theme.spec.ts` and others in this suite already guard against elsewhere), fixed the same way.

One further failure, investigated and *not* fixed, named rather than silently ignored: `report-image-attachment.spec.ts` (RichTextEditor's image-insert flow — untouched by this item's diff) failed twice, both times only as part of a long, multi-run full-suite context late in this session; **4/4 passing** when run in isolation immediately after, at normal speed (~3.5s vs. the failing runs' much longer ones). Treated as load-sensitive flakiness from an unusually long single session (many consecutive Docker rebuilds and 6–47-minute full-suite runs), not a reproducible bug — its own backend-side embed-into-PDF-bytes assertion is independently covered by `backend/tests/test_report_images.py` regardless. Final single-reseed, single-run verification: **86/87 passing** (only this one flake); the eight-spec failure batch seen in an intermediate, non-reseeded rerun was confirmed to be state pollution from this session's own repeated isolated-spec invocations against the same long-lived database, not real bugs — gone entirely once reseeded fresh.

Files changed: `backend/app/models/organization.py`, `backend/app/models/user.py` (stale docstring reference only), `backend/app/schemas/org.py`, `backend/app/routers/orgs.py`, `backend/app/services/oidc_provisioning.py`, `backend/app/services/org_export.py`; `backend/alembic/versions/0014_org_group_granted_role.py` (new); `backend/tests/test_oidc_provisioning.py`, `test_engagement.py`, `test_org_require_2fa.py`, `test_personal_access_tokens.py`, `test_org_rename_and_test_email.py`, `test_org_export_import.py`; `frontend/src/api/types.ts`, `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/ProjectHistoryPage.tsx`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/sso.spec.ts`, `project-history.spec.ts`, `project-admin-templates-and-reports.spec.ts`; `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Deep hardening pass on Stage3 ("do a deep hardening pass")

Requested explicitly against the whole `feature/ui-improvement-stage-3` branch (commit `7c656c4` vs. `main`'s `4b1c556`, 132 files) rather than a single preceding item — scoped to that commit's actual new surface, per this project's established practice: `ADD_ACTION` change requests (item 514), the standalone `POST .../approve` endpoint, `active_only`/`sort` filtering on change requests, and `OrgGroup.granted_org_role` replacing `Organization.sso_group_mappings` (item 522, previous entry above). Identify → verify → remediate: read every changed backend router/model/service/schema line directly (not delegated) for authorization/tenant-isolation and injection/secrets/robustness issues, then a subagent covered the frontend lane (new `ResourcePickerModal`/`ActionMenu`/`FileUploadTrigger` components, `OrgAdminPage`/`PreferencesPage`/`ProjectListPage`'s large diffs, client-side-only authorization assumptions) — its one finding was independently re-verified by reading the actual backend endpoint before being trusted, per this project's standing rule never to act on a subagent's word alone.

**1. Found and fixed: a malformed `granted_org_role` in an org export bundle 500'd the whole import instead of degrading gracefully.** `_import_org_groups` (`backend/app/services/org_export.py`) parsed a bundle group's `granted_org_role` with a bare `OrgRole(granted_org_role)` call — unlike every other piece of untrusted bundle content in the same function (an `idp_synced_group_name` collision, a cycle-forming nested edge, a banned member — all skipped with a warning). Since an org bundle is just a zip file the calling org admin constructs (or received from elsewhere), a bad value there — hand-edited, corrupted in transit, or produced by a future version this one doesn't understand — raised an uncaught `ValueError` past the point where `_parse_org_bundle`'s own malformed-bundle handling could catch it, 500ing `POST /orgs/import` and `POST .../import/merge` instead of reporting a row-level warning like the sibling cases. Fixed by wrapping the parse in `try`/`except ValueError`, adding a warning and dropping just that group's role (same pattern as the sibling cases). New test: `test_org_import_merge.py::test_merge_skips_an_invalid_granted_org_role_with_a_warning_instead_of_500ing`.

**2. Found and fixed: `granted_org_role` was readable by any org member, not just admins — a real narrowing regression from the previous entry's own refactor.** `GET /orgs/{id}/groups` (`list_org_groups`) is authorized for `ORG_ADMIN, PROJECT_CREATOR, MEMBER` — deliberately broad, since a plain member needs group names/ids for the org-group nesting picker elsewhere in the app — and the previous entry added `granted_org_role` to every group in its response without reconsidering that authorization boundary. Before that refactor, the equivalent data (`Organization.sso_group_mappings` — which SSO group grants which org role) lived only behind `GET .../advanced-settings`, `ORG_ADMIN`-only. The result: any org member could call this endpoint directly (or, in principle, a future UI element could render it — the one existing call site, `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s edit `<select>`, happens to also be gated behind an `ORG_ADMIN`-only `sso-config` fetch, which is incidental UI behavior, not a security control) and learn exactly which SSO group auto-grants `org_admin` on sync — privilege-configuration reconnaissance a plain member shouldn't have. Read-only: mutating still correctly requires `ORG_ADMIN` on both `create_org_group` and `update_org_group`, unaffected. Fixed by masking `granted_org_role` to `None` in the response for a non-`ORG_ADMIN` caller (`is_admin = OrgRole.ORG_ADMIN in get_effective_org_roles(...)`), the same field-masking pattern this router already uses elsewhere (`search_org_users`'s `may_see_existing` gate on external-user-match results) — a field mask on an intentionally-broad endpoint, not a new authorization tier. New test: `test_oidc_provisioning.py::test_granted_org_role_is_masked_from_a_plain_member_but_visible_to_an_org_admin`.

**Reviewed and found adequate, no changes needed:** `approve_requirement`'s new standalone endpoint (project-manager gate matches `decide_change_request`'s own identical check exactly; `REQUIRES_APPROVAL_STATUSES = {DRAFT, REVIEWED}` is the exact complement of `LOCKED_STATUSES`, so the two guards can't disagree). `ADD_ACTION` change-request creation and decision (`create_change_request`/`decide_change_request` in `routers/change_requests.py`) — `proposed_action_link_id`/`proposed_action_type_id` validated project-scoped at both creation (`get_requirement_action_in_project`, a 404-on-cross-project IDOR guard) and re-validated independently at approval time (mirroring the existing attachments re-check just above it), matching this codebase's established "don't trust submission-time state at decision time" pattern. `link_action`/`create_and_link_action` in `routers/requirements.py` now correctly reject once a requirement is locked (previously a genuine bypass of the change-request-only rule, closed as part of item 514 itself, not this pass). `list_change_requests`'s new `active_only`/`sort` params — `sort` is regex-constrained (`^(proposed_name|status|created_at)$`), no injection surface. `OrgGroupCreate`/`OrgGroupUpdate`'s `granted_org_role` requiring `idp_synced_group_name` is enforced identically on both create and update via the shared `_require_granted_role_has_sync_target` helper; only an existing `ORG_ADMIN` can ever set it, and the role vocabulary (`OrgRole`) tops out at `org_admin` within org scope — no escalation beyond what that admin could already grant by hand via `assign_org_role`, consistent with the "bundle import can only grant what the target org's own admin could already grant" acceptance established in the org-merge hardening pass above. `sync_org_roles_from_claims`'s replacement plumbing (role-granting groups queried fresh per call, `is_banned`/`is_active` still checked upstream in `auth_oidc.py` before it ever runs) — no change in invariant from the previous entry's own verification. Migrations `0013`/`0014` — additive/nullable columns, backfill logic's "later mapping wins" tradeoff is pre-existing and explicitly documented in the migration's own docstring, not something this pass needed to revisit. Frontend: `ResourcePickerModal`'s resource search and requirement-attachment linking (server-side `organization_id`/`project_id` checks confirmed on both the search and link endpoints); `FavouritesContext`, `ActivityPanel`, `ProjectHistoryPage`, `ProjectListPage`'s `favorite_only` filter (all reuse pre-existing, already-scoped endpoints, no new surface); `PreferencesPage`'s "Leave organisation" (self-service only, `current_user`-scoped server-side); `FileUploadTrigger` (a thin styled-button wrapper with no client-side type/size logic to bypass — `backend/app/services/files.py` has no type/size enforcement either, but that's a pre-existing gap the new component doesn't worsen, out of this pass's scope).

**Verified.** Backend: full suite **577 passed**, 0 failed, against a fresh rebuild with both fixes and their new tests in place. Targeted Playwright (not the full suite, given this pass's changes are backend-only and narrowly scoped): `org-group-nesting.spec.ts`, all 4 real-Keycloak `sso.spec.ts` specs, `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types.spec.ts`, `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts` — 8/8 passing against a freshly reseeded database.

Files changed: `backend/app/routers/orgs.py`, `backend/app/services/org_export.py`; `backend/tests/test_org_import_merge.py`, `test_oidc_provisioning.py`; `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## PR #12 CI failures: a real ruff lint error, then a real OrgAdminPage.tsx race (not a test-timing issue)

PR #12 (`feature/ui-improvement-stage-3`) failed CI three times in a row; each investigated rather than just re-run blind.

**1. Fixed: `backend/tests/test_org_import_merge.py:326`, an `E501` (line too long, 161 > 150) in the new `test_merge_skips_an_invalid_granted_org_role_with_a_warning_instead_of_500ing` test's manifest dict** (added in the Stage3 hardening-pass entry above). Every backend pytest test passed (100%) — this was pure lint, but `ci.yml`'s `Lint backend (ruff)` step has no `continue-on-error`, so failing it skipped every later step (mcp-server lint, dataset reseed, mcp-server tests, and the entire Playwright E2E suite) straight to the `if: always()` reporting steps; `Publish E2E test results` then failed too, but only as a secondary symptom of `playwright-report.xml` never having been generated. Fixed by wrapping the dict onto multiple lines; re-verified with `ruff check .` and the module's own tests against the live dev/test stack.

**2. First attempt, wrong diagnosis: a CI-only "render timing" theory for `org-security-controls.spec.ts`'s org-wide-2FA-enforcement assertion, mitigated by bumping its timeout — disproven by a third CI failure.** After two identical CI failures at the same assertion, a direct backend API call and an instrumented Playwright run both confirmed the 403/"2FA required" UI worked correctly when reproduced natively on this Mac (6+ passing attempts, including two full 87-spec runs), so this was provisionally attributed to a residual gap between `page.waitForResponse` observing the network response and the SPA actually repainting, mitigated by widening that one assertion's timeout to 15000ms. **This was wrong.** A third CI run failed at the *same* assertion after 17.6s — the full 15000ms timeout was consumed, which is far more time than a repaint could plausibly need, ruling out a rendering-speed explanation and pointing at a real, deterministic bug instead.

**3. Actual root cause, found by reproducing CI's exact execution path locally instead of native Playwright.** The one variable the "6+ passing" local runs hadn't controlled for was *how* Playwright itself runs — CI drives the suite from inside a throwaway `docker run --rm --network host ... mcr.microsoft.com/playwright` container (see `ci.yml`'s "Run Playwright E2E suite" comment), not a native process. Running the exact same spec that way, against a freshly reseeded stack, reproduced the CI failure locally on the first try — and reproduced it again with instrumentation added. Logging every `/advanced-settings` and `/projects/*` request showed the actual bug: the PUT that's supposed to save `require_2fa: true` was sending **`require_2fa: false`** — the toggle's own click had registered (`aria-checked` genuinely flipped to `"true"`), but flipped back to `"false"` again about 50ms later, before Save was clicked.

The cause is `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s `reload()` — a single giant function, called after *every* mutating action anywhere on this page (including `toggleDisplayNameLock`, exercised by this same spec's immediately-preceding "lock then unlock a display name" step), that unconditionally re-fetches and overwrites all nine advanced-settings-derived fields (`smtp_*`, `pat_max_lifetime_days`, `require_2fa`, `allow_self_signup`, `auto_accept_email_domain`, `external_user_policy`), including from calls the calling action never awaits. `toggleDisplayNameLock`'s own `reload()` (itself doing ~10 sequential/parallel fetches: users, groups, advanced-settings, sso-config, scim-status, projects, pats, ...) can still be in flight by the time the *next* test step edits and saves that same form — its `advanced-settings` GET, still carrying the pre-edit value, resolves after the toggle click but before Save, clobbering the user's unsaved edit back to the last-saved value. This is architecturally the same class of bug as `ProjectHistoryPage.tsx`'s out-of-order-response race fixed earlier in this project's history (see that entry above) — a slow background refresh overwriting newer local state — except here the "newer state" is an *unsaved form edit*, not a second fetch's own result, and the race window is wide enough (spans an entire preceding test step, not one field's debounce) that it only shows up under CI's slower container-to-container networking, never on this Mac's fast native runs.

Fixed with `advancedDirtyRef`, a ref set by every one of the nine fields' own `onChange` handlers and checked by `reload()`'s advanced-settings block: if the user has an edit pending, a `reload()` in flight from an unrelated action skips re-populating those fields entirely rather than overwriting them. Cleared once `saveAdvanced()` succeeds, so a later, legitimate `reload()` resumes populating the form normally. `org-security-controls.spec.ts`'s assertion itself needed no change once the real race was closed — its 15000ms timeout (from the disproven attempt above) was reverted back to the default.

*Aside, not this item's bug but discovered and fixed while investigating it:* manually driving the Gamma org admin persona through this same enable/disable-org-2FA sequence via direct API calls (to reproduce independently of the test harness) left that persona locked out of its own org-admin endpoints partway through — `require_org_role` calls `_require_org_2fa` for *every* org-scoped endpoint including `advanced-settings` itself, so an admin without personal 2FA who enables the org-wide requirement immediately loses the ability to turn it back off via the API too, exactly as the real spec's own "self-service way out" step (enrol personal 2FA first, `/auth/2fa/enroll` isn't org-scoped) already accounts for. Not a bug — confirmed this is the documented, intended design — but a real trap for any future manual/API investigation of this feature that skips that step, and one that cost real time here since it wasn't recognised on the first two encounters (each read as "database got left in a broken state," requiring the same enrol → verify → disable-org-requirement → disable-personal-2FA recovery sequence the spec itself performs, before local reproduction could proceed); recorded here so it doesn't cost someone else the same detour.

**Verified.** `ruff check .`: clean. `pytest tests/test_org_import_merge.py`: 11 passed. `npx tsc --noEmit` / `npx eslint src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx`: clean. `org-security-controls.spec.ts` run via the exact `docker run --network host` mechanism CI uses — the only reproduction that had ever reliably failed pre-fix — **3/3 passing** against three independent fresh reseeds, plus native-Playwright confirmation. Broader regression check across `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s other consumers (`org-rename-and-test-email.spec.ts`, `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types.spec.ts`, `org-branding-override-reset.spec.ts`, `user-directory-and-bans.spec.ts`, `user-access-panel.spec.ts`, `org-group-nesting.spec.ts`, `single-org-admin.spec.ts`, `multi-org-admin.spec.ts`) — one unrelated failure (`user-directory-and-bans.spec.ts`, the seeded orphan persona found `is_active: false`) traced to this same session's own earlier full-suite runs leaving mutated state behind (the `_e2e_dataset.py`/`seed_demo_data.py` scripts create-if-missing rather than resetting existing rows — harmless in CI's always-fresh database, a local-only trap from reusing one long-lived dev Postgres volume across many manual cycles in one long session); fixed by reactivating the persona directly, re-ran green, not a regression from this fix.

Files changed: `backend/tests/test_org_import_merge.py` (line-length fix); `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx` (`advancedDirtyRef` guard — the real fix); `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/org-security-controls.spec.ts` (comment only, timeout reverted to default); `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

**Follow-up, prompted by "could this same style of race be an issue anywhere else?": audited every other page with the same giant-`reload()`-called-from-everywhere shape, and it was.** Grepped every page for a `reload()`/`function reload` and checked whether any of its unconditional `setXxx` calls fed an editable input rather than a read-only list/display, and whether `reload()` was reachable from an action other than that same field's own save (the precondition for the race to be possible at all, not just theoretical). Four more confirmed, all fixed with the identical `xxxDirtyRef` pattern (set on the field's own `onChange`, checked by `reload()`'s assignment, cleared on that field group's own successful save):

- **`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`** — the single largest exposure: **33** `reload()` call sites (stage/component/category CRUD, custom-field CRUD, action-type CRUD, group membership, ...), unconditionally overwriting three independently-saved field groups: project settings (name, summary, allow-member-CRs, is-template, visibility, status), terminology overrides, and report config (intro, chapters, appendices, default template). Three separate refs (`settingsDirtyRef`, `terminologyDirtyRef`, `reportConfigDirtyRef`), matching the three independent save actions, rather than one shared guard that would block an unrelated group's save.
- **`RequirementDetailPage.tsx`** — **21** `reload()` call sites (posting a comment, uploading a file, linking an action, ...), unconditionally overwriting the entire requirement edit form (name, reasoning, clarification, description, target stage, level, review date/lead/reviewer) plus its custom-field values, both submitted together by the same `save()`. Arguably the highest real-world-likelihood instance: a user mid-edit on a long description while a comment or file upload elsewhere on the same page resolves in the background would have silently lost that edit, with no error surfaced. `form`'s five-plus onChange call sites consolidated behind one `updateForm()` wrapper (sets the ref, then calls `setForm`) rather than repeating the two-line guard at each call site, given the volume; the custom-field-values onChange (submitted in the same `save()` PUT) shares the same ref.
- **`ActionDetailPage.tsx`** — **12** `reload()` call sites, same shape as the requirement page but for an action's title/description/type/assignee/due-date; `setOutcome()` (the outcome-transition action, which also PATCHes the current form fields alongside `outcome_status`) clears the ref on success too, since it's effectively a second save path for the same fields.
- **`ServerManagementPage.tsx`**'s branding tab — narrower exposure (only `uploadLogo`/`uploadLoginBackground` reach its `reload()` from outside the tab's own save), but the same shape: accent color, header title, org label singular/plural, email-footer fields.

Deliberately **not** treated as instances of this bug: the many other `reload()`-shaped functions across `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`, `ChangeRequestDetailPage.tsx`, `ProjectActionsPage.tsx`, `RequirementsPage.tsx`, `ProjectListPage.tsx`, `ServerOrganisationsPage.tsx`, and `ProjectHistoryPage.tsx` (already fixed for an out-of-order-response variant of this same underlying class, see that entry above) — checked and confirmed their `reload()`-equivalents only overwrite read-only lists/detail-display state, not fields bound to an editable input a user could have an unsaved edit pending on.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` / `npx eslint` on all five touched pages: clean. Regression batch — `org-security-controls.spec.ts`, `project-admin-templates-and-reports.spec.ts`, `project-admin-structural.spec.ts`, `project-admin-action-types.spec.ts`, `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`, `requirement-actions.spec.ts`, `requirement-approval.spec.ts`, `requirement-and-action-restore.spec.ts` (×2), `requirement-action-change-request.spec.ts`, `comment-editing-and-attachments.spec.ts`, `org-label.spec.ts`, `server-org-lifecycle.spec.ts`, `server-admin-scope.spec.ts` — **14/14 passing** against a fully wiped-and-rebuilt stack (`docker compose down -v`, matching CI's always-fresh volume exactly). An intermediate run of this same batch against this session's long-lived, heavily-reused local Postgres volume showed 6 unrelated failures (all "create an entity, then find it by name in the default list view" timeouts, including on `RequirementsPage.tsx` — a file this pass never touched); the clean run after the volume wipe confirmed these were this session's own accumulated test-data pollution (many hours, dozens of full-suite runs, one shared dev database never reset), not a regression — consistent with the `is_active`/`require_2fa` seed-script non-idempotency already noted above in this same investigation. `ActionDetailPage.tsx`'s own edit-form fields have no dedicated Playwright coverage of the specific field values (only its `reload()`-triggering side effects — comment/attach — are exercised, and pass); verified by code review against the identical, already-proven pattern instead.

Files changed (this follow-up): `frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.tsx`, `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`, `ActionDetailPage.tsx`, `ServerManagementPage.tsx`; `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Org Users role picker: checkboxes → multi-select dropdown, and a real reload-race bug

Raised directly: "it was set so you could change a user's role in org users and was done as a set of checkboxes... this should be a dropdown list selector, as a) there are errors when you try to select another level, and b) it looks disgusting."

**Checked before changing anything: the checkbox grid was a deliberate design decision, not an oversight** — see decision 14 in the "Hierarchical projects" entry above: "per-row grant/revoke checkboxes on the Users table (independent toggles, not a single-select, since `UserOrgRole` allows a user to hold more than one org role simultaneously...)". Converting straight to a single-value `<select>` would have silently reversed that decision and made it impossible to grant a user more than one `OrgRole` at once through this screen — confirmed still true today: `UserOrgRole`'s unique constraint is `(user_id, organization_id, role)`, `get_effective_org_roles` (`rbac.py:201-208`) returns a plain `set[OrgRole]` with no normalisation (unlike `ProjectRole`'s own `_normalize`), and `assign_org_role`/`revoke_org_role` (`orgs.py:842-927`) operate on one role row at a time with no exclusivity check anywhere. Flagged to the user rather than assumed; asked directly whether to force single-choice or keep multi-select in a proper dropdown shape — chose the latter.

**Fix: `MultiSelectDropdown`** (`frontend/src/components/MultiSelectDropdown.tsx`, new) — a trigger button styled like every other `<select className="input">` in the app, showing checked roles as its summary text, that opens a `Popover`-hosted checkbox list on click. Reuses `Popover`'s existing positioning/focus-trap/outside-click logic, the same reuse `ActionMenu` and `SplitButtonTrigger` already make, rather than a fourth anchored-menu implementation. See `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s new "Pattern: multi-select dropdown" for the full write-up and the "don't use this to fake a checkbox group into looking prettier when the field is actually exclusive" caveat. Wired into `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s Users table Roles column in place of the always-visible three-checkbox stack; the self-row "can't revoke your own role" guard is unchanged in behaviour, now surfaced as a `title` tooltip on the disabled checkbox instead of a silent `aria-label`-only disable.

**The actual root cause of "errors when you try to select another level," found while investigating rather than assumed to be a backend validation rule (there is none — `assign_org_role`/`revoke_org_role` have no cross-role rule beyond the self-targeting block):** `grantOrgRole`/`revokeOrgRole` called the page's own giant `reload()` on every toggle — the exact same "one function re-fetches ~10 endpoints, called from everywhere" shape already fixed once in this file for a different symptom (see the "PR #12 CI failures" entry above, `advancedDirtyRef`). Here the consequence isn't a clobbered form edit, it's two-fold: `reload()`'s own `loadUsers(..., 0, false)` always re-fetches from offset 0, so toggling a role for any user past the first 30 (`USERS_PAGE_SIZE`) made that row vanish from the list immediately after a "successful" change; and nothing serialised two toggles fired close together (the natural motion of switching a role — check the new one, uncheck the old), so two overlapping ~10-request reload bundles could race, and a transient failure in either one replaced the whole page with a load-error state via `reload()`'s own `catch`. Not flagged by the earlier audit of this same pattern because that pass's own criterion was specifically "does this `reload()` overwrite an *editable form field*" — the Users table's `roles` column is read-only display state, not a form field, so it correctly fell outside that fix's scope; it needed its own, different fix.

Fixed by having `grantOrgRole`/`revokeOrgRole` update just the affected row's own `roles` array in local `users` state on success, instead of calling `reload()` at all — a single grant/revoke never changes anything else on the page, so there's nothing else to refresh.

**Tests updated to match:** `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`'s `UsersSectionGrantAndRevokeRole`/`UsersSectionCannotRevokeOwnRole` stories now open each row's dropdown before asserting on its checkboxes (queried via `within(document.body)`, since `Popover` portals there); `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/project-hierarchy.spec.ts`'s "once granted org-level rights..." step now opens the target row's roles dropdown before clicking the grant checkbox. New `frontend/src/components/MultiSelectDropdown.stories.tsx` covers the component itself: closed-state summary text, opening to reveal all options, per-option toggle callbacks, outside-click close, a disabled option with its `title` tooltip, and the empty-selection label.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` on all touched frontend files: clean. No backend changes, so no backend test run was needed. Full Storybook interaction suite (`npx vitest run --project=storybook`) — **540/540 passing**, including the new `MultiSelectDropdown.stories.tsx` (8/8) and the updated `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx` role stories. Rebuilt and recreated the `frontend` container against the already-running local dev/test stack (`tests/container/`), then ran `project-hierarchy.spec.ts` directly (not the full suite) — **4/4 passing**, including the step that opens the new roles dropdown and clicks the grant checkbox inside it against the real backend.

Files changed: `frontend/src/components/MultiSelectDropdown.tsx` (new), `MultiSelectDropdown.stories.tsx` (new); `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx`, `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`; `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/project-hierarchy.spec.ts`; `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Hierarchical (parent/child) projects

Requested directly: "enable the ability for a project to be a child of another project," for large programmes where the overall initiative has its own requirements but sub-components need their own, while still being manageable as a whole. `docs/requirements.md` is silent (not prohibitive) on project nesting — this is recorded here as an interpretation, not a requirements.md edit (which this project cannot make). Two existing entries above (`ActionTypeDefinition`'s project-scoping, and the "Requirement actions" ERD section) already flagged project-scoping as a deliberate seam left open for exactly this; this entry is what fills it in.

### Confirmed design decisions

1. **Unlimited tree depth**, cycle prevention at the application layer only (`would_create_project_cycle`) — no DB constraint can express "no cycle anywhere in this table's transitive closure," the same tradeoff `OrgGroupMember.member_org_group_id`'s nested-group self-join already accepted.
2. **Forward inheritance (parent → child) is a per-project mode, not a boolean**: `ProjectRoleInheritanceMode.NONE` (default) / `MIRROR_ALL` (every role a user holds on the parent, via the parent's own *direct* resolution, mirrors onto the child) / `MIRROR_ROLE` (+ `role_inheritance_filter_role`, one of `STAKEHOLDER`/`PROJECT_ADMINISTRATOR`/`PROJECT_MANAGER` — only that exact role mirrors) / `MEMBER_ONLY` (any role on the parent grants baseline `MEMBER` on the child). The chain walks upward through ancestors and breaks at the first ancestor whose own mode is `NONE` (or that has no parent). Entirely controlled by the **child's** own manager — the child's access boundary is what expands, matching the existing precondition for changing any other project setting.
3. **Reverse inheritance (child → parent) is controlled entirely by the parent**, as an explicit `ProjectMemberSource` list the parent maintains (`POST/DELETE /projects/{parent_id}/member-sources`), not a flag on the child. For each listed child, anyone holding *any* direct role there gets baseline `MEMBER` on the parent. **This is a deliberate correction from an earlier draft**, which had the equivalent as a boolean on the child (`share_members_with_parent`) gated by the child's own manage rights. The user caught this directly: "share_members_with_parent is incorrect as it would allow a child project admin to gain access to a parent when it maybe shouldn't be able to do this. it should be set on the parent, eg consume members from child projects in association with a list of projects." That shape let a low-privileged actor who merely manages some child grant that child's entire membership read access into a potentially confidential parent, with zero involvement from the parent's own manager. Moving the setting to a parent-managed list closes this structurally: no code path lets a child add itself to a parent's list — only someone who already holds `require_project_manage` on the *parent* can populate it. This generalizes cleanly to multiple levels: a grandchild's members reach the grandparent only if the intermediate child is in the grandparent's own list *and* the grandchild is in the intermediate child's own list — every hop up requires that hop's own consent, not just the first.
4. **Action-type fallback is always on**, independent of both RBAC mechanisms: a child with zero of its own `ActionTypeDefinition` rows resolves through its nearest ancestor that has any (`resolve_effective_action_types`, `services/project_hierarchy.py`). Accepted, recorded trade-off: this is a pure structural walk with no visibility check of its own, so a confidential parent's action-type *names* (not content) are visible to a broader-visibility child's audience. Action type names are low-sensitivity metadata; the always-on behaviour was confirmed, not reversed, once this was raised.
5. **Inherited access — from either direction — counts as real membership** for broadcast notification targeting (`get_project_member_user_ids`), consistent with the existing principle that an inherited grant is real access, unlike `ProjectVisibility.ORG_WIDE`'s baseline (which stays excluded, as before).
6. **Tree view is a third `ViewToggle` mode** (tiles/list/tree), shown only when the current page's visible project set actually contains a parent/child relationship (`showTreeOption`) — applied to both `ProjectListPage` and the Favourites page.
7. **C-U-08 ("a project must always have a manager") accounts for forward-inherited managers.** Only `MIRROR_ALL` and `MIRROR_ROLE`-filtered-to-`PROJECT_MANAGER` can ever contribute a manager to a child — `MEMBER_ONLY` and the member-source mechanism both cap at `MEMBER` by construction, so they can never affect this floor. Changing a project's mode away from one of those two, or reparenting/clearing its parent, is blocked if it would leave the project with zero effective managers — computed inside the same row lock the existing last-manager-removal guard already uses (`lock_project_for_update`), closing the immediate-transaction TOCTOU window; a concurrent change further up the ancestor chain in a separate transaction is an accepted, narrow residual risk, not fully closed.
8. **Creating a project supports setting its parent directly** in the create flow, and a project's own page has a discoverable "Add sub-project" entry point, not only a dropdown on the generic list-page create modal — raised directly: "need to make sure when adding a project you can add as a nested project otherwise the workflow may be difficult."
9. **Disabling/reducing inheritance offers converting currently-inherited access to direct roles first** (`POST /projects/{id}/materialize-inherited-access`), so people relying on an inherited grant don't silently lose access the moment a mode is turned off, a project is reparented away, or a parent stops consuming from a child — raised directly: "when inherritence is turned off, there should be a way to convert the current members to be direct prior to disabling." Idempotent (skips a user who already holds an equal-or-higher direct role), a one-time snapshot rather than an ongoing sync.
10. **Project admin views show, per user, whether access is direct or inherited, and how** — raised directly: "Project admin user views, should also note when users are inherrited and how they are inherrited." `GET /projects/{id}/effective-members` returns full provenance (`kind: direct | group | org_wide | forward_inherited | member_source_inherited`, plus `via_project_id`/`via_mode` where applicable) per user, since a user can have more than one source simultaneously (e.g. a direct `MEMBER` grant plus a forward-inherited `PROJECT_MANAGER`) — all sources are returned, not collapsed to one.
11. **Creating a child project doesn't require the org-level `ORG_ADMIN`/`PROJECT_CREATOR` role** — managing the intended parent is sufficient on its own — **but this must not become a way to bypass that gate entirely.** Raised directly, working through the actual attack: "is there a security issue where roles are inherrited from parent to child... Also when inherritence is turned off, there should be a way to convert..." led into asking directly whether a naive "project-manage is enough" design was safe, and the answer is no: create a child under a project you manage, then detach it (clear its own parent) to end up with an ordinary root project you were never actually permitted to create standalone. Closed with a `parent_required` flag: a project created via the relaxed parent-manage-only path is marked `parent_required=True` server-side (never client-settable) and can never have `parent_project_id` cleared to null unless the actor performing that specific detach currently holds `ORG_ADMIN`/`PROJECT_CREATOR` at the org level — checked live against the actor, not just the flag, so someone who later earns real org rights isn't permanently stuck. Reparenting to a *different* real parent is unaffected; only the "become parentless" transition is gated, since that's the only operation that can produce an unrestricted root project.
12. **Both sides can detach a relationship** — a child can already clear its own `parent_project_id` (managing itself is sufficient, unchanged); the parent also gets `DELETE /projects/{parent_id}/children/{child_id}` to detach a specific child from its own side (gated on managing the parent, not the child) — both paths funnel through the same `parent_required` check from decision 11. **Attaching to a new parent** (create or reparent) requires managing *both* the project being attached and the target parent — tightened from an earlier draft that only checked the actor could *view* the target parent, too weak given it exposes that parent's own displayed structure (tree view, "Parent of:" list) to a relationship its manager never agreed to.
13. **The relaxed child-creation path is an org-level toggle**, `Organization.allow_relaxed_child_project_creation`, default enabled — an org admin who wants the stricter "all project creation needs `ORG_ADMIN`/`PROJECT_CREATOR`" status quo can opt back into it. Surfaced as a checkbox on `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s Security group.
14. **The org role-management UI/API gap this toggle exposes as a hard blocker was closed, not deferred.** `POST /orgs/{id}/users/{user_id}/roles` (`assign_org_role`, grants any `OrgRole`, `ORG_ADMIN`-gated) and `create_org_user`'s optional `role` field already existed in the backend — confirmed by reading `routers/orgs.py` in full before assuming a bigger gap existed, correcting an earlier draft of this plan that claimed a new org role needed to be invented. What was actually missing, confirmed by grepping the whole frontend for zero references to the grant endpoint: no UI ever called it, `createUser()` hardcoded `role: "member"` into a field the backend already varied, and there was no revoke counterpart at all. Turning decision 13's toggle *off* with no way to grant `PROJECT_CREATOR` through the UI would have been a dead end, not a real stricter option. Closed with a new `DELETE /orgs/{organization_id}/users/{user_id}/roles/{role}` (mirrors `assign_org_role`'s shape; blocks the caller from targeting their own account, the same invariant `deactivate_org_user` already uses — since the caller must already hold `ORG_ADMIN` and can't touch their own role via this endpoint, an org can never reach zero admins through it, by construction, with no separate count check needed) plus frontend wiring: a role `<select>` on the "New user" modal (member/project creator/org admin, via the existing `ORG_ROLE_LABEL` map), and per-row grant/revoke checkboxes on the Users table (independent toggles, not a single-select, since `UserOrgRole` allows a user to hold more than one org role simultaneously — its unique constraint is `(user_id, organization_id, role)`, not one role per user) — each row's own checkbox disables unchecking (not checking) for the logged-in admin's own row, mirroring the backend's self-targeting block.

### Design principle carried through the whole plan

Forward inheritance and the member-source mechanism are kept fully decoupled, and each is authorized entirely by the side whose access boundary actually expands:
- Forward (`role_inheritance_mode`): the **child's** boundary expands → authorized by `require_project_manage` on the **child** (unchanged existing precondition).
- Member-source (reverse): the **parent's** boundary expands → authorized by `require_project_manage` on the **parent** (decision 3's correction — the opposite side from the flawed first draft).

Both directions resolve using only a project's *direct* roles at each hop (`UserProjectRole` + `ProjectGroup` + nested-org-group + org-wide-visibility — the existing 4-source resolution, extracted as `_direct_effective_project_roles`/`_direct_project_member_ids`), never another project's already-inherited results. Walking the forward chain up only reads each ancestor's *direct* roles; walking the member-source chain down only reads each listed child's *direct* roles (plus, recursively, whatever that child has itself separately consumed). This prevents a sibling-project leak — e.g. child C1 listed in P's member-source list, then P forward-mirroring "all roles" into unrelated sibling C2, accidentally exposing C1's members to C2 — and avoids any mutual-recursion hazard between the two mechanisms. A dedicated regression test (`test_member_source_does_not_leak_into_forward_mirroring_sibling` and its inverse) pins this down; it is exactly the kind of thing a future "improvement" could reintroduce if this weren't written down.

**What a project's own manager can see about its parent, worked through explicitly because the answer isn't obvious:** a direct, non-inherited `PROJECT_MANAGER` of child C with `MIRROR_ALL`/`MIRROR_ROLE` enabled from parent P will see P's name (needed to sensibly manage C's own inheritance setting) and, via the effective-members provenance view, the identities/roles of P's role-holders currently mirrored onto C. This is not new leakage introduced by who added them — it is the direct, already-priced-in consequence of what `MIRROR_ALL`/`MIRROR_ROLE` mean, identical to what *any* manager of C would see, inherited-in or not, and it's exactly the fact the create/edit-time confirmation exists to make an informed, deliberate choice about. What this manager cannot get, regardless of how they came to manage C: P's actual content (requirements, change requests, files), any capability on P itself, or any way to add themselves to P — all independently gated by `require_project_view`/`require_project_manage` on P. The member-source case is symmetric and equally "live," not a snapshot: a brand-new direct member added to a project listed in a parent's member-source list immediately gains `MEMBER` on the parent with no further action from the parent's side, by design — matching the same "live, not a snapshot" resolution as forward inheritance.

### Privilege-exposure friction

Per the blast-radius analysis above: `MIRROR_ALL`/`MIRROR_ROLE` require confirmation before taking effect (create and edit flows), naming the parent and stating both consequences (the access grant, and the provenance visibility) — `MEMBER_ONLY` and adding a member-source entry need none, since both cap at baseline `MEMBER`, the same risk profile `visibility=org_wide` already has with no confirmation. This uses `ConfirmDialog` in its plain (not typed-confirmation) tier — the shipped shape is a real confirmation step but not the typed-name "tier 2" this plan's own drafting language called it; a reasonable simplification given the action is reversible (the mode can be turned back off) and not destructive the way a delete is.

### Corrections made during implementation, beyond what planning anticipated

Each caught by the new test suite or a later verification pass, not a change in the design's intent:

- **`add_member_source`'s `source_project_id` should not be restricted to the caller's own accessible-project set.** The anti-oracle reasoning that motivated restricting the parent-selector similarly didn't hold here: the value space is already constrained to `project_id`'s real structural children (verified server-side), and the caller already manages `project_id` itself — requiring them to *also* independently hold some role on the specific child defeats the mechanism's own purpose (a parent's manager must be able to consume members from any real child, including a brand-new one with no role structure yet). Fixed to rely solely on `require_project_manage(project_id)` + the structural child check.
- **`revoke_project_role`/`remove_project_group_member`'s C-U-08 check needed an `is_inherited_manager` exception.** Once `get_effective_project_managers` became inheritance-aware, `managers == {user_id}` could no longer safely mean "removing this direct role leaves zero managers" — a user who is *both* a direct manager of a project *and* an inherited manager of it (e.g. also manages its parent, which the project mirrors) would be incorrectly blocked from having their redundant direct role removed. Added `is_inherited_manager(db, user_id, project_id)`, gating both checks on `managers == {user_id} and not is_inherited_manager(...)`.
- **`deactivate_org_user`'s C-U-09 fallback loop had a real ordering bug once inheritance existed.** It used to delete-then-check one project at a time; since a project's effective managers can now be pulled from a *different*, not-yet-processed project in the same org, interleaving deletes with checks could let a project silently end up with zero managers if its only inherited manager's own role hadn't been deleted yet at check time. Fixed to a two-phase pass: snapshot managers-before across every project in the org first, delete all this user's roles, then run the fallback check per project.
- **`remove_child_project`'s route used `{parent_id}` as its path parameter name**, breaking `Depends(require_project_manage)` — that dependency looks for a path parameter literally named `project_id`; with no such name FastAPI treated it as a required query parameter (422 on every call). Renamed to `{project_id}` (documented inline as unintuitive but required).

### SOC 2 identify → verify → remediate checkpoint

Run via this repo's `/code-review` skill at high effort, scoped to the diff, after backend implementation and before frontend work — per this project's change-management policy for authorization-affecting changes. Six findings, verified against the actual shipped code:

1. **CONFIRMED, fixed — `ProjectOut` leaked `parent_project_id` unredacted from six endpoints** (`GET`/`PATCH /{id}`, `POST ""`, `PUT .../terminology`, `POST .../archive`, `POST .../unarchive`). `GET /{project_id}` is view-gated (any role), not manage-gated, so any project viewer — not just its manager — could learn a hidden parent's identity by fetching the project directly, even though `list_projects`/`/ancestors` correctly redacted it. The redaction rule had only ever been applied to `ProjectListItemOut`. Fixed with `_project_out_with_redacted_parent`, applied at all six return points, plus a new `parent_project_name` field on `ProjectOut`.
2. **CONFIRMED, fixed — `get_project_users_by_role` (change-request `PROJECT_MANAGER`/`STAKEHOLDER` notification targeting) wasn't inheritance-aware**, so a user who is a real, effective manager purely via `role_inheritance_mode` would silently miss change-request notifications despite genuine approval authority — the original implementation's own docstring conceded this gap rather than closing it, a fix-don't-defer violation per this project's standing rule. Extended with the same forward-chain (+ member-source, for `MEMBER`) walk `get_project_member_user_ids` already had; this also widened the base (own-project) resolution to include nested-org-group holders, correcting an inconsistency with `get_effective_project_roles`'s own resolution.
3. **CONFIRMED, fixed — `_has_member_source_access`/`_member_source_contributed_user_ids` recursed with no depth cap**, unlike every other unlimited-depth walk in `rbac.py` (all others iterative with `_PROJECT_INHERITANCE_ITERATION_CAP`). Since both mechanisms support unlimited tree depth and this walk runs on nearly every project-scoped request, a sufficiently deep member-source chain could raise `RecursionError` (500) instead of degrading gracefully. Rewritten as iterative BFS via a new shared `_member_source_frontier` helper, same cap as everywhere else.
4. **CONFIRMED, fixed — `get_effective_project_managers`'s `filter_role_override` was gated on `mode_override is not None`** instead of its own presence, harmless only because both current call sites always pass both together — a latent bug for any future caller wanting to override just the filter role. Added an explicit `filter_role_override_set` flag, mirroring the existing `parent_override_set` pattern.
5. **CORRECT AS DESIGNED, no change — this decisions.md entry didn't exist yet at review time.** Code comments throughout the change cited it in advance; intentional per this plan's own sequencing (docs land last, folding in the review's own outcome), not a defect.
6. **DEFERRED then closed — seed scripts didn't yet exercise hierarchy fields.** Valid per this project's seed-script-sync rule, deliberately sequenced to after the frontend existed; closed in the seed-script phase below, not silently forgotten.

### Frontend

`ProjectRoleInheritanceMode` type + `PROJECT_ROLE_INHERITANCE_MODE_LABEL` (per the style guide's Principle 12 — never render the raw enum string); new `ProjectAncestor`/`ProjectTreeNode`/`ProjectMemberSource`/`EffectiveMember`/`MaterializeResult` types. New shared components: `ProjectTree.tsx` (presentational, no fetch logic of its own, per-node "+" to add a child), `ProjectHierarchyLabels.tsx` ("Child of:"/"Parent of:" labels, shared between `ProjectListPage` and the Favourites page rather than duplicated, capped at 3 inline children + "view all"). `ViewToggle`'s `ViewMode` extended to include `"tree"`, gated by a new `showTreeOption` prop that hides the third button's rendering entirely (not just disables it) when the page's visible project set has no hierarchy relationship.

`ProjectListPage.tsx`/`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`: parent-project select + inheritance-mode select (+ filter-role select for `MIRROR_ROLE`) in the create modal and the Overview/"Project settings" tab respectively, both routed through the same confirmation flow for `MIRROR_ALL`/`MIRROR_ROLE`; `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` shows the current parent's name plainly (unlike the list/tile "Child of:" label, which redacts a parent the viewer can't see — a project's own manager already holds the highest level of authority over this relationship and needs to see it to do their job) and gained a "Member sources" section (list + add-dropdown, sourced from the project's own `GET .../children`) and an "Add sub-project" button navigating to `/projects?parentProjectId=X&organizationId=Y` (`ProjectListPage.tsx` auto-opens the create modal with both pre-filled via a `useSearchParams` effect, cleared immediately after so a later reload/back-navigation doesn't silently reopen it). `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s "Project groups" tab gained an "Effective members" `CollapsibleSection` (lazy-loaded, not part of the page's main `reload()`, since it iterates every org member server-side): shows each user's effective role plus every provenance source, and a "Convert all inherited access to direct roles" button.

### Real bugs found only by running the finished feature end to end, not by static review

All caught during a full Playwright verification pass against the real `tests/container` stack — none surfaced by `tsc`/`eslint`/Storybook, which is exactly why this project's testing policy requires running the actual stack rather than trusting type-checking and unit-level tests alone for a UI feature:

- **`ProjectListPage.tsx`'s create-modal parent-selector excluded the very project being selected as the parent.** `parentOptions = allProjects.filter((p) => p.organization_id === newOrgId && !p.is_archived && p.id !== parentProjectId)` — the `p.id !== parentProjectId` clause is `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s own "exclude the project currently being edited from its own parent-picker" pattern, copied without adjusting for the create form's different context: on create there is no "self" yet to exclude, and `parentProjectId` here is simply the *selected* parent's own id, not a self-reference to avoid. The effect: once "Add sub-project" pre-filled a parent (decision 8), that parent's own `<option>` never existed in the list at all, so the select could never actually display it as chosen — a real, user-facing bug in the flagship entry point this whole feature added, invisible to every prior verification pass because none of them checked the select's *displayed* value after a pre-fill, only that the field existed. Fixed by dropping the exclusion entirely on this form.
- **The new "Effective members" section's title collided with every project's own default "Members" group.** `DEFAULT_GROUPS` (`routers/projects.py`) seeds a `ProjectGroup` named "Members" on every project — with the new section also titled "Members" on the same "Project groups" tab, `openGroupCard`'s prefix-matching regex helper (`tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/helpers.ts`) started matching both, breaking `org-security-controls.spec.ts`, an entirely unrelated pre-existing spec. Renamed the section to "Effective members" — also just a clearer label on its own merits, not solely a test-fixing move.
- **Two pre-existing Playwright specs assumed the "New project" modal had exactly one/a specific count of `<select>` elements** (`project-list-org-scoping.spec.ts`, `project-admin-templates-and-reports.spec.ts`) — both broke once the new "Parent project" select joined Visibility (and, when present, the template picker) in the same modal. Fixed by updating the expected counts and scoping the template-picker's option-count assertion specifically to that select (`getByLabel("Create from template")`) rather than an unscoped dialog-wide option match, since "Parent project" also lists every project in the org as an option and can now collide on shared project names.
- **`getByLabel`-based locators for "Visibility" became newly fragile, not from a code bug but from an interaction with existing test-data hygiene.** Once "Parent project" lists every non-archived project in the org as `<option>` text, an org that has accumulated a leftover project whose name happens to contain a field's own label word (here, debris from a prior interrupted run of `project-visibility.spec.ts` itself, never cleaned up because the run failed before reaching its own cleanup step) makes a non-exact `getByLabel("Visibility")` match two elements. Not treated as a locator bug to work around — treated as debris to clean up, consistent with how this project's own "cross-spec state pollution" findings elsewhere in this document are always resolved by reseeding rather than by hardening every locator against arbitrary leftover data. A reproduction of this ambiguity is a signal to reseed, documented inline at the one call site most likely to hit it again.
