## Deep hardening pass on `feature/multi-level-projects` ("please do a deep hardening pass")

Requested explicitly against the whole `feature/multi-level-projects` branch (commit `7403f85` "Nested Projects Compatibility" vs. `main`, 50 files) — the entire hierarchical-projects feature described in the "Hierarchical projects" entry above, landed as one branch. That entry's own "SOC 2 identify → verify → remediate checkpoint" ran *during* implementation, before the frontend existed, scoped to the backend diff at that point in time; this pass is a second, independent look at the finished branch as a whole, per this project's standing practice of treating a hardening-pass request as its own scoped review rather than assuming an earlier in-flight review already covered everything. Identify → verify → remediate: every changed backend router/model/service/schema line read directly (not delegated) for authorization/tenant-isolation/injection/robustness issues; a subagent covered the frontend lane (client-side-only authorization assumptions, raw-enum rendering, redaction correctness, confirmation-dialog coverage, the known reload-clobbers-unsaved-edit race class) — both its findings were independently re-verified against the actual current code before being trusted, per this project's standing rule never to act on a subagent's word alone.

**1. CONFIRMED, fixed — a real RBAC escalation: listing an `ORG_WIDE`-visible child as a member source granted every user in the organisation real `MEMBER` access to the parent, not just a read grant on the child.** `_has_member_source_access` (`backend/app/services/rbac.py`) — the per-user check backing `get_effective_project_roles`, the live authorization gate behind `require_project_view` and everywhere else project access is decided — resolved each candidate source project via `_direct_effective_project_roles`, which (correctly, for its own purpose) includes source 4, `ProjectVisibility.ORG_WIDE`'s baseline grant. But `_direct_project_member_ids`, the sibling helper every *other* member-source/forward-inheritance bulk resolution in this same module deliberately uses instead, excludes `ORG_WIDE` specifically to prevent exactly this — its own docstring already warned "if this included `ORG_WIDE`, an org-wide-visible ancestor would flow its *entire organisation's* membership through forward inheritance or the member-source mechanism into every notification and every 'does this descendant have a real member' check". `_has_member_source_access` was the one path in the module that still read through the wrong helper, so that warned-against side channel was live: an org's own docstring for `ProjectMemberSource` frames the mechanism as "consume members from this real child" — a project manager listing a merely-`ORG_WIDE`-visible child (a common, ordinary visibility choice, not a contrived edge case) would unknowingly grant baseline access to their entire organisation on a parent that might be far more sensitive, with no indication anywhere in the UI that this was happening. Fixed to use `_direct_project_member_ids` (mirroring `_member_source_contributed_user_ids`'s already-correct bulk resolution). New test: `test_project_hierarchy.py::test_member_source_does_not_leak_org_wide_visibility_as_membership` — confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code (temporarily reverted via `git stash` of just this one file, rebuilt, reran) before being confirmed to pass post-fix, not just written and trusted.

**2. CONFIRMED, fixed — a project manager with no independent view access to the true parent could silently detach their project from it on the next unrelated "Save settings" click.** Two compounding gaps, found together by the frontend subagent lane and independently verified against the backend:
   - `_project_out_with_redacted_parent` (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`) redacted `parent_project_id`/`parent_project_name` for *any* caller lacking independent view access to the parent, with no exemption for a caller who manages the child itself — contradicting `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s own inline comment and this very document's "Hierarchical projects" entry above ("a project's own manager already holds the highest level of authority over this relationship and needs to see it to do their job"), both of which describe the manager-sees-the-true-parent behaviour as already shipped. It wasn't: nothing ties managing a child to holding any role on its parent, so this was a realistic, ordinary case, not a contrived one.
   - `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s `saveSettings()` unconditionally includes `parent_project_id: parentProjectId || null` in every PATCH regardless of whether the field was touched — defeating the very protection `ProjectUpdate`'s `model_fields_set` distinction (documented in its own docstring) exists to provide.
   
   Combined: a manager who can't see their project's real parent loads the settings tab (sees "No parent" — an artifact of redaction, not truth), edits something unrelated, saves, and the real parent relationship is silently severed — no error, no confirmation, since decision 12 already permits a child to detach by managing itself alone, and `parent_required` doesn't apply to an ordinarily-created project. Fixed at the root: `_project_out_with_redacted_parent` now exempts a caller who manages the project itself (`can_manage_project_settings`), matching the documented intent — they already hold unilateral authority to detach or reparent this exact relationship via this same endpoint, so showing them the true value they can already change is not a new disclosure. This closes the practical risk without needing a second, frontend-side fix: `saveSettings()`'s payload becomes safe again once the value it reads is always the true one for anyone who can actually reach it (every caller of this endpoint is already `require_project_manage`-gated). New test: `test_project_hierarchy.py::test_get_project_shows_true_parent_to_a_manager_with_no_independent_parent_access`.

**3. CONFIRMED, fixed — reparenting an existing MIRROR_ALL/MIRROR_ROLE-configured project to a *different* parent did not re-trigger the required confirmation, on both the create and edit forms.** The parent `<select>`'s `onChange` in both `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` and `ProjectListPage.tsx` only ever called `setParentProjectId` — confirmation is wired solely to the inheritance-*mode* select's own `onChange`. Reproduction: a project already has parent P1 with `role_inheritance_mode=mirror_all` (confirmed and saved earlier, the dialog having named P1); an edit later changes only the parent select to P2, leaving the mode select untouched — no `ConfirmDialog` fires, and on save the project now mirrors *P2's* role-holders, a materially different access grant than what was ever confirmed, violating this document's own decision 4/"Privilege-exposure friction" requirement that MIRROR_ALL/MIRROR_ROLE always show a confirmation naming the actual parent. The create form has the identical gap (pick P1, get the P1 confirmation, switch to P2 before submitting — the create request grants access sourced from P2 with no confirmation ever having named it). Fixed conservatively rather than by extending the confirm-dialog state machine to track a second pending field: changing the parent select while an elevated mode is set resets `role_inheritance_mode` back to `none` (the safe default), so re-selecting MIRROR_ALL/MIRROR_ROLE for the new parent goes through the existing, already-correct `requestInheritModeChange` confirmation flow, which then genuinely names the new parent. No backend change needed — `update_project`/`create_project` were never the gap, only the frontend's failure to prompt before submitting an already-valid, already-accepted request shape.

**Reviewed and found adequate, no changes needed (backend):** `_accessible_project_ids`/`build_project_tree`/`get_project_ancestors`/`get_project_children` (all correctly re-verify each candidate's actual `get_effective_project_roles` before including it, rather than trusting structural adjacency — inherits finding 1's fix automatically once merged); `add_member_source`'s deliberate "no independent accessible-set check on the child" design (re-confirmed correct: the value space is already constrained to real structural children, and requiring independent access would defeat the mechanism's purpose); `remove_child_project`/`update_project`'s `parent_required` and C-U-08 guards (`get_effective_project_managers` override parameters) — re-verified the `filter_role_override_set`-gated-on-its-own-flag fix from the previous hardening pass is genuinely in place, not regressed; `_validate_action_type`'s cross-project `ActionTypeDefinition` FK reference (structurally scoped to the real ancestor chain only, no cross-tenant surface); `revoke_org_role`'s self-targeting block; the `0015` migration (additive/nullable, no backfill risk).

**Reviewed and found adequate, no changes needed (frontend, per the subagent lane, independently re-verified):** every `role_inheritance_mode`/`ProjectRole`/`OrgRole` display routes through its label map, no raw enum strings reach the UI; `ProjectHierarchyLabels`/`ProjectTree`/tree-mode `ViewToggle` all rely on server-redacted fields rather than re-deriving visibility client-side; the org role grant/revoke UI and the `allow_relaxed_child_project_creation` toggle are correctly backed by independent server-side checks, client gating is UX-only; the new hierarchy fields (`parentProjectId`/`roleInheritanceMode`/`roleInheritanceFilterRole`) are correctly guarded by `settingsDirtyRef` against the known reload-clobbers-unsaved-edit race class already fixed elsewhere on this page — finding 2 above is a different bug (wrong *initial* value from redaction, not a clobbered in-progress edit) — and MEMBER_ONLY/member-source add correctly need no confirmation, matching the documented risk parity with `visibility=org_wide`.

**Found and fixed, incidental to verification (not a security finding, but a real bug per this project's own "fix, don't defer" rule):** `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types.spec.ts`'s `getByLabel("Status")` assertion became ambiguous once this branch added a "Parent project" `<select>` to the same `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` tab. A wrapping `<label>{text}<select>...</select></label>`'s computed accessible name flattens in every descendant `<option>`'s text, not just the label's own words — this spec's own fixture creates two same-org sibling projects (`E2E Status Project A`/`B`), and `B`'s name legitimately appears as a `<option>` inside "Parent project", making that select's accessible name contain the substring "Status" too. Unlike the already-documented, already-accepted "Visibility" locator fragility elsewhere in this suite (a cross-run-debris case, whose own inline comment explicitly declines to fix it via locator complication, treating a reproduction as "a signal to reseed" instead — re-confirmed still accurate: a clean-slate rerun of `project-visibility.spec.ts` alone passed), this one reproduces from the spec's *own* legitimate, single-run fixture data, so reseeding cannot fix it. Fixed by locating the Status `<select>` structurally (the one whose own `<option>` list contains a status name) instead of via `getByLabel`, avoiding the ambiguity outright rather than complicating it further.

**Verified.** Backend: `ruff check app tests` clean; full suite green both before and after the fix (confirmed via a deliberate revert-rebuild-retest cycle isolating finding 1's fix, not just "tests pass" trusted at face value), and again green after finding 2's fix, against a freshly wiped+rebuilt `tests/container` database. Frontend: `npx tsc --noEmit`/`npx eslint src/` clean (only the same 7 pre-existing warnings in untouched files). Playwright: `project-hierarchy.spec.ts` (4/4), plus a regression batch across the surfaces this pass touched (`project-list-org-scoping`, `project-admin-templates-and-reports`, `project-admin-structural`, `project-visibility`, `favourites`, `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types`) — 9/9 passing from a genuinely fresh `seed_demo_data.py`/`seed_e2e_dataset.py` reseed after a full schema wipe, the only verification standard this project's own methodology accepts as conclusive (an earlier, non-reseeded repeat run of the same batch showed 2 unrelated failures, both confirmed to be this session's own repeated-run self-pollution — the same already-documented class of shared-database test fragility noted throughout this file — not regressions from this pass's changes).

Files changed: `backend/app/services/rbac.py`, `backend/app/routers/projects.py`; `backend/tests/test_project_hierarchy.py`; `frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.tsx`, `ProjectListPage.tsx`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types.spec.ts`; `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## PR #13 CI failure, a shared-admin-password test hazard, and the `can_be_parent` eligibility gate

Three pieces of follow-up work in one session, each starting from a direct report against PR #13 (`feature/multi-level-projects`).

### 1. CI E2E failure: an unrelated pre-existing spec broken by a new same-named element

`badge-filters.spec.ts` (untouched by this branch's own diff) does `getByRole("link", { name: "Falcon-3 Inspection Drone" }).click()` on the projects list. `seed_demo_data.py`'s new "Falcon-3 Avionics Subsystem" sub-project renders a "Child of: Falcon-3 Inspection Drone" link (`ProjectHierarchyLabels`) with the exact same accessible name as the parent's own tile heading link. Fixed with `.first()` — both links resolve to the identical `/projects/{id}` destination (the child's "Child of" link target *is* the parent's id), so either is a correct click for this test's purpose. Confirmed no other spec references "Falcon-3 Inspection Drone" or the Gamma-3/Gamma-4 fixture pair in a way that collides the same way.

**Two more pre-existing failures found and fixed while verifying the above, not deferred** (both were self-inflicted local-session pollution *and* real, separately-worth-fixing non-idempotency, confirmed by reproducing on a genuinely fresh reseed, not just re-running):
- `project-visibility.spec.ts`: `getByLabel("Visibility")` on `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` becomes ambiguous once "Parent project" shares the same page/modal and a leftover project's name happens to contain "visibility" — the spec's own existing comment already named this exact risk and explicitly declined to fix the locator, treating a reproduction as "a signal to reseed." Given this project's standing rule that a test "must pass whether it runs alone, first, last, or repeated back-to-back against the same database" (not only after a fresh reseed), fixed properly this time: a `visibilitySelect()` helper locates the `<select>` structurally (`.filter({ hasText: "Only specified" })`, a phrase that can never appear as a project name) instead of by label, closing the fragility at the root rather than deferring to "reseed when it happens." The identical `.filter({ has: page.locator("option", {...}) })` construct tried first for this timed out unreliably against a `<select>` inside a modal `Locator` (not `Page`) scope even though the exact same shape worked fine page-rooted elsewhere in the suite; switched to the simpler, more robust `.filter({ hasText })` form everywhere it's used, including retrofitting `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types.spec.ts`'s earlier `has`-based fix from the same session.
- `project-admin-structural.spec.ts` mutated the shared "Beta-2" fixture in place (renaming its default "Scoping" stage, deleting/recreating its components) — a second run without an intervening reseed can no longer find "Scoping" at all. Converted to a disposable, uniquely-named project it creates and seeds itself via direct API calls (mirroring `seed_e2e_dataset.py`'s own `seed_project_content` shape: Hardware/Software components, Functional/Performance categories), the same remedy `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types.spec.ts` had already applied to itself for the identical anti-pattern.

All three (plus the original CI failure) verified passing **twice back-to-back with no reseed between runs**, not just once.

### 2. `pelion-v2.spec.ts` was changing the real bootstrap admin's password

Raised directly: "there is a test that changes the password, can that not use the admin user, as I frequently can't login as I don't know what the password is." `pelion-v2.spec.ts` logged in through the UI as `admin@example.com`/`ChangeMe123!` — the actual shared account used for manual local testing — then changed its password mid-test to exercise the change-password-triggers-a-notification flow, wrapped in a try/finally that reverted it. Two real problems, not just the one reported:
1. The try/finally boundary was drawn *after* the forward change (`await page.waitForURL(/\/login$/)` sat outside the `try`) — once `changeResponse.ok()` is true the mutation has already committed server-side, so a flake in that very next line would skip the revert entirely despite the real account's password already having changed. This is almost certainly the actual mechanism behind "frequently can't login," not just theoretical.
2. Even a gap-free try/finally still leaves the same shared credential hostage to a browser crash or worker kill — no amount of finally-block correctness removes that risk.

Fixed by removing the dependency entirely rather than hardening the revert further: the spec now provisions its own disposable org + org-admin persona via direct API calls (`admin@example.com` is used exactly once, read-only, to obtain a bearer token for that provisioning — never through the UI login form, so this spec can no longer touch that account's real password under any failure mode) and runs its whole walkthrough, including the password-change exercise, against that throwaway persona. The try/finally boundary was also corrected to start before the forward change, as defense in depth for the persona itself. Verified: full local Playwright suite green, and `admin@example.com`/`ChangeMe123!` confirmed to still authenticate via a direct API call after the run.

### 3. `can_be_parent`: an opt-in eligibility gate for the "Parent project" picker

Raised directly, two complaints in one: "when creating a new project, you get the field 'Parent project' when there are none that can be seen by the user. This makes no sense and should not be shown if there are none eligible. I think projects should also have a setting that allows them to be eligible to be parents, which is disabled by default." Asked directly whether eligibility should be a real backend-enforced gate or just a picker-side filter, given the size difference — the user chose full enforcement, matching this codebase's standing "never trust client-side filtering alone" posture.

**`Project.can_be_parent`** (new column, migration `0016`, default `False`) gates whether `parent_project_id` on an *other* project may point at this one — checked on both `create_project` and `update_project` (400 if the target parent hasn't opted in), not just filtered out of the frontend picker. Existing parent/child relationships are grandfathered by the migration's own backfill (`can_be_parent = true` for any project already referenced by another row's `parent_project_id`), so this cannot retroactively break an already-established hierarchy. Turning it back off on a project that already has children does not detach them — the same "changes apply going forward, not retroactively" principle `role_inheritance_mode` already follows (decision 9 in the "Hierarchical projects" entry above) — it only blocks *new* attachments.

**Frontend**: a new "Allow this project to be a parent" checkbox on `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s Project settings tab (always visible, independent of whether *this* project currently has, or could have, a parent of its own — it's the opt-in mechanism *other* projects' managers need). The "Parent project" field itself (and its dependent inheritance-mode sub-fields) is hidden entirely on both `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` and `ProjectListPage.tsx`'s create modal when there's nothing eligible to pick and no parent currently set — directly closing the reported UX complaint — while a project's *already-attached* parent always stays selectable even if that parent's own eligibility was since revoked, so an established relationship never renders as a blank/unselectable value. "Add sub-project" is disabled (with an explanatory `title`) until the project itself has opted in, since it leads straight into a create flow the backend would otherwise reject.

**A real bug found only by the Playwright verification, not by static review or the backend test suite:** `GET /projects` (`list_projects`) and `GET /{id}/children` both construct `ProjectListItemOut` field-by-field rather than via `ProjectOut.model_validate(project)` (the pattern the single-project `GET /{id}` correctly uses) — adding `can_be_parent` to the Pydantic schema without also adding it to those two explicit constructor calls meant it silently fell back to the schema's own default (`False`) for every project, regardless of the real database value, with no error anywhere (Pydantic only defaults missing fields, it doesn't reject them). Confirmed directly: the database correctly held `can_be_parent = true` for the seeded parent projects while the live API response for both listing endpoints reported `false` for all of them. Backend unit tests didn't catch this because `test_project_hierarchy.py`'s own assertions read the single-project `GET /{id}` response, never the list/children endpoints — closed with a dedicated regression test (`test_can_be_parent_is_reported_correctly_by_list_projects_and_children`) that reads both. This is the exact class of bug this project's testing policy runs a real browser for rather than trusting `tsc`/unit tests alone.

**Backend test ripple, mechanical but necessary given full enforcement:** every existing test across `test_project_hierarchy.py` (~25 call sites) and `test_action_types.py` (5 hierarchy-fallback tests, a separate file this session initially missed on the first pass — caught by the full suite, not assumed clean) that creates a parent-then-child pair now passes `can_be_parent=True` at the parent's own creation; the shared `conftest.py::create_project` helper gained the matching kwarg. `seed_demo_data.py` (Falcon-3 Inspection Drone) and `seed_e2e_dataset.py` (Gamma-1, Gamma-3 Hierarchy Parent) set it at seed time on every project used as a live parent target, including the one `project-hierarchy.spec.ts`'s relaxed-creation-path test attaches a child under; `project-hierarchy.spec.ts`'s own first test (which creates a brand-new parent live, not from a seeded fixture) gained an explicit opt-in step before its "Add sub-project" click. `project-list-org-scoping.spec.ts`'s single-org-picker assertions were updated for the new hidden-when-nothing-eligible baseline (a fresh org has zero projects, so nothing can ever be eligible there) rather than left asserting stale "always renders" behaviour.

**Verified.** Backend: `ruff check` clean; full suite **616 passed, 0 failed** (a first clean run surfaced 5 real failures in `test_action_types.py`, fixed and reconfirmed green — not silently left for a later pass). A `sqlalchemy`-connection-error batch seen on one intermediate run (`102 failed, 116 passed, 399 errors`) was traced to this session's own many-hours-long shared local Postgres connection exhaustion — never reproduced again after a schema wipe + backend restart, consistent with this project's own documented DB-pool-wedge pattern, not a code regression. Frontend: `tsc --noEmit`/`eslint` clean; Storybook **532/532** (up from 527), including new coverage for the checkbox (`CanBeParentToggleSaves`), the disabled/enabled "Add sub-project" states, and the hidden-vs-offered "Parent project" field on both pages. Playwright: full suite **91/91 passing** from a genuinely fresh reseed after a full schema wipe — the only verification standard this project's own methodology accepts as conclusive — including `project-hierarchy.spec.ts` and the fixed `project-list-org-scoping.spec.ts`.

Files changed: `backend/app/models/project.py`; `backend/alembic/versions/0016_project_can_be_parent.py` (new); `backend/app/schemas/project.py`; `backend/app/routers/projects.py`; `backend/tests/conftest.py`, `test_project_hierarchy.py`, `test_action_types.py`; `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`, `seed_e2e_dataset.py`; `frontend/src/api/types.ts`, `i18n/strings.ts`, `testing/storybook-helpers.tsx`; `frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `ProjectListPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`); `frontend/src/components/ProjectHierarchyLabels.stories.tsx`; `tests/playwright/tests/badge-filters.spec.ts`, `pelion-v2.spec.ts`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/project-visibility.spec.ts`, `project-admin-structural.spec.ts`, `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types.spec.ts`, `project-hierarchy.spec.ts`, `project-list-org-scoping.spec.ts`; `docs/solution-architecture.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Human UI/UX review batch: seven fixes (attach-on-create, activity-log duplication, dashboard navigation, list styling, login branding, responsive overflow, project users parity)

A second human (non-audit) UI/UX pass produced seven separate pieces of feedback, all implemented in one batch. The one genuine architectural decision among them — the activity-log deduplication — is recorded in detail below; the rest are noted briefly for the file-change record.

### Activity-log duplication: root cause and fix

`services/changes.py::get_project_changes` merges `AuditEvent` rows with `RequirementVersion`/`ChangeRequestVersion` rows into one feed (by design, per its own docstring — three/four sources, one timeline). The bug: every mutation that bumps a version *also* logs an `AuditEvent` for the exact same transition in the same request handler, and both were surfacing as separate rows — confirmed by reading every call site, not assumed: requirement `created`/`updated`/`approved`/`completed`/`uncompleted` (`routers/requirements.py`) each sit immediately after `apply_new_version`/`create_requirement`, and change-request `created` sits after the version-1 `ChangeRequestVersion` insert (`routers/change_requests.py`). `archived`/`unarchived`/`review_recorded` (requirement) and `submitted`/`withdrawn`/approve-reject (change request) do **not** pair with a version bump and were never duplicated.

**Decision: keep the version-history-sourced entry, suppress the redundant `AuditEvent` row**, via a `(entity_type, action)` filter applied only to the audit-sourced list — not a timestamp-matching heuristic, and not a change to what gets logged (both sources still get written; only which ones the *feed* surfaces changed). Chosen over the reverse (keep `AuditEvent`, suppress version-history) because the version-history entry already carries `change_note` (e.g. "Approved directly.", "Marked completed.") in its `detail`, which reads as more informative than the generic `AuditEvent`'s "approved"/"completed" action label alone, and because version-history entries exist for *every* version bump regardless of caller (baseline approval, CSV import, a future code path nobody's written yet) whereas hardcoding around specific `AuditEvent` call sites would only catch pairs known today. Verified the filter is a strict subset by grepping every `log_event(..., entity_type="requirement"/"change_request", ...)` call site against every version-bump call site, including `services/baseline.py` (bumps versions, never logs a paired event — already never duplicated, filter doesn't touch it) and the CSV import path (logs at `entity_type="project"`, not `"requirement"` — also untouched).

Pinned with `test_project_changes_has_no_duplicate_entries_for_version_bumping_actions` (`test_reporting_and_changes.py`): create/edit/approve/complete/uncomplete a requirement and create a change request, assert exactly one feed entry per transition (five for the requirement — one `created` plus four `updated`, since `apply_new_version` only ever synthesizes `created`/`updated`, not the more specific verb — and one for the CR).

### The other six, briefly

- **Attach files / add links during requirement creation**: the create `Modal` on `RequirementsPage.tsx` now advances to a second step (reusing `FileAttachmentList` and the same add-link `Popover` pattern `RequirementDetailPage.tsx` already had) against the just-created requirement's real id, rather than closing — the backend's file/link endpoints require an existing id, so this reuses them rather than building a pre-create staging flow. Also fixed a pre-existing bug found in the same area: Add Link was never disabled even with zero eligible targets, on both the create step and the detail page.
- **Dashboard widgets/charts didn't navigate**: `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`'s glance tiles, status/CR pie charts, and stage-progress bars now link to the Requirements/Change Requests list pre-filtered to match. The hand-rolled CSS-conic-gradient `DonutChart` was retired in favour of **Recharts** (new dependency) — the user's explicit call, made with a future custom-dashboard-builder feature in mind, wrapped in a new `StatusPieChart` component rather than used ad hoc.
- **Project list styling**: `.side-grid`'s base rule (not just its `@media (max-width: 860px)` override, which already had this fix) now uses `minmax(0, 1fr)` instead of a bare `1fr`, so the `FilterPanel` column can no longer be pushed off-screen by wide content at moderate widths; project descriptions now clamp to a fixed number of lines (`-webkit-line-clamp`) instead of an unbounded single line.
- **Login page branding**: `OrgLoginPage.tsx` already had a logo+title block; the plain `LoginPage.tsx` didn't. Extracted into a shared `LoginBrandHeader` component used by both, rather than adding a second inline copy.
- **Responsive table overflow**: several tables (`OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s Users tab, `PreferencesPage.tsx`'s PATs/notifications tables, `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s version-history table) were missing the `overflowX: auto` wrapper the rest of the app's tables already use, letting them overflow their card at narrow widths. The nav-rail collapse itself already existed (`theme.css`'s 860px breakpoint) — nothing to fix there.
- **Project Users page vs. Org Users page**: `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s "Effective members" list (a bare `<ul>`) is now a searchable, sortable table matching Org Admin's Users table's structural pattern. Deliberate deviation from a literal reading of "look similar": `EffectiveMemberOut` has no `last_login_at`/`is_2fa_enabled`/`is_active` (org-account attributes, not meaningful at project scope) — a **Source** column (direct vs. inherited, and via what) takes their place instead of being force-fit. `docs/ux-style-guide.md` updated to state this pattern explicitly.

**Verified**: backend `pytest` (new dedup test plus the existing `test_reporting_and_changes.py`/`test_coverage_gaps.py`/`test_audit_fixes.py`/`test_pagination.py` suites, all of which touch the `/changes` feed); frontend `tsc -b`/`eslint` clean; full Storybook suite (updated `RequirementsPage.stories.tsx`, `ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`, new `StatusPieChart`/`LoginBrandHeader` stories) passing; Playwright specs added for each item and run against the dev/test stack.

Files changed: `backend/app/services/changes.py`; `backend/tests/test_reporting_and_changes.py`; `frontend/package.json`/`package-lock.json` (recharts); `frontend/src/components/StatusPieChart.tsx` (new, replaces deleted `DonutChart.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`), `LoginBrandHeader.tsx` (new); `frontend/src/pages/RequirementsPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`, `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`, `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`, `ProjectListPage.tsx`, `LoginPage.tsx`, `OrgLoginPage.tsx`, `OrgAdminPage.tsx`, `PreferencesPage.tsx`, `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`); `frontend/src/styles/theme.css`; `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`; `tests/playwright/tests/dashboard-navigation.spec.ts`, `login-branding.spec.ts`, `requirement-create-attach.spec.ts`, `project-users.spec.ts` (all new); `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Deep hardening pass on `feature/ui-improvement-stage-4` ("Please do a deep hardening pass")

Requested explicitly against the whole `feature/ui-improvement-stage-4` branch (commit `0046e21` "UX Stage 4 works" vs. `main`'s `4c71a2c`, 31 files) — the entire "Human UI/UX review batch" landed in the entry directly above, treated as its own scoped review rather than assumed already covered by that entry's own "Verified" section, per this project's standing hardening-pass practice. Identify → verify → remediate: the one changed backend file (`services/changes.py`'s activity-feed dedup filter) read and traced line-by-line directly — every suppressed `(entity_type, action)` pair's `AuditEvent.detail` compared against its corresponding `RequirementVersion`/`ChangeRequestVersion` synthesized entry to confirm no information loss, not just that the dedup filter's set matches the entry's own claimed list. A subagent covered the frontend lane (13 changed files: the new create→attach/link step, dashboard-navigation deep links, `StatusPieChart`/Recharts, `LoginBrandHeader`, the `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` members table, and the four responsive/overflow/styling-only files) against this project's standard checklist (client-side-only authorization, raw-enum rendering, the `reload()`-clobbers-unsaved-edit race class, confirmation-dialog tiers) — its five highest-stakes claims (the Add-Link disabled-with-zero-eligible-targets fix on both `RequirementsPage.tsx` and `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`, `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s diff being CSS-only, `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s new member search/sort being read-only local state untouched by any `reload()`, and the dashboard tiles/charts linking only to already-authorized destinations) were independently re-verified by reading the actual diff hunks directly, not trusted from the subagent's summary alone, per this project's standing rule.

## Admin-tier ResourceMenu consistency: Server Admin and Preferences converted from Tabs, reversing Project Admin's earlier "stays on Tabs" call

Product owner-directed reversal of a recorded style-guide decision, not a new finding from an audit pass. `docs/ux-style-guide.md` Principle 1 and its "Pattern: settings hierarchy" decision tree say Resource menu is for more than five setting groups opened rarely as a whole, Tabs for five or fewer views all relevant together. Server Admin (4 groups), Preferences (5 groups), and Project Admin (5 groups) each sit at or under that threshold, and the 2026-08 UX audit roadmap ("Revisit Project Admin's 8-tab bar against the 5-tab ceiling") explicitly recorded a *deliberate* prior decision to keep Project Admin on `Tabs` specifically because those tabs are "all relevant together" and actively used inline, not "opened rarely as a whole." Shown that tension directly, the product owner decided **cross-page consistency across the app's whole admin tier** (Org Admin, Server Admin, Preferences, Project Admin — Org Admin already converted to `ResourceMenu` in the "Org Admin → resource-menu restructure" entry above) now outweighs the original per-page ≤5-groups reasoning: a page that's part of a recognisable set of admin-tier pages shouldn't use a different navigation shape from its siblings just because its own group count happens to clear the threshold the others exceeded.

**Scope: navigation shell only, not content.** All three pages kept their existing group/tab keys, labels, and panel content unchanged — only the container swapped from `Tabs`/`tabPanelProps` to `ResourceMenu`, copying `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s already-established shape exactly rather than reinventing it: a flat `ResourceMenuGroupDef<K>[]` array, a `useParams<{ group?: string }>()` read with an `ORG_ADMIN_GROUP_KEYS`-style whitelist-and-fallback-to-default pattern, and a new `:group?` optional route segment so a bare link into the page (used everywhere today) still resolves.

- **`ServerManagementPage.tsx`**: new `/server/management/:group?` route (`App.tsx`), 4 groups (`accessReview`/`branding`/`signup`/`email`), default `accessReview`. `title`/`ariaLabel` now come from `ResourceMenu`'s own props (`strings.nav.serverManagement`, new `strings.system.sectionsNav`) instead of a bare `<h1>` + `Tabs`.
- **`PreferencesPage.tsx`**: new `/preferences/:group?` route, 5 groups (`profile`/`security`/`access`/`pats`/`notifications`), default `profile`. New `strings.preferences.sectionsNav`.
- **`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`**: new `/projects/:projectId/admin/:group?` route, 5 groups (`overview`/`structure`/`fieldsActions`/`groups`/`reportSetup`), default `overview`. Unlike the other two, this page keeps its own custom header row (`<h1>{project.name}</h1>` + the "Add sub-project" button) above `ResourceMenu` rather than passing `title` into the component — `ResourceMenu`'s own `title` prop would have duplicated the project name a second time next to a button that has nowhere else to live in that layout. New `strings.admin.sectionsNav` (tokenized: `"{Project} admin sections"`). The stale roadmap-referencing comment above the old tab-state `useState` ("per the style guide's own 5-tab ceiling for the Tabs pattern") was removed since it's the exact reasoning this reversal supersedes; the surrounding "8 tabs -> 5 groups" consolidation history comment was kept and reworded to note the later Tabs→ResourceMenu conversion rather than deleted, since that regroup (Terminology folded into Overview, Stages+Components/Categories merged into Structure, etc.) is still the current shape and still worth explaining.
- **`Tabs.tsx`/`tabPanelProps` themselves are untouched.** Grepping the frontend confirms these three pages were `Tabs`' only production call sites (its own file-level comment already said so: "Replaces three byte-for-byte-identical hand-rolled tab bars"), so it now has none — deliberately left in place regardless, per the task's own instruction and Principle 1's continued documented case for `Tabs` (a genuinely ≤5-co-relevant-view surface outside the admin tier), rather than deleted as dead code.

**Docs updated to reflect the reversal explicitly, not silently:**
- `docs/ux-style-guide.md` Principle 1 gained a sentence naming cross-page consistency with an already-converted admin-tier sibling as itself a valid reason to choose `ResourceMenu` even at or under the 5-group threshold.
- `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`'s roadmap: the "Shared, accessible `Tabs` component" row (473) got a "**Superseded 2026-08-27**" note; the "Revisit Project Admin's 8-tab bar" row (488) got a "**Reversed 2026-08-27, by direct product decision**" note explaining the old reasoning is still true in isolation but was outweighed; a new row records the Server Admin/Preferences conversions.

**Playwright**: every spec that drove these three pages via `page.getByRole("tab", { name: ... })` (Tabs' own ARIA role) now instead uses the new route segments, the same idempotent, `aria-current="page"`-checking pattern `helpers.ts`'s existing `selectOrgAdminGroup` already established for Org Admin — generalised into a new `selectResourceMenuGroup(page, groupLabel)`, with `selectOrgAdminGroup`/`selectServerManagementGroup`/`selectPreferencesGroup`/`selectProjectAdminGroup` as thin, page-named wrappers around it (kept as separate exported names rather than one generic call at every site, matching how the existing call sites already read as self-documenting about which page's group menu they operate on). 26 spec files updated across `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/` and the top-level `tests/playwright/tests/` directory — every file that had a `role="tab"` locator on Server Admin, Preferences, or Project Admin, found by grepping the whole suite (confirmed zero remaining `getByRole("tab"` hits against any of the three afterward). One stale comment in `project-admin-structural.spec.ts` ("ProjectAdminPage's tab state resets to the default (Overview) on a full page reload") was corrected in the same pass — it described `Tabs`' client-only-state behaviour, which no longer applies now that the group is a real route segment; a full reload now *preserves* the selected group, so the spec's own re-select-after-reload call is now a harmless, already-idempotent no-op, not a required step.

**Storybook**: no new stories, per the task's own scope call — `ResourceMenu` is reused as-is, not extended. The three pages' *existing* `.stories.tsx` files did need updating, though, since their `play` functions also drove the old `role="tab"` interaction and their `withRouter` decorators didn't yet declare the new `:group?` route pattern: all `getByRole("tab", { name: ... })` calls became `getByRole("link", { name: ... })` (37 call sites across the three files), and each `withRouter(initialPath)` call gained its route's `:group?` pattern as a second argument, matching `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`'s own established decorator shape.

**Verified.** Frontend: `npx tsc -b` and `npm run build` (typecheck + Vite production build) both clean — no new errors introduced by any of the three page conversions, the Storybook updates, or the new `strings.ts` keys; `npm run lint` clean (only the same 7 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings in untouched files). Playwright: the full set of specs touched by this change (26 files, 32 tests spanning both `tests/e2e-workflows/` and the top-level directory) — **32 passed, 0 failed** (3.1 minutes), from a single, uninterrupted run against a freshly `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE`-reset and reseeded (`seed_e2e_dataset.py`) `tests/container` stack. Getting to that clean run took several discarded attempts, worth recording since it's a real instance of this project's own documented DB-wedge/shared-stack class of problem, not a code issue: this session ran concurrently with other agents' unrelated work in the same working tree and against the same shared dev stack (a separate dashboard/result-counts workstream, confirmed directly via `docker top`/`ps aux` mid-session), and two earlier attempts were separately invalidated — once by a live `ObjectDeletedError`/`500`-producing schema wipe from another process's `pytest` run caught mid-flight in `docker compose logs backend`, and once self-inflicted, by accidentally launching two overlapping copies of the same Playwright invocation against the same login/browser state after a session interruption. Every failure from those contaminated runs traced back to either a login/"Sign out button not found" symptom (this project's own documented DB-wedge signature) or stale data from a previous run killed mid-test (e.g. Beta-1's seeded "Review" action type already renamed by an interrupted earlier attempt) — none were `ResourceMenu`/routing/locator failures, and the final clean run's 32/32 confirms none of the three conversions have a real defect.

Files changed: `frontend/src/pages/ServerManagementPage.tsx`, `PreferencesPage.tsx`, `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx` for all three); `frontend/src/App.tsx`; `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/helpers.ts` and 21 spec files in that directory (`project-admin-structural`, `project-hierarchy`, `org-login-2fa-handoff`, `role-display-collapsing`, `two-factor-auth`, `report-image-attachment`, `stage-review-and-completion`, `richtext-insert-link-modal`, `org-rename-and-test-email`, `preferences-and-theme`, `org-label`, `project-admin-groups-and-fields`, `terminology-coverage`, `personal-access-tokens`, `external-project-invite`, `workflow-bypass-attempts`, `project-admin-templates-and-reports`, `project-admin-action-types`, `requirements-bulk-operations`, `org-security-controls`, `leave-organisation`); 5 top-level spec files (`golden-path`, `requirement-create-attach`, `mockup-engagement`, `project-users`, `pelion-v2`); `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Project-wide file browser, and a latent access-control bug found while building it

New feature: "a way to view all files in a project." `FileAsset` has no `project_id` of its own — it's only reachable via a join through whichever requirement/action/comment it's attached to (`RequirementFile`/`RequirementActionFile`/`CommentFile`), and `docs/requirements.md` U-P-05 only asked for a project overview metric ("number of files in project, if files are implemented"), never a browsable list. `GET /projects/{project_id}/files` (`backend/app/routers/projects.py::list_project_files`, `ProjectFileOut` in `backend/app/schemas/file.py`) fills that gap: three separate joins (direct attachment via `Requirement.project_id`, action attachment via `RequirementAction.project_id` directly — an action isn't owned by exactly one requirement, `RequirementActionLink` is many-to-many, so there's no single requirement to attribute a file to — and comment attachment via `ReviewComment.target_id` where `target_type == REQUIREMENT`, joined to `Requirement.project_id`), merged, sorted newest-first, and paginated with the same `limit`/`offset`/`X-Total-Count` convention every other list endpoint in this router uses. Gated by `require_project_view` (member-level content access), matching every other requirement-content-adjacent endpoint. Frontend: `frontend/src/pages/ProjectFilesPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`), a flat read-only table reusing `fileUrl()`'s existing download-link pattern from `FileAttachmentList.tsx` — no upload control, since uploads stay per-requirement/action/comment. Wired up at `/projects/:projectId/files` (`App.tsx`), a new "Files" nav-rail entry (`Layout.tsx`, between Actions and Reports), and `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`'s "Files" metric tile now links here instead of the unfiltered requirements list it previously (incorrectly) pointed at — a separately-flagged bug ("the files glance shouldn't go to requirements"), fixed as part of the same change since the new destination is what the tile always should have pointed to.

**A real, pre-existing access-control bug found while tracing the three join tables this endpoint needed to combine, fixed in the same change rather than deferred** (per this project's standing "fix, don't defer" rule): `GET /api/v1/files/{id}` (`backend/app/routers/files.py::download_file`) resolves which project a non-org-resource, non-avatar file belongs to by checking `RequirementFile` then falling back to a `CommentFile`/`ReviewComment` lookup — but had no branch for `RequirementActionFile` at all. A file attached only via a requirement action (`POST /projects/{id}/actions/{action_id}/files`) therefore always resolved `project_id = None` and fell through to an unconditional 403, for *everyone*, including the uploader and the project's own manager — upload/list/delete all worked, but the file could never actually be downloaded. Confirmed via `test_action_direct_file_attachment` (`backend/tests/test_requirement_actions.py`), which uploaded and listed an action attachment but never called the download endpoint — the gap was invisible to the existing suite. Fixed by adding the missing branch, resolving via `RequirementAction.project_id` directly (no join through a requirement needed, for the same many-to-many reason `list_project_files` above attributes action files to the action itself). This is a fail-closed bug (over-restrictive, not over-permissive) so it doesn't regress the SOC 2 access-control policy's authorization posture, but per CLAUDE.md's guidance on changes touching authorization resolution logic, it's called out explicitly here rather than folded silently into the feature commit.

**Docs and seed data kept in sync:** `docs/solution-architecture.md` gained an implementation note under "Application Layer" explaining the three-way join, matching the existing bundle-export/import notes' style. `backend/scripts/seed_e2e_dataset.py` now seeds one file via each of the three origins on Alpha-1 (a direct attachment, an attachment on the existing "E2E Review Action" action, and a comment attachment) specifically so `project-files.spec.ts` has a realistic multi-source project to assert against — `docs/e2e-workflows.md` gained workflow entry #26 for it. `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py` gained the same three-origin file seeding on Falcon-3 (direct attachment on the still-draft "Complete pre-flight diagnostic checks" requirement — not the already-approved remote-ID requirement, which 409s on a direct attachment per C-G-12 — an action attachment on the completed firmware-review action, and a comment attachment on the flight-time discussion), so the demo dataset now actually demonstrates the feature it previously left implicit in the file-count metric alone.

**Tests added:** `backend/tests/test_files.py::test_project_files_endpoint_combines_sources_and_scopes_by_project` — seeds all three origins across two requirements in one project plus a direct attachment in a second, unrelated project, and asserts the endpoint returns exactly the three same-project rows with correct origin context, and critically that the second project's file never appears (same-target-scoped resolution, not "has access somewhere" — the hard access-control-policy requirement called out in this task). `test_project_files_endpoint_requires_project_membership` — a user with no role on the project gets 403, matching every other `require_project_view`-gated endpoint. `test_requirement_actions.py::test_action_direct_file_attachment` extended to assert the download actually succeeds (and 404s post-delete), pinning the `download_file` fix; `test_non_member_cannot_download_action_attachment` added alongside it, mirroring the existing requirement-attachment non-member test. Frontend: `ProjectFilesPage.stories.tsx` (mixed-sources rendering with origin links, `LoadMoreButton` pagination, empty state) and a new Playwright spec `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/project-files.spec.ts` (files from all three origins listed with correct origin links, the overview tile navigating here instead of to requirements, the nav-rail entry, and an actual download round-trip against the seeded Alpha-1 fixture).

**A messy, heavily-contested shared test environment during verification, not a code problem:** this session's Docker host ports were initially squatted by an unrelated, already-orphaned worktree's stack from an earlier task in the same environment (stopped once identified, freeing the ports); the shared `reqtrack_test` database was then found mid-verification in a partially-seeded, inconsistent state (an org existing with none of its persona users, `httpx.ConnectError: [Errno 99] Cannot assign requested address` transients under concurrent load, and at one point the schema itself was fully dropped by a concurrent process) — consistent with multiple other agents running pytest/seed/Playwright against the same stack concurrently, exactly as flagged separately. Resolved each time by re-running this project's own documented recovery recipe (`DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` + backend restart to re-run migrations, then re-seed both scripts) rather than attempting a partial, riskier row-level patch-up.

**Verified.** Backend: full suite **624 passed, 0 failed** (includes the two new endpoint tests plus the two new action-download tests, run alongside a separate, unrelated in-flight workstream's own changes to `change_requests.py`/`requirements.py`/`test_pagination.py` in the same working tree — no interference either direction). Frontend: `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) clean; `eslint src/` clean (only the same 7 pre-existing warnings in files this change doesn't touch); full Storybook suite **67 files / 561 tests passed**, including `ProjectFilesPage.stories.tsx`'s 5. Playwright: `project-files.spec.ts` **1/1 passing** against a freshly reseeded stack; a small regression batch (`dashboard-navigation.spec.ts`, `requirement-actions.spec.ts`, `comment-editing-and-attachments.spec.ts`) run alongside it turned up 2 pre-existing failures, both in files this change never touches (`RequirementsPage.tsx`'s first-paint status-filter race, `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s create-and-link action dialog) and both reproducing consistently on retry — consistent with the separately-flagged, still-in-progress parallel "result-counts/dashboard-race" workstream, not a regression introduced here; left for that workstream to resolve rather than fixed blind, per the coordination note not to clobber concurrent work outside this task's scope.

Files changed: `backend/app/schemas/file.py`, `backend/app/routers/projects.py`, `backend/app/routers/files.py`; `backend/tests/test_files.py`, `test_requirement_actions.py`; `backend/scripts/seed_e2e_dataset.py`, `seed_demo_data.py`; `frontend/src/pages/ProjectFilesPage.tsx` (new, + `.stories.tsx`), `App.tsx`, `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`; `frontend/src/components/Layout.tsx`; `frontend/src/api/types.ts`; `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`; `frontend/src/testing/storybook-helpers.tsx`; `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/project-files.spec.ts` (new); `docs/solution-architecture.md`, `docs/e2e-workflows.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Persistent "showing X of Y" result counts, and the dashboard glance-tile filter race

The "result-counts/dashboard-race" workstream referenced (as still in progress) in the entry directly above. Two related fixes across the three list pages (`RequirementsPage.tsx`, `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`, `ProjectListPage.tsx`):

**Part A — persistent result count.** `X-Total-Count` (already returned by the three list endpoints) reflects the *filtered* count, but there was never a second, *unfiltered* total to compare it against — `LoadMoreButton`'s own "(loaded/total)" text is the only place `total` was ever shown, and it disappears once every page has loaded. Each of `requirements.py`/`change_requests.py`/`projects.py`'s list endpoints now also returns `X-Total-Unfiltered-Count`: one extra `COUNT(*)`-style query against the same base scope query (project/org + default archived-visibility), taken *before* search/status/stage/category filters narrow it further. `client.ts`'s `Page<T>` gained an optional `totalUnfiltered` field read from the new header (optional, not required — many existing `getPage` mocks across other pages' stories predate this field and don't need updating).

`FilterPanel` (`frontend/src/components/FilterPanel.tsx`) was restructured into a header (a new `ResultCount` component — "57 total" with no filter active, "Showing 12 matching · 57 total" once one is — plus, on `RequirementsPage`/`ProjectListPage` only, the free-text search box relocated here from the main content column) and a collapsible body (the existing `FilterField`/`FilterCheckbox` controls): fully expanded with no toggle on desktop, defaulting to collapsed with a `CollapsibleSection`-driven toggle below the same 860px breakpoint `.side-grid` itself already collapses at (`theme.css`). `ChangeRequestsPage` has no search box (unchanged, per the brief). Four other existing `FilterPanel` consumers (`NotificationsPage`, `ProjectActionsPage`, `ProjectReviewsDuePage`, `ServerOrganisationsPage`) needed a `sectionKey` prop added for the new required collapsible-body key, since `matching`/`total` are optional but `sectionKey` isn't — none of the other three had a comparable "unfiltered total" figure to wire up, so their headers show no `ResultCount`, unchanged in appearance from before this restructure. `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s existing `Pattern: FilterPanel` write-up gained a dedicated subsection documenting this shape, plus corrections to two sentences in the original write-up that the restructure made inaccurate (the "never collapsed behind a menu" claim, and "free-text search box... stays in the main content area" — no longer true for the two pages whose search box moved).

**Part B — dashboard glance-tile filter race.** Root cause: `RequirementsPage.tsx`/`ChangeRequestsPage.tsx` each ran two effects on mount — a reload effect (deps include the filter state) and a separate deep-link effect that read `?status=`/`?stage=` from the URL and called `setStatusFilter(...)`. The reload effect fired first, with the *still-empty default* filter, kicking off an unfiltered fetch; the deep-link effect's `setStatusFilter` call then re-triggered the reload effect with the real filter, kicking off a *second* fetch. Neither `loadRequirements`/`loadChangeRequests` sequenced requests at all, so whichever response resolved last simply overwrote state — usually the correctly-filtered one, since it was kicked off second and (for a narrower query) often finishes faster, but not always: a dashboard tile click landing on `ProjectOverviewPage` → `RequirementsPage`/`ChangeRequestsPage` could show a correct filter dropdown next to an unfiltered list, "fixed" only by the user re-toggling the filter (which forces a fresh, single, correctly-sequenced fetch) — the exact manual workaround that had been masking this.

Fixed by seeding `statusFilter`/`targetStageFilter` (and the change-request tri-state equivalent) directly from `searchParams` in the `useState` initializer, rather than in a separate post-mount effect — the deep-link effect now only strips the URL params, never calls the filter setters itself, so exactly one reload effect run (and one fetch) happens per mount+filter combination. Belt-and-suspenders: `loadRequirements`/`loadChangeRequests`/`loadProjects` (all three list pages, for consistency) each gained a monotonic request-id `useRef` guard that discards a response if a newer request has since been kicked off, covering any other overlapping-fetch path (e.g. rapid filter changes) beyond the specific mount-time race the seeding fix eliminates.

**A CORS bug caught only by a real browser, not curl or pytest:** the new `X-Total-Unfiltered-Count` header was set correctly by the backend (confirmed directly with `curl`) and pytest's `TestClient` (which bypasses CORS entirely) saw it fine, but the frontend's `fetch().headers.get("x-total-unfiltered-count")` silently returned `null` in a real browser — `main.py`'s `CORSMiddleware` only listed `X-Total-Count` in `expose_headers`, and browsers hide any response header not on that allowlist from JS regardless of `allow_headers`. `ResultCount` fell back to `total` in both slots ("N total" only, never "Showing N matching"), which read as a plausible-looking but wrong UI state rather than an outright error — the kind of bug this project's own testing policy runs a real browser for specifically because unit/API-level tests structurally can't see it. Fixed by adding `X-Total-Unfiltered-Count` to `expose_headers`.

**A second, unrelated bug found and fixed to unblock verification, per this project's standing "fix, don't defer" rule:** `seed_demo_data.py`'s newly-added (by the parallel `project-files` workstream referenced above) direct-requirement-file-attachment call targeted `remote_id_req`, which `DRONE_REQUIREMENTS` seeds directly into `complete` status — already locked, so the direct-attachment endpoint 409s every time, deterministically, on a fresh database (confirmed: not a stale-data artifact). Retargeted to `preflight_req` (`draft` at that point in the script) instead — both this session and, independently, the parallel `project-files` workstream (see its own entry above, written concurrently) arrived at the identical fix.
