## Generalized cross-project group permissions: any same-organisation project as a member source, plus project-referencing group members

Requested directly: "It would be good if you could use other projects/groups to give permission to a project. Especially useful for nested projects where an external party may be working in one project but they need to be given access to another project for understanding, and you want to use groups... to add them as members." Investigation found this was already largely built — `ProjectGroup` can nest an `OrgGroup` (C-U-12), and `ProjectMemberSource` already let a project consume baseline `MEMBER` access from a direct child (see this log's "Hierarchical projects" entry) — but two real gaps remained: `ProjectMemberSource` was restricted to a strict parent/child pair and could only ever grant bare `MEMBER`, and there was no way for a project group to be defined as "the members of some other project" directly. This entry covers both, plus the security review performed given this touches `services/rbac.py` (SOC2-governed, per `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md`).

**Scope decision, made with the user up front:** both gaps closed in one piece of work, not either/or — (a) generalize `ProjectMemberSource` beyond parent/child and beyond `MEMBER`-only, and (b) add a `ProjectGroupMember.source_project_id` reference type. Both remain **authorized entirely from the receiving project's side**, matching the existing parent/child design's asymmetry rationale exactly (a source project's manager is never consulted or notified — the same reasoning `ProjectMemberSource`'s own docstring already gives for why authorization isn't split the other way).

### 7a. `ProjectMemberSource` generalization

- **Schema** (`backend/app/models/project.py`): two new columns, `mirror_mode: ProjectRoleInheritanceMode` (default `MEMBER_ONLY` — byte-identical to every row's original behavior) and `mirror_filter_role: ProjectRole | None` (same `MIRROR_ROLE`-pairing validation as `Project.role_inheritance_filter_role`, reusing `_validate_role_inheritance_filter` in `schemas/project.py`, plus a new check rejecting `mirror_mode = NONE` — unlike the forward mechanism, `NONE` makes no sense here since the row's own existence already means "grant something").
- **Relaxed constraint**: the live revalidation in `services/rbac.py` (`_member_source_rows`, formerly `_member_source_frontier`) changed from `source_project.parent_project_id == project_id` to `source_project.organization_id == project.organization_id` plus a self-reference guard — any project in the same organisation, not just a structural child.
- **RBAC resolution rewritten to be mode-aware, per hop**, mirroring how `_forward_inherited_roles` already applies `role_inheritance_mode` for the forward direction: new `_member_source_derived_roles` (replaces the old boolean `_has_member_source_access`, used directly in `get_effective_project_roles`), `_member_source_role_holder_ids` (role-scoped, replaces the `role == MEMBER`-only special case in `get_project_users_by_role`), and a rewritten member-source section of `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance` that now names the actual contributing hop (`via_project_id`/`via_mode`) instead of always `None`/always `MEMBER`. A new `_direct_project_roles_excluding_org_wide` helper (the full-role-granularity counterpart to `_direct_project_member_ids`'s existing boolean exclusion) is what lets `MIRROR_ALL` mirror a source's *actual* direct roles without reintroducing the `ORG_WIDE`-baseline leak that helper's own docstring already warns against — the same class of bug a prior hardening pass on this exact mechanism found and fixed (see this log's "Hierarchical projects" entry).
- **Migration**: `alembic/versions/0017_generalized_cross_project_permissions.py` — `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` for both, backfilling existing rows to `mirror_mode = 'member_only'` (identical behavior, no re-review of existing configuration needed).
- **Router** (`routers/projects.py::add_member_source`): accepts `mirror_mode`/`mirror_filter_role`, validates same-org instead of parent/child, still gated by `require_project_manage` on the receiving project only. **A second, easy-to-miss spot needed the same relaxation**: `_accessible_project_ids`'s own structural-visibility expansion walk (used to decide which projects show up in a user's project list at all) had its own hardcoded `Project.parent_project_id == ProjectMemberSource.project_id` check — generalizing only the grant-resolution side and missing this would have left a real, working grant invisible in the UI (the user could open the project by URL but it would never appear in their list). Fixed the same way, same-org join instead of parent/child.
- **Frontend** (`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`): the member-sources section's picker now offers any same-org project (`orgProjects`, already fetched for the parent-project picker — the now-dead `childProjects`/`GET .../children` fetch was removed rather than left as a backwards-compat shim), plus mode/filter-role selects mirroring the existing forward-inheritance controls. Each listed source shows its mode as a badge.

### 7b. `ProjectGroupMember.source_project_id`

- **Schema**: nullable `source_project_id` FK to `projects.id` (`ondelete="CASCADE"`), and the existing two-way "exactly one of user_id/org_group_id" check constraint widened to three-way.
- **Deliberately non-recursive (one hop only)** — this is the load-bearing design decision, not an implementation detail: "members of project X" means X's *direct* members only, resolved via a new `_direct_project_member_ids_base` helper that the existing `_direct_project_member_ids`/`_direct_project_role_holder_ids`/`_direct_effective_project_roles` all gained a third arm calling into (never into themselves, never into each other's full/recursive versions). This is what makes two projects referencing each other's rosters structurally incapable of causing unbounded recursion — a real scenario checked directly by a new test (`test_project_group_source_reference_is_one_hop_only`, a three-project X→Y→Z chain proving Z's members reach Y but not X). This mirrors, and is more conservative than, `ProjectMemberSource`'s own multi-hop chaining (source 6 deliberately *does* chain through a source's own further member-source list) — the two mechanisms made different tradeoffs here on purpose: `ProjectMemberSource` chaining was an existing, already-reviewed design property being preserved; a *new* recursive-by-default mechanism would have needed its own from-scratch cycle analysis this entry didn't want to take on when "one hop, no recursion possible at all" already satisfies the actual use case (referencing one other project's roster directly).
- Same-organisation constraint, same defense-in-depth shape as the existing nested-org-group arm (`OrgGroup.organization_id == Project.organization_id`, re-checked live at read time even though also enforced at write time).
- **Router** (`routers/projects.py::add_project_group_member`): the existing "exactly one of user_id/org_group_id" 400 check widened to three-way; a `source_project_id == project_id` self-reference guard added (structurally harmless given the one-hop design, but confusing/pointless to allow). `remove_project_group_member`'s delete `WHERE` clause gained the third match arm.
- **Frontend**: each project group's card gained a "reference another project's members…" picker alongside the existing user-autocomplete and org-group-nesting controls, listing referenced projects as `"<name>'s members"` bullets.

### Security review (identify → verify → remediate, per the change-management policy)

**Identify** — what could this weaken: (1) the same-org boundary being the *only* remaining constraint on `ProjectMemberSource`, replacing structural parent/child — could this let a project pull access from an org project its manager has no relationship to at all? (2) `ProjectGroupMember.source_project_id` reading a source project's members with zero consent from that project's own manager — is that a new escalation path? (3) does either mechanism reintroduce the `ORG_WIDE`-baseline leak a prior hardening pass already found and fixed once for this exact mechanism? (4) can the two mechanisms, or either mechanism against itself, be chained into unbounded recursion or a sibling-project leak the way source 5/6 were already deliberately decoupled to prevent?

**Verify**:
1. Same-org-only, not org-unrestricted — confirmed by `_member_source_rows`'/the new group arm's live re-join on `organization_id`, tested directly (`test_member_source_rejects_cross_org_source`, `test_project_group_source_reference_rejects_cross_org`, both asserting 400 at creation time against a genuinely separate organisation).
2. No consent required from the source side is **not a new escalation path** — it's the same authorization asymmetry `ProjectMemberSource`'s original design already established and documented the rationale for (a receiving project's manager already has the standing authority to grant any role to any user in their own project directly; sourcing that grant from another project's roster instead of typing emails one at a time doesn't grant anything the manager couldn't already grant by hand). Project names/existence are not confidential within an organisation (already visible via the ordinary project list to anyone with a role there), so this isn't a new information-disclosure path either. Confirmed both mechanisms remain unreachable from the source project's own management surface (`test_child_manager_cannot_add_itself_as_a_member_source`, pre-existing, still passes unchanged; `test_project_group_source_reference_rejects_self_reference` covers the group side's degenerate case).
3. `ORG_WIDE` leak: the new `_direct_project_roles_excluding_org_wide` helper (for `MIRROR_ALL`'s full-role mirroring) deliberately omits the `ORG_WIDE` visibility branch, matching `_direct_project_member_ids`'s existing exclusion — confirmed via `test_member_source_does_not_leak_org_wide_visibility_as_membership` (pre-existing, still passes unchanged; the generalization didn't touch this code path's exclusion, only added a new, separately-exclusion-respecting one alongside it).
4. Recursion/leak: `ProjectGroupMember.source_project_id` is structurally one-hop-only (see 7b above) — no BFS, no cycle possible by construction, verified directly. `ProjectMemberSource`'s existing multi-hop chaining and its decoupling from forward inheritance were already covered by `test_member_source_multilevel_requires_both_hops`/`test_member_source_listed_sibling_does_not_leak_via_mirror_all` (pre-existing, both still pass unchanged, confirming the generalization didn't disturb that property).

**Remediate**: no gap found beyond the two implementation spots already fixed as part of doing the generalization correctly (the `_accessible_project_ids` visibility-walk relaxation noted in 7a, and building the non-recursive `_direct_project_member_ids_base` split rather than a naive third arm on the existing recursive-capable function).

### Two existing Playwright tests updated for the behavior change

`project-hierarchy.spec.ts`'s `test_member_source_must_be_an_actual_direct_child` (backend) and its two UI-level equivalents no longer hold — replaced with `test_member_source_can_be_any_same_org_project_not_just_a_child` (backend, positive case) and the cross-org/self-reference rejection tests above. `test_stale_member_source_grants_nothing_after_child_reparented` assumed reparenting invalidates the grant (true only because the *old* constraint was structural parent/child); replaced with `test_member_source_survives_reparenting_within_same_org` (same-org reparenting no longer breaks the grant — a deliberate behavior change, not a regression) plus `test_member_source_stale_after_cross_org_move` (exercising the live-revalidation directly via a DB-level org move, since no product feature moves a project cross-org today to trigger it through the API). On the Playwright side, `project-hierarchy.spec.ts`'s existing "Gamma-4 has no way to manage that relationship" step asserted the old empty-state string (`"No direct sub-{projects} available to add."`, now `"No other {projects} available to add."`) and relied on Gamma-4 genuinely having zero candidates (true only under the old children-only restriction) — updated to assert the new, correct behavior (a picker now *does* show other same-org projects, proving the generalization end to end) rather than the coincidental old emptiness.

### Tests

Backend (`backend/tests/test_project_hierarchy.py`): 12 new tests covering both mechanisms — same-org acceptance/cross-org rejection/self-reference rejection for both, reparenting survival, the defensive stale-after-cross-org-move check, `MIRROR_ALL`/`MIRROR_ROLE`/default-`MEMBER_ONLY` mode behavior for `ProjectMemberSource`, and the one-hop-only non-recursion proof for the group mechanism. All existing tests in this file continue to pass unchanged except the two whose premises the generalization deliberately supersedes (see above).

Playwright: a new test in `project-hierarchy.spec.ts` (`generalized member-source (any same-org project, mirror modes) and project-referencing group members work end to end`) exercises both mechanisms through the real UI against Gamma-1/Gamma-2 (unrelated same-org projects) — self-healing against its own prior partial runs via a `cleanup()` helper called both defensively up front and in a `finally` block, since a mid-test failure would otherwise leave the shared Gamma fixture mutated for the next run. The existing "member sources are managed from the parent's admin page only" test's stale assertions were corrected in place (see above).

Storybook: `ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx` gained mode-badge coverage in the existing `MemberSourcesListAndAdd` story (now also exercising the add-with-mirror-mode flow end to end against a mocked `api.post`) and a new `ProjectGroupCanReferenceAnotherProjectsMembers` story exercising the group-reference picker and its POST payload. `mockProjectAdminApis` gained a `groups` override (previously module-level-constant only) to support the new story without disturbing any existing one.

### Seed data

`backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`: Falcon-3 (an existing project, previously only demonstrating the parent/child member-source pair with its own Avionics sub-project) now additionally consumes stakeholders (`mirror_role`) from the *unrelated* Solstice Cloud Platform project, and Solstice Cloud Platform's own default "Stakeholders" group is defined as "Falcon-3's direct members" — one demonstration of each generalized mechanism, deliberately placed in the manual-demo dataset rather than the fixed E2E persona dataset so it can't collide with the new Playwright test's own dynamic Gamma-1/Gamma-2 fixture management. `add_member_source`'s helper signature gained optional `mirror_mode`/`mirror_filter_role` parameters (default to the original behavior when omitted, so every other existing call site — the Falcon-3/Avionics parent/child pair — is untouched); a new `get_project_group_id`/`add_project_group_source_reference` helper pair supports the group-reference demonstration.

### Docs

`services/rbac.py`'s module docstring updated from "six sources" to seven, documenting the generalized source 6 and the new source 7, with the same decoupling-rationale prose style as the existing five. `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md`'s item 2 (target-scoped resolution) gained a paragraph recording that both mechanisms were reviewed against that exact principle before being generalized, not exempted from it. `docs/solution-architecture.md`'s access-control ER diagram gained the `PROJECT |o--o{ PROJECT_GROUP_MEMBER : is` edge and updated prose for both mechanisms' generalized shape.

### Verified

Backend: the full suite, **634 passed, 0 failed**, run with `SMTP_HOST=localhost` (the suite's hardcoded `mailhog` default only resolves inside the Docker Compose network — an environment-invocation detail, not a code issue, that produced 7 spurious failures on an earlier host-run attempt, all confirmed unrelated and passing once corrected). `test_project_hierarchy.py` specifically: 42/42 (30 pre-existing + 12 new), rerun individually and as part of the full suite. Frontend: `tsc -b` and `npm run build` clean; `eslint` clean; the full Storybook suite, **562/562**, including the two updated/new `ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx` interaction tests. Playwright: `project-hierarchy.spec.ts` — **5/5**, rerun twice back-to-back to confirm the new test's self-healing cleanup is genuinely idempotent (not just "passes once"); a regression batch (`project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`, `project-admin-structural.spec.ts`, `project-users.spec.ts`) — **3/3**, confirming the `ProjectGroup`/`ProjectMemberSource` type changes (new required fields) didn't disturb any other page consuming those types.

Migration applied cleanly to a freshly-reset schema (`DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` + restart, confirming `alembic_version` lands on `0017`) and both seed scripts (`seed_e2e_dataset.py`, `seed_demo_data.py`) ran end to end against it without error, including the new demonstration calls.

Files changed: `backend/app/models/project.py`, `backend/app/services/rbac.py`, `backend/app/schemas/project.py`, `backend/app/routers/projects.py`; `backend/alembic/versions/0017_generalized_cross_project_permissions.py` (new); `backend/tests/test_project_hierarchy.py`; `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`; `frontend/src/api/types.ts`, `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.tsx` (+ `.stories.tsx`); `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/project-hierarchy.spec.ts`; `docs/solution-architecture.md`, `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md`, `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Security uplift: full Dependabot + code-scanning remediation ("First stage of dependabot updates")

Requested as a review-and-fix pass across every open GitHub Dependabot alert (32) and code-scanning alert (7) on `feature/security-uplift-August-2026`. Touches authentication (OIDC ID-token verification) and a multi-tenant-adjacent search endpoint, so both fall under the change-management policy's identify → verify → remediate gate below, not just a routine dependency bump.

### Dependency upgrades (32 Dependabot alerts, all closed)

`backend/requirements.txt`: `python-jose[cryptography]` 3.3.0 → 3.5.0, `cryptography` 49.0.0 → 50.0.1, `python-multipart` 0.0.20 → 0.0.32, `python-dotenv` 1.0.1 → 1.2.3, `aiosmtplib` 3.0.2 → 5.1.2, `pytest`/`pytest-asyncio` 8.3.3/0.24.0 → 9.1.1/1.4.0 (pytest-asyncio bumped to stay compatible with pytest 9, though not itself flagged). `mcp-server/requirements.txt`: the same `pytest`/`pytest-asyncio` bump.

**`authlib` removed entirely** rather than bumped — 10 of the 32 alerts, including the critical JWS/JWK-header-injection signature-verification bypass (GHSA-wvwj-cvrp-7pv5), were against it. Its only use in the codebase was `authlib.jose` in `services/oidc_client.py::verify_id_token`, which authlib itself deprecated in favor of `joserfc` (now a direct dependency, `joserfc==1.7.4`, rather than pulled in transitively). Dropping the dependency closes all 10 alerts outright instead of chasing point-releases, and moves the OIDC ID-token verification path onto the library authlib's own maintainers now recommend for exactly this — see the security review below for what the migration itself changed.

`frontend/package.json`: `react-router-dom` 6.26.2 → 7.18.2 (the only real fix for GHSA-jjmj-jmhj-qwj2 — no patched release exists in the 6.x line; the app's usage is entirely "library mode" `BrowserRouter`/`Routes`/`Route`/hooks, none of the v7 data-router APIs, so the migration is a version bump with no code changes needed). `vite` 5.4.6 → 6.4.3 (the minimum fixing all three vite/esbuild CVEs; deliberately not 7.x or 8.x — `@vitejs/plugin-react`'s Babel-based transform triggers an upstream `optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions`-is-deprecated warning under vite 7/8's newer Rolldown-based optimizer regardless of which plugin-react version pairs with it, confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this branch by reproducing it against the pre-upgrade `main` tree too — 6.4.3 avoids it entirely while still closing every CVE). `@vitejs/plugin-react` 4.3.1 → 4.7.0 (matching vite 6). `dompurify` added as a new direct dependency for the RichTextEditor fix below. `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities after `scripts/sync-lockfile.sh`.

### Code-scanning alerts (7, all fixed at the source, not dismissed)

1. **`orgs.py`/`scim.py` polynomial ReDoS (2 alerts).** `_EMAIL_LIKE` (a `^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$`-style regex used to decide whether a project/org user-search query "looks like an email") and `_SIMPLE_EQ_FILTER` (parsing SCIM's `attr eq "value"` filter syntax) both had quadratic-or-worse backtracking on crafted input, and both take attacker-controlled strings (`q` on an org-member-visible search endpoint; `filter` on any SCIM-bearer-token holder's request) with no length cap. Rewritten as plain string operations (`str.partition`/`rfind`/slicing) instead of a single backtracking regex — genuinely linear, not just fast on the inputs a hand-written test happens to try. The first pass at the SCIM fix (anchoring a `\s+eq\s+"..."` regex to the end via `.search()`) was *itself* still polynomial on a long run of whitespace containing no "eq" at all — caught by deliberately stress-testing the fix against a 200k-character all-whitespace attack string before considering it done, not just re-testing the original crafted input the alert named.
2. **`local.py` path traversal (3 alerts, same underlying finding).** The existing guard (`pathlib.Path.resolve()` + `is_relative_to()`) was already correct, but CodeQL's `py/path-injection` sanitizer-recognition doesn't credit that idiom as a barrier. Rewritten using the exact `os.path.realpath()` + `str.startswith()` shape CodeQL's own rule documentation gives as the safe pattern, with identical confinement semantics — `test_local_storage_backend.py`'s existing traversal-rejection test still passes unchanged.
3. **RichTextEditor DOM XSS.** `editableRef.current.innerHTML = renderMarkdown(value)` reinterprets Markdown-rendered HTML built from a requirement/report field (attacker-influenceable in a multi-tenant app) without a sanitization barrier CodeQL recognizes. Added `DOMPurify.sanitize()` with an explicit tag/attribute allowlist matching exactly what `renderMarkdown` ever produces, applied at both this assignment and a second raw-HTML-injection spot found in the same component while fixing the first: `insertImage`'s `document.execCommand("insertHTML", ...)` interpolated an uploaded file's own `filename` into an `alt` attribute unescaped — a `"` in a filename breaks out of the attribute, a real (if narrow) stored-XSS vector via a crafted upload name, fixed by routing that fragment through the same sanitizer.
4. **Incomplete URL substring sanitization (test file).** `test_org_export_import.py` asserted `"smtp.example.com" in org_json_text` to confirm non-secret config survives export — CodeQL's heuristic reads a bare `"host" in text` as a URL/host-allowlist check a crafted value could spoof. Not a real security decision, but the test is more precise anyway asserting against the parsed field (`json.loads(org_json_text)["smtp_host"] == "smtp.example.com"`) rather than raw substring containment against the whole document.

### Security review (identify → verify → remediate, per the change-management policy)

**Identify** — what could removing `authlib` and rewriting `verify_id_token` on `joserfc` weaken: (1) does the new library actually verify the signature against the fetched JWKS, or could it be tricked into trusting an attacker-embedded key/algorithm the way the authlib CVE being removed allowed? (2) are `iss`/`aud`/`exp` still enforced with the same specificity (per-organisation issuer and client id, not just "some issuer")? (3) does the rewrite preserve `_assert_safe_external_url`'s SSRF guard on the JWKS fetch, untouched? (4) is there now *less* test coverage of this path than before, given the fix touches auth-critical code.

**Verify**:
1. `joserfc.jwt.decode(id_token, key_set, algorithms=_ALLOWED_ID_TOKEN_ALGORITHMS)` is called with an explicit allowlist of asymmetric algorithms only (`RS256/384/512`, `PS256/384/512`, `ES256/384/512` — no `none`, no `HS*`) — closing the specific "JWKS public key reused as an HMAC secret" algorithm-confusion class, the same root-cause family as this branch's own python-jose and Authlib CVEs. Proved, not just asserted: `test_verify_id_token_rejects_hs256_algorithm_confusion` signs a token with `HS256` using the RSA key's own public modulus as the HMAC secret and confirms it's rejected.
2. `iss`/`aud`/`exp` are checked twice — once via `JWTClaimsRegistry(iss=..., aud=..., exp=..., essential=True)` enforcing *presence* (OIDC Core 1.0 §2 requires all three), and again via the function's own existing explicit comparison against the specific per-organisation `issuer_url`/`client_id` (unchanged from before the migration, since that logic never touched authlib). Both halves are independently covered: `test_verify_id_token_rejects_wrong_issuer`, `..._wrong_audience`, `..._a_token_missing_exp`.
3. `_assert_safe_external_url` and `_internal_url` are untouched — the migration only replaced the decode/validate call, not anything upstream of it in `verify_id_token` or `discover`/`exchange_code_for_tokens`. Confirmed by diff, not just by assumption.
4. Test coverage *increased*, not decreased: before this change, `verify_id_token`'s actual cryptographic logic had **zero direct tests** — every existing caller-side test (`test_oidc_provisioning.py`, the OIDC callback tests) stubs it out via `monkeypatch.setattr`. Seven new tests in `test_oidc_client.py` exercise it directly with a locally-generated RSA key and real `joserfc`-signed tokens: valid-token acceptance, wrong-signing-key rejection, expiry, wrong issuer, wrong audience, missing `exp`, and the HS256-confusion attack above. Additionally verified against a **real IdP**, not just synthetic tokens: `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/sso.spec.ts`'s 5 tests drive the actual authorization-code flow against the Keycloak container and passed unchanged.

**Remediate**: no gap found — the migration is a net hardening (explicit algorithm allowlist and required-claim presence checks that authlib's call site never had) with materially better test coverage than what it replaced, not just a like-for-like swap.

### A regression the react-router 7 migration exposed in two existing Playwright tests, and a pre-existing non-idempotent test found while verifying it

React Router 7 wraps navigation state updates in React's `startTransition` by default (an opt-in future flag in 6, now the default) — this can keep a just-left page's content painted for one extra frame alongside the new page settling in underneath it. `golden-path.spec.ts`'s final "raise and approve a change request" step hit exactly this: a page-wide `getByText("Boot in under 3 seconds")` transiently matched both the change-request detail view's own "Name: Boot in under 3 seconds" changed-field summary and the new requirements list's card link during the transition, a strict-mode violation Playwright doesn't retry past. Confirmed as an upgrade-induced timing change, not a pre-existing flake, by reproducing the failure against this branch and then re-running the identical test against the pre-upgrade tree (stashing every dependency/source change) where it passed cleanly. Fixed by scoping the assertion to `getByRole("link", { name: "Boot in under 3 seconds" })` — the specific element that's actually unambiguous — matching this same spec file's own established pattern for exactly this class of ambiguity elsewhere.

Separately, running `sso.spec.ts` repeatedly against the same live dev stack while verifying the `joserfc` migration (see above) surfaced a genuine pre-existing non-idempotency: its setup step unconditionally `POST`s a new `OrgGroup` named `reqtrack-org-admins` onto the shared "Default Organization" fixture, which 400s ("idp sync target already in use") on any second run against a database that hasn't been reseeded from scratch — a real bug by this project's own testing-idempotency rule (must pass "whether it runs alone, first, last, or repeated back-to-back"), not something introduced by this branch, but found incidentally while working in this file and fixed per the project's standing "fix it, don't just note it" rule rather than left for someone else. There's no delete-group endpoint (`update_org_group`'s own docstring: "no rename endpoint exists for this... today"), so the fix looks up an existing group with that `idp_synced_group_name` first and `PATCH`es it back to the expected `granted_org_role` instead of always `POST`ing fresh — verified idempotent by running the same test four times back-to-back against the same unreset database.

Backend: full suite, **646 passed, 0 failed**, run with `SMTP_HOST=localhost` (same pre-existing host-vs-Docker-network mailhog-resolution quirk noted in earlier entries — 7 spurious failures on a first host-run attempt, confirmed unrelated and passing once corrected). Includes 5 new tests: `test_looks_like_email_matches_the_original_regexs_semantics`/`..._is_not_vulnerable_to_polynomial_redos` (`test_invites_and_external_users.py`), `test_parse_simple_eq_filter_handles_the_bracket_filter_shape`/`..._rejects_malformed_expressions`/`..._is_not_vulnerable_to_polynomial_redos` (`test_scim.py`), plus 7 new `verify_id_token` tests in `test_oidc_client.py` (see Security review above). `ruff check` clean on every touched file.

Frontend: `tsc -b` and `npm run build` clean (react-router 7 + vite 6.4.3 + the new `dompurify` dependency); `eslint .` clean (same 7 pre-existing unrelated `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings, confirmed pre-existing by reproducing against the pre-upgrade tree, no new ones); full Storybook suite, **67 files / 562 tests passed**, including `RichTextEditor.stories.tsx`'s interaction tests exercising the new `DOMPurify.sanitize()` call in a real Chromium instance (via `@vitest/browser-playwright`), not jsdom.

## UI/UX feedback batch, Phase 1 + Phase 4: mobile filter panel ordering, and Org Admin's "View access" panel collapsed by default

Two independent, small, frontend-only phases from a larger seven-item UI/UX feedback batch (the other phases — "Completed" as an overlay marker, resend a pending invite, and the project membership/groups redesign — are separate, larger pieces of work tracked and implemented independently). Both phases here touch only frontend code/docs — no backend, migration, or API change.

### Phase 1: `FilterPanel` renders first on mobile, not after the whole list

`FilterPanel` (`frontend/src/components/FilterPanel.tsx`) was always the second DOM child of the shared `.side-grid` wrapper used by seven pages (`RequirementsPage.tsx`, `ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`, `ProjectListPage.tsx`, `ProjectReviewsDuePage.tsx`, `NotificationsPage.tsx`, `ProjectActionsPage.tsx`, `ServerOrganisationsPage.tsx`). `.side-grid`'s existing `@media (max-width: 860px)` collapse (`theme.css`) only reduced the grid to one column — it never reordered — so on a phone-width viewport a user had to scroll past the entire list/table to reach the filters.

Fixed with a stable `filter-panel` class added to `FilterPanel`'s root `<div>`, plus one new rule inside the *same* existing mobile-only media query: `.side-grid > .filter-panel { order: -1; }`. This only changes visual/paint order on narrow viewports (CSS `order`, not a DOM move) — desktop's two-column layout, `FilterPanel`'s own header/collapsible-body split, and its `useNarrowViewport`/`CollapsibleSection` accordion behaviour are all untouched.

### Phase 4: Org Admin's "View access" panel — collapsed roles by default, expand per row on demand

**Reverses a decision recorded 2026-08-24/25** in `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: role display — effective highest role only" section, which explicitly carved this panel out as an access-audit exception that should "keep showing the full, uncollapsed role set." The user's new request reverses that — flagged back to the user during planning and resolved via an explicit choice (AskUserQuestion in the planning conversation): default to the same collapsed summary compact lists already use, with the full set available per project row on demand, so the audit detail isn't lost, just not the default view.

Implemented in `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s `viewingUser` `SidePanel`: each project row now computes `collapseProjectRoles(p.roles)` (existing helper, `frontend/src/api/types.ts`) and shows that by default; a small "Show all N roles"/"Show fewer" `<button>` per row (local `expandedAccessProjectIds: Set<string>` state, reset whenever a different user's access is opened) toggles between the collapsed and full role list. Deliberately **not** built on `CollapsibleSection` — that component's collapse state is a per-user, cross-device *persisted* preference (`ui_preferences`), which is the wrong shape for a per-row, per-viewed-user, session-local disclosure that would otherwise leak state between different users' access panels or bloat the preferences bag with one key per project ever viewed.

`collapseProjectRoles()`'s own doc comment (`frontend/src/api/types.ts`) is updated to drop the now-stale "NOT applied to any access-audit view" carve-out and describe the new default-collapsed-with-expand behaviour. `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: role display" section is updated in place (not replaced) to record the reversal and its date/reasoning, matching how earlier entries in that section already layer revisions rather than rewriting history.

A pre-existing Playwright assertion (`role-display-collapsing.spec.ts`'s last step, previously titled "Org Admin's 'View access' panel deliberately keeps showing every role uncollapsed") pinned the exact behaviour being reversed — updated to assert the new collapsed-default/expand-reveals-full-set behaviour instead. Verifying it also surfaced that the test's own fixture user ends up holding **4** effective roles, not the 3 a naive count of directly-granted group roles would suggest: `get_effective_project_roles`'s `_normalize` step (`backend/app/services/rbac.py`) implicitly adds `project_administrator`+`stakeholder`+`member` alongside a directly-granted `project_manager`, so "Show all N roles" reads N=4 there — the test comment now explains this rather than leaving a magic number.

### Tests

Frontend: `npx tsc -b` clean; `npm run lint` clean (7 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings remain, all in files untouched by this work — `SortableHeader.tsx`, `BrandingContext.tsx`, `FavouritesContext.tsx`, `ThemeContext.tsx` — confirmed unrelated, no new warnings introduced). Full Storybook suite, **67 files / 563 tests passed**, including two new `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx` stories: `ViewUserAccessPanel` (updated to also pin the collapsed default) and `ViewUserAccessPanelExpandRoles` (new — exercises expand then collapse-back).

Playwright, against the dev/test Docker Compose stack (frontend rebuilt + force-recreated first, since it doesn't bind-mount source): `result-count-and-filter-panel.spec.ts` — 5/5, including two new tests ("FilterPanel renders first on narrow viewports, unaffected on desktop" for Requirements and Change Requests pages, asserting rendered bounding-box position, not DOM order), rerun standalone a second time to confirm idempotency. `role-display-collapsing.spec.ts` and `user-access-panel.spec.ts` — 3/3, the former rerun standalone a second time to confirm its unique-per-run fixture data doesn't collide with itself. A broader regression batch of 12 files/22 tests touching `.side-grid` pages, mobile viewports, and Org Admin (`mobile-nav-rail.spec.ts`, `mobile-card-grid-overflow.spec.ts`, `multi-org-admin.spec.ts`, `single-org-admin.spec.ts`, `org-admin-nav-link.spec.ts`, `badge-filters.spec.ts`, `dashboard-navigation.spec.ts`, `pelion-v2.spec.ts`, `login-branding.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, `golden-path.spec.ts`, `project-users.spec.ts`) — 22/22, confirming no regression from the shared `theme.css`/`OrgAdminPage.tsx` changes.

No backend changes, so the backend pytest suite wasn't re-run for this entry.

## UI/UX feedback batch, Phase 2: "Completed" becomes an overlay marker, not a lifecycle status (C-G-11)

Third of the same seven-item UI/UX feedback batch (Phase 1 + Phase 4 above; Phase 3 "resend a pending invite" and Phase 5 "project membership/groups redesign" are separate, larger pieces of work tracked and implemented independently). Unlike Phases 1/4, this one is a correctness fix against `docs/requirements.md`, not a UI-opinion change: C-G-11 says plainly that "independently of lifecycle state, a requirement may be marked completed... as an overlay marker subject to the potential of periodic review where it may later be reversed to non-compliant." The pre-existing implementation (Massif v3, "Completion tracking (C-P-02, C-P-03)" entry above) baked `COMPLETED` into the same `RequirementStatus` enum as `draft`/`reviewed`/`approved`/`archived`, reachable only from `approved` — the opposite of "independently of lifecycle state." That entry is marked superseded in place above, for the `Requirement` half only; `ProjectStage`'s own completion tracking (`completed_at`/`completed_by`, `cascade_to_requirements`) was always correctly modelled and is unaffected.

### Data model

`Requirement` gains `is_completed: bool`, `completed_at: datetime | None`, `completed_by: UUID | None` — mirroring the existing `is_archived`/`archived_at`/`archived_by` overlay already on the same table. `RequirementStatus.COMPLETED` is removed, leaving `DRAFT`/`REVIEWED`/`APPROVED`/`ARCHIVED`, matching C-G-11's own list exactly. `StageStatus.COMPLETED` is untouched — stage completion is a separate, legitimate terminal status (C-P-02) that was never the problem.

Migration `0018_completion_overlay_marker.py` adds the three columns and backfills them from whatever was true before: every `Requirement` whose current `RequirementVersion.status == 'completed'` gets `is_completed=true`/`completed_at`/`completed_by` copied from that version's own `created_at`/`created_by` (who/when it was actually marked completed, since completing used to bump the version), then *every* `requirement_versions` row referencing `'completed'` — current and historical alike — is rewritten to `'approved'`. No Postgres `ALTER TYPE`/enum-recreation step was needed, unlike the usual pattern for dropping a native-Postgres-enum value: `RequirementStatus` is stored via `models.base.str_enum` (`native_enum=False`), a plain `VARCHAR` with no Postgres `CREATE TYPE`/`CHECK` constraint backing it at all — removing `COMPLETED` from the Python enum is purely an application-level validation change, so the migration only had to touch data. (This is a deviation from what the original implementation plan anticipated — it expected to need the standard create-new-type/migrate-column/drop-old-type dance and asked to check for precedent; there was none, because this codebase doesn't use native enums for exactly this reason.)

### Behaviour changes

- `services/requirements.py`'s `LOCKED_STATUSES` becomes `{APPROVED}` only — a completed requirement's `status` stays `APPROVED`, so `is_locked()` keyed on status alone is unaffected.
- `complete_requirement`/`uncomplete_requirement` (`routers/requirements.py`) now set/clear the three overlay fields directly on the `Requirement` row instead of calling `apply_new_version` — completing doesn't change content, so (unlike the old implementation) neither endpoint bumps the version number any more. `complete_requirement` also now explicitly rejects double-completing (409), not just a non-`APPROVED` status.
- `update_requirement`'s old "reject `status=completed` in the payload" special case is deleted outright — now that `COMPLETED` isn't a valid `RequirementStatus` value at all, Pydantic/enum request validation rejects it on the way in (422, not the old handler's 400).
- `services/stages.py`'s `complete_stage` cascade sets `is_completed`/`completed_at`/`completed_by` directly on each targeting `Requirement` instead of looping `apply_new_version` — same "don't bump the version" reasoning, still gated on current `status == APPROVED` and the existing `cascade_to_requirements` flag (and now also skips requirements already completed, to avoid clobbering an existing `completed_at`/`completed_by` on re-run).
- `record_review_outcome`: a `FAILED` outcome recorded against a currently-completed requirement now clears the completion overlay as part of recording that outcome — this is the concrete mechanism C-G-11's "may later be reversed to non-compliant... when a review/audit occurs" describes. Logged as a distinct audit event (`completion_cleared_by_review`) from `review_recorded`, not folded into its detail, so the reversal's own cause is independently traceable in the activity feed.
- `services/changes.py`'s `VERSION_HISTORY_COVERED_ACTIONS` (the dedup list that suppresses a generic `AuditEvent` in the project activity feed when a version-history entry already covers the same transition) had `completed`/`uncompleted` removed — they used to belong there because completing/uncompleting used to bump the version; now that neither does, their `AuditEvent` is the *only* record of the transition, and leaving them in that set would have silently dropped both actions from the activity feed entirely. Caught by `test_reporting_and_changes.py`'s existing duplicate-entry regression test failing during verification, not anticipated by the original plan — see "Deviations" below.

### Change-request decision: explicit "Approve and clear completion" choice

The specific design point flagged in the implementation plan and confirmed with the user before building it: a plain "Approve" on a `MODIFY_REQUIREMENT` change request must keep leaving `is_completed` exactly as it was (the existing, already-fixed carry-forward behaviour — `decide_change_request`'s `status_value=None` on the version-apply call was never responsible for the completion overlay either way, since that's a separate field entirely; its own comment is updated to say so rather than reference the now-removed `COMPLETED` status value). What was missing is a way for the approving project manager to say "this particular change is substantial enough that completion needs re-verifying" — added as an explicit, opt-in field rather than an automatic side effect of any edit:

- `ChangeRequestDecision` (`schemas/change_request.py`) gains `clear_completion: bool = False` — meaningful only when `approve=True`, `cr.kind == MODIFY_REQUIREMENT`, and the target requirement currently has `is_completed=True`; a no-op (not an error) otherwise, e.g. on a `NEW_REQUIREMENT`-kind CR or a target that isn't completed.
- `decide_change_request` applies it as a separate step *after* the existing version-apply logic (which is completely unchanged), clearing `is_completed`/`completed_at`/`completed_by` and logging a distinct `completion_cleared_via_change_request` audit event — so it's clear in the activity feed that the approver made that call deliberately, not that it happened as a side effect of approving the CR.
- Frontend (`ChangeRequestDetailPage.tsx`): when the target requirement is completed and the CR is `modify_requirement`-kind, a second "Approve and clear completion" button appears alongside the existing single "Approve" (unchanged everywhere else) — a typo-level CR gets plain Approve, a substantive one gets the second button, which drops the requirement back onto the due-for-review path.

### Frontend

`api/types.ts`: `RequirementStatus` drops `"completed"`; `Requirement` gains `is_completed`/`completed_at`/`completed_by`. `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s `STATUS_OPTIONS` drops `"completed"`; a new, independent `FilterCheckbox` ("Completed") sends `is_completed=true` to the list endpoint's new query param (`GET .../requirements` gained `is_completed: bool | None`, same filter-param pattern as the rest of that endpoint). Status badges (`RequirementsPage.tsx` tile/list views, `RequirementDetailPage.tsx`) keep showing lifecycle status unchanged, plus a separate small "Completed" badge shown alongside when `is_completed` is true — visually distinct, not merged into the status badge, since a completed requirement's status badge now always reads "Approved". `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`'s "% complete" dashboard tile links to the requirements list's new `?completed=1` deep link instead of the old `?status=completed`. `ReportsPage.tsx`'s status filter drops its "Completed" `<option>` (the U-P-05 percentage-complete metric already covers this on the dashboard; reports don't gain a parallel `is_completed` filter in this pass). `backend/app/services/labels.py`'s `REQUIREMENT_STATUS_LABEL` (the PDF/CSV report label map, kept in sync by hand with the frontend's own map per that module's docstring) drops its now-dead `"completed"` entry too.

Dashboard/metrics: `routers/projects.py`'s U-P-05 percentage-complete metric (both the project-wide figure and the per-stage baseline breakdown) now queries `Requirement.is_completed.is_(True)` directly instead of `RequirementVersion.status == RequirementStatus.COMPLETED`.

### Deviations from the plan / judgment calls

- **No Postgres enum-type recreation** (covered above) — the plan anticipated needing it and asked to check for precedent; there was none, because `str_enum`'s `native_enum=False` means there's no Postgres enum type to alter in the first place. Simpler migration than planned.
- **`services/changes.py`'s `VERSION_HISTORY_COVERED_ACTIONS` fix** — not called out in the plan at all, found only because `test_reporting_and_changes.py::test_project_changes_has_no_duplicate_entries_for_version_bumping_actions` failed during the verification pass. Fixed immediately rather than deferred, per this repo's "fix, don't defer, found issues" rule; the test itself was updated to assert the new (correct) action-count breakdown rather than the old one.
- **Bundle export/import (`project_export.py`/`org_export.py`) is not backward-compatible with a bundle exported before this migration** — a bundle whose `requirement_versions[].status == "completed"` (from an older export) will fail import with a `ValueError` from `RequirementStatus("completed")`, rather than being silently coerced to `approved`+`is_completed=true`. No back-compat shim was added: this codebase's own stated pre-release posture (`0001_initial.py`'s docstring — "reasonable pre-release (no real deployments yet to preserve an incremental path for)") and the absence of any precedent for handling a stale enum value in either export module made a shim feel like unrequested scope; flagging it here explicitly rather than silently deciding it doesn't matter.
- **`requirement_csv.py` needed no changes** — despite being called out in the plan as a file to check, its `status` column already round-trips generically via `version.status.value` (which will simply never emit `"completed"` again), and it doesn't export `is_archived` either, so not exporting `is_completed` as a column keeps it consistent with the existing overlay-field precedent rather than a gap.
- **`seed_e2e_dataset.py` needed no changes** — confirmed by direct search that it has no `COMPLETED`/completion references of any kind (the Playwright suite's completed-requirement fixtures are all created dynamically within the specs that need them, per this repo's idempotent-test convention, rather than relying on seeded state).
- **`stage-review-and-completion.spec.ts` had a pre-existing non-idempotency bug, unrelated to this phase's own changes, found and fixed during verification.** The rewritten completion assertions (status stays "Approved", separate "Completed" badge) were a same-file, in-place edit at first — running the suite twice in a row (this repo's own standalone/repeat-safe convention) surfaced that the *original* test already couldn't be rerun against the same database without a reseed: it drove Alpha-2's single seeded stage through its entire one-way scoping→review→approved→completed lifecycle (no "reopen" endpoint exists), so a second run couldn't find "Start review" any more. Not a regression introduced by this phase, but found while working on this exact file, so fixed per this repo's "fix, don't defer" rule rather than left as a pre-existing flake: the spec now creates its own dynamically-named stage and two dynamically-named requirements targeting it each run, scoping every subsequent UI interaction to that specific stage's row rather than assuming it's the project's only one. Verified by running it twice back-to-back with no reseed in between.

### Tests

Backend pytest, all in `backend/tests/`: `test_stage_review_and_completion.py` gained `test_complete_and_uncomplete_do_not_bump_the_version_number`, `test_double_complete_is_rejected`, `test_uncomplete_rejects_a_requirement_that_is_not_completed`, `test_cascade_completion_is_still_gated_on_approved_status`, `test_completing_stage_without_cascade_leaves_requirements_uncompleted`, `test_failed_review_outcome_clears_completion`, `test_met_review_outcome_does_not_clear_completion`, and its existing completion tests updated for the new field shape. `test_requirement_lifecycle.py` gained `test_list_requirements_filters_by_is_completed`, `test_decide_change_request_with_clear_completion_clears_the_overlay`, `test_clear_completion_is_a_no_op_on_a_non_completed_requirement`, `test_clear_completion_is_a_no_op_on_a_new_requirement_kind_change_request`, and its `COMPLETED`-carry-forward regression test renamed/updated to `test_decide_change_request_plain_approve_preserves_completed_overlay`. `test_coverage_gaps.py` gained `test_project_metrics_completed_percent_reflects_is_completed_flag`. `test_project_export_import.py`'s rich-project fixture now also completes a requirement, with a new assertion that `is_completed`/`completed_at`/`completed_by` round-trip through export/import. `test_permission_matrix.py::test_direct_edit_cannot_jump_straight_to_completed` updated to expect 422 (schema validation) instead of the old handler's 400. `test_reporting_and_changes.py`'s duplicate-activity-entry regression test updated per the deviation above.

## UI/UX feedback batch, Phase 3: resend a pending invite

Fourth of the same seven-item UI/UX feedback batch (Phases 1/2/4 above; Phase 5 "project membership/groups redesign" is a separate, larger piece of work tracked and implemented independently, by a different agent, immediately after this one). Addresses the concrete complaint that motivated it: an invited-by-email user's "prod server didn't send one" had no recovery path — `services/invites.py`'s `create_pending_invite` was (and remains) the only way to trigger the invite email, and calling it again from the existing by-email "add member" flow creates a second `PendingInvite` row with a second, separate token rather than fixing the first one — and no endpoint listed a project's outstanding invites at all, so there was nothing to even confirm was stuck.

### Scope decision

Built for the standard (non-SSO) `PendingInvite` flow only, per the plan's own explicit scope cut: an `sso_only` organisation's by-email invites are provisioned immediately (`services.invites.provision_sso_invite`, no token, no `PendingInvite` row, access already granted) — there is nothing to "resend" there in the same sense, and the user's actual complaint (a stuck signup-link email) doesn't apply to that path. A parallel "resend the welcome email" for `sso_only`-org targets was deliberately not built this pass.

### Backend

- `GET /projects/{project_id}/pending-invites` (`routers/projects.py::list_pending_project_invites`) — lists a project's unaccepted `PendingInvite` rows (`project_id` matches, `accepted_at IS NULL`), newest first, including already-expired ones (an expired invite is exactly the case resending exists to fix, so it stays listed rather than disappearing). `status` (`"pending" | "expired"`) is computed at read time from `expires_at` vs. now, not stored. Gated by `require_project_manage` — the same dependency `assign_project_role_by_email` (the only endpoint that creates these rows) already uses, on the reasoning that listing/resending is a continuation of that same capability, not a new one.
- `POST /projects/{project_id}/pending-invites/{invite_id}/resend` (`resend_pending_project_invite`) — rotates the invite's token and `expires_at` and re-sends the signup-link email via `services.invites.resend_pending_invite` (new). A fresh token is issued rather than re-sending the stale one: the original may already have been exposed (logged, forwarded, sitting in an inbox nobody checks), so rotation is the safer default. Works whether the invite is currently pending or already expired; only an already-*accepted* invite is rejected (409), since there's nothing left to resend once someone's redeemed it. A cross-project `invite_id` (belonging to a different project than the one in the URL) 404s via a new `_get_pending_invite_in_project` helper, mirroring the existing `_get_group_in_project` guard against the same privilege-escalation shape (a manager of *some* project passing another project's id). Logs an `invite_resent` audit event (`services/audit.py::log_event`) with the invite's email in `detail`, following this codebase's existing per-mutating-endpoint audit-logging convention.
- `services/invites.py`: `create_pending_invite`'s and the new `resend_pending_invite`'s signup-link email body/subject were duplicated between the two initially; factored into a shared private `_send_invite_email` helper both call, rather than leaving two copies of the same wording to drift.
- Schema: `PendingInviteOut` (`backend/app/schemas/project.py`, next to `AssignByEmailOut`) — `id`, `email`, `role: ProjectRole`, `status: Literal["pending", "expired"]`, `created_at`, `expires_at`.
- SOC2: consulted `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md` before implementing, per this repo's CLAUDE.md requirement for anything touching invite/provisioning. Its Known Gaps item 4 (unverified-email-at-invite-time) already covers the original send; resending doesn't widen it — same caller-typed address, same single already-targeted grant, no new address reachable — so a short note was added to that item recording the review rather than opening a new gap entry.

### Frontend

New, deliberately self-contained component `frontend/src/components/PendingInvitesSection.tsx` — its own state and fetch (`GET .../pending-invites` on mount), a table (email/role/sent date/status/Resend button per row), toast feedback on resend success/failure (Principle 7, "every mutation ends with feedback"), and the label-map convention for the `pending`/`expired` status (`PENDING_INVITE_STATUS_LABEL`, `frontend/src/api/types.ts`) rather than the raw enum string. Deliberately built as a standalone component rather than inline JSX inside `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` — it's rendered from that page's "Project groups" tab (inside a `CollapsibleSection`, collapsed by default, alongside the existing "Effective members" section, both being member-directory concerns distinct from the groups list below) purely because that's where the equivalent Phase 5 "Members" page doesn't exist yet; per the plan's explicit sequencing note, the next agent (Phase 5, membership/groups redesign) is expected to fold this into a new Members page it creates, and moving a self-contained component's one usage + import is a much smaller diff for that agent than untangling inline JSX would have been. No cancel/revoke action — not asked for, not added speculatively.

No new endpoints were added under `/orgs` or any org-scoped path — this is purely a project-scoped addition, matching where the by-email invite flow that creates these rows already lives.

### Tests

Backend pytest (`backend/tests/test_invites_and_external_users.py`, extended in place — same file the rest of the by-email/invite flow is already tested in): `test_list_pending_invites_computes_pending_and_expired_status`, `test_list_pending_invites_excludes_already_accepted`, `test_resend_pending_invite_rotates_token_and_resends_email` (old token rejected at signup, new token redeems — same redemption pattern the existing invite-flow test already uses; `send_email` mocked/captured via `patch.object(invites_module, "send_email", ...)`, the same style `test_org_rename_and_test_email.py` already uses for the other email-sending endpoints), `test_resend_pending_invite_works_on_an_already_expired_invite`, `test_resend_pending_invite_rejects_an_already_accepted_invite` (409), `test_resend_pending_invite_404s_for_an_invite_belonging_to_a_different_project` (cross-project guard), `test_pending_invites_endpoints_are_gated_at_project_manage_tier` (403 for a plain project member on both new endpoints).

Playwright (`tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/external-project-invite.spec.ts`): the existing signup-completion test's org/project setup was factored into a shared `setupInviteOrgAndProject` helper (each test needs its own isolated org/project so dynamically-named invites can't collide) and its MailHog-link extraction into `extractInviteLinksFromMailHog`, without changing its own assertions. A new second test sends an invite, confirms it's listed with "Pending" status (`ensureExpanded(page, "Pending invites")` + `getByRole("row", ...)`), clicks Resend, confirms the toast feedback and that a second, different signup link actually lands in MailHog (order-independent — asserts the link set contains something other than the original, rather than indexing into MailHog's own unspecified message ordering, which an earlier draft of this assertion got backwards and had to fix). Both tests run/pass standalone and rerun back-to-back with no reseed in between (idempotency).

Storybook (`frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`): `mockProjectAdminApis` gained a `pendingInvites` override and a `/pending-invites` branch in its `api.get` mock; three new stories — `GroupsTabPendingInvitesEmpty`, `GroupsTabPendingInvitesShowsPendingAndExpired` (both status labels, not raw enum strings), `GroupsTabPendingInvitesResend` (asserts the exact `api.post` call and the resulting toast).

Frontend: `npx tsc -b` clean; `npm run lint` clean (same 7 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings as the Phase 1/2/4 entries, all in files untouched by this work — confirmed, not just assumed). `npm run test-storybook` (full suite) — **67 files / 569 tests passed, 0 failed**, including the three new stories above.

Playwright, against the dev/test Docker Compose stack (backend + frontend rebuilt and force-recreated first): `external-project-invite.spec.ts` — **2/2 passed**, run twice back-to-back with no reseed in between to confirm idempotency; `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts` (regression check on `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s Groups tab, which this phase's new section shares a tab with) — **1/1 passed**.

Rebuilding+recreating the backend container for this verification pass surfaced, again, the shared-test-DB wedge this repo's memory notes already describe (`backend`'s `DATABASE_URL` in `tests/container/docker-compose.yml` points at the same `reqtrack_test` database `pytest` truncates between/after every test) — running the full backend pytest suite wiped the demo/e2e seed data the just-rebuilt frontend/backend needed for the Playwright run, including the bootstrap server-admin account, which required restarting the backend container (to re-run bootstrap) and re-running both `seed_demo_data.py` and `seed_e2e_dataset.py` before Playwright could log in at all. Not a bug introduced by this phase — a pre-existing environment characteristic — but recorded here since it's exactly the sequencing this repo's own testing conventions call for after touching both suites in one verification pass.

## UI/UX feedback batch, Phase 5: project membership/groups redesign

Fifth and last of the same seven-item UI/UX feedback batch (Phases 1/2/4 in this log's earlier entries, Phase 3 immediately above). Addresses the three remaining items together, since all three converge on the same shared component: **project groups' role was fixed at creation** (no way to add members first and assign a role later); **Org Admin's per-project "Manage users" duplicated a worse, bespoke version of the project admin page's own membership UI**; and **Members and Groups were one combined "Project groups" tab**, making a mixed directory of two structurally different row shapes (individual users, project groups) harder to scan and impossible to deep-link into.

### Backend (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`, `backend/app/schemas/project.py`)

- **`PATCH /{project_id}/groups/{group_id}`** (`ProjectGroupUpdate{role: ProjectRole}`, modeled directly on `orgs.py::update_org_group`/`OrgGroupUpdate`) makes a `ProjectGroup`'s role editable after creation. No data migration needed — `services/rbac.py`'s effective-role resolution already reads `ProjectGroup.role` live at query time, confirmed by reading `get_effective_project_roles`/`get_effective_project_members_with_provenance` before assuming it, per the plan's own instruction. Gated `require_project_manage` (same tier `create_project_group`/`add_project_group_member` already use). Guard (C-U-08): moving a group's role *away from* `PROJECT_MANAGER` locks the project row (`lock_project_for_update`), tentatively sets the new role and flushes, then re-checks `get_effective_project_managers` is non-empty before commit — raising instead aborts via the request-scoped session's own close-without-commit (no explicit rollback needed), the same idiom `remove_project_group_member`/`revoke_project_role` already use. Because the check re-derives *actual* effective managers post-flush rather than pre-checking "was this specific group the target," it correctly allows the change whenever a backup manager source exists (a second group, or a direct grant) — pinned by `test_update_group_role_away_from_manager_allowed_with_backup_manager`.
- **`DELETE /{project_id}/groups/{group_id}`** (new — grep confirmed no such route existed). 400s for one of the four `is_default=True` standard groups (C-U-10) regardless of C-U-08 (checked first, since deleting a default group is never allowed at all, independent of whether it happens to also be the sole manager source). Otherwise, same lock-then-flush-then-recheck C-U-08 guard as the `PATCH` above, shaped for a whole-group removal: `ProjectGroupMember` rows cascade via the FK's existing `ondelete="CASCADE"`, so the check has to run *after* the delete is flushed (a pre-check the way `remove_project_group_member`'s single-membership check works would have to separately reproduce "what would managers look like without every membership this group grants," rather than just asking the ordinary live-state question afterward).
- **`GET /{project_id}/direct-members`** (`DirectMemberOut{user_id, display_name, email, roles: list[ProjectRole]}`, new) lists every user holding at least one direct `UserProjectRole` grant, one row per user with a real multi-valued `roles` array — confirmed by reading the model that `UserProjectRole`'s unique constraint is `(user_id, project_id, role)`, not one row per user, so a user can hold e.g. both `stakeholder` and `member` as simultaneous direct grants; force-collapsing to one role per row would have been a real regression against that. Gated `require_project_view_or_manage` (same tier `list_project_groups` uses — this exposes role *structure*, not requirement/change-request content, so any genuine project member can see it, not just managers). `GET /{project_id}/effective-members` was deliberately left untouched — confirmed it answers a different question (resolved-per-user-with-provenance for audit) from this new direct-grants listing, and continues to power the pre-existing "Effective members" table unchanged.
- **SOC2 review (identify → verify → remediate, per `docs/soc2/policies/change-management-and-secure-development-policy.md`'s practice for security-sensitive changes, since this is RBAC-adjacent — consulted `access-control-policy.md` first):**
  - *Identify:* the two new mutating endpoints could in principle let a lower-privileged caller reach `PROJECT_MANAGER` for themselves by repurposing an *existing* group's role rather than creating a new one.
  - *Verify:* `create_project_group` + `add_project_group_member` were already gated at `require_project_manage` before this phase — a `project_administrator` (below manager tier but still passing that gate) could already create a brand-new group with `role=project_manager` and add themselves to it. `PATCH .../groups/{group_id}` at the same gate tier adds an *alternate path to a capability that already existed*, not a new privilege boundary crossing — consistent with the plan's explicit choice to gate it identically. Cross-project IDOR: both new mutating endpoints route through the existing `_get_group_in_project` helper (404 unless the group belongs to the `project_id` in the URL), the same guard `add_project_group_member`/`remove_project_group_member` already rely on. `GET /direct-members`'s gate tier matches `list_project_groups` exactly, so no new disclosure beyond what that endpoint (and the by-role/by-email grant endpoints, which already imply the same information) already exposes.
  - *Remediate:* no gap found requiring a code change beyond what was already built; nothing added to `access-control-policy.md`'s Known Gaps, since this phase closes a product/UX gap (group role immutability) without opening or widening a documented security exception.

### Frontend

- **New shared component, `frontend/src/components/MemberRoleTable.tsx`** — the "add a user or group, then assign a role" table, built from existing primitives only (`SortableHeader`/`cycleSort`, `MultiSelectDropdown`, `LoadMoreButton`, `react-router-dom`'s `Link`). Rows are a `kind: "user" | "group"` discriminated union (`MemberRoleRow`); a `Type` badge column plus `SortableHeader`-sortable Name/Email columns match the existing "Effective members" table shape and Org Admin's Users table, per the style guide's already-recorded "project-scoped member lists match Org Admin's Users table" pattern. The Role cell deliberately differs by row kind — a user row gets `MultiSelectDropdown` (`UserProjectRole` is genuinely multi-valued, the same treatment `OrgRole` already gets on `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s Users table); a group row gets a plain `<select className="input">` (`ProjectGroup.role` is one column, genuinely single-valued) — this is intentional, not an inconsistency the component should "fix." Both wire a client-side "last manager" disabled+`title` hint (computed from how many rows in the table currently grant `project_manager` at all), mirroring `MultiSelectDropdown`'s existing self-role-revoke treatment on `OrgAdminPage.tsx` — an approximation only (it can't see e.g. a forward-inherited manager from a parent project), with the backend guard above remaining authoritative regardless. `search` plus a client-side "load more" window (not a fresh network request per page) since both call sites merge two already-fully-loaded, unpaginated fetches (`GET .../groups` with no `limit`, `GET .../direct-members`) rather than paginating server-side — the same "small enough to load whole, search/paginate client-side" precedent `GET .../effective-members` already established, extended here to a second, newly-added source. `addControl` is a caller-supplied `ReactNode` slot (composing `UserAutocomplete` + a role `<select>`), since what can be added differs slightly per call site. Final prop shape: `{ rows: MemberRoleRow[]; onToggleUserRole(userId, role, checked); onChangeGroupRole(groupId, role); groupHref?(groupId): string; addControl?: ReactNode; ariaLabel: string }`.
  - **Deviation from the plan's literal wording:** the plan described the group-row navigation prop as `onGroupClick`; built instead as `groupHref?: (groupId: string) => string`, rendering a real `<Link>` rather than a button+`onClick` — matching this codebase's own stated "a real URL, not client-only state" bookmarkability principle (`ResourceMenu`'s own framing, which the plan itself invokes for the `?openGroup=` deep link one paragraph later) more directly than a callback would have. The `aria-label` originally planned for that link was dropped after a Storybook story caught it silently replacing the link's own visible name (the same "accessible-name-from-content" pitfall `SortableHeader.tsx`'s own code comment already documents) — replaced with a `title` tooltip instead, which doesn't have that effect.
- **`frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.tsx`:** `ProjectAdminGroupKey` gains `"members"`, inserted before `"groups"` in `projectAdminGroups` — no routing change needed. **Members** section: `MemberRoleTable` fed by `memberTableGroups` (new state, `GET .../groups` with no `limit`) merged with `directMembers` (new state, `GET .../direct-members`) into `MemberRoleRow[]`; an add-control (`UserAutocomplete` + role `<select>`) calling `POST .../roles` for an existing org member or reusing the existing `addExternalMember(email, role)` for the by-email/invite branch; `PendingInvitesSection` (Phase 3) and the pre-existing "Effective members" `CollapsibleSection` both relocated here unchanged, below the new table (a different question — resolved-with-provenance audit data — from the new table's direct-grants editing, so not merged into it). Role-toggle/role-change handlers (`toggleDirectMemberRole`, `changeGroupRole`) update `directMembers`/`memberTableGroups` (and, for `changeGroupRole`, also the Groups section's own `groups` state) locally on success rather than calling the page's giant `reload()` — the same fix the style guide's "Pattern: multi-select dropdown" section already recorded for `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s analogous `grantOrgRole`/`revokeOrgRole`, both to avoid an unnecessary full-page refetch and to avoid the exact stale-reload race that fix was written to close. **Groups** section: unchanged `GET .../groups` + `LoadMoreButton` + search + "+ New group" `Modal` (`ProjectGroupCreate` still requires a role at creation — deliberately *not* made optional even though `PATCH` now makes it correctable afterward, matching the plan's explicit scope boundary). Each group row is now a plain button opening a `SidePanel` (`openGroupId` state) instead of an always-expanded `CollapsibleSection` accordion, containing the pre-existing 3-way composition editor (direct users/nested org groups/nested source-project refs — same handlers, relocated unchanged) plus a `Group role` `<select>` at the top (`changeGroupRole`) and a `Delete group` button (disabled + explanatory `title` for a default group, otherwise opening a Tier-1 `ConfirmDialog` before `DELETE .../groups/{group_id}`). A `member_source_project_ids` reference now also renders a `Link` to that project's own new Members page plus a clarifying "this is live, not a fixed list" hint line, extending the pre-existing `viaProjectMembers` labelled-line treatment (which already correctly never let one of these be edited/removed member-by-member) rather than replacing it. **`?openGroup={groupId}` deep link:** a `useSearchParams()` effect, scoped to the Groups section being active, opens that group's `SidePanel` on load and clears the param via `setSearchParams(..., { replace: true })` so browser-back doesn't reopen it — resolved first against `memberTableGroups` (the Members section's unpaginated fetch) rather than the Groups section's own paginated `groups`, so a deep-linked group not on the currently-loaded page is still found. Incidental fix while in this code: the org-group-nesting `<select>` inside the group panel had no `aria-label` (unlike its sibling source-project-reference `<select>`, which already had one) — added, since leaving it out was both a real accessibility gap and made the new `SidePanel`'s two `<select>`s ambiguous to `getByRole` queries once a `Group role` select was added alongside it.
- **`frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx`:** the inline "Manage users" expand-in-place (`expandedProjectId`/`expandedProjectGroups`/`toggleExpandedProject`/`addExpandedProjectGroupMember`/`removeExpandedProjectGroupMember`) is deleted outright, replaced by a `Modal` (`size="lg"`) opened by the existing "Manage users" button, wrapping the same `MemberRoleTable` — fed by the same two endpoints (`manageUsersGroups`/`manageUsersDirectMembers` state, fetched fresh on open via `openManageUsers`), with its own add-control and its own local-state-update-on-success role handlers mirroring `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s. `groupHref` wires to that project's own `/projects/{id}/admin/groups?openGroup={groupId}` page — a small extra beyond the plan's literal ask, since it was a one-line reuse of a prop the component already needed for the other call site, and gives an org admin a genuine way to jump from "manage users" straight into a group's full composition editor rather than a dead end.

### Tests

Backend pytest (new file, `backend/tests/test_project_group_role_editing.py`): `test_update_group_role_reflected_live_with_no_membership_row_change`, `test_update_group_role_no_op_when_role_unchanged`, `test_update_group_role_away_from_manager_blocked_when_sole_manager`, `test_update_group_role_away_from_manager_allowed_with_backup_manager`, `test_delete_default_group_is_rejected`, `test_delete_custom_manager_group_blocked_when_sole_manager`, `test_delete_custom_manager_group_allowed_with_backup_manager`, `test_update_and_delete_group_gated_at_manage_tier` (403 below manage tier; success for an org admin holding no project role at all, per `can_manage_project_settings`'s existing carve-out), `test_direct_members_gated_at_view_or_manage_tier`, `test_direct_members_returns_multi_role_array_per_user`. `test_permission_matrix.py` was checked and does **not** track a route inventory to extend (it's a flat set of discrete behavioural tests, not an enumerated endpoint table) — the plan's own instruction to extend it was conditional ("if that file tracks a route inventory"), so this was a no-op by design, not an oversight.

Four real bugs were caught during this verification pass and fixed, not deferred:
1. A `getByRole("combobox")` in a Groups `SidePanel` story became ambiguous once the panel gained a second `<select>` (the new `Group role` one) — fixed by scoping to the specific input.
2. `EffectiveMembersSortByEmail`'s `getAllByRole("row")` picked up the new `MemberRoleTable`'s own rows once it started sharing a page with the Effective Members table — fixed by scoping to the Effective Members `CollapsibleSection`'s own card.
3. `MemberRoleTable`'s group-row `Link` originally carried an `aria-label` that silently replaced its visible name as the accessible name (see the component's own deviation note above) — a `Members Tab Shows Users And Groups` story assertion caught it (`getByRole("cell", { name: "Stakeholders" })` failed since the cell's computed name had become "View Stakeholders's members").
4. **A genuine app bug, found only once the full Storybook suite ran repeatedly:** `externalAddResult` (the by-email invite/add outcome message) was only rendered inside the new Members section — the Groups section's own per-group `SidePanel` invite-by-email flow (`addExternalMember`, unchanged, still reachable from there) sets the exact same state but had nowhere left to show it, since that rendering call site moved with the rest of the Members-section JSX during the split. Silent on the Groups tab: an admin inviting someone by email from a group's own panel got no on-screen confirmation their invite was sent at all (Principle 7 violation) — caught by three separate `external-project-invite.spec.ts`/`org-security-controls.spec.ts` Playwright failures (below), not by Storybook, since no existing story asserted on that specific banner from the Groups tab. Fixed by rendering `externalAddResult` a second time, inside the group `SidePanel`, next to its own `UserAutocomplete`.
5. **A genuine, reproducible test-timing bug**, not a real app defect: `GroupsTabAddMemberViaSidePanel` typed into the panel's `UserAutocomplete` (armed with `organizationId`, so a 250ms debounced search fetch) and ended without closing the panel, leaving that debounce timer's effect cleanup to run only whenever the Storybook/vitest test runner itself got around to tearing down that story's tree — which, empirically, did not always happen before the timer fired, producing an intermittent "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')" in the *unrelated, untouched* `UserAutocomplete.tsx`, caught by vitest as an "Unhandled Error" (not a failed assertion — all 587 tests passed even on the run(s) where this fired). Root-caused by noting it was 100% reproducible at the same point across multiple full-suite runs, and that no other story left an armed debounce timer un-torn-down at story end. Fixed by having the story explicitly close the panel (a real `SidePanel`/`onClose` unmount within this app's own lifecycle, not a hope that the test harness tears the tree down first) before ending — confirmed clean (zero unhandled errors) on two consecutive full-suite runs afterward.

Playwright, against the dev/test Docker Compose stack (backend + frontend rebuilt and force-recreated first; `seed_demo_data.py`/`seed_e2e_dataset.py` both ran clean with no errors, confirming they're still in sync with the current schema/endpoints per this repo's testing conventions — no changes needed to either): every spec this phase touched or added, run together — **19/19 passed** (`project-admin-members.spec.ts` (new, 1), `org-admin-manage-users-modal.spec.ts` (new, 1), `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts` (1), `project-users.spec.ts` (1), `project-hierarchy.spec.ts` (5), `org-security-controls.spec.ts` (1), `role-display-collapsing.spec.ts` (1), `external-project-invite.spec.ts` (2)), plus a broader same-run regression sweep of specs exercising `OrgAdminPage`/`ProjectAdminPage`/shared components this phase didn't directly touch — **6/6 passed** (`golden-path.spec.ts`, `org-group-nesting.spec.ts`, `single-org-admin.spec.ts`, `multi-org-admin.spec.ts`, `mockup-engagement.spec.ts`, `pelion-v2.spec.ts`). Two genuine bugs in this phase's own new spec files were found and fixed during this run: `project-admin-members.spec.ts` and `org-admin-manage-users-modal.spec.ts` each asserted `getByRole("cell", { name: PERSONAS.<x>.name })` without `exact: true` — Playwright's role-name matching defaults to substring (unlike Testing Library's default-exact, which is why the equivalent Storybook assertions never hit this), so the assertion also matched that same row's Role-cell `MultiSelectDropdown` trigger button, whose own accessible name ("`<name>`'s roles") contains the plain name as a substring; fixed by adding `exact: true` to both.
