## Follow-up UX batch, Phase A: org-level invites, and telling "new user" apart from "invite" in the UI

First of a follow-up five-phase batch (Phase 0 — the shared `DirectoryTable` component — landed first and separately; Phases B/C/D/E are separate, larger pieces of work tracked and implemented independently, by other agents). Prompted by two pieces of direct user feedback on the previous batch: (1) Org Admin's "New user" sets a password immediately, which read as surprising — "I expected a single-use code"; (2) a freshly-created user shows "Active" immediately, with no visible "invited/pending" state anywhere at the org level. Investigation confirmed both are real, distinct gaps rather than one: `create_org_user` (I-M-05: "users must have email, a display name and a password") and the token-link invite flow (`services/invites.py`, built in the prior batch's Phase 3) are two genuinely separate, both-legitimate provisioning paths — but the invite flow was, before this phase, only reachable from *inside a project* (a project's by-email "add member" flow); there was no org-level entry point into it at all, even though `services.invites.create_pending_invite` already supported an org-only invite (`project=None`). `is_active` correctly means "not deactivated," not "has completed onboarding" — but with no invited/pending state visible anywhere at the org level, an invited-but-unregistered person was simply invisible in Org Admin.

### Backend

Mirrors the project-level pending-invite pattern (Phase 3 above) almost exactly, scoped to `project_id IS NULL` rows:

- `GET /orgs/{organization_id}/pending-invites` (`routers/orgs.py::list_org_pending_invites`) — lists an organisation's unaccepted, **org-only** `PendingInvite` rows (`organization_id` matches, `project_id IS NULL`, `accepted_at IS NULL`), newest first, including already-expired ones. Project-scoped invites (created via a project's by-email flow) are never double-listed here — they stay owned by `list_pending_project_invites`. Gated by `require_org_admin_or_server_admin`, the same dependency `create_org_user` uses (the only other endpoint that creates these rows).
- `POST /orgs/{organization_id}/pending-invites` (`create_org_pending_invite`) — the actual new capability: a thin wrapper over `services.invites.create_pending_invite(db, email=..., organization=org, project=None, project_role=None, invited_by=current_user.id)`. Rejects with 400 for an `sso_only` organisation, mirroring `create_org_user`'s existing guard, and deliberately *not* falling back to `provision_sso_invite` the way `assign_project_role_by_email`'s sso_only branch does — that branch has a concrete project/role to provision ahead of a real SSO login; a bare org-only "invite" has no such target, and introducing a second, immediate-provision response shape just for this case was judged not worth the complexity for what's already reachable another way (configure the person's IdP group/role claim to match on their first real SSO login). Also 409s if an account with that email already exists anywhere (same check `create_org_user` makes), since an invite to an existing account would never be consumed (`consume_pending_invites` only ever fires from native signup or first OIDC login, neither of which an existing account goes through again).
- `POST /orgs/{organization_id}/pending-invites/{invite_id}/resend` (`resend_org_pending_invite`) — same token-rotation-and-resend behaviour as the project-level endpoint, via the same `services.invites.resend_pending_invite`, which already accepted `project: Project | None` and needed no signature change. Cross-org-boundary guard (`_get_org_only_pending_invite`, mirroring `_get_pending_invite_in_project`) 404s an invite belonging to a different organisation or a project-scoped invite passed against this org-level endpoint.
- Schema: `OrgPendingInviteOut` (`backend/app/schemas/org.py`) — `id`, `email`, `status: Literal["pending", "expired"]`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, and (new, not on the project-level `PendingInviteOut`) `invited_by_display_name`, since the Org Users table surfaces who sent each invite. `OrgPendingInviteCreate` — `email` only.
- `GET /orgs/{id}/users`'s `org_role` filter param (`backend/app/routers/orgs.py`) already existed and worked correctly server-side — confirmed by reading `list_org_users` directly (`if org_role is not None: results = [r for r in results if org_role in r.roles]`) and pinned with a new test (`test_list_org_users_filters_by_org_role`); it had simply never had a frontend control wired up to it. Not a bug to fix, just an unused capability to finally expose.
- SOC2: consulted `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md` before implementing, per this repo's CLAUDE.md requirement for anything touching invite/provisioning. Same reasoning as the Phase 3 entry above applies unchanged (org-only invite, same caller-typed address, same single grant, no new address reachable) — a short note was added to that entry's SOC2 review recording that this org-level addition was also reviewed and doesn't widen the existing unverified-email known gap.

### Frontend (`OrgAdminPage.tsx`)

- **"Invite user" button** next to "New user," opening its own small `Modal` (email only — no password/name fields, since the invitee sets those at signup). A hint line under both buttons spells out the difference (`newUserVsInviteHint`) directly answering the user's "I expected a single-use code" feedback.
- **Users table rebuilt on the shared `DirectoryTable`** (Phase 0), replacing the old hand-rolled `<table>`+`SortableHeader` markup, wrapped in the standard `.side-grid` + `FilterPanel` layout every other list page in this app already uses (`RequirementsPage.tsx` etc.) instead of a bare table with inline controls. `GET /orgs/{id}/pending-invites` is fetched alongside `GET /orgs/{id}/users` and merged client-side into one row list, `kind: "user" | "invited"` — the same discriminated-union pattern `MemberRoleTable`'s `kind: "user" | "group"` established. An invited row repurposes three column slots rather than adding new ones: **Name** shows "Invited by {name}" instead of a display name (none exists yet), **Last login** shows "Sent {date}" instead of a login date, and **Status** shows a Pending/Expired badge (`PENDING_INVITE_STATUS_LABEL`, never a raw string) plus a Resend button in place of the active/deactivated text. **Roles** and **2FA** go blank/em-dash (neither concept applies pre-signup), and **Actions** (View access/lock) is user-only. Invited rows aren't part of `users`' own server-side sort/pagination (they come from a separate, unpaginated fetch), so they're always rendered ahead of the sorted/paginated user rows rather than interleaved into that order — documented as a deliberate simplification, not an oversight.
- **Filters migrated into the shared `FilterPanel`**: the three existing ad-hoc toggle `<button>`s ("stale," "no 2FA," "no project access") were a single-select `"" | "stale" | "no2fa" | "noaccess"` state — mutually exclusive by construction, even though the three backend params (`stale_since_days`/`has_2fa`/`has_project_access`) were always independent. Migrated to three separate `FilterCheckbox`es (`userFilterStale`/`userFilterNo2fa`/`userFilterNoAccess`), each now genuinely independent — checking "stale" no longer silently clears "no 2FA." A new `FilterField` role filter (`<select>` over `OrgRole`, through `ORG_ROLE_LABEL`) wires up the previously-unused `org_role` param. A new "Show invited" `FilterCheckbox`, defaulting on, hides/shows the merged invited rows. The existing name/email search moved onto `FilterPanel`'s own `search`/`onSearchChange` header prop, replacing the separate `<input>` that used to sit above the table.
- **Clarity pass on "Active"**: wrapped in a `title` tooltip (`statusActiveHint`) spelling out "not deactivated, not necessarily logged in" — a one-line addition, not a schema change, directly answering the second piece of feedback.
- Label-text collision found and fixed while building the role filter: the New User modal's own "Role" field label and a bare "Role" `FilterField` label would both resolve to the same accessible name "Role" while the modal is open (it renders via a portal to `document.body`, so the underlying page's filter select stays mounted behind it) — an ambiguity that would only surface at test-authoring time, not runtime, but was still real. Fixed by using the already-defined-but-previously-unused `strings.orgAdmin.orgRole(orgCap)` ("Organisation role") for the filter's label instead of reusing `strings.orgAdmin.role` ("Role").

### Tests

Backend pytest (new file, `backend/tests/test_org_pending_invites.py`, mirroring `test_invites_and_external_users.py`'s project-level coverage): token rotation on resend (old token rejected at signup, new one redeemable), resend on an already-expired invite, resend rejects an already-accepted invite (409), org-only invite creation rejected for an `sso_only` org (400) and for an already-existing email (409), `GET /pending-invites` never includes project-scoped invites (checked both directions — an org-only invite doesn't leak into the project-level list either), 403 gating on all three new endpoints below `require_org_admin_or_server_admin`, and `test_list_org_users_filters_by_org_role` pinning the previously-untested-but-working `org_role` filter.

Storybook (`frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`): `mockOrgAdminApis` gained an `orgInvites` override, a `/pending-invites` branch in its `api.get` mock (also added to the separate `mockProjectsWorkflowWithOneProject` mock used by the "Manage users" modal stories, which replaces rather than composes with the shared mock), and its `/users` `getPage` mock now honours an `org_role` query param so a story can exercise the new filter end to end. New stories: `InviteUserOpensModalAndCreates`, `InviteUserModalCancel`, `UsersSectionShowsInvitedRowWithResend`, `UsersSectionHideInvitedFilter`, `UsersSectionRoleFilterNarrowsResults`, `UsersSectionMigratedFilterCheckboxesWorkIndependently`. One pre-existing story (`UsersSectionAndCreateUser`, plus its `LightTheme`/`DarkTheme` aliases) broke on this change — its `canvas.getByText("Org admin")` assertion became ambiguous once the new role filter's own "Org admin" `<option>` existed on the same page — fixed by scoping the assertion to the roles-dropdown trigger button's own text content instead of a page-wide text search.

Playwright (new file, `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/org-level-invite.spec.ts`, three tests, each creating its own fresh organisation the same way `external-project-invite.spec.ts` does): invite-then-signup confirms org access without project access; invite-then-resend confirms a rotated, different link via MailHog (split into a separate test from signup, mirroring the project-level spec's own two-test shape, rather than chaining signup after resend in one test — redeeming an already-resent invite's *original* link 400s, and MailHog's own message ordering isn't a documented "newest-last" contract, so picking "the latest link" to redeem after a resend would have been non-deterministic); filtering by organisation role narrows results. Two pre-existing specs needed updates for the migrated filter checkboxes and the new invited-row merge: `org-security-controls.spec.ts`'s filter-button clicks became checkbox clicks (uncheck instead of a since-removed "Clear filters" button); `user-access-panel.spec.ts`'s column-sort test (`visibleEmails()`, which asserts every visible row's first cell forms a sorted sequence) now unchecks "Show invited" first, since an invited row merged in ahead of the sorted user rows isn't part of that sort and would otherwise corrupt the assertion the moment any org it runs against ever has a pending invite.

Seed scripts: not extended to demonstrate this feature, matching the precedent already set by the project-level invite flow (Phase 3 above), which was also never added to `seed_demo_data.py`/`seed_e2e_dataset.py` — an invite is inherently transient/no-account-yet, not the kind of steady-state fixture those scripts otherwise model.

## Follow-up UX batch, Phase B: Org Groups and Project Groups both rebuilt on `DirectoryTable`

Second phase of the same follow-up batch as Phase A above, independent of it (both build on Phase 0's shared `DirectoryTable`, neither depends on the other). Widened from the original "make Org Groups a table like Users" ask after Phase 0's own design-review pass found a second, adjacent gap: Project Admin's existing Groups tab (built in the prior batch's Phase 5) wasn't a real `<table>` either — a `<button style={{width:"100%"}}>` per row, no `SortableHeader`. Both "groups" directories moved onto `DirectoryTable` together in this phase rather than Org Groups alone.

### A real bug, found and fixed, not just a refactor

Reading `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s old accordion body carefully (rather than assuming the SSO-sync fields were already gated, as the original plan draft did) found that only the `granted_org_role` `<select>` was actually conditioned on `ssoConfig?.oidc_issuer_url && ssoConfig?.oidc_client_id` — the `idp_synced_group_name` text `<input>` and the "Save sync settings" button rendered **unconditionally**, regardless of whether SSO was configured for the org at all. An org admin could type a sync name and click Save with no SSO ever set up; the backend would accept and persist it (`update_org_group` has no SSO-configured precondition of its own — only `_require_granted_role_has_sync_target`, which is unaffected either way), leaving a dormant `idp_synced_group_name` waiting for SSO to eventually be configured. Not a privilege-escalation bug (the role-granting field was correctly gated the whole time, so no role could actually be granted via this path without SSO), but a real UI-gating inconsistency the user asked to have fixed, not merely refactored around. Fixed by gating the entire sync sub-section — checkbox, name input, role select, Save action — behind the same `ssoConfigured` check; with SSO unconfigured, only the existing muted hint renders, nothing else.

On top of the fix, added the requested explicit toggle: a "Sync membership and role from an SSO/IdP group" checkbox inside the now-fully-gated section, checked by default only when `idp_synced_group_name` is already non-null, showing/hiding the name+role fields together. Unchecking clears both immediately via the existing `PATCH /orgs/{id}/groups/{id}` (`{idp_synced_group_name: null, granted_org_role: null}`) — no backend schema change, since both fields already existed and were already validated together. The field's label was renamed from "IdP-synced group name" to "SSO group name," matching this org's existing "Required SSO group" (`oidcRequiredGroup`) terminology rather than the more technical "IdP" term this codebase's own SSO copy doesn't otherwise use. The Save action previously had no success feedback at all (only the inline error state on failure) — added a "Sync settings updated" toast, closing that Principle 7 gap in the same pass since it's the same code path the toggle's own auto-clear now also calls.

### Frontend — Org Groups (`OrgAdminPage.tsx`)

Replaced the `CollapsibleSection`-of-`CollapsibleSection`s accordion (which rendered every group's full member list open and inline, unconditionally) with `DirectoryTable` (Name sortable, Members count not sortable) inside the standard `.side-grid` + `FilterPanel` layout, matching Phase A's Users table composition exactly — search via `FilterPanel`'s own header prop, no additional filter fields exist for Groups so its body is empty besides the search box. Each row opens a `SidePanel` (style guide "Pattern: entity detail panel") containing, relocated unchanged in logic: the member-users editor (`UserAutocomplete` add + remove), the nested-org-groups editor (`<select>` + remove), and the now-fully-gated SSO-sync sub-section described above. The old accordion rendering is deleted entirely — this table + panel is now the only way org groups are shown.

### Frontend — Project Groups retrofit (`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`)

Replaced the `<button>`-row list with `DirectoryTable`: Name (sortable), Role (badge via `PROJECT_ROLE_LABEL`, not sortable), Members (count, not sortable). The Name column's render function still embeds the `is_default` "Default" badge alongside the name (unchanged from the old list) — Phase C is what removes `is_default` and this badge entirely, out of scope here.

**`onRowClick`, not `rowHref` — a real ambiguity found during verification, not assumed either way.** The original plan preferred `rowHref` (a real, deep-linkable `<Link>`) if it composed naturally with the existing `?openGroup=`/`useSearchParams` handling, since a `<Link>` is strictly more capable than a click handler. It does compose mechanically, but a first implementation with `rowHref` broke two existing Playwright specs: every standard project seeds a default group literally named **"Members"** (`DEFAULT_GROUPS`, `routers/projects.py`) — the exact same accessible name as this page's own `ResourceMenu` "Members" nav link. With `rowHref`, both render as `role="link"` elements sharing one accessible name on the same page, which is a genuine ambiguity (the same confusion a screen-reader user navigating by link text would hit, not just a test-selector artifact) rather than a Playwright-only concern. Reverted to `onRowClick` (a `role="button"` trigger, which can't collide with a nav `<Link>`) — the existing manual `openGroupId`/`useSearchParams` `useEffect` (unchanged since Phase 5) still owns the `?openGroup=` deep link either way; `onRowClick` just calls the same `setOpenGroupId` a URL-driven open already used. This is exactly the plan's own documented fallback ("otherwise keep the existing manual handling and just call it from `onRowClick`"), landed on after finding the concrete reason to take it rather than assuming `rowHref` up front.

Existing search/`LoadMoreButton`/"+ New group" `Modal` behaviour is unchanged, just re-hosted on `DirectoryTable` inside the same `.side-grid` + `FilterPanel` shell.

### Backend — a small, deliberate addition beyond the original plan

Neither `list_org_groups` nor `list_project_groups` had a `sort`/`order` param — both always returned name-ascending. The original plan didn't call for adding one (it only used the absence of a sort param to justify *not* sorting the Members column). Implementing Name-column sort as a client-side re-sort of only the currently-loaded page would have reproduced exactly the anti-pattern `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s own "Pattern: sortable column header" warns against: both lists already page via `limit`/`offset`, and "sorted by name, descending" has to mean sorted across every match, not just whatever page happened to be loaded first. Added a minimal `order: "asc" | "desc"` query param (default `asc`, unchanged behaviour) to both endpoints instead — a one-line `ORDER BY` direction flip each, no `sort` field param needed since Name is each list's only sortable column. `applyGroupSort` in both `OrgAdminPage.tsx`/`ProjectAdminPage.tsx` mirrors `applyUserSort`'s existing shape exactly: refetch with the new sort rather than re-sort in place.

`docs/ux-style-guide.md`: "Pattern: directories at scale" and "Pattern: sortable column header" both updated — the first no longer describes Org/Project Groups' always-expanded-accordion problem as current (both are `DirectoryTable`+`SidePanel` now); the second no longer carves Groups out as "no column headers to make sortable," and its own paragraph also had a stale mention of Org Users' pre-Phase-A state that hadn't been updated when Phase A shipped — fixed in the same pass since it was the same paragraph. Added a new "Pattern: directory table" section documenting `DirectoryTable` itself (Phase 0 built it, no phase had written it up yet) — what it deliberately excludes and why, and which directories share it as of this phase (three: Org Users, Org Groups, Project Groups — Project Members and Server Admin's Access Review are later phases of the same batch, not yet landed as of this entry).

`docs/solution-architecture.md` gained an "Implementation note (Org/Project Groups rebuilt on `DirectoryTable`, follow-up UX batch Phase B)" paragraph, right after the Phase A one.

SOC2: consulted `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md` before starting, since the SSO-sync fix touches SSO-driven role granting. Concluded no policy update was needed — the actual authorization/validation logic (`require_org_role(ORG_ADMIN)` on the endpoint, `_require_granted_role_has_sync_target`'s server-side check) is completely unchanged; the bug and its fix are both frontend-only visibility, not a backend control. The policy's existing item 2/2a already documents the `granted_org_role`/`idp_synced_group_name` mechanism at the level that matters (backend enforcement), unaffected by this phase.

### Tests

Backend pytest: `backend/tests/test_pagination.py`'s existing `test_org_groups_search_and_paginate`/`test_project_groups_search_and_paginate` extended with `order=asc`/`order=desc` assertions for the new param.

Storybook (`OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`): the Groups-section stories rewritten for the table+panel shape — `GroupsSectionOpensSidePanel` (new), `GroupsSectionSaveIdpSyncAndGrantedRole`, `GroupsSectionSyncToggleDefaultsCheckedWhenAlreadySynced` (new), `GroupsSectionToggleSyncOffClearsFields` (new), `GroupsSectionSsoSyncSectionHiddenWithoutSso` (renamed/widened from `GroupsSectionGrantedRoleHiddenWithoutSso` — now pins the *entire* sub-section absent, including the name input and Save button, not just the role select, per the regression this phase fixes), `GroupsSectionShowsMembers`, `GroupsSectionNestGroup`. `mockOrgAdminApis` gained a `groups` override so a story can exercise an already-synced group.

Storybook (`ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`): the existing Groups-tab stories (`GroupsTabOpensSidePanelWithRoleSelectAndDelete`, `GroupsTabAddMemberViaSidePanel`, `GroupsTabAddOrgGroupViaSidePanel`, `GroupsTabDeleteDefaultGroupDisabled`, `GroupsTabDeleteGroupRequiresConfirmation`) updated for the new `DirectoryTable` row shape (role/member-count column assertions added), row-trigger role unchanged (`button`, per the `onRowClick`-not-`rowHref` decision above) so most of these needed only a light touch.

Playwright: `org-group-nesting.spec.ts` rewritten for the new table+panel shape (`helpers.ts`'s old `openGroupCard`, built for the retired accordion, replaced by `openOrgGroupPanel`, mirroring the existing `openProjectGroupPanel`). New file `org-groups-sso-sync.spec.ts` — the regression-pin test the plan specifically asked for: gating absent-without-SSO (name field, role select, toggle, and Save button all genuinely absent, not just the role select), then the toggle's on/off round trip against a real SSO-configured org, verified both through the UI and by re-fetching the group via the API. Runs against a dedicated, freshly created throwaway org/admin (same pattern `org-rename-and-test-email.spec.ts` already uses) rather than a shared seeded persona, since it mutates `PUT /orgs/{id}/sso-config` — doing that against a persona shared with other specs in this suite's single-worker run would leak SSO state into specs that don't expect it. Two real issues found while first running this new spec, both fixed: (1) the org-scoped `PUT /sso-config` call needs the *newly created org admin's own* token, not the platform admin's — `require_org_role(ORG_ADMIN)` deliberately does not let a server admin bypass it (I-M-05); (2) the spec must close a `SidePanel` before reopening it in a later step, since its backdrop (`role="presentation"`) otherwise intercepts the next click on the underlying row. `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts` and `project-admin-members.spec.ts` (both already covering Project Groups' row-open flow) needed no shape changes since the row stayed a `<button>` — confirmed by running them, not assumed. `docs/e2e-workflows.md` not updated — like `org-rename-and-test-email.spec.ts`, the new spec uses a dedicated throwaway org rather than the fixed persona/project catalogue that doc indexes.

## Follow-up UX batch, Phase E: Server Admin's Access Review moved onto `DirectoryTable`/`FilterPanel`, matching Org Admin's Users table

Fifth phase of the same follow-up batch as Phases A/B/C/D above, independent of all of them (builds only on Phase 0's shared `DirectoryTable`). Server Admin's "Access Review" tab (`ServerManagementPage.tsx`'s `AccessReviewTab`) already had real filters (a `view` dropdown for orphaned/server-admins/all, an `includeDeactivated` checkbox) and backend-paginated `LoadMoreButton`, but — confirmed by reading both the frontend and `list_system_users` directly — no free-text search, no sortable columns (a plain static `<table>`/`<th>`, not `SortableHeader`-based like Org Admin's Users table), and its `view`/`includeDeactivated` filters were plain inline controls, not `FilterPanel`.

### Backend (`backend/app/routers/system.py`)

- **`search: str | None = None`** on `list_system_users` — name/email substring, case-insensitive, applied as the exact same Python-side `needle in x.display_name.lower() or needle in x.email.lower()` check `list_org_users` (`backend/app/routers/orgs.py`) already uses, reused verbatim rather than reinvented as a SQL `ilike`, per the plan's own instruction.
- **`sort`/`order` — a deliberate addition beyond the plan's literal text, following the same reasoning Phase B already established for `list_org_groups`/`list_project_groups`'s `order` param.** The plan's Phase E section named only `search` as a backend change, but also asked for "Email/Name/Last login/Created sortable" columns on a table that's backend-paginated (`limit`/`offset`, `LoadMoreButton`). Without a backend sort, a `DirectoryTable` "sortable" column can only mean a client-side sort of whatever page happens to be currently loaded — exactly the anti-pattern `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: sortable column header" warns against, and the same one Phase B's own entry above already declined to reproduce for Org/Project Groups. Added `sort: str | None` (`display_name|email|last_login_at|created_at`, `created_at` being the one addition beyond `list_org_users`'s own three sortable fields — Org Users has no "Created" column) and `order: "asc"|"desc"`, mirroring `list_org_users`'s contract exactly, including its null-handling for `last_login_at` (never-logged-in accounts always sort last, regardless of direction).
- `search` and `sort`/`order` both apply to the already-materialized `list(db.scalars(query).all())` before the `X-Total-Count` header is computed and before `limit`/`offset` slicing — same ordering as the existing filters, so total counts and pagination stay correct against the narrowed/sorted set.

### Frontend (`ServerManagementPage.tsx`)

`AccessReviewTab` wrapped in the same `.side-grid` + `FilterPanel` layout as Org Admin's Users table (the direct composition template): `view` became a `FilterField` `<select>` (identical options/labels), `includeDeactivated` became a `FilterCheckbox` (identical label, so existing `getByLabel("Include deactivated accounts")` call sites needed no change), and the new search box uses `FilterPanel`'s own `search`/`onSearchChange` header prop. The table itself moved onto `DirectoryTable`: Email/Name/Last login/Created sortable (backed by the new `sort`/`order` params), Organizations/Groups not sortable (comma-joined names, no natural order — style guide "Pattern: sortable column header"), Actions unchanged (deactivate/ban/grant-or-revoke-server-admin via the existing `ConfirmDialog`s). No `onRowClick`/`rowHref` — this directory has no per-row detail panel, so both props are simply omitted, per the plan.

**A real bug found and fixed during Storybook verification, not assumed away:** the old implementation's `reload()` called `setUsers(null)` before every refetch (filter change, search keystroke, sort click, or post-action reload), which — when the search/filter controls lived *outside* the `!users`-gated block — was harmless (a brief `<Spinner>` swap, nothing the user was actively interacting with disappeared). Migrating the search box *inside* the same `.side-grid`/`FilterPanel` this list renders changed that: nulling `users` on the first keystroke unmounted the whole `FilterPanel` (search input included) in favour of the `<Spinner>`, dropping focus and losing every keystroke after the first. The new `AccessReviewFilterPanelSearchAndFilters` Storybook story caught this directly — `userEvent.type`ing "orphan" into the search box only ever produced a `getPage` call for `search=o`, since the input vanished after the first character. Fixed by removing the `setUsers(null)` reset from `reload()` entirely (rows now simply stay as-is, stale, until the new page resolves) — the same behaviour Org Admin's own `loadUsers` already has (its `users` state is never nullable in the first place). `!users` is now only ever true on the very first, pre-any-fetch mount, exactly matching Org Admin's `Spinner`-then-populate shape.

### Tests

Backend pytest (`backend/tests/test_access_review.py`): `test_system_users_search_matches_name_or_email_case_insensitively` (name and email substring, case-insensitive, mirroring `test_pagination.py`'s existing `test_org_users_search_and_paginate`), `test_system_users_search_combines_with_view_and_active_filters` (search ANDs with, doesn't override, `no_org_membership`/`is_active` — the params `view`/`includeDeactivated` map to), `test_system_users_sort_by_email_and_created_at` (pins the new `sort`/`order` params, ascending and descending).

Storybook (`ServerManagementPage.stories.tsx`): `AccessReviewFilterPanelSearchAndFilters` (pins the migrated `view`/`includeDeactivated` controls keep their accessible names, and the new search box narrows the request via `search=`), `AccessReviewSortByEmail` (clicking the Email header cycles `sort=email&order=asc` → `sort=email&order=desc`). All pre-existing `AccessReview*` stories (`AccessReviewOrphanedAccounts`, `AccessReviewShowsGroups`, `AccessReviewBannedAndAdminBadges`, `AccessReviewGrantServerAdmin`, `AccessReviewDeactivateCancelled`, `AccessReviewLoadMoreAppendsTheNextPage`) needed no changes — the Actions column's buttons and their accessible names are unchanged, just re-hosted inside `DirectoryTable`.

Playwright (`tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/user-directory-and-bans.spec.ts`): three new `test.step`s added to the existing spec — search narrows the list by both a name and an email fragment (and an empty search restores the full list), the Email column cycles through `aria-sort` `none → ascending → descending → none` via its `SortableHeader` button, and the migrated "Show"/"Include deactivated" controls still narrow results identically to before. Inserted before the spec's existing deactivate/ban steps, ending back at the default "orphaned" view with an empty search so those unchanged steps still find the orphan persona's row.

### Docs

This entry; `docs/solution-architecture.md` gained an "Implementation note (Server Admin's Access Review moved onto `DirectoryTable`/`FilterPanel`, follow-up UX batch Phase E)" paragraph after the Phase B one.

Backend: full suite via the dev/test Docker Compose stack (`tests/container`, backend rebuilt + force-recreated first) — **687 passed, 0 failed**, 72 pre-existing warnings (same count as every earlier entry in this batch, none new).

Frontend: `npx tsc -b` clean; `npm run lint` clean (same 7 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings as every earlier entry, none new, none in files touched by this work). `npm run test-storybook` (full suite) — **608/608 passed**, including the 2 new `AccessReview*` stories (the search-race bug above was caught and fixed during this run, not after).

Playwright, against the dev/test Docker Compose stack (backend + frontend rebuilt and force-recreated first, `seed_demo_data.py`/`seed_e2e_dataset.py` re-run after the backend pytest run truncated the DB): `user-directory-and-bans.spec.ts` (the spec this phase extended) — passed, including the three new `test.step`s; `org-rename-and-test-email.spec.ts`, `org-label.spec.ts` (both found via grep to navigate through `/server/management`, Access Review's own route, before exercising other tabs) — all passed, confirming the page still mounts and hands off correctly with the rebuilt tab.

- **Added `sort`/`order` to `list_system_users`**, beyond what the plan's Phase E text specified (only `search`) — see "Backend" above. ## Follow-up UX batch, Phase C: default project groups removed; migrated to direct grants

Third phase of the same follow-up batch (Phases A/B/E above), and the highest-risk one — a real data migration affecting every existing project's manager-of-record, so this entry documents the identify→verify→remediate security review performed alongside the change itself, per the change-management policy's practice for RBAC-adjacent work.

**Why default groups existed, and why they're being removed now.** `create_project`'s non-template path (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`) used to auto-create four "standard" `ProjectGroup` rows on every project (`is_default=True` — "Project Managers"/"Project Administrators"/"Stakeholders"/"Members", `DEFAULT_GROUPS`) and grant the creator's initial `PROJECT_MANAGER` role by adding them to the manager-role one — the only way a fresh project ever got its first manager. Those four groups could never be deleted (`delete_project_group` special-cased `is_default`) and existed on every project whether wanted or not, even though a direct `UserProjectRole` grant was always available as a simpler, equally-supported mechanism for a single person, and Project Admin's own Groups tab already lets an admin create exactly this shape of group by hand when they actually want one. The user's ask that started this batch — "Members should just be effective members; the four default groups are redundant" — is what surfaces this cleanly: with pending invites now folding into the Members table (Phase D, dependent on this phase) and direct-grant-with-inline-role-picker already a first-class flow, the four auto-created groups add structural noise (and undeletable rows) without giving anything a direct grant doesn't.

### Backend — `create_project`'s non-template path (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`)

Stops creating `DEFAULT_GROUPS` entirely (the constant itself is deleted). The creator's initial `PROJECT_MANAGER` role is granted via the exact same fallback the template-clone branch already used when a cloned project ended up with no manager — rather than duplicate that logic, both branches now call a single new shared helper, `_ensure_project_has_a_manager(db, project, fallback_user_id)`: if `get_effective_project_managers` already finds one, it's a no-op; otherwise it prefers adding the fallback user to an existing manager-role `ProjectGroup` if one exists (only reachable via a template clone that copied a custom, user-created manager-role group — a from-scratch project has zero groups at this point, so this branch is structurally unreachable there), falling through to a direct `UserProjectRole` grant otherwise. The template-clone path itself is otherwise unaffected — it still clones whatever groups a template actually has, all non-default, user-created ones.

### Data migration (`backend/alembic/versions/0019_remove_default_project_groups.py`)

For every existing `is_default=True` `ProjectGroup`: every direct user member (`project_group_members.user_id IS NOT NULL`) is materialized into a direct `UserProjectRole(user_id, project_id, role)` grant, idempotently (`ON CONFLICT (user_id, project_id, role) DO NOTHING` against the existing unique constraint — a user who already independently held the same direct role ends up with exactly one row, not a duplicate). Then: if the group has *only* plain direct members (no nested org-group ref, no cross-project member-source ref), it's deleted outright (`project_group_members` rows cascade via the existing `ON DELETE CASCADE` FK); if it has composition beyond plain direct members — confirmed this happens for real, not just hypothetically: `seed_demo_data.py` attaches a `source_project_id` reference to the default "Stakeholders" group — it's *not* deleted, only demoted (`is_default = false`), so it survives as an ordinary, fully-manageable custom group with its nested composition intact. Written as a single `DO $$ ... $$` block (`alembic`'s established style in this repo for data-shape migrations, see 0012/0014's precedent), guarded by an `information_schema.columns` existence check the same way 0014/0017/0018 guard their own backfills — a brand-new database's `0001_initial.py` runs `Base.metadata.create_all()` against the *current* models, which no longer define `is_default` at all, so the whole backfill is a no-op there; only a database migrated from before this revision has real rows to convert. `ProjectGroup.is_default` is dropped from the column set at the end of the same migration.

C-U-08 ("every project must retain at least one manager") is preserved exactly by construction: every direct member of a manager-role default group ends up holding that same role directly before the group is ever touched, and a group is only ever deleted (never silently emptied) once every one of its direct members has already been carried forward; a group whose manager contribution comes from a nested org-group or cross-project reference is demoted, not deleted, so that contribution is completely unaffected. Pinned by `backend/tests/test_default_group_migration.py`, which runs the *real* migration (not a reimplementation of its logic) — downgrades the live test database to revision 0018, seeds pre-migration-shaped rows directly via raw SQL (project/user setup goes through the normal API; only the `is_default` group rows need raw SQL, since that column no longer exists on the ORM model to insert through at all), upgrades back to head, and asserts against the result via the ordinary API — covering both the plain-group (materialize-then-delete) and extra-composition (materialize-then-demote, manager coverage preserved) cases.

### Cleanup

- **`delete_project_group`**'s `is_default`-based delete rejection is removed entirely; its docstring (previously "the four standard groups... cannot be deleted") now describes the current, single guard — C-U-08, which already applied to every group regardless of `is_default` and needed no change of its own.
- **`is_default` dropped everywhere**, not just the DB column: `ProjectGroup` model, `ProjectGroupOut` schema (`ProjectGroupCreate`/`ProjectGroupUpdate` never had it), `project_export.py`'s bundle format (stops writing `"is_default"` into exported group JSON; import tolerates but ignores an old bundle's `"is_default"` key, same "retired field, silently ignored on import" treatment any other dropped field gets), and the frontend: `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s "Default" badge on the Groups tab's Name column and the disabled-delete-button-with-explanatory-title branch on the group `SidePanel`'s Delete button — both removed, confirmed non-trivial as the design review flagged (not already clean). `frontend/src/api/types.ts`'s `ProjectGroup` interface loses the field; every Storybook fixture/story literal constructing a `ProjectGroup` across `ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`/`OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx` updated to match. `MemberRoleTable.tsx`'s own `MemberRoleGroupRow.isDefault` field is untouched here (confirmed genuinely unused beyond being stored) — it disappears with that component's own retirement in Phase D, not this phase; the two call sites that used to populate it from `g.is_default` (`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`, `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s "Manage users" modal) now pass a literal `false`, since no group is ever default again.
- **`clone_project` gap, found in design review before this phase was finalized** (`backend/app/services/templates.py`): it previously only copied `ProjectGroup`/`ProjectGroupMember` rows from a template, never `UserProjectRole` rows — harmless while every grant went through a group, but a real, silent regression once direct grants become the *normal* mechanism (this phase): a template's directly-granted managers/admins/stakeholders/members would vanish on clone for everyone except whoever happened to be doing the cloning (covered by the C-U-08 fallback, but nobody else the template creator intended). Fixed: `clone_project` now also copies the source project's `UserProjectRole` rows verbatim. **A second, smaller gap found while making that fix, not in the original plan**: the existing `ProjectGroupMember` copy loop already only carried `user_id`/`org_group_id` across, silently dropping any `source_project_id` ("this group's members = that project's own direct members") reference a template group had — fixed in the same pass, copying all three member-target kinds now, per this repo's "fix issues found, don't defer" rule. `source_project_id` itself is copied verbatim (pointing at the original referenced project, never remapped to the new project even if it happens to reference the template being cloned) — a deliberate, load-bearing choice, not an oversight.
- **`backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`**: since projects no longer auto-create a "Stakeholders" group, the script now explicitly creates a plain (non-default) group of that name via a new `create_project_group` helper before attaching the `source_project_id` reference to it — same end demo state (Solstice Cloud Platform's "Stakeholders" group still resolves to Falcon-3's own direct members), just an explicit creation step. `get_project_group_id` (name-lookup-by-default-group helper) is deleted along with it.
- **Tests updated across the backend suite** (grepped for `is_default`/`DEFAULT_GROUPS`/"Project Managers" across `backend/tests/`, not assumed to be a short list): `test_rbac.py`, `test_project_group_role_editing.py` (rewritten most heavily — its `_default_manager_group` helper no longer has anything to find, replaced with `_make_group_the_sole_manager`, which grants a *second* person the role via a brand-new group then revokes the creator's own direct grant, since `revoke_project_role`'s own C-U-08 guard only allows removing a direct grant when the grantee isn't left as the *sole* effective manager — a fresh project's creator always starts as exactly that, so a real second manager source has to exist first), `test_project_hierarchy.py`, `test_audit_fixes.py`, `test_security_hardening.py`, `test_coverage_gaps.py`, `test_pagination.py`, `test_templates.py` — every one of these previously reached a project's post-creation groups list assuming at least a manager-role group would be there; each now either creates the group it needs explicitly or asserts against the creator's new direct grant instead.

### Tests

Migration test (`test_default_group_migration.py`, described above). Pytest: `test_project_creator_becomes_project_manager` (a freshly created project's creator has a direct `UserProjectRole(PROJECT_MANAGER)` row and zero `ProjectGroup` rows); `test_group_response_has_no_is_default_field_and_delete_never_special_cases_it` (`delete_project_group` no longer special-cases `is_default` — its only remaining guard is C-U-08 — and the field is genuinely gone from the response body, not just unused); `test_cloning_a_template_preserves_a_directly_granted_non_manager_role` and `test_cloning_a_template_with_zero_managers_still_produces_a_valid_manager` (the two review-found `clone_project` gaps — the latter reaches the zero-manager state via a direct DB delete of the template creator's `UserProjectRole` row, since `revoke_project_role`'s own C-U-08 guard makes that state genuinely unreachable through the live API once a project has exactly one manager, the same reason `test_project_group_role_editing.py`'s helper needed a second manager source above).

### Security review (identify → verify → remediate, per the change-management policy's practice for RBAC-adjacent changes)

Consulted `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md` and `change-management-and-secure-development-policy.md` before starting, since this touches authorization scaffolding directly (how a project's first manager grant is expressed, a data migration converting group membership into direct grants at scale, and a relaxed delete guard).

**Identified** five candidate risks, each independently verified against the actual code/behaviour rather than reasoned about in the abstract:

1. *Does the migration ever silently drop a manager?* No — verified by reading the migration's own logic and by `test_default_group_migration.py::test_plain_default_group_materializes_members_then_is_deleted` and `test_default_group_with_extra_composition_materializes_members_and_survives_demoted`, which run the *real* SQL (not a reimplementation) against seeded pre-migration-shaped data and assert the exact same people remain managers afterward, now via direct grants. Every direct member is materialized *before* a group is ever deleted; a group is only deleted once fully materialized, never while it still carries composition (nested/cross-project) the migration can't reproduce as a direct grant.
2. *Does removing `is_default`'s delete-rejection weaken any real protection?* No — verified that `is_default` was a purely structural "this specific group can never be deleted" rule with no relationship to actual access; the substantive protection (C-U-08, "a project must always retain at least one manager") is unconditional on `is_default` today and was already the *only* guard `delete_project_group` needed for the manager-role case specifically — removing the redundant structural check doesn't touch it, confirmed by the full existing `test_delete_custom_manager_group_blocked_when_sole_manager`/`test_delete_custom_manager_group_allowed_with_backup_manager` coverage passing unchanged.
3. *Does `clone_project` now copying `UserProjectRole` rows cross any tenant boundary?* No — `clone_project` only ever runs within `create_project`'s existing same-organization validation (the template and the new project share `organization_id` by construction), so copying direct grants moves access between two projects in the *same* organization, to users who already held that exact role on the template — no new person gains access, no cross-org exposure.
4. *Does the now-copied `source_project_id` on `ProjectGroupMember` (the second, smaller `clone_project` fix above) introduce any new cross-project reference risk?* No — `source_project_id` was already a same-organization-only, receiving-side-authorized mechanism before this fix (see `ProjectGroupMember`'s own docstring and the "generalized cross-project permissions" review this repo already performed on it); copying it verbatim during a clone doesn't create a new reference, it just stops silently dropping an existing one the template's manager had already explicitly set up and consented to.
5. *Does the migration's idempotent `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` insert ever mask a real error rather than a genuine already-exists case?* No — the only way a conflicting row can exist is a user who already independently held the identical `(user_id, project_id, role)` direct grant, which is exactly the case where inserting a duplicate would be wrong; verified by reading the unique constraint definition and by the migration test's own assertions.

**Verified**: every finding above was checked against the real, current code (`rbac.py`'s `_direct_project_managers`/`get_effective_project_managers`, `revoke_project_role`/`delete_project_group`'s guards, `templates.py::clone_project`, the migration's actual SQL) and against a live run of the migration itself, not taken on description alone. The full backend pytest suite (690 tests) was run twice against the real dev/test Docker Compose stack to confirm no regression and rule out a one-off flake — see Verification below.

**Remediated**: no new gap was found requiring a user decision or a policy update — this phase *removes* a structural restriction (`is_default`) that had no independent security value beyond what C-U-08 already provided, and *adds* a fallback path (`_ensure_project_has_a_manager`) that is strictly the same guarantee the template-clone branch already gave, now shared rather than duplicated. `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md` was read in full and needed no update: nothing in its Known Gaps list references default project groups or this creation-time mechanism, and the actual authorization surface it documents (project role resolution, C-U-08's manager-retention guarantee) is unchanged in substance, only in which underlying rows express it.

### Two small incidental fixes, found while verifying this phase's own Playwright coverage

**A real, pre-existing accessibility bug: Escape inside a nested `Popover` closed its enclosing `Modal`/`SidePanel` too.** Found while writing the "Manage users" modal's own Playwright coverage above — opening a row's role `MultiSelectDropdown` (a `Popover`) *inside* the "Manage users" `Modal` and pressing Escape closed both, not just the popover. Root cause: `Modal`/`SidePanel`/`Popover` all share `useDialogA11y` (`frontend/src/components/dialogA11y.ts`), and each independently registers its own `window` "keydown" listener with no coordination between instances — `addEventListener` has no built-in "only the topmost dialog" concept, so a single Escape press fired every currently-mounted dialog's `onClose` at once. This bug pre-dates this phase (`OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s "Manage users" modal has wrapped `MemberRoleTable`, itself already using `MultiSelectDropdown`/`Popover` for user rows, since Phase 5) — it was simply never exercised by any existing spec until this phase's new test tried to close a row's dropdown from inside that modal. Fixed with a containment check already implicit in the same function's Tab-trap logic just below it: Escape now only closes a dialog whose own `dialogRef` currently contains `document.activeElement` — since `Modal`/`SidePanel`/`Popover` are each portalled to `document.body` as independent DOM subtrees (never actually nested in the DOM even when opened "inside" one another logically), and each already moves focus into itself on open, this correctly identifies the innermost/topmost currently-open dialog as the only valid target, with no new state or dialog stack needed. Verified safe for every other Escape-to-close flow in the app: the full Storybook suite (607/607, exercising `Modal`/`SidePanel`/`Popover` across many isolated scenarios) and the full set of this phase's own Playwright specs were re-run after the fix and stayed green — see Verification below.

**Enum/derived-string rendering gap, flagged directly by the user mid-pass:** `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s Terminology section (Overview tab) rendered each configurable term's row label by deriving it from the raw key via CSS `text-transform: capitalize` + `.replace("_", " ")` (`change_request` → "Change request") instead of a real label map — exactly the pattern this repo's Principle 12 forbids, with a sibling role/status value two lines away already doing this correctly. Fixed: added `strings.admin.terminologyKeyLabel` (`frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`), a plain literal label map for the six `TERMINOLOGY_KEYS` ("Project", "Stage", "Component", "Category", "Requirement", "Change Request") — deliberately *not* run through the `{project}`-style terminology-substitution system, since these rows are the canonical default term names being configured, not yet-possibly-overridden usage elsewhere in the UI (substituting them through the override they themselves name would be circular). `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` now reads from it instead of the CSS/replace hack.

### Judgment calls and deviations from the plan

- **Both `clone_project` gaps were fixed together** — the plan's own review only named the `UserProjectRole`-copy gap; the `source_project_id`-member-copy gap was found while reading the same function to fix the first one, and fixed in the same pass per this repo's "fix issues found, don't defer" rule rather than filed separately.
- **`test_project_group_role_editing.py`'s `_default_manager_group` helper became `_make_group_the_sole_manager`, not a simple rename** — a fresh project's creator now always starts as the sole *direct* manager (not group-derived), and `revoke_project_role`'s own C-U-08 guard refuses to remove a direct grant that would leave its holder as the sole effective manager (even though they'd remain one via a group they're also in) — so every test that needs "a group is the project's only manager source" has to first establish a *second* manager (a different person, via the new group) before revoking the creator's own direct grant. This is a real behavioural consequence of the phase, not a test-only inconvenience: the same asymmetry now exists for real project managers reorganizing their own project's structure.
- **Chose `_ensure_project_has_a_manager` as a shared helper rather than inlining the fallback in the non-template branch** — the plan explicitly asked for "reuse that same code path/helper," and a from-scratch project's own call into it always takes the direct-grant branch in practice (zero groups exist at that point), but sharing the one function keeps that guaranteed by construction rather than by two independently-maintained copies staying in sync.
- **Two real Playwright locator/behaviour bugs found and fixed while writing this phase's own new coverage, not scoped in the plan**: (1) `PROJECT_ROLE_LABEL.project_manager` renders as "Project manager" (lowercase "m"), not "Project Manager" — two new specs' Escape-guard assertions initially used the wrong casing in their `getByRole("checkbox", { name: /Revoke Project Manager from .../ })` locators and found nothing; fixed to match the real label. (2) The `dialogA11y.ts` Escape-nesting bug described above, found by the same new coverage, fixed at the shared-component level rather than worked around per-spec.

## Follow-up UX batch, Phase D: unified Members table — `MemberRoleTable`/`PendingInvitesSection` retired, `kind` split for safe inline role-toggling

Sixth and final phase of the follow-up batch (Phases 0/A/B/C/E above), depending on Phase C (default project groups had to be gone first — otherwise this phase would be building the new table against a group shape that was about to disappear). With that phase landed, groups stopped being the common way to grant a role, which is what made the previous batch's split of Project Admin's Members section into an editable `MemberRoleTable` (direct users + groups) *plus* a separate effective-members audit table *plus* a separate `PendingInvitesSection` look like three sections doing one job rather than three genuinely different concerns. This phase folds all three into one: `components/ProjectMembersTable.tsx`, built on `GET /{project_id}/effective-members` (now editable and paginated) with pending invites merged in as a per-row status.

### Backend — splitting the collapsed `"direct"` provenance kind (`backend/app/services/rbac.py`)

The highest-risk change in this phase, per the plan's own design-review finding: `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance`'s `kind: "direct"` was **not** "directly-granted-role only" — `_direct_effective_project_roles` already internally distinguished five sources (a genuine `UserProjectRole` row, same-project `ProjectGroup` membership, a nested org group, a project-referencing group, and `ProjectVisibility.ORG_WIDE`) before collapsing all five into one bucket. Building "checked + kind is `direct` ⇒ freely toggle-off-able" directly on that collapsed value would have been actively wrong: a role held only via a surviving custom group or org-wide visibility would show as `"direct"` and *look* editable, but `DELETE /{project_id}/roles/{user_id}/{role}` only ever deletes `UserProjectRole` rows — unchecking it in the UI would 204 as a silent no-op while the person kept the role.

Fixed by adding `_direct_effective_project_roles_by_kind` (new function, `rbac.py`) — the same five-source resolution `_direct_effective_project_roles` already did internally, but returning a `dict[str, set[ProjectRole]]` keyed by `direct_role`/`direct_group`/`direct_org_group`/`direct_project_ref`/`direct_org_wide` instead of one unioned set. `_direct_effective_project_roles` itself is now just this new function's five sets unioned together (byte-identical behaviour for every one of its many existing callers — RBAC resolution, notification targeting, C-U-08 checks — none of which needed the finer granularity). `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance`'s own direct-sources loop now emits one provenance entry per `(kind, role)` pair from the breakdown instead of one collapsed `"direct"` entry per role. `forward_inherited`/`member_source_inherited` are unaffected — only the direct-sources bucket needed splitting.

Only `direct_role` is ever safe to present as toggle-off-able: it's the sole kind that corresponds to a real `UserProjectRole` row `DELETE .../roles/{user_id}/{role}` can act on. The other four are shown checked-but-disabled in the frontend, with a title explaining the role must be changed at its actual source (the group's own membership/role, or the project's visibility setting).

### Backend — `search`/`limit`/`offset` on `GET /{project_id}/effective-members`

`get_effective_project_members_with_provenance` still resolves every candidate user's full provenance in Python before any sorting/filtering — a full rewrite to real DB-level pagination was out of scope for this batch (higher risk, no evidence current data volumes need it). Instead, the *endpoint* (`get_effective_members`, `routers/projects.py`) sorts the fully-materialized `EffectiveMemberOut` list by `display_name` (case-insensitive), applies an optional `search` substring filter (name or email) to that sorted list, sets `X-Total-Count` to the post-search count, then slices by `limit`/`offset` — the same `list_project_groups`/`list_org_groups` contract (`X-Total-Count` header, omitting `limit` returns everything). A code comment on the endpoint spells out explicitly that this is application-level, not database-level, pagination, so a future pass doesn't assume it scales indefinitely.

**Deviation from the plan's literal wording**: the plan described this sort/filter/slice as living inside `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance` itself. It's implemented in the router instead — that function returns `dict[UUID, list[dict]]` with no `display_name`/`email` (the router builds those from `User` rows afterward, and also feeds `POST /materialize-inherited-access`, which needs the *complete*, unsliced set). Sorting/filtering/slicing where the named fields already exist, without changing the shared service function's contract for its other caller, is the same outcome with less risk.

**The new frontend component doesn't actually use `search`/`limit`/`offset` for its primary fetch** — see the frontend section below for why, and why that's a deliberate choice, not an oversight; the backend support is still real, pytested, and available to any caller that does need it.

### Frontend — `components/ProjectMembersTable.tsx` (new), replacing `MemberRoleTable.tsx`/`PendingInvitesSection.tsx` (both deleted, with their Storybook stories)

One `DirectoryTable` row per effective member — Name/Email (sortable, client-side re-sort of an in-memory array), Role (`MultiSelectDropdown` over the four `ProjectRole` values; checked options come from `sources`; an option whose only source is `direct_role` is freely togglable via `POST`/`DELETE /roles`, reusing `MemberRoleTable`'s proven "last manager" disabled+title treatment, now sourced from `direct_role`-kind entries only so it can't misreport for a manager whose role actually comes from a group or org-wide visibility; any other kind is checked-but-disabled with an explanatory title), Source (the existing per-role provenance text, one line per kind). Pending invites (`GET .../pending-invites`, unchanged endpoint) are merged in client-side as `kind: "invited"` rows — Role cell becomes a status badge + Resend button. Filters live inside the component itself (not page-composed, unlike every other `DirectoryTable` call site) specifically so the two call sites below render and behave *identically*, not just similarly: a `FilterField` role filter (checks `sources`, not just the collapsed `effective_role`), a `FilterCheckbox` "Show invited" (default on), and `FilterPanel`'s own search box.

**Why the component still loads `members`/`invites` fully and paginates/filters/searches entirely client-side, despite the new backend support existing**: role-filtering and the pending-invite merge both need the *complete* loaded set to stay correct. A `LoadMoreButton` backed by real server-side offset pagination would make the role filter silently incomplete for any member not yet loaded (a page 2 stakeholder simply wouldn't appear when filtering to "Stakeholder" if page 2 hadn't been fetched yet) — a strictly worse failure mode than the existing "this doesn't scale indefinitely" caveat the backend endpoint's own docstring already carries. This mirrors the precedent `MemberRoleTable`'s two data sources already set (small enough to load whole, search/filter/paginate client-side) rather than introducing a new one.

`ProjectAdminGroupKey`'s `"members"` section now renders only `ProjectMembersTable`; effective-members/pending-invites are fetched eagerly in the page's main `reload()` (not gated behind a lazy "Show members" button any more, since this is now the primary content of the tab, not a secondary audit view) — and eagerly for a second reason: the Groups section's own per-group `SidePanel` role `<select>` still needs an equivalent "how many project-manager sources exist" count for its own last-manager disabled state (`groupManagerSourceCount`, recomputed from `memberTableGroups` + `effectiveMembers`' `direct_role`-kind entries — the same two sources the retired `memberRoleRows` used to merge, just read separately now that Members no longer merges them into one row list). Org Admin's "Manage users" modal switches from `MemberRoleTable` to the same `ProjectMembersTable`, fed by the same per-project endpoints — one real shared implementation, which is what actually satisfies the original "org admin's view should look like project admin's" ask precisely.

`GET /{project_id}/direct-members` (`DirectMemberOut` schema, `list_direct_members` endpoint) — added last batch specifically to feed `MemberRoleTable`'s user rows — had no remaining caller once this landed, so it was removed entirely (endpoint, schema, its two dedicated pytest tests) rather than left as unused surface area. Several existing backend tests used it purely as a convenient "does this user hold this direct grant" assertion (`test_templates.py`, `test_default_group_migration.py`, `test_rbac.py`) — these were switched to a new `tests.conftest.direct_project_roles(project_id)` helper that reads `UserProjectRole` straight from the database, the same underlying data the removed endpoint exposed.

### Tests

Backend pytest (`backend/tests/test_effective_members_provenance.py`, new): `test_all_five_direct_kinds_distinguished_for_one_user_one_role` (a user holding the *same* role via all five direct sources simultaneously shows all five kinds separately, not collapsed — the core regression the split guards against), `test_different_roles_via_different_sources_not_cross_contaminated` (a direct `project_manager` grant and a group-sourced `stakeholder` grant on the same user don't leak kinds across roles), `test_revoking_a_direct_role_kind_role_actually_removes_it`, `test_revoking_a_group_sourced_role_leaves_it_untouched` (the backend-side half of "must not silently no-op" — `DELETE /roles` 204s against a role with no matching `UserProjectRole` row, but the group-derived access is still in effect afterward; the frontend's own disabled+title treatment is what actually stops a caller from trying), `test_effective_members_search_narrows_results`, `test_effective_members_limit_offset_paginate_deterministically` (two same-sized pages from the same sorted set never overlap and together reconstruct the full set). Existing tests updated: `test_project_hierarchy.py` (`kind == "direct"` → `"direct_role"`), `test_project_group_role_editing.py` (its two dedicated `/direct-members` tests removed with the endpoint; one gate-tier assertion mid-test switched to `GET /effective-members`, the same manage-tier endpoint at the same gate).

Storybook (`ProjectMembersTable.stories.tsx`, new): mixed member/invited rows, empty state, paginated (`LoadMoreButton`), a group-sourced role showing disabled with its explanatory title, the last-manager hint, search-narrowed, role-filtered, "Show invited" toggled off, and the `addControl` slot. `ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`/`OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx` updated: the old `MemberRoleTable`-fed stories (users-and-groups mixed rows, group-role-change-from-Members) removed since groups are no longer rows in this table at all; new stories cover add-direct-member, toggle-a-direct-role-off, and pending-invite-resend at the page-integration level (the component's own stories already cover the UI behaviours themselves in isolation, so these just confirm the real endpoint/callback wiring).

### Docs

### Judgment calls and deviations from the plan

- **`search`/`limit`/`offset` sort/filter/slice logic lives in the router (`get_effective_members`), not inside `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance`** — see the backend section above; the shared service function's contract for its other caller (`materialize-inherited-access`, which needs the complete set) is unaffected, and the display fields the sort/filter need don't exist on that function's own return shape.
- **The new frontend component doesn't actually issue paginated requests using the new backend params** — a deliberate choice, not a partial implementation: role-filtering and the pending-invite merge both need the complete set to stay correct, and real server-side offset pagination combined with a client-only role filter would silently hide legitimate members on a later page. The backend support is still real and pytested, for future consumers.
- **`GET /{project_id}/direct-members` removed entirely, per the plan's own "check whether it still has any caller" instruction** — several backend tests used it as a convenient assertion helper rather than exercising it as a feature; those were migrated onto a direct DB-read helper (`tests.conftest.direct_project_roles`) rather than treated as "still needs this endpoint to exist."
- **`groupManagerSourceCount` (Groups section's own last-manager hint) recomputed from two separately-fetched arrays instead of one merged row list** — the retired `memberRoleRows` used to combine `memberTableGroups` and direct-member data into one array specifically so both the Members table and the Groups section's own hint could read from it; now that Members no longer needs that merge, the Groups section's hint reads the same two underlying sources directly instead, preserving the exact same count/semantics it always had.

### An incidental fix, found while verifying this phase's own Playwright coverage: `ServerSettings` singleton race

Unrelated to anything this phase otherwise touches, but a real, previously-undiscovered bug — fixed here per this repo's "fix issues found, don't defer" rule rather than filed separately. While chasing an inconsistently-failing full Playwright run (`self-signup.spec.ts` and `org-bundle-export-import.spec.ts` failing with different symptoms on different runs — a classic non-deterministic-bug signature, not a deterministic UI regression), a live inspection of the test database found **two** real `server_settings` rows, with different `signup_mode` values. `ServerSettings` (`services/branding.py::get_server_settings`) was a "lazily created singleton row" by application convention only — `settings = db.scalar(select(ServerSettings)); if settings is None: create one` — with no DB-level constraint preventing two concurrent requests from both observing "no row yet" and both inserting: a textbook TOCTOU race, previously *documented* as a deliberate omission in the model's own docstring, not flagged as a live risk. Once two rows exist, `db.scalar(select(ServerSettings))`'s "first row" (no `ORDER BY`) is not deterministic — different requests can transiently see different rows, which explains both this run's inconsistent failures and, in hindsight, an earlier "genuine, non-reproducing flake" the Phase C entry above already logged against `test_signup.py` without root-causing it.

Fixed with a real DB-level constraint, not just a stricter application check (an application-level fix alone can't close a genuine two-concurrent-transactions race): migration `0020_server_settings_singleton_guard.py` deduplicates any existing extra rows (keeps the most recently updated one — the one most likely to reflect the latest real admin action, since either row could have "won" any given write unpredictably, so there's no principled way to *merge* two independently-diverged rows' field values) and adds `singleton_guard` (`BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, `UNIQUE`) — a second `INSERT` now fails with an `IntegrityError` instead of silently succeeding as a duplicate. `get_server_settings` catches that `IntegrityError` on the losing side of the race and re-reads instead of letting it propagate, so the race becomes "the loser retries and gets the winner's row" rather than "the loser also succeeds." Pinned by two new tests (`test_server_settings_singleton.py`): the DB constraint itself rejects a manually-attempted second row, and a monkeypatched `db.scalar` forces `get_server_settings`'s own initial read to lie about "no row yet" (simulating exactly the race window) while a real row already exists, confirming the recovery path returns that row rather than raising.

### Verification

Backend: full suite via the dev/test Docker Compose stack (`tests/container`, backend rebuilt + force-recreated first), run to completion twice — once before the `ServerSettings` singleton fix above (**694 passed, 0 failed**) and once after, including its own 2 new tests (**696 passed, 0 failed**) — 72 pre-existing warnings both times (same count as every earlier entry in this batch, none new). `ruff check app tests` clean on both runs.

Frontend: `npx tsc -b` clean; `npm run lint` clean (same 7 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings as every earlier entry in this batch, none new, none in files touched by this work); `npm run test-storybook` (full suite, 69 files) — **604 passed, 0 failed**, including the new `ProjectMembersTable.stories.tsx` (11 tests).

Playwright, against the dev/test Docker Compose stack (backend + frontend rebuilt and force-recreated first, `seed_demo_data.py`/`seed_e2e_dataset.py` re-run after each backend pytest run truncated the DB): the full suite (`npx playwright test`, every spec, 116 tests) — **116 passed, 0 failed** on the final run, after the `ServerSettings` fix above. A first full run (before that fix) showed 8 inconsistent failures across unrelated areas (`self-signup.spec.ts`, `org-bundle-export-import.spec.ts`, `server-admin-scope.spec.ts`, `server-org-lifecycle.spec.ts`, `user-access-panel.spec.ts`) — investigating why is what surfaced the `ServerSettings` singleton race documented above; 5 of the 8 were confirmed as ordinary flakes on isolated re-run, but `self-signup.spec.ts`'s two mode-dependent tests reproduced consistently across three separate attempts (including live manual reproduction via direct browser automation, which is what led to inspecting the database directly and finding the duplicate row) until the singleton fix landed, after which every previously-flaky spec passed cleanly and repeatably.

**This is the final phase of the follow-up UX batch** (Phases 0, A, B, C, D, E) — with this phase's own verification green, the batch as a whole is complete: `DirectoryTable` is now the shared shell behind all six directories (Org Users, Org Groups, Project Groups, Project Members, Server Admin's Access Review), org-level invites exist alongside password-set "New user," Org/Project Groups both render as real tables with a `SidePanel` per row, default project groups are gone in favour of direct grants, and Project Admin's Members section — now shared verbatim with Org Admin's "Manage users" modal — is a single unified, editable, filterable table over effective membership with pending invites folded in as a status rather than a parallel section.
