## Project hierarchy on Project Overview + org-admin bypass (PR2 of the follow-up UX batch, 2026-09)

Second PR of the batch, the first of two flagged for identify → verify → remediate rigor (the plan's own PR2 section — see the "Sequencing" note at the top of the plan document): shows parent/child hierarchy on `ProjectOverviewPage` (previously shown on list pages only, never on the single-project dashboard) and gives an org admin visibility into the true hierarchy of any project in their own organisation, regardless of their own role/membership on that project.

### Identify

Read `docs/decisions.md`'s existing "Hierarchical projects" entry and the current code (not the plan's line-number guesses, which had drifted somewhat) before changing anything. Three claims from the plan needed independent verification:

1. **"`_project_out_with_redacted_parent` needs no change — it already calls `can_manage_project_settings`, which already checks `is_org_admin`."** Confirmed true by reading both functions (`backend/app/routers/projects.py:225-266`, `backend/app/services/rbac.py:282-291`): `can_manage_project_settings` returns `True` for `is_org_admin(db, user.id, project.organization_id)` before ever checking the caller's own project role, and `_project_out_with_redacted_parent` already ORs that check alongside `_accessible_project_ids` membership. No change needed here, exactly as the plan said.
2. **Parent/child are same-organisation at write time**, so an admin bypass keyed off the *child's* (or anchor project's) own organisation is safe for every ancestor/descendant in the chain. Confirmed by grep: `create_project` (`projects.py:365-366`) and `update_project` (`:940-941`) both reject a cross-organisation `parent_project_id` with "parent_project_id must be a project in this organisation."
3. **The gap is narrow — just `list_projects`, `get_project_ancestors`, `get_project_children` need an explicit `is_org_admin(...)` OR-condition at their internal `_accessible_project_ids` checks, no change to that shared function's own meaning.** Confirmed by reading `_accessible_project_ids` in full (a genuinely complex, multi-hop, iteratively-expanded set used by several other callers — the plan was right that changing its own return value would be the wrong, broad-blast-radius fix) and grepping every one of its callers (`create_project`'s tree endpoint, `list_projects`, `get_project_ancestors`, `get_project_children`, and `_project_out_with_redacted_parent` itself) to confirm none of the *other* callers needed touching.

**A fourth issue, not in the plan, found while verifying claim 1 above:** the plan's reasoning for "no change needed" implicitly assumes the org admin can already *reach* `GET /{project_id}` in the first place. That endpoint (and `get_project_ancestors`/`get_project_children`) were gated by `require_project_view`, which requires a genuine effective project role via `get_effective_project_roles` — org-admin status alone does **not** satisfy it (per the existing C-U-01 clarification baked into that dependency's own docstring: "org admin only guarantees the ability to manage project settings, not general content access"). Default project visibility is `ONLY_SPECIFIED`, not `ORG_WIDE`, so an org admin with zero direct/group role on a given project gets 403 "Not a member of this project" before the request body — and `_project_out_with_redacted_parent`'s already-correct exemption inside it — is ever reached. This directly contradicts the product requirement ("regardless of their own role/membership on that specific project") and the exact positive test scenario specified for this PR ("an org admin with NO role/group membership on either the parent or child project").

### Verify

Wrote a throwaway probe test (`tests/test_zzz_probe.py`, deleted before finishing — never committed) reproducing the scenario directly: an org admin created via `create_org_user(..., role="org_admin")`, granted no project role at all, calling `GET /{child_id}`, `GET /{parent_id}/children`, and `GET /{child_id}/ancestors`. All three returned `403 {"detail": "Not a member of this project."}` against the real backend and test database — confirmed empirically, not just reasoned about.

Checked whether `require_project_view_or_manage` (an existing dependency, already used by `list_project_groups` for the identical "structure, not content" reasoning — its own docstring: "so an org admin can see... a project they otherwise can't open, without this becoming a general content-access grant") was the right, precedented fix rather than inventing new logic. Also checked whether switching `get_project`'s auth dependency from `require_project_view` to `require_project_view_or_manage` was a genuine authorization *widening* or just closing an inconsistency: `update_project` (`PATCH /{project_id}`) already uses `require_project_manage`, which has the identical `can_manage_project_settings`/`is_org_admin` bypass — so an org admin with zero role could already unilaterally *change* every field `GET /{project_id}` returns, just not *read* them first. Letting the same admin read what they can already write is not a new privilege.

Grepped the full backend test suite for every bare `GET /{project_id}` call (not a sub-resource) to find any test whose 403 expectation this dependency swap could flip to 200: `test_org_group_nesting.py:91`, `test_org_lifecycle.py:71`, `test_org_require_2fa.py:41`, `test_rbac.py:432`, and every `test_project_hierarchy.py` assertion. Read each one's setup: the two "require_project_view-gated" 403 assertions in `test_org_lifecycle.py`/`test_org_require_2fa.py` are for an org admin who created the project themselves (holds a direct `PROJECT_MANAGER` role, so `require_project_view` already passed for them) hitting a *disabled org*/*2FA-required* wall — both of those checks (`_require_org_active`/`_require_org_2fa`) run identically inside `require_project_view_or_manage`, before the role/manage check, so unaffected. `test_rbac.py:432`'s outsider is a member of a *different* organisation entirely — `is_org_admin(db, user, project.organization_id)` is false for them regardless, so unaffected. None of the existing hierarchy tests use an org-admin token with zero project role against a bare `GET /{project_id}`.

### Remediate

**Backend** (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`):
- `get_project`, `get_project_ancestors`, `get_project_children` switched from `require_project_view` to `require_project_view_or_manage` — the fourth finding's fix, not in the original plan text, but required to make the plan's own stated positive test scenario reachable at all.
- `list_projects`: the parent/children population (`visible_parent_ids`/`children_by_parent`) now also includes any project whose *own* `organization_id` the caller is `is_org_admin` of, computed once per distinct organisation present in the result set (not per row) and unioned with the existing `_accessible_project_ids`-based check — `list_projects` itself still only *lists* rows the caller is independently accessible on (unchanged; the endpoint's own "No server-admin bypass (I-M-05)" comment and behaviour stand), only the parent/children *fields on an already-visible row* gained the bypass.
- `get_project_ancestors`: an `admin_bypass` flag (`is_org_admin` on the anchor `project_id`'s own organisation) short-circuits the truncate-at-first-inaccessible-ancestor loop.
- `get_project_children`: the same `admin_bypass` flag widens the `WHERE` filter from `Project.id.in_(accessible_ids)` to unconditional (all children of `project_id`), since children are guaranteed same-organisation as their parent.
- No change to `_accessible_project_ids` itself or to `_project_out_with_redacted_parent` — both confirmed correct in Identify above.

**Frontend**:
- `frontend/src/api/types.ts`: new `ProjectHierarchySummary` interface — the narrow `{id, parent_project_id, parent_project_name, children}` subset `ProjectHierarchyLabels` actually renders, rather than the full `ProjectListItem` it was previously typed against.
- `frontend/src/components/ProjectHierarchyLabels.tsx`: retyped to accept `ProjectHierarchySummary` instead of `ProjectListItem` — `ProjectListItem` still satisfies it structurally, so `ProjectListPage`/`FavouritesPage` needed no changes at their call sites.
- `frontend/src/pages/ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`: the existing load `useEffect` gained two more parallel fetches (`GET /{id}/ancestors`, `GET /{id}/children}` — the latter confirmed via grep to have zero other frontend callers before this, matching the plan). A root-first breadcrumb (ancestors, then the current project's own un-linked name) renders above the header when any ancestors are visible; `ProjectHierarchyLabels`, fed a `ProjectHierarchySummary` assembled from the `Project` GET response plus the fetched `children`, renders inline under the summary line — same plain `.stack`/`text-muted` styling as the rest of the page, no new component pattern introduced.

### Tests

Backend (`backend/tests/test_project_hierarchy.py`, new section "Org-admin hierarchy-visibility bypass"): `test_org_admin_sees_true_parent_children_and_ancestors_with_zero_project_role` (the plan's exact positive scenario — zero role on either project, all three endpoints reachable and truthful), `test_org_admin_of_a_different_organisation_gets_no_bypass` (an org admin of an unrelated organisation gets ordinary 403s — proves the bypass is scoped to *that project's* organisation, not "any org admin anywhere"), `test_non_admin_with_role_on_child_only_still_gets_redacted_parent_and_truncated_ancestors` (the negative/regression case — an ordinary `stakeholder` with a role on the child only still gets `parent_project_id: null`, an empty ancestors chain, and a 403 on the parent's children endpoint), `test_list_projects_shows_true_parent_and_children_to_org_admin_across_the_visibility_boundary` (the `list_projects` field-population case specifically, including confirming the *listing itself* stays unchanged — the parent row still isn't listed for an admin with no independent access to it).

Frontend: `frontend/src/pages/ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx` gained `WithHierarchy` (a parent + two children fixture, asserting the breadcrumb, the "Child of"/"Parent of" labels, and — since "Atlas Platform"/"Atlas Core" each legitimately render twice across the breadcrumb and the header/labels — using `getAllByRole`/`getAllByText` with explicit counts rather than the ambiguous singular query). The pre-existing `Dashboard`/`LoadError` stories' `api.get` mocks were extended to answer `/ancestors`/`/children` explicitly (previously falling through to a `buildProject(...)` default that would have handed `ProjectHierarchyLabels` a non-array `children` value and crashed on `.slice()`).

### Verified

Backend: `pytest tests/test_project_hierarchy.py` — **46 passed** (42 pre-existing + 4 new), confirming no regression in the file this PR edits most heavily. A broader regression sweep of every other file found (via the grep above) to call a bare `GET /{project_id}` with a token whose access level could plausibly interact with the dependency swap — `test_org_group_nesting.py`, `test_org_lifecycle.py`, `test_org_require_2fa.py`, `test_rbac.py`, `test_permission_matrix.py`, `test_project_statuses.py` — **71 passed**. `ruff check app/routers/projects.py` clean. Per this task's own scope (new/edited files in isolation, not the full suite — that happens once, after all six PRs land), the full backend suite was not run here.

Frontend: `npx tsc -b` clean. `npx eslint` on every touched file (`ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`, `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx`, `ProjectHierarchyLabels.tsx`, `api/types.ts`) clean. Storybook, targeted rather than full-suite (same reasoning as backend): `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx` alone — **5 passed** (`Dashboard`, `WithHierarchy`, `LoadError`, `LightTheme`, `DarkTheme`); `ProjectHierarchyLabels.stories.tsx` + `ProjectListPage.stories.tsx` + `FavouritesPage.stories.tsx` (the three other consumers of the retyped component/its callers) — **38 passed**, confirming the `ProjectListItem` → `ProjectHierarchySummary` retype didn't break either existing call site.

### Judgment calls and deviations from the plan

- **The dependency swap on `get_project`/`get_project_ancestors`/`get_project_children` (`require_project_view` → `require_project_view_or_manage`) is not in the plan's PR2 section**, which described only the three internal `_accessible_project_ids` call sites. It's a necessary consequence of the plan's own stated requirement and test scenario, found during Identify/Verify above and confirmed empirically before fixing (never assumed) — documented explicitly here per this repo's "flag an authorization change explicitly, don't silently diverge" rule rather than silently expanding scope. Chosen over inventing new logic because it reuses an existing, already-precedented dependency (`list_project_groups`'s own use of it) rather than adding a fourth pattern for the same "org admin sees structure without content access" need.
- **`GET /{project_id}` now also returns full project settings (not just hierarchy fields) to an org admin with zero role**, as a side effect of the dependency swap — judged acceptable and consistent (not a new escalation) because `PATCH /{project_id}` already grants that same admin unilateral write access to every one of those same fields via the identical `can_manage_project_settings` bypass; GET was the outlier, not PATCH.
- **`docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md` was read before making this change** (per the change-management policy's practice for anything touching authorization) — its item 1 ("Organization role... scoped to one organization" implying org-wide authority over that organization's own projects) and item 2 (per-request re-resolution of the caller's *effective* role from the specific target's own organisation id, never "has this role anywhere") both support this shape of check; no wording update was needed there, since it already documents org-admin authority in general terms without enumerating which specific endpoints implement it.

## Direct org-group project role grants (PR4 of the follow-up UX batch, 2026-09)

Fourth PR of the batch, the second flagged for identify → verify → remediate rigor (the plan's own PR4 section — see the "Sequencing" note at the top of the plan document, `/Users/rballard/.claude/plans/eventual-sleeping-pony.md`). Unlike PR2 (a redaction-bypass fix), this is a genuinely **new** access-grant pathway: an organisation group can now hold a project role *directly*, as its own independently-revocable record (`OrgGroupProjectRole`), the same way `UserProjectRole` already lets a single user do — additive alongside, not a replacement for, nesting an org group inside a `ProjectGroup` (C-U-12). Both mechanisms coexist by explicit product decision (see the plan's "Background" section).

### Identify

Read `backend/app/services/rbac.py`'s whole provenance-resolution area, `backend/app/models/project.py`, `backend/app/routers/projects.py`'s `assign_project_role`/`revoke_project_role`/`add_project_group_member`, the Alembic version history, and the frontend's `MemberSourceProvenanceKind`/`isDirectRoleKind` (post-PR1) before changing anything — the plan's own line numbers had drifted (PR1/PR2/PR3 already landed) and PR1 in particular had already reshaped `_direct_effective_project_roles_by_kind`'s `direct_group`/`direct_org_group` kinds from `set[ProjectRole]` to `set[tuple[ProjectRole, UUID, str]]` (role, group_id, group_name), with `via_group_id`/`via_group_name` already threaded through `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance`. Five things needed independent verification before writing any code:

1. **Where a new kind needs to plug in.** `_direct_effective_project_roles_by_kind` is the single place all five (now six) direct sources are resolved per-user; `_direct_effective_project_roles` (the flat union used by `_forward_inherited_roles`'s `MIRROR_ALL` case and `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance`'s own `MIRROR_ALL` forward-inherited loop) is *just that function's sets unioned together* — confirmed by reading it line by line. This means adding a `direct_org_group_role` kind to the dict makes it participate in `MIRROR_ALL` forward inheritance **automatically**, with no separate code change to the inheritance walk itself.
2. **Which helpers `MIRROR_ROLE`/`MEMBER_ONLY` forward inheritance and all three member-source modes actually go through**, since they do *not* call `_direct_effective_project_roles_by_kind` — traced every call site: `_direct_project_role_holder_ids` (used by `MIRROR_ROLE` forward inheritance, `get_project_users_by_role`, and two of the three member-source helpers), `_direct_project_member_ids_base` (used, via `_direct_project_member_ids`, by `MEMBER_ONLY`/`MIRROR_ALL` member-counting and the project-reference arm), and `_direct_project_roles_excluding_org_wide` (used by `_member_source_derived_roles`'s own `MIRROR_ALL` case). All three needed their own extension; nothing else did. Confirmed by reading `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance` end to end and checking every one of its forward/member-source branches resolves through one of these three functions plus the flat union above — no fourth path exists.
3. **The exact shape to mirror for the new model.** `UserProjectRole` (`backend/app/models/project.py:334-342`): `UUIDPKMixin`/`TimestampMixin`, a bare FK to `users.id` (no `ondelete`, since users aren't hard-deleted), an `ondelete="CASCADE"` FK to `projects.id`, and a three-column unique constraint. The plan's own instruction to cascade-delete both FKs needed one adjustment: `ProjectGroupMember.org_group_id` (not `UserProjectRole.user_id`) is the correct precedent for the org-group side, since org groups *are* hard-deletable (`ondelete="CASCADE"` on `org_groups.id`), unlike users.
4. **The actual current migration head.** `alembic history` (not a line-number guess): `0020` ("Enforce ServerSettings singleton semantics at the DB level"), so the new migration chains as `0021`.
5. **Whether `revoke_project_role`'s C-U-08 guard has a group-scoped equivalent already, and whether one is even meaningful here.** Read `_direct_project_managers`/`get_effective_project_managers` in full: they deliberately count only direct `UserProjectRole` grants and a `ProjectGroup`'s *direct user* members towards the "at least one manager" floor — **no group-derived manager has ever counted**, not even the pre-existing nested-org-group mechanism (`ProjectGroupMember.org_group_id`). This is load-bearing for the guard design below.

### Verify

- **Traced every downstream cascade path a second time**, forward from the three extended helpers rather than backward from the provenance function, to confirm no fifth call site was missed: `_forward_contributed_member_ids` (notification membership), `get_project_users_by_role` (change-request/notification role targeting), `_member_source_contributed_user_ids`, `_member_source_role_holder_ids`. All resolve through `_direct_project_role_holder_ids`/`_direct_project_member_ids_base`, confirming the three-function extension is complete, not partial.
- **Confirmed empirically, not just by reading code, that a group's direct grant on a *parent* project cascades to a *child*** under `MIRROR_ALL`, `MIRROR_ROLE`, and `MEMBER_ONLY`, and via the member-source mechanism — four separate tests (`test_org_group_project_roles.py`, "Inheritance cascade" section below), each asserting both the actual access (a real HTTP call against the child/receiving project) and the provenance shown (`kind="forward_inherited"`/`"member_source_inherited"`, correct `via_project_id`/`via_mode`).
- **Confirmed the C-U-08 guard's practical scope by constructing the edge case directly**, rather than assuming: a project's real (individually-accountable) manager count is unaffected by any group-role grant or revoke, in both directions — revoking a group's `project_manager` grant while a real direct manager still exists succeeds normally even though it removes manager-level access from every group member at once (`test_revoking_a_groups_manager_role_succeeds_when_a_real_manager_remains`); and — since that state can't normally be reached through the API (every existing manager-count-reducing endpoint already guards against reaching zero) — a direct database write bypassing every API-level guard was used to construct an already-zero-real-manager state and confirm the new endpoint's own post-check still catches it (`test_revoking_a_groups_manager_role_is_blocked_if_no_real_manager_remains`), the same defense-in-depth behaviour `delete_project_group`/`update_project_group` already rely on for the identical reason.
- **Read `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md`** before writing the endpoints (per the change-management policy's practice for anything touching authorization). Its Authorization item 1 defines project role as one of three independent scopes "scoped to one project," and item 2 requires every check to resolve from the specific target's own ID, never "has this role anywhere" — the new endpoints satisfy both unchanged: `require_project_manage` (the same dependency `assign_project_role`/`revoke_project_role` already use) and a live re-check that the org group belongs to `project.organization_id` (mirroring `add_project_group_member`'s identical check for its own `org_group_id` target) are the only two gates, no new scope or bypass introduced. No policy wording update was needed — like PR2's conclusion, it already documents project-role authorization in general terms without enumerating every specific grant mechanism (nesting isn't named either).
- **Checked for escalation beyond what nesting already allowed**, the specific question the plan called out: the new mechanism grants exactly the same fixed `ProjectRole` vocabulary (`member`/`stakeholder`/`project_administrator`/`project_manager`) that `ProjectGroup` nesting and `UserProjectRole` already grant, through the identical `require_project_manage` gate and the identical cross-tenant check — there is no new role, no new bypass, and no path from this mechanism to any capability nesting couldn't already reach. **Checked that revocation cleanly removes the cascade**: resolution is entirely query-time (no cached/materialized row anywhere in the chain — `_direct_effective_project_roles_by_kind` and the three extended helpers all query `OrgGroupProjectRole` fresh on every call), so deleting the row removes it from every consumer's very next query, including both inheritance mechanisms; `test_revoke_removes_the_grant` and the cascade tests' own revoke-then-recheck steps confirm this empirically, not just by construction.

### Remediate

**Backend**
- New model `OrgGroupProjectRole` (`backend/app/models/project.py`, placed immediately after `UserProjectRole`) — `org_group_id` (FK `org_groups.id`, `ondelete="CASCADE"`), `project_id` (FK `projects.id`, `ondelete="CASCADE"`), `role` (`ProjectRole`), unique on `(org_group_id, project_id, role)`. Registered in `backend/app/models/__init__.py`.
- New migration `backend/alembic/versions/0021_org_group_project_roles.py` (`0020` → `0021`), raw-SQL `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + two indexes, matching this codebase's post-0001 migration style (see `0015_project_hierarchy.py`'s `project_member_sources` table for the closest precedent) — additive only, the new table starts empty.
- New schema `OrgGroupProjectRoleAssign` (`backend/app/schemas/project.py`) and `MemberSourceProvenanceOut`'s docstring updated to include the new kind.
- New endpoints in `backend/app/routers/projects.py`: `POST /{project_id}/group-roles` (`assign_group_project_role`) and `DELETE /{project_id}/group-roles/{org_group_id}/{role}` (`revoke_group_project_role`), placed immediately after their user-level counterparts. Both gated by `require_project_manage`; the POST re-validates the org group's organisation matches the project's, mirroring `add_project_group_member`'s identical check; the POST is idempotent (a duplicate grant is a silent no-op, no 409, matching `assign_project_role`'s exact behaviour — verified no second audit event is written either); neither sends a per-member notification, matching `add_project_group_member`/`remove_project_group_member`'s own group-target behaviour (not `assign_project_role`/`revoke_project_role`'s single-user notify) since a group grant can affect many users at once and this codebase's existing group-composition endpoints don't notify on that basis either. The DELETE's engagement (subscription/favourite) cleanup loops every member of the group — direct or via a nested subgroup, using the same descendant-expansion `_direct_project_role_holder_ids` uses to resolve the mechanism — checking each one's remaining effective access individually, rather than the single-`user_id` cleanup `revoke_project_role` does (see "An incidental fix considered and deliberately not made" below for a related pre-existing gap found, not fixed, in `remove_project_group_member`'s own equivalent line).
- `backend/app/services/rbac.py`: `DIRECT_ROLE_KINDS` gains `"direct_org_group_role"`; `_direct_effective_project_roles_by_kind` gains a new branch (reusing the same `user_org_group_ids` — direct + transitively-nested org groups — already computed for the `direct_org_group` branch) that queries `OrgGroupProjectRole` with the same cross-tenant re-check every sibling branch applies; `_direct_project_role_holder_ids`, `_direct_project_member_ids_base`, and `_direct_project_roles_excluding_org_wide` each gain the equivalent extension (Identify finding 2 above) — this is what makes both inheritance mechanisms cascade the new source automatically, without either walk needing its own group-aware branch. `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance`'s per-kind tuple-unpacking check gains the new kind. Module and function docstrings updated throughout (module docstring's source count 7 → 8, with a new numbered source-8 entry; two stale docstring references — "six sources" that should have read the already-correct seven, and a comment in `_direct_project_role_holder_ids` referring to an *earlier*, since-widened version of `get_project_users_by_role` — corrected in passing, since both were directly adjacent to text this change already had to touch).

**Frontend (type-level only, per this PR's explicit scope)**
- `frontend/src/api/types.ts`: `MemberSourceProvenanceKind` gains `"direct_org_group_role"`. `isDirectRoleKind` is **not** extended to return `true` for it — see "Judgment calls" below for the reasoning, since the plan flagged this as a decision to make and document either way.

### Tests

New `backend/tests/test_org_group_project_roles.py` (16 tests): grant + provenance (`kind`/`via_group_id`/`via_group_name`), revoke removes it (API response and a direct DB check), idempotent grant (no duplicate row, no second audit event), a no-op revoke of a never-granted role 204s harmlessly, two groups granting the same role produce two source entries (matching the existing `direct_group`/`direct_org_group` precedent in `test_effective_members_provenance.py`), descendant-expansion through a nested subgroup, cross-tenant grant rejection (400), 403 for both a bare org-role user and a genuine-but-insufficient (`stakeholder`) project role on both grant and revoke, audit log entries for both grant and revoke (entity/action/detail/project_id), and the C-U-08 guard's two edge cases described in Verify above. Four inheritance-cascade tests: `MIRROR_ALL`, `MIRROR_ROLE` (including the negative case — a differently-roled group must not cascade), `MEMBER_ONLY`, and the member-source mechanism — each granting the role to an org group *only*, with no user-level `UserProjectRole` anywhere in the chain, so a passing test can only mean the new source 8 cascade path actually worked.

### Verified

Backend: `pytest tests/test_org_group_project_roles.py` (new) — **16 passed**. Regression sweep of the files most directly exercising the code this change edits most heavily (`_direct_effective_project_roles_by_kind` and its three cascade-helper siblings): `tests/test_effective_members_provenance.py` (8), `tests/test_project_hierarchy.py` (46), `tests/test_rbac.py` (20), `tests/test_org_group_nesting.py` (7) — **81 passed, 0 failed**, confirming the PR1 kind-split and every pre-existing inheritance/member-source/nested-org-group test still passes unchanged. `ruff check` on every changed backend file clean. Per this task's own instructions, the full backend suite was not run — that happens once, after all six PRs land. `alembic heads` confirms a single head at `0021`, chained onto `0020`.

Frontend: `npx tsc -b` clean. `npx eslint src/api/types.ts` clean. No Storybook/Playwright run in this PR, per its explicit scope (type-level plumbing only, no UI wiring).

### Judgment calls and deviations from the plan

- **The C-U-08 guard on `DELETE /{project_id}/group-roles/{org_group_id}/{role}` is shaped like `delete_project_group`'s (lock, delete, flush, re-check `get_effective_project_managers` before commit), not `revoke_project_role`'s single-user pre-check (`managers == {user_id}`).** A group-role revocation can remove effective access from every member of the group at once, so there is no single user id to compare against; the post-check pattern is the correct generalisation, and it's the one `delete_project_group`/`update_project_group` already use for an equivalent whole-group access change. **This guard is, by design, very unlikely to ever actually trip on a group-role-specific cause**: `get_effective_project_managers` has never counted a group-derived manager — not the pre-existing nested-org-group mechanism, and not this new one — towards the "at least one manager" floor (Identify finding 5), so a project's *real* manager count is unaffected either way by granting or revoking a group's `project_manager` role. This is not a new gap PR4 introduces; it's the same, pre-existing, deliberately narrow C-U-08 semantics nested groups have always had (a project can have zero individually-accountable managers while a group still grants many users effective `PROJECT_MANAGER`-level access) — extending `get_effective_project_managers` to count group-derived managers would be a materially larger, separate change to a longstanding invariant across *both* mechanisms, not something this PR's scope covers, and not requested. The guard is kept anyway for defense-in-depth and consistency with its two siblings, and `test_revoking_a_groups_manager_role_is_blocked_if_no_real_manager_remains` confirms it still does something (catches a pre-existing zero-manager state) even though it can't be tripped by the group action itself through any normal API sequence.
- **`isDirectRoleKind` is not extended to return `true` for `"direct_org_group_role"`.** It is, on its current merits, a real and equally strong candidate: `OrgGroupProjectRole` is a genuine, individually-revocable row exactly like `UserProjectRole`, deleted outright (no silent no-op) by `DELETE /{project_id}/group-roles/{org_group_id}/{role}`. But reading how the function's result is actually meant to be consumed (per the task's own instruction to check this before deciding) surfaces the real problem: every existing and anticipated caller of `isDirectRoleKind` is checking "is it safe to let *this member's own row* show a toggle-off that revokes *only this member's* access" (see `ProjectMembersTable.tsx`'s `purelyDirect` check, `kinds.size === 1 && kinds.has("direct_role")` — not currently routed through this helper at all, but the same semantic). A `direct_org_group_role` entry on a user's row is not that: the backing row belongs to the *group*, not the user, so a toggle-off driven from one member's row would silently revoke the role for every other member of that group too — correct-but-surprising at best, a real footgun at worst, once a future UI naively extends this helper to "any individually-revocable kind" without re-deriving that distinction. Extended the function's doc comment substantially (rather than its return value) to spell this reasoning out explicitly, name the future direction (a group-row UI should use its own predicate against the raw kind, not this one), and point at this entry. Per the plan's own instruction, this is UI-consuming-side plumbing only for PR5/PR6 to build — no component, page, or toggle was added or changed in this PR.
- **`_direct_project_managers`/`get_effective_project_managers` were deliberately left unchanged** (not extended to count `OrgGroupProjectRole`-derived managers) — see the C-U-08 bullet above. Flagged explicitly here per this repo's "flag rather than silently diverge" rule, even though it's a decision to leave existing, longstanding behaviour alone rather than a new divergence.
- **An incidental bug found while implementing the new endpoint's own engagement cleanup — fixed in the same pass, not deferred, per this repo's "fix, don't defer" rule.** `remove_project_group_member`'s own equivalent cleanup line (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`) called `get_effective_project_roles(db, member_id, ...)`/`remove_subscriptions_and_favorites_for_projects(db, member_id, ...)` with `member_id` potentially being an org-group id or a source-project id, not a real user id, for a group/project-reference removal — its own docstring already said as much ("member_id may be a user id, an org-group id, or a source-project id here"). Since no real user shares that id, this was a silent no-op for those two cases: removing a nested org group or a project-reference from a group never actually cleaned up the now-inaccessible former members' subscriptions/favourites. Fixed by resolving the group's/source project's real member set first (a new `removed_member` lookup before the delete, then branching on which of `user_id`/`org_group_id`/`source_project_id` was actually set — the org-group branch reuses the same descendant-expansion `revoke_group_project_role` already uses; the source-project branch reuses `_direct_project_member_ids_base`, the same non-recursive roster resolution the project-reference mechanism already uses elsewhere), then looping the existing per-user check/cleanup over that real set. Two new regression tests in `test_project_group_role_editing.py` (`test_removing_a_nested_org_group_member_cleans_up_its_users_favourites`, `test_removing_a_project_reference_member_cleans_up_its_roster_favourites`) — both favourite a project as the affected user, remove the group/reference membership, and assert the favourite is actually gone; the first would have failed with the favourite still present before this fix (confirmed by running it against the pre-fix code).
- **A second, related, more consequential gap found and fixed in the same pass, discovered while writing the listing-visibility test for this PR's own new mechanism**: `_accessible_project_ids` (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`) — the function behind `GET /projects` (search/listing), `/ancestors`, and `/children`, and *distinct* from `get_effective_project_roles`/`require_project_view`, which `GET /{project_id}` uses directly — only ever covered a user's *direct* membership (a `UserProjectRole`, or being a plain `user_id` member of a `ProjectGroup`). It never accounted for a role reached only via an org group the user belongs to, whether through the pre-existing nested-org-group mechanism (`ProjectGroupMember.org_group_id`) or this PR's own new direct grant (`OrgGroupProjectRole`). Concretely: a user whose *only* access to a project was via either mechanism could already open it directly (`GET /{project_id}` returned 200, confirmed by the pre-existing `test_transitive_nesting_grants_effective_project_role_through_a_chain`), but the project never appeared in that user's own project list or search — a genuine, user-visible correctness bug, and for this PR's own new mechanism specifically, an incompleteness in PR4 itself, not just a pre-existing sibling gap. Fixed by adding two more source sets to `_accessible_project_ids`'s base computation (reusing `get_user_org_group_ids`, already used elsewhere for the identical direct+transitively-nested resolution, once per organisation the user belongs to): projects reachable via a nested org group's `ProjectGroupMember` row, and projects reachable via `OrgGroupProjectRole`. The existing iterative expansion loop (children / member-source / project-reference propagation) needed no change — it already propagates outward correctly from whatever the base set contains, and the project-reference case was independently confirmed still correct via `test_removing_a_project_reference_member_cleans_up_its_roster_favourites`, which passed without needing this fix (that test's member reaches the source project via a *direct* `UserProjectRole`, not a group). Two new tests in `test_org_group_project_roles.py` (`test_grant_makes_the_project_appear_in_the_groups_members_own_project_list`, `test_nested_org_group_membership_also_appears_in_the_project_list`) cover both sources; the first would have failed (`StopIteration`/project missing from the listing) before this fix.
- **Verified (this addendum)**: `pytest tests/test_project_group_role_editing.py` — 10/10 (8 pre-existing + 2 new). `pytest tests/test_org_group_project_roles.py` — 18/18 (16 pre-existing + 2 new). Regression sweep of every file most directly exercising `_accessible_project_ids`/the RBAC provenance functions this addendum touches — `test_project_hierarchy.py`, `test_rbac.py`, `test_org_group_nesting.py`, `test_project_config.py`, `test_effective_members_provenance.py`, plus the two files above — **115/115 passed, 0 failed**. `ruff check` on both changed files clean.
- **Two stale docstrings corrected in passing** (module docstring's source count, `_direct_project_role_holder_ids`'s reference to an already-superseded `get_project_users_by_role` behaviour) — both directly inside text this change already had to edit for the new source, not a separate drive-by pass over the file.
- **`docs/solution-architecture.md` updated**: the identity/access-control ER diagram gains `ORG_GROUP_PROJECT_ROLE` and its two relationships, with explanatory prose distinguishing it from `PROJECT_GROUP_MEMBER`'s `org_group_id` arm; the table-count line and the "Identity, organisation membership, and access control" table list are corrected from 46 to 48 tables. **A second, unrelated pre-existing drift found and fixed in the same pass**: `project_member_sources` (present in the ER diagram and every migration/model since the "Hierarchical projects" entry above) had been missing from the table list entirely, undercounting by one independently of this PR's own new table — fixed alongside rather than left as a second, separately-discovered gap.

### Files changed

`backend/app/models/project.py`, `backend/app/models/__init__.py`; `backend/alembic/versions/0021_org_group_project_roles.py` (new); `backend/app/schemas/project.py`; `backend/app/routers/projects.py`; `backend/app/services/rbac.py`; `backend/tests/test_org_group_project_roles.py` (new); `backend/tests/test_project_group_role_editing.py` (addendum); `frontend/src/api/types.ts`; `docs/solution-architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Unified groups directory: combined user/group autocomplete, Groups tab merges member sources (PR5 of the follow-up UX batch, 2026-09)

Fifth PR of the batch — pure frontend, no backend changes, since PR4 already built both endpoints this PR consumes (`POST`/`DELETE /{project_id}/group-roles`). Two independent pieces, both scoped by the plan's own PR5 section: (1) the "Add member" button/`Modal` PR3 built (a user-only `UserAutocomplete` + role `<select>`) is expanded so its autocomplete also matches org groups by name, and selecting one grants it a role *directly* via PR4's mechanism; (2) the Groups tab's `DirectoryTable` merges in `ProjectMemberSource` rows, previously a structurally-disconnected section on the Overview tab.

**Corrected during this PR's own review, changing the original plan** (see the plan's PR3 section, "Decision (revised after PR4 landed...)"): the plan originally described two adjacent buttons, "Add member" and "Add group," with PR3 shipping the shell and PR5 filling in the second button. The corrected design has **no second button or modal for groups at all** — a single "Add member" control whose autocomplete search itself is expanded to match both users and org groups, distinguished by a badge in the results dropdown. Nesting a group inside another group (an org group inside a project group, or an org group inside another org group) is explicitly out of scope for this control — that composition stays exactly where it already was: a project group's own "nest an org group" affordance in its `SidePanel`, and an org group's own `SidePanel` for nesting a subgroup.

### Frontend

**`frontend/src/components/UserAutocomplete.tsx`** — new optional `groups?: OrgGroup[]`/`onSelectGroup?: (groupId: string) => void` prop pair. Group matching is *always* client-side against the passed-in array (mirroring the existing default, no-`organizationId` user-matching branch's own substring-on-`name` logic exactly), regardless of whether user matching in that same instance is running client- or server-side — there is no server-side group search endpoint, and none was needed: every call site already has the full org group list loaded for the Groups tab. `Option` becomes a three-way union (`user`/`group`/`external`); group matches render after user matches and before the external-invite option, each with a `Users` icon (`lucide-react`) and a "Group" text badge. **Icon choice**: grepped every existing group-related header/row in the app (Groups tab heading, Org Groups heading, a group row's own rendering) for a precedent icon first — none exists anywhere in this codebase for "a group of users" as a concept, only plain text. `Users` (plural) was picked over the singular `User` glyph implicitly used elsewhere, since it reads as "more than one person" without colliding with an already-claimed icon meaning. Keyboard nav (`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Enter`/`Escape`, `aria-activedescendant`) needed no new logic — it already walks the generic `options` array positionally, so it moves through group options automatically once they're part of that array; pinned by a new Storybook story (`KeyboardNavigationMovesThroughGroupOptionsToo`) rather than just trusted.

**`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`** — new `addProjectGroupRole(orgGroupId, role)` handler (`POST /{project_id}/group-roles`, then `reloadEffectiveMembers()` — same "re-fetch just effective-members, not a full `reload()`" convention `addProjectMember` already uses), wired as `onSelectGroup` on the Members tab's "Add member" modal's `UserAutocomplete`, passed `groups={orgGroups}` (already loaded for the Groups tab, no new fetch). **`OrgAdminPage.tsx`** — the identical `addManageUsersGroupRole` on the "Manage users" modal's own `UserAutocomplete`, passed `groups={allGroups}`.

**Groups tab merge** (`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`) — a new frontend-only `GroupsTabRow = {kind: "group"; group: ProjectGroup} | {kind: "member_source"; source: ProjectMemberSource}` union, the same pattern `ProjectMembersTable.tsx`'s own `member`/`invited` `Row` already established (not a new pattern invented for this PR). `groupsTabRows` puts every `memberSources` entry first (a small, always-fully-loaded fixed set), then the paginated/sortable `groups` — so `DirectoryTable`'s `LoadMoreButton` only ever appends more real groups after the fixed member-source rows, never reordering them; `total` is `groupsTotal + memberSources.length` to keep the "N of M loaded" count honest. A new "Type" column badges each row ("Project group" vs. "Project," both through `{Project}` terminology substitution — deliberately not "Org group," since a member source names another whole project this one mirrors members *from*, not an org group; see [ux-style-guide.md](ux-style-guide.md)'s new pattern below). `onRowClick` only opens the group `SidePanel` for `kind === "group"` rows; a member-source row is read-only detail rendered directly in its own cells (its mode/filter-role badge, and a "Remove" button reusing the existing `removeMemberSource` handler unchanged) rather than getting the real group's click-to-open/add-member affordances.

The Overview tab's old "Member sources" section (heading, `<ul>` list, and its inline add-controls) is removed entirely from Overview; its add-controls (the source-project/mirror-mode selects and "Add" button — same `addMemberSource`/`sourceCandidates`/`addSourceId`/`addMirrorMode`/`addMirrorFilterRole` state and validation, untouched) relocate onto the Groups tab as their own card below the merged `DirectoryTable`, keeping the "Member sources" heading so the control still has a name (and so this PR's Playwright updates below only needed a tab-navigation step added, not a wording change).

**`frontend/src/components/ProjectMembersTable.tsx`** — an incidental gap found while verifying this PR's own group-grant flow actually reads back correctly, not something the plan called out: `sourceLine`'s `switch` over `MemberSourceProvenanceKind` had no case for `direct_org_group_role` (PR4's new kind), falling through to the `default: return ""` branch — a group's direct grant would have rendered a *blank* Source cell for every member of that group, silently. Fixed with a `sourceDirectOrgGroupRole` string (`"Via group 'X' (direct)"` — distinct wording from `sourceDirectOrgGroup`'s "Via nested org group," since they're genuinely different mechanisms per PR4's own docstring) and the missing `case`. Per this repo's "fix, don't defer" rule, fixed in this same PR rather than filed separately, since it's directly in the path of the feature this PR builds.

### Tests

Storybook: `frontend/src/components/UserAutocomplete.stories.tsx` gained `GroupMatchRendersAndSelects` (a group match renders with the "Group" badge, click calls `onSelectGroup` not `onSelect`, and resets the input) and `KeyboardNavigationMovesThroughGroupOptionsToo` (arrow keys reach a group option, `Enter` selects it). `frontend/src/components/ProjectMembersTable.stories.tsx` gained `NamedOrgGroupRoleSourceLine`, pinning the `sourceLine` fix above and confirming the row's role checkbox is still checked-but-disabled (never a per-user toggle over a group-owned grant — see `isDirectRoleKind`'s own doc comment, PR4). `frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx` gained `MembersTabAddMemberAutocompleteMatchesGroup` (typing into "Add member" matches an org group, selecting it posts `/group-roles` with the currently-selected role, modal closes) and `GroupsTabShowsGroupsAndMemberSourcesTogether` (both row kinds render with their correct Type badge in the same table; the member-source row's "Remove" button calls `DELETE /member-sources/{id}`); `MemberSourcesListAndAdd` updated to navigate to the Groups tab first and assert against a `<tr>`/`<td>` instead of the retired `<ul>`/`<Link>`. `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx` gained the equivalent `ManageUsersModalAddMemberAutocompleteMatchesGroup`. Both page-level mock helpers (`mockProjectAdminApis`, `mockProjectsWorkflowWithOneProject`) gained an explicit `/users/search` branch (`{members: [], external: null}`) — needed once a story actually types into the autocomplete in `organizationId` mode; previously every story exercising that control stopped short of typing specifically to avoid triggering the unmocked debounced search.

Playwright: `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/project-hierarchy.spec.ts` — its three "Member sources" heading assertions updated to select the Groups tab first (`selectProjectAdminGroup(page, "Project groups")`) before asserting, and the row-shape assertions changed from `<li>`/`<Link>` to `<tr>`/`<td>` (a member-source row has no `<Link>` any more — see the read-only-detail decision above). ### Judgment calls and deviations from the plan

- **A member-source row's "Remove" action is a plain button in its own `DirectoryTable` cell, not something reached by clicking the row.** The plan's own wording ("read-only detail... and a way to remove the source") didn't specify the exact mechanic. `DirectoryTable`'s `onRowClick`/`rowHref` apply table-wide, not per-row, and are already committed to opening a real group's `SidePanel` for `kind === "group"` rows — reusing the same click for a member-source row would need either a second, meaningless "detail panel" with nothing more to show than what's already in the row, or a same-table-wide handler with an inert no-op branch for member-source rows (confusing: a first cell that looks clickable but silently does nothing). Putting Remove directly in its own column avoids both, and keeps the mode/filter-role detail directly visible in the row rather than gated behind a click, which is arguably better discoverability than the original Overview-tab list already had.
- **Dropped the member-source row's outbound `<Link>` to the source project** (present on the old Overview-tab `<li>` row) rather than finding a way to preserve it. Nesting a `<Link>` inside `DirectoryTable`'s own row-click `<button>` wrapper would be an invalid nested-interactive-elements pattern; adding a second "View" action alongside "Remove" was considered and rejected as unnecessary scope growth for a control this PR's own constraints ask to keep minimal ("if you find yourself needing more than one action... keep it minimal, note it for PR6"). The source project is still reachable via the existing "Parent project"/global search paths; this is a minor, explicitly-noted regression, not a silent one.
- **`sourceDirectOrgGroupRole`'s missing `switch` case was fixed as an incidental bug, not filed separately** — per this repo's standing "fix, don't defer" rule, and because it sits directly in the render path of the feature this PR adds a UI entry point for (a group grant with no visible Source text would have made the whole feature look broken the first time someone used it).
- **No `docs/decisions.md`-mandated identify → verify → remediate write-up** for this entry, unlike PR2/PR4 — the plan's own sequencing note reserves that rigor for PRs that change or add an access-control pathway; this PR only adds UI on top of PR4's already-reviewed mechanism and moves presentation of already-existing data, with no new backend code and no change to any authorization check.

## Project group roles become independent grants (PR7 of the follow-up UX batch, 2026-09)

Seventh PR of the batch, moved ahead of PR6 in execution order (see the plan's own "Sequencing" note) and given the same identify → verify → remediate rigor as PR2/PR4 — the plan's own explicit instruction, since this is **the most invasive PR in the whole batch**: it doesn't just add a new grant pathway alongside an existing one (PR4's shape) or fix a redaction gap (PR2's shape), it changes the *meaning* of an existing, previously-required field. `ProjectGroup.role` — a single value fixed at creation, the only role a group could ever grant — is replaced by `ProjectGroupRole`, a separate grant table: a group now holds zero, one, or several independently-revocable roles, mirroring the exact shape PR4's `OrgGroupProjectRole` established one level up (org group → project role) and `UserProjectRole` established for a single user — "one row per role," confirmed with the product owner explicitly as "the same as users with multiple roles," never an array/JSON column.

### Identify

Read `backend/app/models/project.py`'s `ProjectGroup`/`OrgGroupProjectRole` (the exact structural precedent to mirror), `backend/app/routers/projects.py`'s full project-groups section (`create_project_group` through `remove_project_group_member`, plus `assign_group_project_role`/`revoke_group_project_role`, PR4's closest precedent), `backend/app/services/rbac.py`'s whole provenance-resolution area, the current Alembic head, `backend/tests/test_project_group_role_editing.py`/`test_default_group_migration.py` (existing coverage and the Phase C migration-test precedent to copy), and the frontend's `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` Groups tab / `UserAutocomplete.tsx` (PR5's current state) before changing anything. The plan itself flagged that its own guesses at "which functions need this" might be wrong and told this pass to verify by grepping rather than trust the plan's list — that grep surfaced real drift in both directions:

1. **Every literal reference to `ProjectGroup.role`/`group.role`**, found by grepping the whole backend rather than trusting the plan's enumerated list: `backend/app/routers/projects.py` — `_ensure_project_has_a_manager`'s fallback-group lookup (not named in the plan at all), `create_project_group`, `list_project_groups`, `_project_group_out`, `update_project_group`/`ProjectGroupUpdate` (the whole endpoint+schema, since there is no longer a single field to `PATCH`), `delete_project_group`'s C-U-08 guard, `remove_project_group_member`'s C-U-08 guard. `backend/app/services/rbac.py` — the `direct_group` branch (Step 3's own scope) *and* two sites the plan's Step 3 text didn't name: the `direct_org_group` nesting branch's own enclosing-group role read (source 3 also grants "the enclosing `ProjectGroup`'s role," so it needed the identical treatment) and the source-7 project-referencing-group branch (the *referencing* group's role, not the source project's). All three read the granting `ProjectGroup`'s role and all three needed the same one-row-per-(group,role) join rewrite as the `direct_group` branch the plan did name. Also `_direct_project_role_holder_ids` (three call sites) and `_direct_project_roles_excluding_org_wide` (two call sites) — matching the plan's guidance. And, **not named by the plan at all**: `_direct_project_managers`, the function `get_effective_project_managers` (the actual C-U-08 "at least one manager" check) is built on — missing this would have left the primary manager-floor guard querying a column the migration was about to drop, breaking project creation/every guard site outright the moment the column left the schema. `backend/app/services/project_export.py` (bundle export/import) and `backend/app/services/templates.py` (`clone_project`) also read/write `group.role`/`role=payload.role` and needed the `roles`-list equivalent — neither named in the plan's file list.
2. **`_direct_project_member_ids_base`'s `ProjectGroupMember` arms never actually referenced `ProjectGroup.role` at all**, contrary to the plan's assumption that all three "sibling helpers" PR4 extended read the scalar directly — grepping confirmed this function has no `ProjectGroup.role` reference anywhere; it already treats any group membership (regardless of role) as "belongs to this project's roster," which was harmless while every group necessarily had exactly one role. A first pass left this deliberately unchanged, reasoning membership and role-holding were separate concepts elsewhere in this module — see Verify below for why that reasoning was wrong in practice and had to be reversed.
3. **The current migration head** (`alembic history`, not a line-number guess): `0021` ("Direct org-group project role grants," PR4's own new migration), so this PR's migration chains as `0022`.
4. **Whether `ProjectGroupUpdate`/`PATCH /projects/{id}/groups/{group_id}` has any other reason to exist once `role` is gone.** It doesn't — a `ProjectGroup` has only ever had `name` (no rename endpoint, matching `OrgGroup`) and `role`; with `role` moved to its own grant table, the endpoint has nothing left to update and was removed entirely, not left as a dead stub.

### Verify

- **Ran the new migration against the live local test database both directions** (`alembic upgrade head` / `alembic downgrade 0021` / re-`upgrade head`) before writing any test for it, against a database already carrying real pre-existing `project_groups` rows from other work in this session — confirmed the backfill and the lossy-but-safe downgrade (picks the highest-privilege role a group holds; a zero-role group falls back to `'member'`, matching how a freshly-created post-PR7 group with no grants yet would have looked under the old required-field shape) both run cleanly against real data, not just a hand-built fixture.
- **`test_schema_migrations_match_models.py` (this repo's own drift guard) failed on first real run** — not against this PR's own new table, but against a **pre-existing gap already present in the working tree from PR4**: `OrgGroupProjectRole.org_group_id`/`.project_id` had no `index=True` even though migration `0021` already creates `ix_org_group_project_roles_org_group_id`/`_project_id` explicitly, so `Base.metadata` never matched the live schema for that table either — the drift test would have failed for PR4's table regardless of anything in this PR. Fixed alongside this PR's own identical new gap (`ProjectGroupRole.project_group_id` needed the same `index=True`) rather than left as a second, separately-discovered problem, per this repo's "fix, don't defer" rule — both are in `backend/app/models/project.py`, directly adjacent to code this PR already had to touch.
- **Confirmed, by writing a listing-visibility test and watching it fail before investigating why, a second real regression this PR's own schema change introduced**: `_accessible_project_ids`'s `project_ids_via_group` (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`, the function behind `GET /projects`) joined only `ProjectGroup`→`ProjectGroupMember`, with no role check at all — meaning a user whose *only* connection to a project was membership in a group that had just had its *last* role revoked still appeared in their own `GET /projects` listing, and (via the identical join shape in `rbac._direct_project_member_ids_base`) could still be pulled into an *unrelated* project through the project-reference mechanism, or still get notified via `get_project_member_user_ids`, despite `get_effective_project_roles` — the actual authoritative access check — already correctly seeing zero roles for them. This directly invalidated the Identify-phase reasoning that left `_direct_project_member_ids_base` unfiltered (finding 2 above): "membership without role still counts" was fine when every group had exactly one role by construction, but the schema change this PR makes broke that invariant, and a test proved the consequence concretely rather than the change being caught only by reasoning about it. Both `_accessible_project_ids`'s `project_ids_via_group` and `_direct_project_member_ids_base`'s two `ProjectGroupMember` arms now require an `EXISTS`/`JOIN` against `ProjectGroupRole` — a group's membership only counts (for listing visibility, project-reference roster resolution, and notification targeting alike) while that group still holds at least one role, consistent with what the authoritative check already required.
- **Checked every SQL join this PR added compiles and executes correctly, not just reads correctly** — three of the rewritten `rbac.py` queries (`direct_group_rows`, `nested_group_rows`, `project_ref_rows`) initially raised `psycopg2.errors.UndefinedTable`/`missing FROM-clause entry`: selecting `ProjectGroupRole.role` without `ProjectGroup` also appearing as a selected column meant SQLAlchemy never added `project_groups` to the FROM/JOIN chain at all, since nothing in the original `.join(ProjectGroupMember, ... == ProjectGroup.id)` call established `ProjectGroup` as a join anchor when `ProjectGroup` itself wasn't part of the select. Fixed by explicitly joining `ProjectGroup` first (`.join(ProjectGroup, ProjectGroup.id == ProjectGroupRole.project_group_id)`) before any join that references it in its `ON` clause — caught by actually running the new test module against the live database, not by code review alone; the three call sites this affected are exactly the three "not named in the plan" rewrites in Identify finding 1.
- **Checked for escalation beyond what a single role already allowed**, the specific question the plan called out: multiplicity (a group holding several roles at once) only ever produces the *union* of what each of those roles individually grants a user through the group's existing membership — the exact same union any of that group's members could already reach one role at a time by being granted each role via a *separate* group (already proven possible, and already tested, since PR1). No new capability, no new bypass, and no code path treats "holds N roles" as anything other than N independent, individually-revocable entries — `get_effective_project_members_with_provenance`'s existing per-kind loop (unchanged by this PR) already renders one Source row per entry regardless of how many a single group contributes, the same generic mechanism that already handled two *different* groups granting the same role (PR1) now also correctly handles one group granting two *different* roles, with no special-casing needed on either side.
- **Read `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md`** before touching the guard sites (per the change-management policy's practice). Its Authorization items (project role scoped to one project; every check resolves from the specific target's own ID) are unaffected in shape — every guard site still resolves from `project_id`/`group_id` exactly as before, just checking a joined table instead of a scalar column. No policy wording update needed, matching PR2/PR4's identical conclusion.

### Remediate

**Backend**
- New model `ProjectGroupRole` (`backend/app/models/project.py`, placed immediately after `OrgGroupProjectRole`) — `project_group_id` (FK `project_groups.id`, `ondelete="CASCADE"`, indexed), `role` (`ProjectRole`), unique on `(project_group_id, role)`. No separate `project_id` column, unlike `OrgGroupProjectRole` — a `ProjectGroup` already belongs to exactly one project by construction. `ProjectGroup.role` removed from the model entirely; its docstring rewritten to document the new shape and point at this entry.
- New migration `backend/alembic/versions/0022_project_group_roles.py` (`0021` → `0022`): creates `project_group_roles` + index, backfills exactly one row per existing `project_groups.role` value (`INSERT ... SELECT ... ON CONFLICT (project_group_id, role) DO NOTHING`, guarded by the same `IF EXISTS (information_schema.columns ...)` check `0014`/`0017`/`0018`/`0019` already use so a fresh database's `create_all()`-based schema — which never has the `role` column at all — is a safe no-op), then drops `project_groups.role` — the exact "backfill then drop in one migration" convention `0019`'s `is_default` removal established, chosen deliberately over a two-migration approach so there is never an intermediate revision with both the old and new shapes half-coexisting. Downgrade is lossy for a group holding more than one role (documented, same acknowledged lossiness `0019`'s own downgrade has) — picks the highest-privilege role rather than an arbitrary one, so a downgrade never silently drops a manager grant down to a lesser role.
- New schema `ProjectGroupRoleAssign` (`role: ProjectRole` — no `group_id` field needed, unlike `OrgGroupProjectRoleAssign`'s `org_group_id`, since the target group is already named by the URL path and needs no cross-tenant re-validation). `ProjectGroupCreate.role` removed. `ProjectGroupUpdate` removed entirely (Identify finding 4). `ProjectGroupOut.role` → `roles: list[ProjectRole]`.
- New endpoints in `backend/app/routers/projects.py`, replacing `update_project_group`: `POST /{project_id}/groups/{group_id}/roles` (`assign_project_group_role`) and `DELETE /{project_id}/groups/{group_id}/roles/{role}` (`revoke_project_group_role`) — mirror `assign_group_project_role`/`revoke_group_project_role` (PR4) as closely as sensible: same 204-no-body shape, same idempotent-grant-is-a-silent-no-op behaviour, same audit-log pattern. No cross-tenant re-check (unlike PR4's `org_group_id` validation) since a `ProjectGroup` already belongs to exactly one project. `create_project_group` now creates a bare group (zero roles); `list_project_groups`/`_project_group_out` compute `roles` from a live join instead of reading a stored scalar (same "reads live at query time, never a value copied at member-add/creation time" property `update_project_group` used to have).
- **Every C-U-08 "must retain a manager" guard site changed from `group.role == PROJECT_MANAGER` to "does this group currently hold a `PROJECT_MANAGER` row in `ProjectGroupRole`"**, explicitly enumerated (Identify finding 1): `_ensure_project_has_a_manager`'s fallback-group lookup (`create_project`'s manager-guarantee, template-clone-adjacent path), `delete_project_group`, `remove_project_group_member`, and the new `revoke_project_group_role` (the group-scoped guard site this PR itself adds — shaped like `delete_project_group`'s lock-then-recheck-after pattern, since a role revocation can remove access from every member of the group at once, not a single-user pre-check). Unlike PR4's org-group-role guard (defense-in-depth only, since a nested/direct-grant org group's managers have never counted toward the C-U-08 floor at all), **this one is the actually load-bearing guard for its mechanism**: `_direct_project_managers` *does* count a `ProjectGroup`'s direct user members toward the floor when the group holds `PROJECT_MANAGER` (unchanged behaviour, just re-pointed at the new table) — so `revoke_project_group_role`'s guard is what a real "last manager" scenario actually trips on, not just a defensive backstop.
- `backend/app/services/rbac.py`: the `direct_group` branch and the two additional sites Identify finding 1 surfaced (the `direct_org_group` nesting branch's enclosing-group role, the source-7 project-reference branch's referencing-group role) now join through `ProjectGroupRole` instead of reading a scalar, each producing one entry per (group, granted role) pair — mirroring PR4's `direct_org_group_role` extension pattern exactly, per the plan's own instruction. `_direct_project_role_holder_ids`, `_direct_project_roles_excluding_org_wide`, and `_direct_project_managers` (the last not named by the plan — Identify finding 1) all gained the equivalent rewrite. `_direct_project_member_ids_base` and `_accessible_project_ids`'s `project_ids_via_group` both gained a new `ProjectGroupRole` join requirement (Verify finding above) — a correction to the Identify-phase's own first-pass reasoning, not a plan-specified change. Module docstring's source-2 entry and every touched function's docstring updated.
- `backend/app/services/project_export.py`: `groups_json` export/import now round-trips `roles` (a list) instead of `role`; import reads either `"roles"` (current shape) or a legacy `"role"` singular key (a bundle exported before this PR), so an older export can still be imported without losing its group's role. `backend/app/services/templates.py`: `clone_project` copies every `ProjectGroupRole` row a template's group holds, not just one.
- `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`: `create_project_group` now creates bare then grants the role via the new endpoint (two calls instead of one), matching how the frontend and every other caller now has to.

**Frontend**
- `frontend/src/api/types.ts`: `ProjectGroup.role` → `roles: ProjectRole[]`. `isDirectRoleKind`'s doc comment extended to note `direct_group` (this PR) is now, like `direct_org_group_role` (PR4), backed by a genuine per-role revocable row — and, for the identical blast-radius reason PR4's entry already gives, deliberately still excluded from this predicate (a toggle on one member's row must never silently revoke a *group's* role for every other member at once).
- `frontend/src/components/MultiSelectDropdown.tsx` reused (not extended) for two new call sites in `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`: the Groups tab's per-row "role" column, and the group's own `SidePanel` role editor — both replace the old fixed-role `<select>`/badge, both call the same new `toggleProjectGroupRole(groupId, role, checked)` handler, and both share a client-side "last manager" hint (`groupManagerSourceCount`) with the identical `cannotRemoveLastManager` title text `ProjectMembersTable.tsx`'s own Role column already uses — the same shared-component reuse this repo's style guide requires rather than a third bespoke implementation.
- "New group" modal: role `<select>` removed entirely; `createProjectGroup` no longer sends `role`. A freshly created group's row/panel shows "No roles assigned" (`MultiSelectDropdown`'s own `emptyLabel`) until a role is granted.
- `frontend/src/components/UserAutocomplete.tsx`: new optional `projectGroups?: ProjectGroup[]`/`onSelectProjectGroup?: (groupId: string) => void` prop pair, following `groups`/`onSelectGroup`'s (PR5) exact pattern — client-side substring match against the passed-in array, rendered after org-group matches and before the external-invite option. **Visual distinction from an org-group match** (the plan's own explicit requirement, since the two are genuinely different concepts — a project group is local to one project, an org group is org-wide): `FolderKanban` (the same icon `Layout.tsx`'s nav rail already uses for "Projects," reused rather than inventing a fourth group-adjacent icon) instead of `Users`, and a "Project group" badge instead of "Group"/"Org group." The existing org-group badge text was tightened from the original bare "Group" to "Org group" at the same time — see "Judgment calls" below.
- `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s "Add member" modal: the same `UserAutocomplete` instance now also matches project groups (`projectGroups={memberTableGroups}`, the tab's own already-loaded unpaginated group list). Per the product owner's confirmed answer, picking a project group does **not** grant it a role (unlike picking a user or an org group) — it switches the same modal into a second step, "add someone to this group," reusing the existing `addGroupMember`/`addOrgGroupMember` handlers (`POST .../groups/{group_id}/members`, no new backend call) via a second, nested `UserAutocomplete` instance (itself without a `projectGroups` prop, so this can't recurse a second level deep) scoped to that one group. A "Back" control returns to the first step without adding anything.

### Tests

Rewrote `backend/tests/test_project_group_role_editing.py` in place (its old coverage was entirely `PATCH /groups/{group_id}`, an endpoint that no longer exists) — 21 tests: bare creation with an empty `roles` list (plus a defense check that a stray legacy `role` field in the payload is silently ignored, not erroring), grant/revoke with provenance (`kind="direct_group"`, `via_group_id`/`via_group_name`), idempotent grant, no-op revoke of a never-granted role, gating (403 below manage tier, 200 for an org admin with no project role), audit logging (grant/revoke, idempotent-grant-doesn't-double-log), **a group holding two roles producing two separate provenance entries** (the core new-behaviour test, plus a regression check that two *different* groups granting the same role — PR1's original case — still also produces two entries, unchanged), every C-U-08 guard site in its new per-role form (revoke-blocked-when-sole-manager, revoke-allowed-with-backup, delete-blocked/-allowed, and a group holding `project_manager` *alongside* another role still correctly guarded on delete), and the two pre-existing engagement-cleanup regression pins (nested-org-group/project-reference removal) carried over adapted to the new bare-then-grant creation shape, plus a new one for the revoke endpoint's own cleanup path.

New `backend/tests/test_project_group_role_migration.py` (3 tests, following `test_default_group_migration.py`'s exact downgrade/seed/upgrade-via-real-migration technique): a single group's role survives as exactly one grant row (plus its live effect on `effective-members` provenance, not just the stored row); all four `ProjectRole` values backfill correctly, including a zero-member group; the backfill's `ON CONFLICT` idempotency guard doesn't error or duplicate if re-run. Project/user setup deliberately happens *before* entering the downgraded-schema window in every test here (and, after the fix below, in `test_default_group_migration.py` too) — see Verify's SQL-join-bug finding's sibling issue: `create_project`'s manager-fallback needs the new table to exist, so it can't run while downgraded past this PR's own migration.

**Fixed as a direct consequence of this PR's schema change, not a new feature**: `backend/tests/test_default_group_migration.py`'s two existing tests broke the moment `_ensure_project_has_a_manager` started depending on `project_group_roles` — both downgrade to `0018`, which now also removes this PR's table, and both called `create_project` *inside* that downgraded window. Restructured to create the project/users first, matching the new tests' own ordering; one assertion (`reloaded["role"]`) updated to `reloaded["roles"] == [...]`.

**Sibling test files updated for the `ProjectGroupCreate.role` removal** — a mechanical but real consequence found by grepping every `POST .../groups` call site across the suite (pydantic silently drops an unknown `role` field rather than erroring, so these would have failed quietly downstream at whatever later assertion depended on the role actually being granted, not loudly at the call site itself): `test_api_lifecycles.py`, `test_audit_fixes.py`, `test_effective_members_provenance.py` (gained a small `_create_group_with_role` helper, used at all 9 of its own call sites), `test_org_group_nesting.py`, `test_org_group_project_roles.py`, `test_project_hierarchy.py`, `test_rbac.py`, `test_scim.py`, `test_security_hardening.py` — each either drops the now-inert `role` key (where the test's own assertions never depended on it) or adds the follow-up `POST .../groups/{id}/roles` call (where they do).

**Playwright**: `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`'s "create a new project group" step rewritten for the simplified modal (asserts the role `<label>` is gone, the fresh row reads "No roles assigned," then grants a role via the new row `MultiSelectDropdown` and asserts the badge updates) and extended with a new step exercising the "Add member" autocomplete's project-group match end to end (types into the search, asserts the "Project group" badge distinguishing it from an "Org group" match, picks it, confirms the modal switches to its second "add to this group" step with no grant call fired, fills the nested autocomplete, and confirms "Back" returns to the first step cleanly); its throwaway API-created fixture group also had its now-inert `role` field dropped. `role-display-collapsing.spec.ts` (three project groups created purely to exercise its role-tier-collapsing assertions) and `project-admin-members.spec.ts` (one group whose granted role a later assertion directly depends on) both updated from single-call role-at-creation to the bare-then-grant two-call shape — the former via the new `MultiSelectDropdown` UI interaction (matching how a real user would now do this), the latter via the equivalent direct API call (already using API setup for its own fixture). `project-hierarchy.spec.ts`'s one throwaway project-reference group had its inert `role` field dropped, since that test never exercised the group's granted access. Per this PR's own scope, these specs were mechanically updated/written but not executed against the Docker Compose stack — the plan's own verification step runs the full spec suite once, after all planned work lands.

### Verified
