### Judgment calls and deviations from the plan

- **Two real, previously-passing tests broken by this PR's own schema change, both fixed in the same pass rather than deferred**: `test_schema_migrations_match_models.py` failing against PR4's own pre-existing (not this PR's) index-declaration gap, and `test_default_group_migration.py`'s two tests breaking because `create_project` now needs a table this PR's migration adds while they're testing a *different, earlier* migration's downgrade window. Neither is this PR's own bug in the sense of "code this PR wrote is wrong" — both are real regressions this PR's change caused in code/tests it didn't otherwise need to touch — flagged explicitly here rather than silently fixed with no record, per this repo's "flag rather than silently diverge" rule, even though both are clearly correct to fix rather than leave broken.
- **`_direct_project_member_ids_base` and `_accessible_project_ids`'s `project_ids_via_group` were changed beyond what the plan's Step 3 literally asked for.** The plan named `_direct_project_role_holder_ids`, `_direct_project_member_ids_base`, and `_direct_project_roles_excluding_org_wide` as "the three sibling helpers PR4 already extended" needing the equivalent treatment — but `_direct_project_member_ids_base` never actually read `ProjectGroup.role` at all (Identify finding 2), so there was nothing analogous to "join through the grant table instead of a scalar" to do there. A first pass concluded no change was needed and documented that reasoning in the function's own docstring; a listing-visibility test written for an unrelated assertion failed and traced back to this exact function (and its `_accessible_project_ids` sibling, not named by the plan at all) genuinely needing a new `ProjectGroupRole` existence check that didn't exist as a concept before this PR's schema change — see Verify above. Reversed the first-pass decision and documented why in both functions' docstrings, rather than leaving the incorrect reasoning in place alongside a silent behavioural fix.
- **`ProjectGroupUpdate`/`PATCH /projects/{id}/groups/{group_id}` removed entirely rather than left as a deprecated stub.** The plan didn't explicitly say to remove the endpoint, only that `create_project_group` should drop `role` from its payload — but once `role` is the *only* thing a `ProjectGroup` had ever exposed for update (no rename endpoint exists, matching `OrgGroup`), keeping a `PATCH` with nothing left to patch would be dead code, not backward compatibility (no meaningful request body remains for it to accept). Removed outright, replaced by the two new grant/revoke endpoints.
- **The autocomplete's org-group badge text was changed from "Group" to "Org group"**, alongside adding "Project group" for the new match kind — not requested by the plan, but leaving the existing bare "Group" text next to a new "Project group" badge in the same dropdown would read as an unexplained inconsistency (why does one group concept get a generic label and the other a specific one) rather than the two being genuinely parallel, equally-specific concepts. Every Storybook/Playwright assertion checking for the literal string "Group" was updated to "Org group" (four call sites — `project-admin-groups-and-fields.spec.ts`, `UserAutocomplete.stories.tsx`, `ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`, `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`).
- **The "add someone to this project group" second step (Add-member modal) reuses a second, nested `UserAutocomplete` instance rather than inventing a new control.** The plan's own wording ("selecting an existing project group adds the picked user (or org group) as a member of it via the existing `add_project_group_member` endpoint") is compatible with more than one concrete UI shape; the two-step modal reuses the *exact* existing user-or-org-group matching/selection logic (just without the `projectGroups` prop, so it can't recurse into a third level) rather than building a bespoke second picker, keeping this PR's frontend surface to "compose existing pieces" rather than "add a fifth reimplementation of a search-and-pick control."
- **A pre-existing, unrelated documentation drift found and fixed in the same pass**: `docs/solution-architecture.md`'s "One diagram covering all N tables" sentence had been left at a stale "45" through at least the two most recent table additions (`org_group_project_roles`, `project_member_sources`'s own re-add) — both of which updated the table count/list further down the same page but missed this earlier mention. Fixed alongside this PR's own table-count update (48 → 49) rather than left as a second, separately-discovered gap.

## Per-row action menus: per-user/per-group materialize, org-user removal, "Add to group" reachability fix (PR6 of the follow-up UX batch, 2026-09)

Sixth PR of the batch, held to last per the plan's own sequencing note ("PR6's access-mutating actions... get the same review rigor as F/PR4, so they're held to last, after the lower-risk UI work, and depend on PR4's grant mechanism existing to write into"). This entry covers a resumed pass: a previous session had already built the two backend materialize endpoints (`POST /{project_id}/materialize-inherited-access/{user_id}` and `.../group/{org_group_id}`, `backend/app/routers/projects.py`, plus `get_group_inherited_project_roles` in `backend/app/services/rbac.py`) before being interrupted — confirmed complete and importing cleanly before writing anything further, per this pass's own explicit verification step, rather than trusting the interruption summary. Everything else below (their tests, the frontend UI, the org-removal endpoint, the reachability fix, and the no-org-user robustness check) was built in this pass.

### Identify

Per the plan's own "Step 0" verification list, checked before writing any code rather than assumed:

1. `materialize_inherited_access_for_user`/`materialize_inherited_access_for_group` (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`) and `get_group_inherited_project_roles` (`backend/app/services/rbac.py`) exist, are complete (not truncated mid-function), import cleanly (`python -c "import app.routers.projects"`), and `get_group_inherited_project_roles` is correctly imported into `projects.py`. All confirmed.
2. Grepped `backend/tests/*.py` for any existing coverage of these two endpoints or their URL paths — none found.
3. Grepped `ProjectMembersTable.tsx` for `ActionMenu` — not present; the per-row actions column didn't exist yet.
4. Grepped `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s Users table actions column — still two bare buttons (`Eye`/`Lock`/`Unlock`), not an `ActionMenu`.
5. Grepped the whole backend for an existing "remove user from org" endpoint. Found `DELETE /{organization_id}/membership` (`leave_organization`, self-service only — the caller removes their own membership), `POST /{organization_id}/users/{user_id}/deactivate` (sets `is_active=False` on the *whole account*, a cross-org lockout, not a per-org membership removal), and `POST .../archive` (hides an already-deactivated user from lists, doesn't touch membership rows). No admin-initiated removal of *another* user's org membership existed — this is genuinely new, not a rename of something already there.
6. `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/no-org-user.spec.ts` didn't exist.
7. Read `ActionMenu.tsx` (reused verbatim, no new kebab-menu component built), `ConfirmDialog.tsx` (the Tier-1 plain-confirm shape — no `requireTypedText`, matching `PreferencesPage.tsx`'s own "Leave organisation" confirm's severity, not the org-deletion Tier-2 shape), and `ProjectMembersTable.tsx`'s current `Row`/column structure (post-PR1/PR5: `kind: "member" | "invited"`, a `MultiSelectDropdown` Role column already computing a per-role "purely `direct_role`" check for its own disable logic).
8. `revoke_project_role` and PR4's `assign_group_project_role`/`revoke_group_project_role` as the precedent shape for the mutations the new UI calls into (idempotent grant, 204 on no-op revoke, `require_project_manage` gate).
9. `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s `addGroupMember` handler (existing, unchanged, reused directly) and the Roles `MultiSelectDropdown`'s self-targeting guard (`u.user_id === user?.id`, mirroring the backend's `revoke_org_role`/`deactivate_org_user` self-targeting blocks) — the precedent shape for "Remove from {org}"'s own self-targeting guard below.

### Verify

- **The "last-admin guard" originally written for `remove_org_user` turned out to be unreachable dead code, caught before shipping it, not after.** A first draft mirrored `leave_organization`'s "the org must retain at least one admin" count check directly. Working through it against `remove_org_user`'s own preconditions — the caller must already hold `ORG_ADMIN` on this exact organisation (`require_org_role`), and self-targeting is blocked earlier in the same function — shows the caller is *necessarily* a second, distinct `ORG_ADMIN` still present after any removal they perform on someone else, for every `user_id` the endpoint can ever legally be called with. This is the identical "by construction" reasoning `revoke_org_role` already documents for itself in this codebase (not `leave_organization`'s reachable version, where caller and target are the same person) — the check could never fire through the live API, sequentially or under the row lock's protected concurrency, so shipping it would have been misleading dead code rather than real defense-in-depth. Removed the count-check branch, replaced it with a docstring bullet spelling out the "by construction" reasoning explicitly (mirroring `revoke_org_role`'s own), and pinned the reasoning with a test that exercises the real, reachable shape instead (`test_remove_org_user_cannot_zero_out_org_admins`: a co-admin removes the *other* admin, then confirms their own admin access survives) rather than a test asserting an impossible 409.
- **The sole-project-manager guard, by contrast, is real and reachable** — confirmed by the same reasoning, in the other direction: an org admin's own `ORG_ADMIN` status does not imply *any* project role (PR2's whole "org admin sees hierarchy without a role" premise), so the target being removed can genuinely be the sole real manager of a project the caller has no role on at all. Built as a close mirror of `leave_organization`'s own identical check, applied to the target instead of the caller — `test_remove_org_user_blocked_if_target_is_sole_project_manager` exercises this for real, not via DB manipulation.
- **"Remove all access" eligibility checked at the member-row level, not the per-role level.** The Role `MultiSelectDropdown`'s existing `purelyDirect` check is per-role (a member can hold one role that's purely direct and another that's group-sourced). Looping the per-role `DELETE` over only a member's *currently-held direct roles* while a non-direct role silently remains would leave real access in place under an action labelled "Remove all access" — a correctness bug had the eligibility check been copied at the wrong granularity. `ProjectMembersTable.tsx`'s new `allDirectRoleSourced` check requires *every* source entry on the row to be `direct_role`-kind before the action is offered at all, not just the specific role(s) being revoked.
- Read `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md` before writing `remove_org_user` (per the change-management policy's practice for anything access-mutating). Its Authorization items are unaffected in shape: the endpoint resolves everything from `organization_id`/`user_id` in the URL, gated by `require_org_role(ORG_ADMIN)` (already-established), no new scope introduced. No policy wording update needed.
- Checked the two per-target materialize endpoints' own idempotency/rank-selection logic directly against the bulk endpoint's `_ROLE_RANK` table (both endpoints literally redeclare the same dict inline, matching the bulk endpoint's own style) rather than assuming it was correct from the interrupted attempt's docstrings alone — `test_materialize_for_user_selects_highest_ranked_inherited_role`/`test_materialize_for_group_selects_highest_ranked_inherited_role` construct a user/group with two inherited roles at different ranks and assert only the higher one is written, pinning the selection logic empirically.

### Remediate

**Backend**
- `backend/app/routers/orgs.py`: new `DELETE /{organization_id}/users/{user_id}/membership` (`remove_org_user`), placed immediately before `deactivate_org_user`. Gated by `require_org_role(ORG_ADMIN)`. Self-targeting blocked (400, directs the caller to `leave_organization` instead). No separate last-admin count check (Verify above). Sole-project-manager guard mirroring `leave_organization`'s own. Cleanup mirrors `leave_organization`'s exact shape, applied to `user_id` instead of `current_user.id`: every `UserProjectRole`/`ProjectGroupMember` row across this org's projects, every `OrgGroupMember` row for this org's groups, subscriptions/favourites (`engagement.remove_subscriptions_and_favorites_for_projects`), then this org's own `UserOrgRole` rows last. Row-locks the organisation before the admin check and each project before its own manager check (`lock_organization_for_update`/`lock_project_for_update`), same ordering as `leave_organization`. 404 if `user_id` isn't currently a member. Audited (`entity_type="user_org_role"`, `action="removed_from_organization"`).

**Frontend**
- `frontend/src/components/ProjectMembersTable.tsx`: new Actions column (only rendered when the caller supplies `onRemoveAllAccess`/`onConvertToDirect`), one `ActionMenu` per member row. "Remove all access" offered only when `allDirectRoleSourced` (every source is `direct_role`-kind) — behind the table's own `ConfirmDialog` (Tier 1), which calls the caller's `onRemoveAllAccess(userId)` on confirm. "Convert inherited access to direct roles" offered only when the member has a `forward_inherited`/`member_source_inherited` source — calls `onConvertToDirect(userId)` directly (additive, no confirm step, matching the bulk button's own confirm-free treatment). Both props wired in `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` (`removeAllProjectMemberAccess`/`convertProjectMemberToDirect`) and `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s "Manage users" modal (`removeAllManageUsersMemberAccess`/`convertManageUsersMemberToDirect`) — each loops the existing per-role `DELETE /roles/{user_id}/{role}` over the member's currently-held roles, or calls the new per-user materialize endpoint, then refreshes `effective-members` the same way `toggleProjectMemberRole` already does.
- New `frontend/src/components/AddToGroupControl.tsx`: a small `Popover`-based quick-pick (a `<select>` of the org's groups the user isn't already in, filtered client-side, plus Add/Cancel) reusing the caller's existing `addGroupMember(groupId, userId)` handler — no new backend call. Kept as its own small control next to (not inside) the Users table's `ActionMenu`, not because the style guide asks for that specifically, but because `ActionMenu`'s items are plain `onSelect` callbacks with no way to host a second component's own anchored `Popover` trigger — a real implementation constraint, not a style preference (see "Judgment calls" below).
- `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx`: Users table Actions column consolidates the two previously-bare buttons (View access, lock/unlock display name) into one `ActionMenu`, adds "Remove from {org}" (withheld on the caller's own row — self-removal routes to the existing "Leave organisation" flow instead, matching the backend's self-targeting guard) behind a Tier-1 `ConfirmDialog` calling the new endpoint, and renders `AddToGroupControl` alongside it (reusing the page's own already-loaded `allGroups`, no refetch).
- `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`: new `membersTable`/`orgAdmin` entries for all of the above, following the existing per-namespace convention (functions for parameterised copy, `{project}`/`{org}` template placeholders left for the terminology-substitution layer).

### Tests

No crash, hang, or console error found — the app shell already degrades correctly for a zero-org user, so nothing needed fixing as a result of this check (the "Additional test" note's own expected outcome when the rest of this session's work hasn't introduced a regression, not evidence the check was skipped).

### Judgment calls and deviations from the plan

- **The last-admin guard originally planned for `remove_org_user` was dropped in favour of a "by construction" docstring, rather than built as literally instructed.** The plan's Step 3 asked for "a last-admin guard mirroring the existing self-targeting-guard precedent... a org must always retain at least one admin, same shape as this codebase's other 'must retain at least one X' guards." Building it as asked, then verifying it before shipping (this repo's own change-management practice), showed it can never fire through the live endpoint — see Verify above. Flagged explicitly here rather than silently shipping either the dead check or a silent deviation from the plan's literal wording.
- **`AddToGroupControl` is a separate control next to `ActionMenu`, not a fourth item inside it.** The plan's wording ("a quick popover/small menu listing the org's groups") doesn't mandate it live inside the kebab specifically — but `ActionMenu`'s `items` are plain `{label, icon, onSelect: () => void}` rows with no way to host a second component's own anchored `Popover` trigger without changing `ActionMenu`'s own contract for every existing call site. A separate small icon-button-plus-`Popover` control, reusing `Popover` directly (the same component `ActionMenu` itself is built on), was judged the lower-risk shape — extending a shared component's contract for one caller's one-off need is exactly the kind of change this repo's style guide asks to be deliberate about, not a default reach.
- **No frontend UI renders a group row in an "inherited" state for `materialize_inherited_access_for_group` to be called from — matching what that endpoint's own docstring (written by the interrupted prior session) already documents, not a new gap found in this pass.** PR5's unified Groups directory (`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`'s `groupsTabRows`) only has `ProjectGroup` rows (direct by construction since PR7) and `ProjectMemberSource` virtual rows (no "inherited" state of their own) — no row kind currently represents an org group's own `OrgGroupProjectRole` provenance. The endpoint is built, tested directly via the API (per-group materialize coverage above), and documented as ready for a future UI to call into without any backend change, per the plan's own framing of this as the "highest-risk, most novel" piece worth having in place ahead of a UI that surfaces it.
- **`remove_org_user` was placed in `backend/app/routers/orgs.py` immediately before `deactivate_org_user`, not next to `leave_organization`.** Both orderings are defensible; this one groups the three "admin acts on another member's standing" endpoints (`remove_org_user`, `deactivate_org_user`, `archive_org_user`) together, with `leave_organization` (self-service) staying where it already was, immediately after `revoke_org_role`.

## Hardening pass: org-level pending-invite endpoints regressed the I-M-05 server-admin scoping invariant (2026-09-02)

Requested as a general hardening pass over the whole `feature/ui-improvement-stage-6` branch (everything since it diverged from `main`, ~15k lines across backend RBAC/org/project-group work and the frontend UX batches). Given the identify → verify → remediate rigor this codebase's security-sensitive reviews use (per the change-management policy): a scan sub-agent proposed candidates over the full diff, oriented via `graphify` and its own reading of `rbac.py`/`orgs.py`/`projects.py`, primed specifically to look for the tenant-scoping gaps the *original* Ossa (v1) hardening pass (see that entry above) found in this exact area (group/role management across orgs and projects) — every candidate it raised was then independently re-verified by direct code reading (not by trusting the sub-agent's own claim) before being treated as real.

### Identify

The scan surfaced one real issue, in the "Org-level invites" Phase A work (see that entry above, ~line 2725): `list_org_pending_invites`/`create_org_pending_invite`/`resend_org_pending_invite` (`backend/app/routers/orgs.py`) were gated with `require_org_admin_or_server_admin` — the dependency `services/rbac.py` and this log's own I-M-05 entry (~line 164) document as a single, narrow, deliberate carve-out used *only* by `create_org_user` (bootstrapping the first user of a brand-new org, a genuine chicken-and-egg case since no `org_admin` exists yet to do it themselves). The Phase A entry's own reasoning for reusing it — "the same dependency `create_org_user` uses (the only other endpoint that creates these rows)" — never re-derives *why* the server-admin bypass is still warranted once the bootstrap justification no longer applies: an already-existing org already has an admin by the time invites are reachable, so there's no equivalent chicken-and-egg problem here. The rest of this PR's RBAC-heavy surface (`assign_group_project_role`/`revoke_group_project_role`, the `OrgGroupProjectRole` endpoints) was spot-checked against the same original-hardening-pass pattern and found correctly tenant-scoped — this is an isolated regression, not a systemic one.

### Verify

- Confirmed directly by reading `services/rbac.py:1729-1749` (the dependency's docstring, unmodified by this branch, still asserting "used only by the create-org-user endpoint") and `docs/decisions.md`'s existing I-M-05 entry, then confirming the three new call sites in `orgs.py` do in fact use it (`grep -n require_org_admin_or_server_admin backend/app/routers/orgs.py`).
- Confirmed the concrete exploit is real, not theoretical: `require_org_admin_or_server_admin` returns early for any `current_user.is_server_admin`, with no check that the caller holds any role in the *target* `organization_id` at all — a server admin with zero standing in organisation X could list every outstanding invite in X (invitee email + inviter name), create a new one (seeding a `MEMBER`-role account into a customer org), or rotate/resend an existing one's token.
- Confirmed the "already reviewed and found adequate" note in `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md`'s known-gaps section (item 4, updated by this branch's own Phase A work) addresses a *different* question — whether resending trusts an unverified caller-typed email more than the original send did (no) — not whether the *gate itself* is scoped correctly. Not a documentation contradiction, just a different concern than this finding.
- Spot-checked the rest of this PR's group/role-management surface (`assign_group_project_role`/`revoke_group_project_role` in `projects.py`) directly: both correctly re-validate `org_group_id` against `project.organization_id` (mirroring `add_project_group_member`'s existing guard), and `revoke_group_project_role`'s `DELETE` is inherently scoped by its own `WHERE org_group_id = ... AND project_id = ...` regardless. No second instance of this pattern found.
- No existing test exercised (or pinned as intentional) a server-admin-with-no-org-role call against these three endpoints — `test_org_pending_invite_endpoints_are_gated_at_org_admin_tier` only covered a plain org member, one tier *below* org_admin, never the server-admin bypass itself.

### Remediate

- `backend/app/routers/orgs.py`: `list_org_pending_invites`, `create_org_pending_invite`, `resend_org_pending_invite` re-gated to `require_org_role(OrgRole.ORG_ADMIN)` — the same I-M-05-compliant pattern every other org-property endpoint in this file uses (`update_org_branding`, `list_org_users`, etc.). `require_org_admin_or_server_admin` itself is untouched and remains used only by `create_org_user`, so its existing docstring is accurate again with no edit needed. `list_org_pending_invites`'s own docstring rewritten to explain the fix and why the old gate was wrong, in place of the "gated the same tier as `create_org_user`" claim that motivated the bug.
- `backend/tests/test_org_pending_invites.py`: new regression test `test_org_pending_invite_endpoints_reject_a_server_admin_with_no_role_in_the_org` — creates a fresh org via `create_org_admin_in` (so the bootstrap server admin, `admin_token`, holds no `UserOrgRole` in it) and asserts 403 from the bootstrap server admin on all three endpoints. The existing `test_org_pending_invite_endpoints_are_gated_at_org_admin_tier` docstring updated to name the new gate.

### Tests

`pytest tests/test_org_pending_invites.py` — 10 passed (8 existing + 2 new/updated), against the live local test database. `pytest tests/test_security_hardening.py` — 8 passed, unaffected. `ruff check app/routers/orgs.py tests/test_org_pending_invites.py` — clean. `tests/test_invites_and_external_users.py` has 12 pre-existing failures in this environment, confirmed via `git stash` to fail identically without this fix's changes — an un-mocked `send_email` in those tests trying to reach a live SMTP endpoint not reachable from this shell, unrelated to this change (none of the files it touches were modified here).

### Verified

Manual code verification (not sub-agent-reported) of both the vulnerability and the fix: read `services/rbac.py`'s `require_org_admin_or_server_admin`/`require_org_role` definitions, all three affected endpoints in `orgs.py` before and after the edit, and the spot-checked `projects.py` group-role endpoints, before concluding this was the only real finding in the branch's RBAC-heavy surface.

### Deeper pass: `revoke_group_project_role` fabricated audit entries on a no-op

Requested to go deeper after the above — five parallel sub-agents (`projects.py`, `rbac.py`, the rest of the RBAC-adjacent backend surface, and, per the user's explicit go-ahead to look further back, the last two PRs merged to `main`: #17 "Feature/security uplift august 2026" and #16 "UI/UX Stage 5 changes," the PR that introduced generalized cross-project permissions) audited the branch's full backend RBAC-adjacent surface plus that recent history. Four came back clean after independent verification; one (`projects.py`) surfaced a real, if narrower, issue.

**Found**: `revoke_group_project_role` (`backend/app/routers/projects.py`, `DELETE /{project_id}/group-roles/{org_group_id}/{role}`) never validated `org_group_id` before use, and unconditionally called `log_event(..., action="revoked", ...)` plus ran the affected-user cleanup query even when the `DELETE` removed zero rows (a genuine no-op — the grant never existed, or `org_group_id` didn't exist/belonged to a different organisation entirely). Its sibling `revoke_project_group_role` (the `ProjectGroupRole`-scoped endpoint, added in the same PR7) already gets this right: `_get_group_in_project` 404s a foreign group up front, and `if removed.rowcount:` guards the log/cleanup — this endpoint just didn't get the same treatment. Verified by direct read (`backend/app/routers/projects.py:3137-3204` before the fix), not sub-agent-reported.

Impact assessed as Medium, not High: the `DELETE`'s own `WHERE project_id=... AND org_group_id=... AND role=...` clause meant no real cross-tenant `OrgGroupProjectRole` row could ever actually be removed this way (such a row can only be created by the already-validated `assign_group_project_role`), so this was never a privilege-escalation or data-disclosure path — but a project manager could fabricate audit-trail entries claiming a role was "revoked" from an arbitrary (including nonexistent, or foreign-org) group on their own project, which this codebase's audit-logging control (per the change-management/secure-development policy) depends on being trustworthy.

**Fixed**: `org_group_id` is now validated to exist and belong to the project's own organisation before anything else runs (404 otherwise, matching `_get_group_in_project`'s existing convention for the exact same shape of check), and the log/cleanup block is now gated on `removed.rowcount`, mirroring `revoke_project_group_role` exactly. Three new tests in `backend/tests/test_org_group_project_roles.py`: a no-op revoke writes no audit event, a foreign-org `org_group_id` 404s, and a nonexistent `org_group_id` 404s. `pytest tests/test_org_group_project_roles.py` — 28 passed (25 existing + 3 new). `ruff check` clean.

**Everything else**: `rbac.py`'s full diff (effective-role resolution for the new `OrgGroupProjectRole`/`ProjectGroupRole` mechanisms) — no findings, every new join correctly tenant-scoped. The rest of the branch's backend RBAC-adjacent surface (`orgs.py` remainder, `requirements.py`, `change_requests.py`, `invites.py`, `project_export.py`, `templates.py`, `stages.py`, `branding.py`, `changes.py`, `services/requirements.py`, `labels.py`, `system.py`, models/schemas, migrations 0018-0022) — no findings. PR #16 ("Generalized cross-project group permissions," `main` history) — re-verified independently against its own decisions.md entry's claims, no findings, same conclusion the original PR's own identify/verify reached.

**PR #17 ("Feature/security uplift august 2026," `main` history) — found and fixed one real regression, despite the PR's own name**: its ReDoS-fix rewrite of `backend/app/routers/scim.py::_parse_simple_eq_filter` (replacing a backtracking regex with plain string operations, to close a CodeQL `py/polynomial-redos` finding) silently dropped the original regex's `\s+` requirement between the `eq` token and the filter value's opening quote — `before = s[:start_quote].rstrip()` has nothing to strip when the quote immediately follows `eq`, so a filter like `userName eq"active"` (invalid per the SCIM grammar this module implements, rejected by the original `...\s+eq\s+"..."` regex) was silently accepted instead of 400ing. Verified with a live interpreter (not just reading the diff): confirmed the exact accept/reject divergence, and confirmed `attr` is still checked against a fixed allowlist (`username`/`emails.value`/the one supported bracket-filter shape) at every call site regardless — so this was never an attribute-allowlist bypass, an org-scoping bypass, or otherwise exploitable, just a parser accepting a narrower class of malformed input than it should. Worth fixing anyway (not deferring) both because it's auth-adjacent parsing code and because the PR's own `docs/decisions.md` entry and this function's own docstring both claim the rewrite "reproduces the same match/no-match semantics" as the original — a claim this proved false for this one case. Fixed by checking the raw (pre-`rstrip()`) character immediately before the opening quote is whitespace, before doing the existing rstripped "eq" token check — same O(n), no backtracking reintroduced. New test `test_parse_simple_eq_filter_requires_whitespace_between_eq_and_the_quote` in `backend/tests/test_scim.py`; `pytest tests/test_scim.py` — 16 passed (15 existing + 1 new). `ruff check` clean. Everything else in PR #17 (the `orgs.py::_looks_like_email` ReDoS fix, the `authlib`→`joserfc` OIDC migration's algorithm-confusion/expiry enforcement, and `storage_backends/local.py`'s path-traversal confinement check) held up under direct testing (differential fuzzing against the original regex, live exploit scripts against the path confinement, and reading the installed `joserfc` library's own source to confirm its algorithm allowlist is actually enforced) — no further findings.

Files changed (this addendum): `backend/app/routers/projects.py`; `backend/tests/test_org_group_project_roles.py`; `backend/app/routers/scim.py`; `backend/tests/test_scim.py`; `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).
