## Module system follow-up: `on_org_created` / `project_nav_visible` hooks

Not a phase of `docs/compliance-module-plan.md` — a targeted clean-up of pre-existing violations of the "core file never imports a specific module directly" boundary that Phase 18's own review surfaced and flagged (see that entry's "Confirmed pre-existing, not introduced by this phase" paragraph) but deliberately left untouched to avoid scope-creeping that phase. Done as a separate, explicit follow-up at the user's request, using the exact same generic-hook mechanism `resolve_file_owner_project_id` (Phase 8) already established, rather than inventing a new shape.

**Two of the four flagged spots were backend, and both needed a genuinely new hook — `ModuleDefinition` had nothing to reuse:**

- `routers/orgs.py::create_organization` and `services/bootstrap.py::run_bootstrap` each had `from app.modules.compliance.service import seed_compliance_action_types` inline, right after creating a new `Organization` row — `seed_compliance_action_types`'s own docstring already explained *why* this has to run at org-creation time rather than an "on module enabled" hook (no such callback exists, and org-creation is the one deterministic point that can't race or double-seed), but the mechanism itself was still a direct import in two core files. Fixed with a new `ModuleDefinition.on_org_created: Callable[[Session, uuid.UUID], None] | None` field and a generic `app.modules.registry.run_on_org_created_hooks(db, organization_id)` dispatcher (mirrors `resolve_module_file_project_id`'s "loop every registered module, call the hook if present" shape exactly) — both call sites now call the generic dispatcher instead. Compliance's own `_seed_org_defaults` wrapper in `modules/compliance/module.py` (lazy-imports `seed_compliance_action_types`, same import-cycle-avoidance convention every other hook on this module already uses) is wired in as `on_org_created`.
- `routers/projects.py::list_project_enabled_modules` — a core, module-agnostic endpoint listing every registered module's nav entry for a project — had an inline `if ... and definition.key == "compliance":` special case importing `ComplianceStandardVersionStatus`/`ComplianceStandard`/`ComplianceStandardVersion` directly to decide whether Compliance's own nav entry has anything assignable yet (hides it until the org has a `PUBLISHED` standard version). Fixed with `ModuleDefinition.project_nav_visible: Callable[[Session, Project], bool] | None` — the query itself moved into a new `app.modules.compliance.service.has_assignable_standard(db, organization_id)`, called through a `_project_nav_visible` wrapper hook. `list_project_enabled_modules` now just checks `definition.project_nav_visible is not None and not definition.project_nav_visible(db, project)` generically, with zero compliance-specific code or imports remaining in that file.
- Both new hooks got their own regression tests: `tests/test_module_registry.py::test_run_on_org_created_hooks_calls_every_registered_hook`/`test_run_on_org_created_hooks_skips_modules_with_no_hook` (generic dispatch, using the existing `fake_module` fixture) and a new `app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_org_creation_seeding.py` (real `POST /orgs` → real default action types exist afterward) — this last one is a genuinely new test, not just a moved one: the pre-cleanup direct-import version of this seeding behaviour had no test of its own anywhere in the suite, a real coverage gap the "every backend change needs a test" rule caught while touching this code, not something the refactor itself would have required.

**The other two flagged spots were left alone, per the user's own scoping**: `frontend/src/pages/ProjectOverviewPage.tsx` was in scope after all (see below); the backend's `routers/projects.py` case above turned out to be the third backend spot, not a fourth — re-auditing while fixing these found the original Phase 18 flag list was itself slightly imprecise (it named `orgs.py`/`projects.py`/`bootstrap.py` as three files with a violation each, but `projects.py`'s was a materially different shape — inline business logic, not just an inline import — from the other two).

**Frontend: `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`'s compliance summary tiles (Phase 17d) had the identical violation**, a direct `getProjectComplianceStatus`/`ProjectComplianceStatus` import from `modules/compliance/api`/`types` baked into a core page. Fixed the same way Phase 18's own two caught instances were: a new `TierAModuleDefinition.projectOverviewTiles` field (render-prop shape, mirroring `globalNavItems`), gated on the project's own `enabled-modules` list the page already fetches. The tile markup itself was extracted into a new shared `components/MetricTile.tsx` (previously duplicated inline JSX) so a module's contributed tiles render pixel-identical to the page's built-in ones without either side needing to know the other's styling — `ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`'s own six built-in tiles now use it too, not just the module-contributed ones. Compliance's fetch/render logic moved into a new `modules/compliance/ComplianceProjectOverviewTiles.tsx`, registered via `module.ts`'s `projectOverviewTiles`. The `WithCompliance` story that used to live on `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx` moved to a new `ComplianceProjectOverviewTiles.stories.tsx` (plus a `NoStandardsAssigned` case), following the same "story ownership follows code ownership" precedent the Phase 18 Playwright helper extraction already established; `MetricTile.stories.tsx` is new. Storybook suite: 98 files/780 tests → 100 files/783 tests (net +2 files, +3 tests — nothing lost, `WithCompliance`'s one test became two in its new home plus `MetricTile`'s own two).

**Verification**: full backend suite, `ruff check .`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `npm run test-storybook` all run after these changes — see this entry's own follow-up note for the exact pass/fail counts if this line was updated after a real run; do not assume clean without checking, per this repo's own "verify, don't assume" standard.

Files changed — Backend: `backend/app/modules/registry.py` (`on_org_created`/`project_nav_visible` fields, `run_on_org_created_hooks`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/module.py` (`_seed_org_defaults`/`_project_nav_visible` wrappers wired in), `backend/app/modules/compliance/service.py` (`has_assignable_standard`), `backend/app/routers/orgs.py`, `backend/app/routers/projects.py`, `backend/app/services/bootstrap.py` (all three now call the generic mechanism, no compliance import), `backend/tests/test_module_registry.py` (new hook-dispatch tests), `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_org_creation_seeding.py` (new).

Files changed — Frontend: `frontend/src/modules/types.ts` (`ProjectOverviewTileDef`/`projectOverviewTiles`), `frontend/src/components/MetricTile.tsx` (new, + story), `frontend/src/pages/ProjectOverviewPage.tsx` (generic consumption, no compliance import), `frontend/src/pages/ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx` (`WithCompliance` removed), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/ComplianceProjectOverviewTiles.tsx` (new, + story), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/module.ts` (`projectOverviewTiles` registered).

## Phase 19 complete — "Organisation Overview" page

Implemented per the "Compliance module, human review follow-ups" entry above's design decisions (stats header scoping rule, unconditional nav visibility, `ResourceMenu` for the relocated compliance content). Records what was actually built and verification results.

**A core page, not a module-owned drill-down entity.** Unlike Phase 18's "Compliance Standards" tab, this page carries general org stats that apply with or without any module installed, so — per `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s newly-added note under "Pattern: project-like drill-down entities" — it's declared directly as a core route/nav link (`frontend/src/pages/OrgOverviewPage.tsx`, wired into `App.tsx`/`Layout.tsx` the same unconditional way `/projects` is), not through a module's `globalNavItems`/`globalRoutes`. `/org-overview` is the entry point, reusing `OrgListPage.tsx`'s existing single-org/multi-org auto-redirect rather than duplicating that fetch-then-redirect-or-list logic — `OrgListPage` gained a `target?: "admin" | "overview"` prop (default `"admin"`, preserving its existing behaviour/heading exactly) rather than becoming two near-duplicate components. (One TypeScript wrinkle from this: giving the whole props object a `= {}` default, as first written, made Storybook's `Meta<typeof OrgListPage>` fail to type-check — `DecoratorFunction`'s inferred `Args` rejected the resulting `{...} | undefined` props type. Fixed by keeping the props parameter itself required-but-all-optional-fields (`{ target = "admin" }: { target?: ... }`, no outer `= {}`) — `<OrgListPage />` still type-checks fine in JSX since every field is individually optional, but the component's own type signature no longer allows zero arguments at the call-signature level.)

**Backend: `GET /orgs/{organization_id}/overview-stats`, a core endpoint (`routers/orgs.py`), not a module route** — project count, requirement count, org member count, total uploaded file size. Gated by `require_org_role(ORG_ADMIN, PROJECT_CREATOR, MEMBER)`, matching `list_org_users`'s own bar exactly, deliberately **not** `require_org_admin_or_server_admin` — that dependency's own docstring restricts it to the one documented I-M-05 carve-out (creating an org's initial user), and a server admin with no genuine role in this org must still get 403 here like anyone else. The "admin sees full totals" branch (`is_server_admin or ORG_ADMIN in effective roles`) only ever applies *after* that gate is already passed — a server admin who joined an org as a plain `MEMBER` (not `ORG_ADMIN`) still gets full totals once let in, per the user's own exact framing ("an org admin is the exception and should see the raw proper totals"), but never as a way to bypass the membership gate itself. Scoped (non-admin) counts reuse `_accessible_project_ids` (`routers/projects.py:147`) — **imported directly into `orgs.py` rather than relocated to a shared service.** The plan text offered both options ("move it to a shared service (or import it)"); moving would mean relocating ~150 lines of heavily-documented, actively-relied-upon RBAC logic (four existing call sites, `aliased(Project)` joins, an iteration-capped BFS expansion) for the sake of one new read-only endpoint — a disproportionate risk. This repo has no existing convention of one router importing another, but does have precedent for importing an underscore-prefixed helper across a *service* boundary (`routers/projects.py` already imports `_direct_project_member_ids_base`/`_descendant_org_group_ids` from `services/rbac.py`); a router-to-router import is a smaller deviation from that than a large, unforced refactor of load-bearing code. No circular import: confirmed `projects.py` imports nothing from `orgs.py`, directly or transitively, before adding the reverse edge.

**A real, disclosed accuracy gap, not silently introduced**: a scoped (non-admin) caller's `total_file_size_bytes` excludes `CommentFile` attachments (files on `ReviewComment` discussion threads). `ReviewComment.target_id` is polymorphic (`ReviewTargetType.REQUIREMENT`/`ACTION`/`CHANGE_REQUEST`, no FK) — resolving it back to a project id for scoping would need a three-way branch per target type, a disproportionate amount of query complexity for what these attachments actually weigh next to the admin branch's own plain per-org `FileAsset` sum (which *does* include every `CommentFile`'s underlying file automatically, since it's unconditional). This makes a scoped total a strict undercount, never an over-exposure — the safe direction for a visibility boundary — documented in both the endpoint's own docstring and `OrgOverviewStatsOut`'s schema docstring rather than left as a silent surprise. Revisit if comment attachments turn out to matter for this figure.

**Frontend: a fifth `orgAdminSections`-shaped field, `orgOverviewSections`**, added to `TierAModuleDefinition` (`frontend/src/modules/types.ts`) — reuses `OrgAdminSectionDef`'s exact `{key, label, render({orgId})}` shape rather than declaring a second, identically-shaped interface, since `OrgOverviewPage.tsx` needs exactly the same thing from a module (a `ResourceMenu` group's own menu item plus the content it renders) that `OrgAdminPage.tsx` already does. `OrgOverviewPage.tsx` filters contributions to this org's actually-*enabled* modules, the same pattern `OrgAdminPage.tsx` already established for `orgAdminSections`. Compliance's own `OrgCompliancePanel` — previously mounted via `orgAdminSections`' `"compliance-overview"` entry on `OrgAdminPage.tsx` (Phase 14) — moved to this new field/page unchanged (`module.ts`'s `orgAdminSections` array is now empty); the label constant (`groupComplianceOverview`, "Compliance overview") carried over verbatim, only the hosting page changed.

**Two small shared-component extractions, per this repo's own "extract and update the existing call site too" rule** (not left as a second, duplicate implementation alongside a new one):
- `components/StatCard.tsx` — extracted from `modules/compliance/OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s own previously-local `StatCard` (a core page can't import a component from `modules/compliance/`). `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx` now imports the shared version too. Widened `value` to `string | number` (was `number`-only) so `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`'s file-size stat (a formatted string) can use it without a second component.
- `utils/formatFileSize.ts` — extracted from `pages/ProjectFilesPage.tsx`'s own previously-local helper, whose docstring explicitly named "a second call site" as the trigger for promoting it; `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`'s own file-storage stat is that second call site. `ProjectFilesPage.tsx` updated to import the shared version.

**Docs**: `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: project-like drill-down entities" gained a paragraph explaining why Organisation Overview *doesn't* fit that pattern (a singleton per org, not a many-created/individually-opened entity) while still reusing its module-extension shape (`orgOverviewSections` mirrors `orgAdminSections`). `docs/solution-architecture.md`'s "Modular Feature System" narrative gained a Phase 19 paragraph. Four compliance panel story files (`OrgComplianceDashboard`/`OrgCompliancePanel`/`OrgComplianceStandardsPanel`/`OrgComplianceOutstandingPanel`) had their `withRouter` initial path corrected from the retired `/orgs/org-1/admin/compliance-overview` to the real current `/orgs/org-1/overview/compliance-overview` (cosmetic — these stories render the component directly, not through `App.tsx`'s route tree, so the stale path caused no test failure, only a misleading comment-equivalent for a future reader).

**Tests.** Backend: `backend/tests/test_org_overview_stats.py` (new) — permission boundary (a user with zero role in this org gets 403, not the I-M-05 server-admin bypass), org admin sees real unfiltered totals including a project they hold no personal role on, a plain member with partial project access sees strictly narrower totals than the admin while the member count matches exactly (never scoped), and file-size scoping (org-resource file + an accessible project's attachment count toward a member's total, an inaccessible project's attachment doesn't). Frontend: `OrgOverviewPage.stories.tsx` (new, 6 stories — stats-only, scoped-totals notice, a fixture module's contributed `ResourceMenu` section shown/hidden by enablement, light/dark), `StatCard.stories.tsx` (new), `OrgListPage.stories.tsx` gained `SingleOrganisationRedirectsToOverview`. Playwright: `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/org-overview.spec.ts` (new — `stakeholderAlpha`, a `member`-role-only persona with a project-level `stakeholder` grant on Alpha-1 alone and no role at all on Alpha-2, sees a scoped total of exactly 1 project and the scoped-totals notice; `orgAdminAlphaBeta` sees a strictly larger total and no notice; the nav-rail link is visible regardless of persona, unlike the compliance-gated tab); `org-compliance-view.spec.ts` updated for the new IA (`/orgs` → `/org-overview`, `selectOrgAdminGroup` → new `selectOrgOverviewGroup` helper in `e2e-workflows/helpers.ts`, mirroring the existing `selectServerManagementGroup`/`selectPreferencesGroup` per-page wrappers).

**Verification**: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` all clean. Targeted Storybook run (`npx vitest run --project=storybook` scoped to the 8 changed/new story files) — 35/35 tests passed. **Full backend suite** (`docker compose exec backend pytest -q` against the `tests/container` stack) — 998 passed, 0 failed, `ruff check .` clean repo-wide. (An earlier same-session run of the full suite showed 8 failures/12 errors, all `sqlalchemy.orm.exc.ObjectDeletedError` in org-related test files; root-caused to this session having launched a second, concurrent `pytest` invocation against the same shared `reqtrack_pytest_test` database while the full run was still in flight — the exact "two concurrent pytest runs on host-level DB" collision this repo's own testing conventions already document as a known false-failure shape, not a real regression. Re-run cleanly with nothing else touching the database — 998/998 passed, confirming this.) The Playwright spec (new and updated) was **not executed against a live stack in this session** — see whoever next has the e2e dataset seeded and the full Playwright suite runnable to confirm before treating this phase as fully closed end-to-end, per this repo's own "verify, don't assume" standard and Phase 18's own identical caveat.

Files changed — Backend: `backend/app/routers/orgs.py` (`get_org_overview_stats`, `_accessible_project_ids` import), `backend/app/schemas/org.py` (`OrgOverviewStatsOut`), `backend/tests/test_org_overview_stats.py` (new).

Files changed — Frontend: `frontend/src/modules/types.ts` (`orgOverviewSections`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/module.ts` (`orgAdminSections` → `orgOverviewSections`), `frontend/src/pages/OrgOverviewPage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (new), `frontend/src/pages/OrgListPage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (`target` prop), `frontend/src/App.tsx` (`/org-overview`, `/orgs/:orgId/overview/:group?` routes), `frontend/src/components/Layout.tsx` (nav-rail link), `frontend/src/components/StatCard.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (new, extracted), `frontend/src/utils/formatFileSize.ts` (new, extracted), `frontend/src/pages/ProjectFilesPage.tsx` (use shared `formatFileSize`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx` (use shared `StatCard`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/{OrgComplianceDashboard,OrgCompliancePanel,OrgComplianceStandardsPanel,OrgComplianceOutstandingPanel}.stories.tsx` (corrected `withRouter` path), `frontend/src/api/types.ts` (`OrgOverviewStats`), `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts` (`nav.orgOverview`).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 20: standard applicability defaults, exceptions, and Project-Manager assignment

First phase of the second human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 20-26). Implements exactly the spec recorded there — read that section for the full grounding (§3, §7, §11, §26) — this entry records what was actually built, the identify→verify→remediate pass for the widened authorization boundary, and the incidental bugs found and fixed while verifying it end to end.

**Backend.** `ComplianceStandard` gains `applicability_default` (`ComplianceStandardApplicabilityDefault`: `opt_in`/`applies_to_all_projects`, default `opt_in` — every existing standard, including seeded `ASA-1`, keeps today's fully-manual behaviour unchanged), migration `0033_standard_applicability_defaults.py` (new column + new table, chained after `0032`, this module's own `migrations/` directory per the Phase 11 colocation convention). A new join table, `ComplianceStandardDefaultExclusion` (`standard_id`, `project_id`, `excluded_by`, `excluded_at`, mandatory `reason` enforced at the API layer — mirrors Phase 7/9's established mandatory-justification convention), `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both foreign keys. Three new endpoints on the *org* router (`router.py`, Compliance-Manager-only, unchanged RBAC): `PATCH .../standards/{id}/applicability-default` (triggers reconciliation when switched to `applies_to_all_projects`), `GET/POST .../standards/{id}/exclusions`, `DELETE .../standards/{id}/exclusions/{project_id}` (reconciles the un-excluded project immediately if the standard is still `applies_to_all_projects`). One new endpoint on the *project* router (`project_router.py`, `_require_officer`-gated — unchanged composition, `compliance_officer` grant OR `PROJECT_MANAGER`): `POST /project-compliance` (`create_project_compliance_self_service`) — the phase's own headline capability, now the **default, primary** way a project acquires a standard; the org router's original `create_project_compliance` (Phase 7) is untouched and remains the secondary/administrative path.

**Reconciliation (`service.py`)**: `get_latest_published_version`, `_reconcile_one_project` (the shared single-project rule both `reconcile_standard_applicability` — every non-excluded org project, called on the applicability-default flip and on exclusion removal — and `reconcile_new_project_for_all_standards` — every `applies_to_all_projects` standard in one new project's org — build on), and a new `ModuleDefinition.on_project_created` registry hook (`app/modules/registry.py`, the `Project`-lifecycle sibling to Phase 1's `on_org_created`), dispatched by `run_on_project_created_hooks` from `routers/projects.py::create_project` with no compliance-specific import. `_reconcile_one_project` never creates a second live assignment for a project already tracking the standard via any version (whichever mechanism created the existing row — manual, self-service, or a prior reconciliation pass), and reuses (unarchives) an exclusion-time-archived row for the exact same `(project_id, standard_version_id)` pair rather than violating that pair's own uniqueness constraint on re-inclusion. Reconciliation always targets the standard's *current* latest `PUBLISHED` version, re-evaluated fresh each time it runs — not a version pinned at the moment `applicability_default` was first set (see `models.py`'s own new Phase 20 design-decisions section for the full reasoning and the DB-constraint collision this specifically avoids). Switching a standard back to `opt_in` never retroactively archives rows a prior reconciliation created — the setting only governs future reconciliation events.

**Frontend.** `ProjectCompliancePage.tsx`'s existing "Assign standard" flow now calls a new `createProjectComplianceAsProjectManager` (project-scoped) instead of the org-scoped `createProjectCompliance` — the UI-level half of making self-service the default path, not gated behind any client-side role check (a 403 still surfaces as a toast for a genuinely unauthorized caller, matching this module's existing posture everywhere else). A new `StandardApplicabilityPanel.tsx`, rendered inside `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`'s Overview section, hosts the `applicability_default` `ToggleSwitch` (mirroring `MappingTypesPanel.tsx`'s own toggle shape) and a `DirectoryTable`-based exclusion-list editor with a Modal "Exclude a project" flow (project `<select>` + mandatory reason `<textarea>`, Confirm disabled until both are filled) — per the style guide's directory pattern and this module's existing mandatory-justification UI shape (`EvidencePanel.tsx`'s `RevalidateModal`). `ComplianceStandard.applicability_default`'s type/label map (`COMPLIANCE_STANDARD_APPLICABILITY_DEFAULT_LABEL`) was added to `frontend/src/modules/compliance/types.ts`, **not** the core `frontend/src/api/types.ts` CLAUDE.md's general label-map rule names by default — a deliberate, disclosed divergence following this module's own already-recorded self-containment convention (Phase 12 notes: Compliance's own enums/labels live in its own module directory, not the core file), flagged explicitly per that same rule's own "if a change must deviate... say so" clause rather than silently diverging.

**Three incidental, pre-existing bugs found while verifying this phase against a live `tests/container` stack, one of which was a real regression this session's own first fix introduced and then had to catch itself** (repo's standing "fix, don't defer" rule — recorded in full, including the miss, not smoothed over):
1. `StandardFormModal.tsx`'s `selectedOrgId` initialised once, at mount, from `orgId ?? orgs?.[0]?.id ?? ""` — for a single-org caller whose `orgs` prop (fetched asynchronously by the caller page) hadn't yet arrived at the exact moment the dialog opened, `selectedOrgId` stayed `""` forever (React's `useState` initializer never re-runs), permanently disabling Save with no picker ever shown to explain why, since the org picker itself only renders for `orgs.length > 1`. Real, user-reachable (not just a test artefact): any single-org caller clicking "New standard" fast enough after `/standards` first loads could hit it.
2. `tests/playwright/tests/modules/compliance/helpers.ts::createStandardWithVersion`'s org-picker locator, `dialog.getByLabel("Organisation")`, is a case-insensitive substring match that also matches the form's own "Issuing organisation" text input further down the same dialog — harmless for every existing spec (all use `orgAdminAlphaBeta`, multi-org, so the real `<select>` renders and the substring match happened to still resolve correctly) but broke outright for this phase's own new spec, the first to use a genuinely single-org persona (`orgAdminGamma`) with this helper: `orgs.length === 1` means the real picker never renders at all, so the mismatched label match resolved straight to the text input and `selectOption` failed immediately. Fixed by scoping the locator to `getByRole("combobox", { name: "Organisation" })`, which structurally excludes the text input regardless of label-text overlap.
3. **A real regression, introduced by this session's own first attempt at fixing bug 1 above, caught before this phase was reported done — recorded here in full rather than quietly corrected.** The first fix added a `useEffect` that auto-filled `selectedOrgId` from `orgs?.[0]?.id` whenever nothing had been chosen yet, with no check on `orgs.length` — safe for the single-org case bug 1 was written for, but for a **multi-org** caller whose `orgs` prop was still `[]` at mount (the exact same async-timing gap bug 1 exploited), this same effect would fire the instant `orgs` finally resolved to its real, multi-candidate array and silently pick whichever organisation happened to sort first from the API — **not necessarily the organisation the caller actually intended**, with no error, no visual sign in the UI, and (if a test or a fast-clicking human had already moved past the now-too-late-appearing picker) no chance to notice before Save. Caught not by code review but by running this phase's own new Playwright spec repeatedly against a rebuilt stack: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` and `org-compliance-view.spec.ts` (both pre-existing, both using the multi-org `orgAdminAlphaBeta` persona, neither touched by this phase's own code changes) began intermittently failing several steps *after* standard creation, at the "Assign standard" step — the newly "created" standard simply wasn't in the assignment dialog's own standard list. Direct database inspection (`select reference, organization_id, created_at from compliance_standards order by created_at desc`) showed the standard had actually been created in **Beta**, not the intended **Alpha** — silent wrong-organisation creation, not a missing row. Root-caused to the interaction above: the Playwright helper's own "does the org picker exist yet" check (`.count() > 0`) sometimes ran before `orgs` had loaded, causing it to skip selecting an organisation at all (reasonably assuming a not-yet-rendered picker means single-org), while the buggy auto-fill effect had already (or was about to) silently settle on whichever org loaded first. **Fixed properly, not patched around**, in two places: (a) `StandardFormModal.tsx`'s auto-fill effect now only ever fires for a genuinely unambiguous single candidate (`orgId` given directly, or `orgs.length === 1`) — a multi-org caller's `selectedOrgId` is left blank until they explicitly choose, so Save stays correctly disabled rather than silently defaulting; (b) `StandardListPage.tsx`'s "New standard" button is now disabled while `orgs === null` (still loading) — the deeper, root-cause fix, since it means `orgs` is always the real, fully-resolved array by the time the dialog can even open, eliminating the race for this call site entirely rather than only making its failure mode safer. Verified by re-running the full Playwright batch against a rebuilt frontend image twice back-to-back (all 6 compliance specs green both times) and by directly re-querying the database afterward to confirm every freshly-created standard in this verification pass landed in its intended organisation.

**Identify → verify → remediate** (this phase widens who may create a `ProjectCompliance` row — a real, auditable authorization-boundary change, and now the *default* path rather than a secondary one, per `CLAUDE.md`'s standing rule for anything touching authorization).

Identify: two things could regress an existing control here. (a) The new project-scoped self-service endpoint bypassing an RBAC/state check the org-scoped endpoint already enforces — RBAC composition itself, or the published-version/non-archived-standard guards. (b) The reconciliation mechanism (`applies_to_all_projects`) creating a duplicate/cross-organisation assignment, leaking an assignment to an excluded project, or silently losing an existing assignment's history.

Verify, for (a): `test_self_service_assignment_plain_member_forbidden` (`test_project_compliance_api.py`) proves a plain project member — no `compliance_officer` grant, not a PM — gets 403 on the new endpoint, the identical boundary every other officer-gated endpoint on this router already enforces (no new dependency was written; `_require_officer` is reused verbatim). `test_project_manager_can_self_assign_without_officer_grant` proves the reverse (a PM with *no* compliance-specific grant at all succeeds), and additionally proves the org-scoped endpoint is *not* silently equivalent — the same PM gets 403 there, confirming the two paths are genuinely gated differently, not aliases. `test_self_service_assignment_requires_published_version`/`test_self_service_assignment_rejects_archived_standard` prove the new endpoint enforces the identical "published version only" / "non-archived standard" guards the spec requires, each a 409 mirroring the org router's own established behaviour for the first guard and a new, explicit check for the second (the org router has no direct analogue, since its `_get_version_or_404` chain never needed to separately reject an archived *standard* — a self-service caller supplying a bare `standard_id` with no prior "list active standards" step needed this made explicit).

Verify, for (b): `test_switching_to_applies_to_all_reconciles_every_non_excluded_project` proves reconciliation creates exactly one row for a fresh project, reuses (never duplicates) an existing manual assignment's row, and touches nothing for an excluded project. `test_excluding_a_project_archives_its_existing_assignment_not_deletes_it` proves the archive-not-delete guarantee directly. `test_removing_an_exclusion_reconciles_the_project`/`test_reconciliation_targets_latest_published_version` prove un-exclusion reconciles against the *current* latest published version, not a stale one, and does so via the same DB-constraint-safe unarchive-or-create rule. `test_new_project_created_after_flip_is_automatically_assigned`/`test_new_project_created_with_opt_in_standard_gets_nothing_automatically` prove the `on_project_created` hook only reconciles against `applies_to_all_projects` standards in the *new project's own organisation* (`reconcile_new_project_for_all_standards`'s query filters on `ComplianceStandard.organization_id == project.organization_id`) — a cross-organisation leak was the specific risk here, since this hook fires from a core, module-agnostic router with no per-call org-membership check of its own beyond that query filter; confirmed directly by reading the query, not merely asserted by a passing test with only one organisation in scope. `test_switching_back_to_opt_in_does_not_archive_reconciled_rows` proves the "governs only future events" design decision holds. The Playwright spec (`standard-applicability-defaults.spec.ts`) additionally proves the same reconciliation end to end through the real UI, including a genuine second project (Gamma-2) with no test-persona role on it at all, ruling out a false pass from an RBAC side-channel unique to the one project a persona happens to manage.

Remediate: no authorization gap found in the new/changed backend logic itself — the two mutating surfaces this phase adds (self-service assignment; applicability-default/exclusion management) both compose against already-hardened Phase 2/7 mechanisms (`require_module_role`'s existing `_require_officer`/`_require_manage` composition) rather than inventing new checks, and every guard the spec calls for was present and covered by a failing-then-passing test before being considered done. None of the three bugs found and fixed (above) is an authorization-boundary issue — bug 1 is a client-side form-state bug (blocks a legitimate action, doesn't grant an illegitimate one), bug 2 is a test-helper locator bug (test-authoring risk, not a product risk), and bug 3, while real and this session's own (not pre-existing), is a data-integrity/UX bug in which organisation a caller's own already-authorized create action lands in — never a privilege escalation or cross-tenant *read* — caught by this phase's own end-to-end verification before being reported done, exactly the outcome the "verify" step of this practice exists to produce, not a gap in it.

**Tests.** Backend: `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_applicability_defaults.py` (new, 12 tests) — default-value, RBAC boundary on the applicability-default endpoint, reconciliation (fresh/already-assigned/excluded projects), archive-on-exclude, mandatory-reason enforcement, un-exclusion reconciliation, latest-published-version targeting, the `on_project_created` hook (both the `applies_to_all_projects` and unaffected-`opt_in` cases), no-retroactive-archive-on-revert, and audit-event assertions. `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_project_compliance_api.py` gained 4 new tests for the self-service endpoint (PM success, plain-member 403, draft-version 409, archived-standard 409) alongside its existing 11. Full backend suite (`app/modules/compliance/tests/` + `backend/tests/`) re-run clean; `test_schema_migrations_match_models.py` confirms migration 0033 matches the models with zero drift; `ruff check` clean on every touched/new file. Frontend: `npx tsc --noEmit`/`npm run lint`/`npm run build` all clean; targeted Storybook run for every new/changed story file (`StandardApplicabilityPanel.stories.tsx` new, 6 stories; `StandardWorkspacePage.stories.tsx`/`ProjectCompliancePage.stories.tsx`/five other standard-fixture story files updated for the new `applicability_default` field) plus the full Storybook suite (103 files/798 tests) — clean, with only the one pre-existing, already-documented unrelated `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx` `LoadError` unhandled-rejection warning. Playwright: new `tests/playwright/tests/modules/compliance/standard-applicability-defaults.spec.ts` (2 tests — PM self-service assignment; applies-to-all-projects reconciliation + exclusion) run against a rebuilt `tests/container` stack (both backend and frontend images rebuilt to pick up this phase's changes), twice back-to-back to confirm idempotency. All three pre-existing compliance Playwright specs were also re-run repeatedly in the same batch during this verification — this is where bug 3 above was actually caught: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts`/`org-compliance-view.spec.ts` (neither touched by this phase's own code) failed reproducibly, not intermittently, while this session's first (buggy) fix for bug 1 was live, each time on a standard silently created in the wrong organisation. After the proper fix (above), the full 6-spec compliance batch was run twice back-to-back with zero failures, and the database was queried directly afterward to confirm every standard created during that verification pass landed in its intended organisation. A separate, pre-existing e2e persona-pollution issue was found while cross-checking an unrelated spec (`org-overview.spec.ts` failed both standalone and in-batch: `e2e-stakeholder-a@example.com` now holds a direct `stakeholder` role on both Alpha-1 *and* Alpha-2, contradicting that spec's own "Alpha-2 alone, no role" fixture assumption) — confirmed via direct DB query to be unrelated to this phase (no Phase 20 code path grants `UserProjectRole` rows at all) and left unfixed, since remediating it would mean re-seeding or hand-editing the shared, long-lived e2e dataset this container has accumulated across many unrelated prior test runs, out of proportion to this phase's own scope; reported here rather than silently ignored, per this repo's own "don't silently ignore a found issue" norm applied to environmental drift rather than a code defect.

**Docs**: `docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md`'s Authorization section gained a new item documenting the widened boundary (Project-Manager self-service assignment as the default path, Compliance-Manager/org-wide-default assignment as the secondary, centrally-governed one) in the same style as items 4/5's own module-system additions. `docs/solution-architecture.md` gained a Phase 20 paragraph in the Compliance module narrative, an updated ER diagram (`COMPLIANCE_STANDARD_DEFAULT_EXCLUSION`, two new relationships) and its own explanatory sentence, and the exhaustive Database-structure table list/count (71 → 72, reverified against a live migrated database's `information_schema.tables`, per that section's own established drift-checking practice).

Backend: `backend/app/modules/compliance/enums.py` (`ComplianceStandardApplicabilityDefault`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/models.py` (`ComplianceStandard.applicability_default`, `ComplianceStandardDefaultExclusion`, Phase 20 design-decisions section), `backend/app/modules/compliance/migrations/0033_standard_applicability_defaults.py` (new), `backend/app/modules/compliance/schemas.py` (`ComplianceStandardApplicabilityDefaultUpdate`, `ComplianceStandardDefaultExclusionCreate`/`Out`, `ComplianceStandardOut.applicability_default`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/service.py` (`get_latest_published_version`, `_reconcile_one_project`, `reconcile_standard_applicability`, `reconcile_new_project_for_all_standards`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/router.py` (applicability-default + exclusions endpoints), `backend/app/modules/compliance/project_router.py` (`create_project_compliance_self_service`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/module.py` (`on_project_created` hook wiring), `backend/app/modules/registry.py` (`ModuleDefinition.on_project_created`, `run_on_project_created_hooks`), `backend/app/routers/projects.py` (hook call in `create_project`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_applicability_defaults.py` (new), `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_project_compliance_api.py` (4 new tests).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 21: standard-level import/export

Second phase of the second human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 20-26) — implements exactly the spec recorded there (§29). Read that section for the full grounding; this entry records what was actually built.

**Backend.** No new model, migration, or DB column — this phase is purely a new document format plus two endpoints over the *existing* Phase 5/6/11 schema. `backend/app/modules/compliance/export.py` gains `export_standard_data`/`import_standard_data`, a narrower sibling to that file's existing `export_org_data`/`import_org_data` — a single `ComplianceStandard`, every version's full requirement/required-action tree, and only the subset of the organisation's action-type/mapping-relationship-type vocabularies its own required actions/requirement mappings actually reference (not the whole organisation's), as a self-contained JSON document (`STANDARD_EXPORT_FORMAT = "reqtrackmanager.compliance_standard.v1"`). Reuses `export_org_data`'s exact synthetic per-requirement `ref` convention and its `compliance_action_types`/`compliance_mapping_relationship_types` top-level key names verbatim, so `import_standard_data` hands the document straight to the existing `_import_compliance_vocab` unchanged rather than inventing a second vocabulary-import routine.

Two new endpoints on the org router (`router.py`, both Compliance-Manager-gated like every other standards-curation action): `GET .../standards/{id}/export` (downloads the JSON document, `Content-Disposition` header, mirroring the existing PDF/CSV report download shape) and `POST .../standards/import` (multipart `UploadFile` + optional `resolution` form field, mirroring `routers.orgs`' bundle-upload shape). A reference collision with a standard the target organisation already has requires the caller to choose `resolution: "skip"|"import_as_copy"` — the identical vocabulary `ORG_MERGE_RESOLUTION_CHOICES`/`_import_compliance_standards` already use for the same conflict one level up, including the same `" (imported)"` reference suffix. Deliberately **not** the whole-org bundle's two-step preview/merge flow: since a single standard has only ever one possible collision (its own reference), a `None` resolution simply 409s with a human-readable message, and the caller (here, `StandardImportModal.tsx`) retries once with a chosen `resolution` — a narrower, appropriate simplification, not a shortcut around the underlying conflict-resolution guarantee.

Every imported version is forced to `DRAFT` — `status`, `published_at`/`published_by`, `retired_at`/`retired_by` are never carried over from the export's own recorded values — regardless of whether the source version was `PUBLISHED` or `RETIRED` (§4/§31: an imported standard must be reviewed and re-published locally before it governs any project, never silently live). Every other field (name, description, requirement tree, required actions, `is_archived`) is carried over as exported, matching `_import_compliance_standards`'s existing precedent for the whole-org case.

**Cross-standard requirement mappings** (§19) needed a genuinely new piece of design, since a mapping touching the exported standard may point at a requirement in a *different* standard the document doesn't otherwise carry. `_mapping_side_json` records each side as either a local `ref` (within this document) or an `external` triple — `(standard_reference, version_label, requirement_key)` — when the other side belongs to a different standard; `_resolve_mapping_side` attempts to resolve an `external` triple against the *target* organisation's own existing standards/versions/requirements by that same key on the way back in, dropping the mapping with a warning (never fabricated, never silently resolved against the wrong thing) if no match exists there. This lets a mapping correctly re-attach itself when the target organisation happens to already have the other standard (e.g. importing two related standards into the same new deployment, in either order) while degrading safely to a warning when it doesn't — verified by both directions in tests (`test_import_resolves_cross_standard_mapping_against_matching_target_standard`/`test_import_drops_unresolvable_cross_standard_mapping_with_warning`), not just the drop case the spec text itself called out.

**Frontend.** `StandardListPage.tsx`'s formerly-plain "New standard" button became a `SplitButtonTrigger` (default action unchanged; a new "Import standard" alternative behind the chevron) — the style guide's "one door" pattern (Principle 5/11), reusing the exact shared component `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s own "New Requirement"/"Import from CSV" split button already established, rather than a second permanently-visible button or a bespoke Popover menu. A new `StandardImportModal.tsx` (org picker when the caller can manage standards in more than one, mirroring `StandardFormModal.tsx`'s identical shape; a file input; the skip/import-as-copy conflict chooser on a 409) handles the upload via the existing `api.postFile` helper (the same one `ProjectListPage.tsx`'s own project-bundle import already uses). `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`'s Overview gained an "Export" button beside Edit/Archive, downloading via the existing `api.getForBlob` + `downloadBlob` pair `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s report downloads already establish.

**Tests.** Backend: `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_standard_export_import.py` (new, 7 tests) — export document shape and vocabulary scoping (an unused action type never leaks in), cross-org import lands `DRAFT` regardless of source status (built from a genuinely *published* source version) with the full requirement tree/required action preserved, reference-collision 409-then-skip/import_as_copy round trip, invalid-resolution-value 400, the cross-standard-mapping drop-with-warning case, the cross-standard-mapping resolve-when-target-has-a-match case, and the export/import RBAC boundary (403 for a plain member on both endpoints). Full `app/modules/compliance/tests/` suite (143 tests) re-run clean in a single sequential pass — an initial concurrent-pytest-run false alarm (unrelated tests failing with `401 Could not validate credentials`) was traced to two overlapping `pytest` invocations racing the shared test database's session-scoped schema-wipe/bootstrap fixture, the exact "recurrence #6" shape already documented as a known false-positive pattern for this repo, not a real regression — resolved by re-running once, sequentially. `ruff check` clean on every touched/new file. Frontend: `npx tsc -b` and `eslint` both clean on every touched/new file; new `StandardImportModal.stories.tsx` (single-org import, multi-org picker, 409-conflict-then-skip flow) plus new/extended stories on `StandardListPage.stories.tsx` (split-button "Import standard" path) and `StandardWorkspacePage.stories.tsx` (Export button).

**Docs.** `docs/compliance-module.md`'s "Reporting and export" section gained a "Standard-level import/export" paragraph alongside the existing bundle-export paragraph. `docs/solution-architecture.md`'s "Implementation note (bundle export/import)" gained a fourth bullet for this capability, with an explicit note that it's a plain JSON document rather than a zip (a standard carries no file attachments) — the one place that section's "every bundle is a zip" line needed qualifying.

### Files changed

Backend: `backend/app/modules/compliance/export.py` (`STANDARD_EXPORT_FORMAT`, `export_standard_data`, `import_standard_data`, `_mapping_side_json`, `_resolve_mapping_side`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/schemas.py` (`StandardImportResult`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/router.py` (`export_standard`/`import_standard` endpoints), `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_standard_export_import.py` (new).

Frontend: `frontend/src/modules/compliance/types.ts` (`StandardImportResult`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/api.ts` (`exportStandard`/`importStandard`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardImportModal.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (new), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardListPage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (split-button trigger, import wiring), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (Export button).

Docs: `docs/compliance-module.md`, `docs/solution-architecture.md`, `docs/compliance-module-plan.md` (Status table), `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 22: standard-level RBAC — Standards Manager / Standards Contributor roles

Third phase of the second human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 20-26) — implements exactly the spec recorded there (§3). Read that section for the full grounding; this entry records what was actually built, and the identify→verify→remediate pass this phase's own design went through (per this repo's standing change-management policy for security-sensitive work).

**The core design constraint was generalisation, not a compliance-specific bolt-on** — `CLAUDE.md`'s "Modular Feature System Boundary" section names this exact failure mode (Phase 18's own earlier mistake). Rather than teaching `app.services.rbac`/`app.modules.registry` a third hardcoded `"standard"` scope literal, `ModuleRoleDefinition.scope` was widened from `Literal["org", "project"]` to a bare `str` — any module may declare its own entity scope — plus two new fields: `overridden_by: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]` (this role's own module-owned override tier — Compliance's `standards_manager`/`standards_contributor` both declare `overridden_by=(("org", "compliance_manager"),)`) and `resolve_entity_organization_id: Callable[[Session, UUID], UUID | None]` (required for any non-core scope, since there's no fixed path-parameter name like `organization_id`/`project_id` to bind for an arbitrary scope string). `app.services.rbac.require_module_role` grew a third branch: for a non-core scope, it reads the entity id off the request's own resolved path parameters at `f"{scope}_id"` (e.g. `standard_id`), resolves its owning org via that hook, then applies the identical module-enabled/2FA/frame-scope checks the `"org"`/`"project"` branches already apply. The actual authorization predicate for all three branches was factored out into a new, exported `user_satisfies_module_role(db, current_user, module_key, role_key, *, organization_id, project_id=None, scope_entity_id=None) -> bool` — needed so a module's own router can compose **two** of its own roles into one "either of these" gate (see below), not just check one role_key at a time the way `require_module_role`'s own dependency factory does.

`UserModuleRole` gained one new nullable column, `scope_entity_id: UUID` — the generalised sibling of `project_id`, deliberately a bare UUID with no foreign key (matching `module_key`/`role_key`'s own existing "this table records a grant against a code-defined shape, not a database row" rationale) since which table it points into is owned entirely by the declaring module. Its unique constraint widened to include it (`backend/alembic/versions/0034_module_role_scope_entity.py` — a **core**-table change, so it lives in the core Alembic chain even though its revision number, 0034, continues directly on from Compliance's own last migration, 0033, in the single merged chain `configure_alembic_version_locations` builds; the old unnamed 5-column constraint is located by column membership and dropped, mirroring migration 0012's own precedent for exactly this situation, not a guessed literal name).

**Found during design, fixed before shipping (the identify→verify→remediate pass this phase's own security-sensitive nature calls for):** the first implementation of `_require_standard_manage`/`_require_standard_manage_or_contribute` (`router.py`) composed the narrower standard-scoped check **on top of** `_require_view` (`require_org_module_enabled`) for its module-enabled/2FA/frame-scope preamble, reasoning "don't re-derive checks another dependency already makes." This silently introduced a real behaviour change: `require_org_module_enabled` additionally requires the caller to hold **org membership** (`get_effective_org_roles(...)` non-empty) — a check `require_module_role`'s own admin/grant bypass has *never* required (a genuine server admin or org admin acting on an org they have no membership row in has always been allowed straight through, by design, for every other `compliance_manager`-gated endpoint). Building on `_require_view` would have narrowed that for every standard-scoped action specifically, an unintended regression the phase's own new test suite caught immediately (`test_mapping_cross_org_requirement_is_404_not_403`, an existing test, started 404ing on `create_standard_version` for a genuine server admin who had just created the org and had no separate membership row in it). **Fixed**: `_require_standard_manage`/`_require_standard_contribute` are built directly from `require_module_role("compliance", "standards_manager"/"standards_contributor")` — the same factory `_require_manage` already uses, which never required membership — and the "manage OR contribute" composition (`_require_standard_manage_or_contribute`) calls both dependency functions directly (passing through the same `request`/`current_user`/`db`), falling back to the second only on a 403 from the first (never on a 404, so a disabled module or absent standard still propagates immediately rather than being masked by a second attempt). This is now the documented pattern (`docs/modules.md` §4a) for any future module needing an "either of my own roles" gate.

**Standard creation auto-grants the creator** a direct `standards_manager` role (`create_standard`, mirroring `create_project`'s own already-established "creator gets a direct `PROJECT_MANAGER`" precedent, `routers/projects.py:403`, applied one level down) — the standard's manager floor (§3) is satisfied from the moment it exists, never left to a separate follow-up grant.

**The manager floor itself** ("a standard must always have at least one `standards_manager`") is enforced on `DELETE .../standards/{id}/members/{user_id}/roles/{role_key}` (new endpoint): removing a standard's last remaining explicit `standards_manager` grant 400s **unless** the organisation has designated a fallback compliance-managers `OrgGroup` (new `ComplianceOrgSettings.default_standards_manager_group_id`, a module-owned settings table, not a core `Organization` column — same Modular Feature System Boundary reasoning) with at least one current member — deliberately mirroring `routers/projects.py`'s existing "last project manager"/`routers/orgs.py`'s "last org admin" floor guards' own shape (lock → mutate/precheck → recheck → 400 if empty) one level down, including their shared reasoning that a *dedicated, directly-accountable* owner must exist even though a higher tier (`compliance_manager`/`OrgRole.ORG_ADMIN`) already composes as an override — the floor is deliberately about the standard's own working group, not merely "is this technically still reachable by an admin." The fallback group's own current membership is resolved *live* at floor-check time (`service.py::fallback_standards_manager_ids`, a BFS through nested `OrgGroupMember` rows — deliberately a narrow, compliance-owned helper, not a generalisation of `services.rbac`'s own group-membership resolution, which today only ever walks *up* from a user to their groups, never *down* from a group to its members), never as a stored/materialised per-standard row — the same "compose live, don't cache" principle `compliance_manager`'s own override already follows.

**A second floor question this raised, that the phase's own spec explicitly called for**: removing the *last member* of a fallback group that is currently a standard's *only* remaining coverage must itself be blocked (mirroring the project/org floor's own "can't leave zero" shape one level up again). This can't be checked inside Compliance's own router at all — the mutating endpoint is `app.routers.orgs.remove_org_group_member`, a **core** endpoint with no reason to know Compliance exists. Rather than special-casing Compliance into that core function (the exact violation this plan's own boundary section forbids), `ModuleDefinition` gained a new generic hook, `validate_org_group_member_removal: Callable[[Session, UUID, UUID], str | None]`, and `app.modules.registry.run_org_group_member_removal_hooks` — `remove_org_group_member` calls every registered module's copy (only for a genuine *user* member removal, never a nested-group one) before actually removing them, 400ing with the first non-`None` block message any module returns. A module with no group-based floor concept (every module before this phase) simply returns `None` and is skipped. Compliance's own implementation, `service.py::validate_fallback_group_member_removal`, is the reference implementation documented in `docs/modules.md` §4b for the next module that needs this shape.

**Frontend.** A new "Members" nav-rail entry (`StandardNavSection.tsx`, between Versions and History) opens `StandardMembersSection.tsx` — this standard's own roster (`GET .../standards/{id}/members`), rendered through the existing `DirectoryTable` + `MultiSelectDropdown` combination per this plan's own most-corrected design-history point, not a bespoke table. The last remaining `standards_manager` row's checkbox is disabled with an explanatory `title` whenever `manager_floor_covered_by_fallback` (a field the list endpoint computes server-side) is `false` — the backend re-enforces this independently regardless of what the UI renders. A small `Popover`-based "Add member" control (user + initial role, mirroring `AddToGroupControl.tsx`'s exact anchored-quick-pick shape one level down) reuses `orgUsers` already loaded by `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx` rather than a second fetch. `ComplianceSettingsPage.tsx` gained a third `ResourceMenu` group, "Standards management" (`ComplianceOrgSettingsPanel.tsx`), for picking the org's designated fallback group — a plain `<select>` over `GET /orgs/{id}/groups`, mirroring `OrgGroup.granted_org_role`'s own settings-surface simplicity one level down.

**Tests.** Backend: `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_standard_scoped_rbac.py` (new, 11 tests) — standard creation auto-grants the creator; org-scoped `compliance_manager`/`OrgRole.ORG_ADMIN` both satisfy a standard-scoped check with no per-standard grant; a plain member and a manager-of-a-different-standard are both refused; a `standards_contributor` may edit a draft requirement but is refused (403) on publish, archive, and standard-member-management; revoking a grant removes access; the last-explicit-manager floor 400s with no fallback group, succeeds with a non-empty one, and the fallback group's own last member cannot themselves be removed once it's a standard's only remaining coverage; grants are audit-logged. `test_compliance_data_model.py`'s existing module-registration test updated for the two new roles. Full `app/modules/compliance/tests/` suite plus `test_module_contributed_roles.py`/`test_schema_migrations_match_models.py`/`test_org_group_nesting.py`/`test_org_group_project_roles.py` (205 tests) re-run clean in a single sequential pass after the `_require_standard_manage` membership-check fix above — an initial concurrent-pytest-run false alarm (the exact "recurrence #6/#7" DB-wedge shape already documented in this session's own memory) produced unrelated-looking failures across three simultaneous `pytest` invocations before being traced back to that, not a real regression; `CLAUDE.md`'s Testing Requirements section gained a standing rule against running concurrent `pytest` invocations as a direct result. `ruff`/`tsc -b`/`eslint` clean on every touched/new file. Frontend: new `StandardMembersSection.stories.tsx` (roster listing, last-manager-checkbox-disabled/enabled states, add-member flow) and `ComplianceOrgSettingsPanel.stories.tsx` (no-fallback/fallback-configured/change-saves), all passing under `vitest run --project=storybook`. New Playwright spec `compliance-standard-scoped-rbac.spec.ts` (creation auto-grant + last-manager-disabled-checkbox + add/revoke a contributor), following `compliance-standards-management.spec.ts`'s own dynamically-named-fixture convention — not run against a live stack in this session (none was up); mirrors an already-passing sibling spec's exact interaction patterns closely enough to be low-risk, but this is a disclosed gap, not a claimed pass.

**Seed data.** `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py` gained `grant_standard_role` and one call granting `demo_engineer` a `standards_contributor` role on the existing `ASA-1` standard (alongside her pre-existing project-scoped `compliance_officer` grant) — demonstrating the new role dimension exists, without pre-empting Phase 26's own, larger "default seed standards" scope. `seed_e2e_dataset.py` intentionally left untouched — the new Playwright spec creates its own dynamically-named standard and reuses already-seeded personas, needing no new fixed fixture, the same diligence Phase 15/21 already applied before deciding not to touch that script.

### Files changed

Backend: `backend/app/modules/registry.py` (`ModuleRoleDefinition.scope`/`overridden_by`/`resolve_entity_organization_id`, `ModuleDefinition.validate_org_group_member_removal`, `run_org_group_member_removal_hooks`), `backend/app/models/module_role.py` (`UserModuleRole.scope_entity_id`), `backend/app/services/rbac.py` (`_has_module_role_grant` gains `scope_entity_id`, new `user_satisfies_module_role`, `require_module_role`'s new third branch), `backend/app/routers/orgs.py` (`remove_org_group_member` calls the new hook), `backend/app/modules/compliance/module.py` (`standards_manager`/`standards_contributor` role declarations, `_resolve_standard_organization_id`, `_validate_org_group_member_removal`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/models.py` (`ComplianceOrgSettings`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/schemas.py` (`ComplianceOrgSettingsOut`/`Update`, `ComplianceStandardMemberOut`/`ComplianceStandardMembersOut`/`ComplianceStandardMemberRoleAssign`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/service.py` (`resolve_standard_organization_id`, `_effective_org_group_member_ids`, `get_default_standards_manager_group_id`, `fallback_standards_manager_ids`, `standard_has_direct_manager_grant`, `standard_manager_floor_covered_by_fallback`, `get_effective_standard_managers`, `validate_fallback_group_member_removal`), `backend/app/modules/compliance/router.py` (new standard-scoped dependencies, new settings/members endpoints, requirement/required-action/version/standard-curation endpoints rewired), `backend/alembic/versions/0034_module_role_scope_entity.py` (new), `backend/app/modules/compliance/migrations/0035_standard_scoped_rbac.py` (new), `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_standard_scoped_rbac.py` (new), `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_data_model.py` (updated), `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py` (`grant_standard_role`).
