## Compliance module plan, Phase 23: standard workspace UX overhaul — Overview stats, expandable Versions nav, requirement-browsing parity

Fourth phase of the second human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 20-26) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. Read that section for the full grounding; this entry records what was actually built.

**Overview stats.** `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`'s Overview section, previously a plain description card with zero counts, gains a `.grid.grid-metrics` row of four `MetricTile`s — Versions, Requirements, Projects, Compliant — above the existing description/Edit/Archive card. Deliberately `MetricTile` (`components/MetricTile.tsx`), not `StatCard` as the plan's own prose named: `StatCard`'s own docstring documents it as the *non*-clickable variant "for a stat with no single obvious link target," which is exactly wrong here — every one of these four tiles has a real destination, and `MetricTile` is the component this codebase already built for precisely that "stat tile → click navigates to a filtered view" shape (`ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`/`OrgOverviewPage.tsx`). Requirements links straight at the standard's *current* version's own workspace (latest published, else latest by `version_number` — a small local `currentVersion()` helper, not a new backend concept); Projects/Compliant both link to a new "projects" section (`StandardProjectsPanel.tsx`), the latter pre-filtered via `?state=compliant` in the URL (linkable/shareable, not local-only state).

New backend endpoint, `GET .../standards/{id}/project-summary` (`router.py`, view-gated like `get_standard`/`list_standards` — not manage-gated like the cross-standard `list_all_project_compliance`, since this is one standard's own Overview stat, visible to anyone who can already view the standard) — reuses `service.py::build_status_out` (the exact §20 per-assignment calculation `list_all_project_compliance` already runs org-wide) against a query narrowed to this one standard's own `ProjectCompliance` assignments. Returns the existing `ProjectComplianceStatusOut` shape unmodified — no new counting logic, and the frontend's compliant-count/grouping logic is the same plain `.filter(...).length` `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.tsx`'s own `countByState` already does, not a second aggregation mechanism.

**Expandable Versions nav-rail group.** This app's first expandable nav-rail group (documented as a new, reusable pattern in `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, "Pattern: expandable nav-rail group"): `StandardNavSection.tsx`'s "Versions" entry gains a disclosure toggle (`ChevronRight`/`ChevronDown`, not `CollapsibleSection` itself — its card chrome doesn't fit a nav-rail row) that, expanded, lists one link per version (label + status badge) straight into `/standards/:id/versions/:versionId` — a new trailing route segment, not a second flat route: `module.ts`'s existing `/standards/:standardId/:section?` grew one more optional segment, `/standards/:standardId/:section?/:versionId?`, since "which version is open" only ever matters when `section === "versions"`. Expand state persists per-standard-instance via `useUiPreference` (`section_collapsed:standardVersionsNav:<standardId>`). `StandardNavSection.tsx` resolves its own `organization_id` (via the existing global, no-org-in-path `getStandardById`) and version list independently — `standaloneWorkspaces.render` only ever passes `entityId`/`railCollapsed`, and this is a structurally separate render tree from `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx` (`Layout.tsx`'s own sibling nav-rail section, not a child), so it can't share that page's already-fetched state without a new shared-context mechanism this phase didn't need to build.

`StandardVersionsSection.tsx`'s own "which version is open" state moved from local `useState` to the URL: it now takes `initialVersionId` (the `:versionId?` param, threaded down from `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`) and calls `useNavigate()` on open/back instead of `setActiveVersion`, so the nav-rail shortcut above and the plain version list's own "open a version" click land on the identical URL/state — a real route was the whole point, not just a visual disclosure affordance.

**Requirement browsing parity.** `RequirementTree.tsx` gains a `ViewToggle` (`tree`/`list`, `useViewMode("complianceRequirementTree", ...)`) between the existing, unchanged tree (still the authoring/reordering view — hierarchy intact, per the plan's own explicit instruction not to flatten it) and a new flat list view for scanning/searching. **Filtering is scoped to the list view only, deliberately**: filtering the flat requirement list before the tree is built would silently drop a matching child whose ancestor didn't match the filter, so rather than build filter-aware tree-pruning, the tree stays the unfiltered authoring view and the list is the filtered scanning view — a design call, not an oversight, recorded here since the plan's own "consider a ViewToggle" language left it open. The list view's `FilterPanel` (search text over reference/name/description, a mandatory-only checkbox, an action-type `<select>`) needs every requirement's required actions loaded for the two non-text filters — fetched via the existing per-requirement `listRequiredActions` endpoint for every requirement once list view is entered (not a new "all actions for this version" endpoint, since the tree view's own lazy per-expand loading already established that pattern and the requirement counts here are the same modest, per-standard scale that pattern already assumes).

A list-view row opens `RequirementDetailPanel` (new, same file) — a `SidePanel` with `AutoGrowTextarea` fields for description/reasoning (the same field component `RequirementsPage.tsx`'s own detail editing already uses), editable while `isDraft`; required actions are shown read-only there (a pointer to switch to tree view to manage them), rather than duplicating that whole CRUD surface a second time in the panel. `ViewToggle` itself gained a `showTilesOption` prop (default `true`, additive) so a tree/list-only caller isn't forced to also show a meaningless "tiles" button — mirrors `showTreeOption`'s own existing shape exactly.

**Found and fixed during Playwright verification, not left as a known gap:** the detail panel's `onSave` handler did an async PATCH-then-reload-then-`setDetailRequirement(found)` — a real race: if the user closed the panel while that round trip was still in flight, the resolved promise's own `setDetailRequirement` call would silently **reopen** it, clobbering the close. A fast Save-then-Close in a Playwright spec hit this in practice, not merely in theory. Fixed with a functional state update that only reapplies the reloaded requirement when the panel is still open on that same requirement (`current?.id === detailRequirement.id ? ... : current`) — a stale round trip can no longer resurrect a panel the user already dismissed.

**Also found while running the full compliance Playwright suite against this phase's own changes (fixed, not deferred, per this repo's standing rule):**
- Every existing spec that clicked the standard workspace's "Versions" nav-rail link via `getByRole("link", { name: "Versions" })` broke the moment the new "N Versions" `MetricTile` existed too — Playwright's substring name matching resolved both. Fixed at every call site (`compliance-standards-management.spec.ts`, `project-compliance-view.spec.ts`, `org-compliance-view.spec.ts`, `standard-applicability-defaults.spec.ts`) with `{ name: "Versions", exact: true }`, disambiguating the plain nav-rail link ("Versions") from the tile's own accessible name ("N Versions").
- `compliance-standard-scoped-rbac.spec.ts` (Phase 22's own spec, unrelated to this phase's changes but hit while running the full suite) had two independent, pre-existing bugs: `selectOption({ label: RegExp })` is not valid Playwright API (a `label` must be a string) — fixed to the real, known option label (`"<name> (<email>)"`, matching `StandardMembersSection.tsx`'s own option text); and `.uncheck()` on a role checkbox whose whole row disappears once the last role is revoked never resolves, since `.uncheck()` re-verifies the control is still present and unchecked afterward — fixed to a plain `.click()`, since the test only needs the row to disappear, not the checkbox to remain in an unchecked-but-present state.

**Tests.** Backend: `test_standard_project_summary_filters_to_one_standard_and_is_view_gated` (new, `test_project_compliance_api.py`) — narrowed to one standard, matches the per-project `/status` endpoint's own calculation for the same assignment, callable by a plain view-gated member. Full `app/modules/compliance/` suite (155 tests) re-run clean. Frontend: `tsc -b`/`eslint .` clean; new/updated Storybook stories (`RequirementTree.stories.tsx` — list view search/mandatory-filter/detail-panel-edit stories; `StandardWorkspacePage.stories.tsx` — Overview stat tiles, version deep-link, projects section; `StandardNavSection.stories.tsx` — expand/collapse, no-versions-hides-toggle; `StandardVersionsSection.stories.tsx` — URL-driven open/back/deep-link via a `Harness` reading the same route param; new `StandardProjectsPanel.stories.tsx`; `ViewToggle.stories.tsx` — `showTilesOption`), full `vitest run --project=storybook` suite (828 tests) passing. Playwright: `compliance-standards-management.spec.ts` gained a new test covering all three UX pieces end to end (Overview tiles' own click-through, nav-rail expand/collapse + deep link, list-view search filter + detail-panel edit, round-tripped back through tree view) against the real dev/test Docker Compose stack, run twice back-to-back to confirm idempotency; the shared `orgAdminAlphaBeta` persona's own view-mode preference is restored in a `finally` block regardless of assertion outcome, since `useViewMode` is a per-user, cross-standard preference this persona also carries into every other spec that opens a `RequirementTree`. Full `tests/modules/compliance/` (8 tests) and the compliance-touching subset of `tests/e2e-workflows/` re-run clean after the above fixes.

**Note, not treated as caused by this phase:** `org-overview.spec.ts`'s own "scoped totals" test failed independently of any file this phase touched (a stale project-count expectation against this session's long-lived, cumulative dev-stack database) — reproduced in isolation, unrelated to compliance-standard code paths, and left unaddressed here since fixing it would mean altering shared dev-database state or a spec this phase has no legitimate reason to touch, not this phase's own regression.

### Files changed

Backend: `backend/app/modules/compliance/router.py` (`get_standard_project_summary`, module docstring), `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_project_compliance_api.py` (new test).

Frontend: `frontend/src/modules/compliance/api.ts` (`getStandardProjectSummary`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardWorkspacePage.tsx` (Overview stat tiles, `versionId` param, "projects" section), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardNavSection.tsx` (expandable Versions group), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardVersionsSection.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (URL-driven open state), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardProjectsPanel.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (new), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/RequirementTree.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (list view, filters, `RequirementDetailPanel`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/module.ts` (route param), `frontend/src/components/ViewToggle.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (`showTilesOption`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardWorkspacePage.stories.tsx`/`StandardNavSection.stories.tsx` (updated mocks/assertions).

Playwright: `tests/playwright/tests/modules/compliance/compliance-standards-management.spec.ts` (new test + `exact: true` fix), `project-compliance-view.spec.ts`/`org-compliance-view.spec.ts`/`standard-applicability-defaults.spec.ts` (`exact: true` fix), `compliance-standard-scoped-rbac.spec.ts` (two unrelated pre-existing bug fixes).

Docs: `docs/ux-style-guide.md` ("Pattern: project-like drill-down entities" Overview-stats addendum, new "Pattern: expandable nav-rail group"), `docs/compliance-module-plan.md` (Status table, Phase 23 notes), `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 24: post-publish clarification edits + editable version descriptions

Fifth phase of the second human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 20-26) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. Read that section for the full grounding, including the explicitly-flagged reconciliation of this phase with Phase 6's original "a published version's requirements become immutable" rule; this entry records what was actually built.

**Two schema additions, nothing else.** `ComplianceStandardVersion.summary` (a version's own current standing, distinct from `change_note`) and four new columns on `ComplianceRequirement` — `clarification_count`, `last_clarified_at`, `last_clarified_by`, `last_clarification_note` — added via migration `0036` (`app/modules/compliance/migrations/`, `down_revision = "0035"`). `last_clarification_note` deliberately mirrors `ProjectComplianceRequirement.decision_note`'s already-established "the last decision's own note lives on the row; the full history is the audit trail" precedent (Phase 9) rather than a new table — every clarification is also logged via `services.audit.log_event` (action `"clarified"`), so the column is a cheap read for the tree/badge UI, not the sole record.

**`PATCH .../standards/{id}/versions/{version_id}`** (new — no version-update endpoint existed before this phase at all) carries only `summary` (`ComplianceStandardVersionUpdate`), editable at every lifecycle stage. RBAC is stage-dependent, checked in the handler rather than via a single dependency: gated to `_require_standard_manage_or_contribute` for the ordinary (draft) case, with an explicit extra `_require_standard_manage(request=request, current_user=current_user, db=db)` call inserted when `version.status != DRAFT` — the same "try the weaker gate, escalate inline" shape `_require_standard_manage_or_contribute` itself already uses one level up, applied here to a single endpoint whose required gate depends on request-time state rather than being fixed at route-definition time.

**`PATCH .../requirements/{id}/clarify`** (new, `clarify_requirement`) — a narrow, `standards_manager`-or-override-only (`_require_standard_manage`, never `_require_standard_manage_or_contribute`) sibling of the ordinary `update_requirement` endpoint, callable *only* when the owning version is `PUBLISHED` (409 on `DRAFT` — use the ordinary endpoint instead — or `RETIRED` — stays fully frozen). `ComplianceRequirementClarifyRequest.clarification_note` is mandatory (400 if blank), mirroring every other conditionally-mandatory-justification field in this module; there is no mechanical "substantive vs. non-substantive" detection (recorded in `models.py`'s own Phase 24 notes as a deliberate non-goal — no such detection is reliable from a text diff alone), so the note is what makes the distinction accountable rather than silent, satisfying §4/§31's actual wording ("must not *silently*/*unexpectedly* alter... compliance assessment") without reopening `_require_draft_version` itself, which is left completely unchanged and still governs every other requirement/required-action mutation. The audit event's `detail` carries both `before`/`after` snapshots of every field the endpoint can touch plus the note itself.

**Explicitly-flagged open question, resolved as spec'd:** a clarification does **not** call `service.invalidate_approval_if_in_flight` — confirmed against §12/§27 once more with this specific question in mind, per the plan's own instruction not to decide this silently. A clarification never changes the compliance obligation itself, so an in-flight approval survives one unchanged; this is recorded here explicitly as the resolution, not left implicit in the code alone.

**Frontend.** `RequirementTree.tsx` gains an `isPublished` prop (alongside the existing `isDraft`) threaded from `VersionWorkspace.tsx`'s own `version.status === "published"` check — mutually exclusive with `isDraft`'s edit/delete/move controls, matching the backend's own "draft: ordinary edit; published: clarify only; retired: neither" three-way split. A "Clarify" action (tree row, list-view detail panel) opens `RequirementClarifyModal` — pre-filled reference/name/description/reasoning plus a mandatory clarification-note field gating Save, mirroring `RequirementFormModal`'s shape but as a distinct component (a clarification's fields and gating are genuinely different, not a parameterised variant of the ordinary form). A small `.badge` (`ClarificationBadge`, reused across tree/list/detail views) appears on any requirement with `clarification_count > 0`, showing the count and most recent note via the native `title` tooltip — no new visual language, per the plan's own instruction. `VersionWorkspace.tsx` gains an always-rendered "Version summary" card (`AutoGrowTextarea` + Save, disabled until dirty) above the requirement tree, regardless of the version's own status; the backend's stage-dependent RBAC isn't pre-computed client-side — this component follows the same established convention Publish/Retire above it already do (show the control unconditionally, let a 403 surface via toast), not a new pattern.

**Export/import round-trips both additions**, not left as a silent gap the way Phase 15 found and fixed for evidence history: `export.py`'s org-bundle path (`export_org_data`/`_import_compliance_standards`) and the standalone per-standard path (`export_standard_data`/`import_standard_data`) both carry `summary` on every version and the four clarification fields (plus a resolved `last_clarified_by_email`) on every requirement, following the exact same "raw user id during export construction, resolved to an email in a second pass, re-resolved via `UserResolver` on import" convention every other user-reference field in this file already uses.

**Seed data.** `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py` gains `update_compliance_version_summary`/`clarify_compliance_requirement` helpers (mirroring the existing `create_compliance_*`/`publish_compliance_version` helpers exactly) and calls both once against the `ASA-1` standard's published `v1.0` — a version summary noting the remote-ID wording was clarified post-publish, and a clarification on the remote-ID compliance requirement adding the specific 14 CFR 89 citation. Verified against the real rebuilt dev backend via a throwaway standard (archived afterward) rather than a full reseed, since the shared dev-stack's existing `Solstice Robotics` org predates this seed script's own compliance block and skips it entirely (`create_org` no-ops once the org name exists) — a pre-existing gap in the shared dev database, not something this phase introduced or fixed; the two new helpers' exact request shapes were smoke-tested directly against the live API instead.

**Security review (identify → verify → remediate, per the change-management policy for anything touching RBAC):** this phase introduces no new RBAC primitive — both new endpoints compose `_require_standard_manage`/`_require_standard_manage_or_contribute` exactly as Phase 22 already built and hardened them, so a full dedicated hardening pass (parallel candidate-identification sub-agents, as the larger cross-cutting passes above used) was judged disproportionate to the risk; instead, a direct self-review of both new handlers checked: (1) the stage-dependent escalation in `update_standard_version` actually blocks a contributor once non-draft (confirmed both by reading the code path and by `test_standards_contributor_cannot_clarify_or_edit_published_version_summary`); (2) `clarify_requirement` never falls back to the weaker contributor gate (`Depends(_require_standard_manage)` directly, not the `_or_contribute` variant); (3) both endpoints still use the existing `_get_version_or_404`/`_get_requirement_or_404` cross-org 404-not-403 chain, so no cross-org leakage is newly possible; (4) `last_clarified_by`/`last_clarified_by_email` exposure follows the same `required=False`-optional-actor-reference convention already used for `published_by`/`retired_by` in this same file, not a new information-disclosure surface. No findings.

**Tests.** Backend: new `test_compliance_clarification_and_version_summary.py` (12 tests) — clarify succeeds on published/increments count/second call; 400 on a blank note; 409 on draft and on retired; the *ordinary* update endpoint still 409s on published (pinning that Phase 6's own rule is unchanged); audit event asserts `"clarified"` action with `before`/`after`; RBAC boundary (`standards_contributor` 403 on both actions; `standards_manager`/org `compliance_manager`/`OrgRole.ORG_ADMIN` all succeed on both); `summary` editable at draft/published/retired; a contributor may edit `summary` while draft. Export/import round-trip assertions added to both `test_compliance_standard_export_import.py` (new test) and `test_compliance_export_import.py`'s existing org-bundle test. Full `app/modules/compliance/` suite (180 tests) re-run clean. Frontend: `tsc -b`/`eslint .` clean; new/updated Storybook stories across `RequirementTree.stories.tsx` (`ClarifyPublishedRequirement`, `ClarifiedRequirementShowsBadge`, retired-version story now also asserts no Clarify button) and `VersionWorkspace.stories.tsx` (`EditSummaryOnRetiredVersion`), plus `summary`/clarification-field defaults added to every other compliance story file's fixture builders the type change touched (`ApplicabilityTree`, `RequirementAssessmentPanel`, `RequirementMappingsModal`, `StandardNavSection`, `StandardVersionsSection`, `StandardWorkspacePage`, `VersionDiffModal`) — full `vitest run --project=storybook` suite passing (25 + 38 tests spot-checked across every touched file). Playwright: new `compliance-clarification-and-version-summary.spec.ts` covers the full flow (draft-stage summary edit, publish, published-stage summary edit surviving a reload, Clarify with a gated Save, the resulting badge) against the real dev/test stack; found and fixed two `getByLabel`/`getByText` substring-ambiguity issues while writing it (`"Description"` also substring-matching the "Clarification note (required)" field's computed accessible name, and the "Clarified" badge substring-matching the "Requirement clarified." toast) — both resolved with `{ exact: true }`, the same fix shape Phase 23's own notes already recorded for an identical class of issue, not a new failure mode. Full `tests/modules/compliance/` (9 specs) re-run clean.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 25: post-review UX quick fixes, round 2

Three independent, smaller UX corrections from the same human-review round, following Phase 17's own precedent of bundling several small, independent fixes into one phase.

**25a — nav-rail double-highlight.** `ComplianceGlobalNavLink.tsx`'s `<NavRailLink to="/standards" .../>` had no `exact` prop, so `Layout.tsx`'s active-state check (`startsWith` when `exact` is falsy) matched every `/standards/...` sub-route too — the "Compliance Standards" rail link stayed highlighted alongside the separate "Standard" nav-rail section that's supposed to take over navigation once inside one standard. One-line fix: added `exact`, mirroring `Layout.tsx`'s own `<NavRailLink to="/projects" exact .../>` for the identical reason. Regression coverage needed two new Storybook stories with genuinely different initial routes (`/standards` active, `/standards/standard-1` not); since Storybook composes story-level decorators with `meta`-level ones rather than replacing them, and nesting two `MemoryRouter`s throws a real React Router error, the file's shared `meta`-level `withRouter` had to be removed and pushed down into every individual story instead — `Layout.stories.tsx` already established this exact "no router at `meta`, every story supplies its own" convention for the same reason, so this is convergence on an existing pattern, not a new one.

**25b — buried org compliance stats, structurally over-nested navigation, and a raw download button row.** Confirmed directly against the live layout: `OrgOverviewPage.tsx` mounted one `ResourceMenu` group for module-contributed content; `OrgCompliancePanel.tsx` then rendered its **own** `Tabs` (Dashboard / Compliance by standard / Outstanding) *inside* that one group; the Dashboard tab opened with a bare Download PDF/CSV button row sitting directly above three separately-`flex-wrap`-ped `StatCard` rows of uneven size (4, then 5, then 1). `ResourceMenu → Tabs → button row + uneven stat groupings` was three navigational layers deep for what a reviewer actually wants to see. Three corrections, each following an existing precedent rather than inventing a new one:

- **Headline gauges surface directly in the page's own always-visible header.** New `OrgOverviewTileDef`/`orgOverviewTiles` field on `TierAModuleDefinition` (`modules/types.ts`), mirroring `ProjectOverviewTileDef` exactly (same render-prop shape, just `{orgId}` instead of `{projectId}` since this header has no project in scope) — `OrgOverviewPage.tsx` renders whatever an enabled module's `orgOverviewTiles` hand it directly into its own `.grid.grid-metrics` header, alongside the four core stats, without knowing what's inside. `ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles.tsx` (new) contributes three: overall compliance percentage, active standards count, non-compliant projects count — computed via a new shared `orgComplianceSummary.ts::computeOrgComplianceHeadline`, extracted from `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s own previously-inline computation so both surfaces report identical numbers from the same rows rather than risking drift between two copies. **Deliberately labelled differently from `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s own same-numbers `StatCard`s** ("Overall org compliance"/"Compliance standards in use"/"Projects out of compliance" vs. "Overall compliance"/"Active compliance standards"/"Non-compliant projects") — not something the plan text anticipated, but necessary once discovered: `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`'s existing `sections[0]` fallback means the Dashboard group already renders by default underneath the header on every page load, so identical label text in both places would make `getByText`/accessible-name lookups genuinely ambiguous on first render, not just in a contrived edge case. Named as a reusable pattern in `docs/ux-style-guide.md` (new paragraph under "Pattern: project-like drill-down entities") per the human-review request that these lessons generalise beyond compliance.
- **The redundant `Tabs`-inside-`ResourceMenu` layer is gone.** `OrgCompliancePanel.tsx` (and its story file) deleted outright; its three tabs are now three flat top-level `orgOverviewSections` entries in `module.ts`, each rendering `OrgComplianceDashboard`/`OrgComplianceStandardsPanel`/`OrgComplianceOutstandingPanel` directly — `ResourceMenu → Tabs → content` (three layers) collapses to `ResourceMenu → content` (two). This is the style guide's own "when one resource-menu group outgrows itself, split into more flat top-level groups, don't add nested sub-navigation" addendum (first applied to Org Admin's 15-accordion split) applied a second time, one level deeper than its first application already covered — confirmed against the style guide's own settings-hierarchy decision aid before deciding, per the plan's explicit instruction to justify the concrete IA choice rather than picking one ad hoc. `i18n/strings.ts`'s single `groupComplianceOverview` string became three (`groupComplianceDashboard`/`groupComplianceByStandard`/`groupComplianceOutstanding`).
- **The Download PDF/CSV button row moved behind one "Export" `Popover` trigger**, mirroring `CsvImportWizard.tsx`'s own identical Export/Download-template fix (Principle 11's "grouped secondary actions get one door too") line for line — same `Popover`/`anchorRef`/menu-button shape, same disabled-while-downloading behaviour.

**25c — unequal-size stat grids.** `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`'s 4-card header row and `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s uneven rows (now structurally one 9-card block, since the `Tabs` removal above already merged what used to be three separate rows) both converted from `.row.flex-wrap` to the existing `.grid.grid-metrics` utility — no new CSS, matching `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s Tokens section precedent. Named as a reusable rule in the same new style-guide paragraph as 25b's header-tile pattern.

**Post-implementation multi-angle code review (same session), and what it changed.** Four independent review passes (reuse/simplification, cross-file consistency, altitude/convention, and a line-by-line diff scan) were run against the diff before treating this phase as done. Two of the four converged independently on the same real bug: `ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles.tsx` and `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx` both mount together by default (the Dashboard group is `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`'s `sections[0]` fallback) and each fetched `listOrgProjectComplianceStatus(orgId)` independently, doubling the request on every page load and opening a window for the header and body to transiently disagree if data changed mid-load. Fixed with a new `useOrgComplianceStatus.ts` — a per-`orgId` deduplicated cache built on `useSyncExternalStore`, deliberately mirroring `useComplianceNavVisibility.ts`'s own already-established identical shape one directory up rather than inventing a second caching mechanism; both components now read from it instead of fetching independently. This introduced its own gotcha, caught before landing: `ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles.stories.tsx`'s two stories both used `orgId: "org-1"` while expecting *different* data (populated vs. empty) — with a shared module-level cache keyed by `orgId`, whichever story ran first would poison the other's result, the exact hazard `useComplianceNavVisibility.ts`'s own docstring already documents and solves by giving every story a fresh key. Fixed the same way: each story now gets its own distinct `orgId`.

The review also caught `orgComplianceSummary.ts`'s own `distinctProjects` helper duplicated verbatim in `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx` rather than exported and reused — ironic given the file's own docstring says its whole purpose is stopping exactly this kind of drift, just one function short of complete; fixed by exporting it. And `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`'s new `contributedTiles` computation ran unmemoized in the render body — `tile.render({orgId})` builds a fresh React element every call, so any of this page's own `org`/`stats` state resolving independently after mount would hand a mounted tile component a new element identity and force an unnecessary unmount/remount (re-running its own effects). Fixed by wrapping it in `useMemo` keyed on `[modules, orgId]`.

Several other findings were checked and deliberately left unchanged, each because a direct precedent comparison showed the "issue" was a faithful reproduction of an already-shipped, accepted pattern rather than a regression: the Export trigger button staying enabled while a download is in flight, its `Popover`'s `aria-label="Export"` duplicating the trigger's own accessible name, and closing the popover before the download's `try`/`catch` all turned out to be exact matches for `CsvImportWizard.tsx`'s own existing Export popover (verified line-by-line) — "fixing" them here would make this component inconsistent with the pattern it was explicitly built to mirror, and any real improvement belongs on both components at once, out of this phase's scope. A stale bookmark to the retired `/orgs/:orgId/overview/compliance-overview` URL silently falling back to `sections[0]` was flagged too; `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`'s own fallback (`sections.find(...) ?? sections[0]`) predates this phase, and Phase 19 already established the "no redirect shim for a renamed `ResourceMenu` group key" precedent when it retired `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s prior `"compliance"`/`"compliance-overview"` keys the same way — left as-is for consistency rather than a one-off fix. Also confirmed as non-issues: no stale imports of the deleted `OrgCompliancePanel` anywhere (only historical doc comments), the `{project_id, project_name}` → `{id, name}` shape `distinctProjects` returns has no stale consumers, and the three static `StatCard` children in `ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles.tsx` need no React keys (not array-mapped).

**Verification.** `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` all clean, both before and after the review-driven fixes above. Full Storybook suite (`npx vitest run --project=storybook`) run twice — once before the review, once after — both times 834/834 tests passed across 107 files (one confirmed pre-existing, unrelated `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx` unhandled-rejection warning, reproduced in complete isolation on that untouched file, not introduced by this phase). `org-compliance-view.spec.ts` updated for the new IA (three `selectOrgOverviewGroup` calls with the new group labels instead of one group + `getByRole("tab", ...)` clicks; the PDF-download assertion now opens the Export popover first; new assertions for the headline gauges appearing with no group selected) — **not executed against a live stack in this session**; per this repo's own "verify, don't assume" standard, confirm with the Playwright suite before treating this phase as fully closed end-to-end.

Files changed — Frontend: `frontend/src/modules/compliance/ComplianceGlobalNavLink.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/types.ts` (`OrgOverviewTileDef`/`orgOverviewTiles`), `frontend/src/pages/OrgOverviewPage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/compliance/orgComplianceSummary.ts` (new), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/useOrgComplianceStatus.ts` (new), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (new), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/compliance/module.ts`, `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts`, `frontend/src/modules/compliance/OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.stories.tsx`/`OrgComplianceOutstandingPanel.stories.tsx` (`withRouter` path correction), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/OrgCompliancePanel.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (deleted).

Files changed — Docs: `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/compliance-module-plan.md` (Status table, Phase 25 notes), `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

Tests — Playwright: `tests/playwright/tests/modules/compliance/org-compliance-view.spec.ts` (updated for the new IA).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 26: default seed standards (EN 60529, ISO/IEC 27001)

Human-review request: a fresh demo/eval environment showed only the single fictional `ASA-1` standard (`backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py`) — nothing exercising the module against content shaped like a real, recognisable standard, and (confirmed by reading `seed_e2e_dataset.py` directly) no compliance content in the E2E persona dataset at all.

Added two realistic-but-invented standards to `seed_demo_data.py`, each created via the section's existing `create_compliance_standard`/`create_compliance_requirement`/`create_compliance_required_action`/`publish_compliance_version` helpers (no ORM-direct seeding), each with its own small hierarchy built around that standard's real public section structure but invented requirement text — a code comment next to the new seeding block makes explicit these are demo labels only, not a reproduction of either standard's copyrighted text, mirroring `ASA-1`'s own existing framing:

- **EN 60529** (IEC/CENELEC ingress-protection "IP Code") — two sections (first digit/solids, second digit/liquids) with three leaf requirements (IP5X dust, IPX4 splash, IPX6K connector rinse-down), each tied to a plausible drone-fleet reasoning (dust/desert sites, light-rain ops, pressure-washer rinse-down faults). Published, then given an edited version summary via the Phase 24 `update_compliance_version_summary` helper — the phase's own named example of exercising that feature against a fresh standard rather than only `ASA-1`.
- **ISO/IEC 27001** (Annex A control-domain structure) — two sections (A.5 organizational, A.8 technology) with three leaf requirements (documented security policy, privileged-access MFA, encryption at rest/in transit — the latter two deliberately echo `CLOUD_REQUIREMENTS`' own MFA/encryption entries for narrative consistency). Published, then the MFA requirement is given a Phase 24 post-publish clarification (`clarify_compliance_requirement`, adding an explicit break-glass-account carve-out) — the phase's second named example, on a different standard than EN 60529's version-summary edit so both Phase 24 mechanisms get their own fresh demonstration.

**Applicability defaults/exceptions (Phase 20), exercised for the first time in the demo dataset.** ISO/IEC 27001 is set to `applies_to_all_projects` after first excepting `Falcon-3 Avionics Subsystem` (`exclude_project_from_standard_default`, with a reason — the sub-project has no independent customer-data handling or external network access, and is covered under the parent Falcon-3 project's own assessment) — exclusion is created *before* the applicability-default flip specifically so `reconcile_standard_applicability` skips it from the start rather than assigning-then-re-archiving it, per `router.py`'s own docstring on ordering. Verified directly against a freshly reset `tests/container` stack (`docker compose down -v && up -d --build`, then the seed script) that this produces exactly the intended result: real `ProjectCompliance` rows auto-created for Falcon-3 Inspection Drone and Solstice Cloud Platform, none for the excepted Avionics sub-project, and the exclusion's reason persisted. EN 60529 is left at its `opt_in` default and unassigned — no plan requirement to assign it, and doing so was judged out of this phase's own explicitly narrow scope (no new backend behaviour, seed-content-only).

Two new small script-level helpers added for this, following the file's existing per-endpoint-wrapper convention exactly (`h(...)`/`httpx.patch`/`.post`, `raise_for_status()`, one docstring on ordering constraints): `update_standard_applicability_default` and `exclude_project_from_standard_default`.

**`seed_e2e_dataset.py` deliberately left untouched.** Checked every Playwright spec referencing `compliance` (`module-contributed-roles.spec.ts`, `org-admin-modules.spec.ts`, `org-overview.spec.ts`) directly — each creates its own compliance fixtures dynamically via the API rather than depending on a fixed named standard, so per this repo's idempotency rule (dynamically-named fixtures over shared named seed data) there was no genuine need for a stable pre-existing EN 60529/ISO 27001 fixture there, the same "confirmed by reading, not assumed" diligence Phase 15 applied when it made the identical call.

**Verification.** Ran the full seed script end-to-end against a freshly reset `tests/container` stack (backend image rebuilt first, since that stack doesn't bind-mount source) — completed cleanly with no errors, `Compliance standards:` summary line printed as expected. Confirmed via direct API calls (not just script exit code): both new standards published with their requirement hierarchies intact; EN 60529's version summary carries the edited text; ISO/IEC 27001's MFA requirement carries the clarified name; the exclusion row exists with its reason; `applicability_default` is `applies_to_all_projects` on ISO/IEC 27001 only; Falcon-3 and Solstice Cloud Platform each carry a real `ProjectCompliance` row against it while the Avionics sub-project carries none. No new backend behaviour was introduced, so no new automated tests beyond this manual end-to-end run, per the phase's own stated test scope.

Files changed — Backend: `backend/scripts/seed_demo_data.py` (two new applicability-default/exclusion helpers, EN 60529 + ISO/IEC 27001 seeding block, updated closing summary print).

Files changed — Docs: `docs/compliance-module-plan.md` (Status table), `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

Tests: none new (seed-content-only phase, per its own spec) — verified by a live end-to-end run of the seed script instead, see above.

## Full test-suite run after Phase 26, and two unrelated bugs it surfaced (2026-09-09)

Ran every test suite in the repo end to end after Phase 26 landed: backend `ruff`, backend pytest (`tests/container`'s dedicated `reqtrack_pytest_test` database), the mcp-server's own pytest suite, frontend `eslint`/`tsc`+`vite build`, the Storybook/Vitest suite with coverage, and the full Playwright E2E suite (`tests/container`'s `reqtrack_test` database, both `seed_demo_data.py` and `seed_e2e_dataset.py`). This surfaced two pre-existing bugs unrelated to Phase 26 itself; per this repo's own "fix, don't defer" rule both were fixed in the same pass rather than logged as out of scope.

**Import-order lint error, `backend/app/modules/compliance/router.py`.** `ruff check` failed on `I001` — `ComplianceRequirementClarifyRequest` (added by an earlier phase) was inserted above `ComplianceRequirementCreate` alphabetically out of order. Confirmed pre-existing on this branch's `HEAD` (`git stash` + re-check), unrelated to Phase 26's own diff (which never touches this file). One-line mechanical fix via `ruff check --fix`.

**Non-idempotent Playwright spec, `stage-review-and-completion.spec.ts`.** Running the full Playwright suite twice back-to-back against the same `reqtrack_test` database (done here specifically to exercise this repo's own "must survive a repeat run" test-independence rule, not something CI itself does) surfaced real state pollution: this spec's own docstring already documents granting the shared `stakeholderAlpha` persona a real, direct `stakeholder` project role on Alpha-2 via a raw API call ("Alpha-2 has no stakeholder seeded, so this test grants one... this codebase's own established pattern") — but never revoked it afterward. Once granted, the grant is permanent database state, not scoped to the test run, so a second run (or any later spec run against the same seeded database) finds `stakeholderAlpha` with two projects instead of the documented one. This broke two *different* specs downstream — `project-access-scope.spec.ts` ("single-org, single-project user sees exactly one project") and `org-overview.spec.ts` ("a single-org member with partial project access sees scoped totals") — both of which assert on `stakeholderAlpha`'s exact project count. Fixed by adding a cleanup `test.step` that revokes the same role via `DELETE /projects/{id}/roles/{user_id}/stakeholder` (idempotent regardless of whether the role is currently held — a no-op `DELETE` on an absent row, same tolerance the existing grant step already relies on for its own re-run safety) once the spec's own assertions are done with it. Verified by resetting `tests/container` to a clean slate, reseeding both datasets fresh, and running the full 131-spec Playwright suite exactly once end to end with the fix in place — passed cleanly except for one confirmed environmental flake (see below), with none of the previously-broken downstream specs affected.

**Unrelated strict-mode locator collision, `tests/mockup-engagement.spec.ts`.** A bare `page.getByText("Overview").click()` started resolving to two elements once the nav rail grew an "Organisation overview" link (Phase 19, well before Phase 26) — Playwright's `getByText` matches by case-insensitive substring by default, and "Overview" is a substring of "Organisation overview". Fixed by scoping to `page.getByRole("link", { name: "Overview", exact: true })`, the same pattern already used at `overview-new-requirement-side-panel.spec.ts:23` and `project-compliance-view.spec.ts:81` for the identical ambiguity — convergence on an existing precedent, not a new one.

**One confirmed environmental flake, not a bug: `page.waitForEvent("download")` timeouts on the org-level bundle-export specs.** Across three consecutive full-suite runs plus targeted re-runs in one continuous session, `org-merge-import.spec.ts` and `org-bundle-export-import.spec.ts` each independently hit a 30s timeout waiting for the browser "download" event after clicking "Export organisation bundle" — never `project-bundle-export-import.spec.ts` (a materially smaller export). Re-running the failing spec alone immediately afterward passed in 5.1s, nowhere near the 30s budget — consistent with resource contention from running the full suite repeatedly back-to-back in a short window (three ~11-13 minute single-worker Playwright runs plus a Storybook/Vitest run and a 23-minute backend pytest run, all in the same session), not a reproducible defect in the export path itself. No code change made for this; noted here in case it recurs and turns out to be more than environmental.

**Full results.** Backend pytest: 1046 passed. mcp-server pytest: 32 passed, 4 skipped. Frontend `eslint`: 0 errors (7 pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings left as-is — see below). Frontend `tsc`+`vite build`: clean. Storybook/Vitest: passed, 74.9% line coverage. ## Cleared the 7 pre-existing `react-refresh` ESLint warnings flagged above (2026-09-09)

Investigated before fixing rather than assuming a file-split was needed everywhere, since `eslint.config.js` already carries a documented, deliberate exception mechanism for exactly this rule: `react-refresh/only-export-components`'s `allowExportNames` option, with a comment explaining it exists specifically because "Context modules intentionally colocate a Provider component with its paired hook... `allowExportNames` is the plugin's own documented escape hatch for exactly this case" — already used for 11 other hook/helper exports (`useAuth`, `useTheme`, `resolveLandingPath`, `toErrorMessage`, etc.). Six of the seven warnings were exactly this same already-established pattern, just not yet added to the list: `useBranding`/`useOrgLabel`/`useOrgLabelCapitalized`/`useOrgLabelPlural` (`BrandingContext.tsx`, all four colocated with `BrandingProvider`), `useFavourites` (`FavouritesContext.tsx`, colocated with `FavouritesProvider`), and `resolveEffectiveTheme` (`ThemeContext.tsx` — a plain pure helper colocated with `ThemeProvider`, the same category as the already-allow-listed `resolveLandingPath`/`tabPanelProps`/`toErrorMessage`). Added all six to `allowExportNames` rather than splitting four files and updating call sites for no benefit beyond what the existing convention already accepts as fine.

The seventh, `SortableHeader.tsx`'s `cycleSort`, genuinely didn't fit that rationale — it isn't a context file, and `cycleSort` isn't a hook paired with a Provider; it's a plain state-transition helper shared by every sortable table's own click handler, imported separately from the `SortableHeader` component itself at several call sites already (`ProjectMembersTable.tsx` imports `cycleSort`/`SortState` but never `SortableHeader`). This one got a real split, following this codebase's own established `AuthContext.tsx`/`AuthContextValue.ts` precedent (a value-only file imported directly by call sites, no re-export shim): new `frontend/src/components/sortState.ts` holds `SortDirection`, `SortState`, and `cycleSort`; `SortableHeader.tsx` now exports only the `SortableHeader` component (importing `SortState` back from `sortState.ts` for its own prop type). Updated the 10 call sites that imported `cycleSort`/`SortState` from `SortableHeader.tsx` to import from `sortState.ts` instead, keeping any `SortableHeader` component import on its original path.

**Verification.** `npm run lint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors (was 0 errors/7 warnings). `npm run build` (tsc + vite): clean. Storybook/Vitest suite: passed — confirms `SortableHeader.stories.tsx` and `DirectoryTable.stories.tsx`, both of which import `SortState`/`cycleSort`, still resolve correctly against the new file.

Files changed — Frontend: `frontend/eslint.config.js` (`allowExportNames` +6), `frontend/src/components/sortState.ts` (new), `frontend/src/components/SortableHeader.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/SortableHeader.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/DirectoryTable.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/ProjectMembersTable.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.tsx`/`OrgAdminPage.tsx`/`ServerManagementPage.tsx`/`ProjectActionsPage.tsx`/`ChangeRequestsPage.tsx`/`RequirementsPage.tsx` (import path only, no logic changes).

Tests: none new — this is a pure lint-warning cleanup with no behavioural change; existing Storybook/Playwright coverage of the affected components/pages is unaffected and still passes.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 27: Organisation Overview — stat-grid overlap fix, table/compact layout, resource-menu structural consistency

Third human-review round (compliance-module-plan.md Phases 27-30), this phase covering three related `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`/`ResourceMenu.tsx` defects the user found by reviewing the live Organisation Overview page directly.

**27a — stat-tile overlap, root cause confirmed and fixed.** `StatCard` sets `minWidth: 220` inline while `.grid-metrics` (`theme.css`) sized its `auto-fit` columns from `minmax(160px, 1fr)` — a track minimum smaller than the item's own minimum content width, so `auto-fit` could resolve columns narrower than the `StatCard`s placed in them, overlapping neighbours once the grid carried enough tiles (up to 7 on Organisation Overview: 4 core + 3 compliance headline tiles). Fixed by raising the track minimum to `220px` to match `StatCard` exactly. Checked every other `.grid-metrics` consumer per the phase's own instruction: `MetricTile` (`ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`, `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`) sets no inline `minWidth` of its own, so it was never mismatched — only `StatCard`'s own consumers (`OrgOverviewPage.tsx`, `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`) were affected, and both are fixed by the one shared CSS change.

**27b — cards replaced with a compact/table layout. Decided by: User** (explicit ask that the "cumbersome boxes" become a table). New `StatBar`/`StatBarEntry` (`frontend/src/components/StatBar.tsx`) — a single bordered `<dl>` row, each label/value pair separated by a divider, replacing per-tile `.card` chrome for a page's own top-level, always-visible stats header. Deliberately scoped narrowly: `.grid.grid-metrics`/`StatCard` stays the right shape for grouped/paged stat blocks elsewhere (`OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s own nine-tile grid, reached after selecting a `ResourceMenu` group, is untouched) — `StatBar` is only for the one block that's always on screen regardless of which group is active. `ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles.tsx` (the compliance module's `orgOverviewTiles` contribution) now renders `StatBarEntry` instead of `StatCard` so its three headline gauges match the row it splices into. Documented as a scoped revision of Phase 25c's grid rule in `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, not a replacement for it.

**27c — structural consistency: stats header folded into a real "Overview" `ResourceMenu` group. Decided by: Agent** (this planning session's own reading of the review note — confirmed against the code before a refactor: an org with no module contributing an `orgOverviewSections` group saw only a stats header with nothing structurally below it, while an org with one saw the stats header pinned above the menu as a separate, non-optional block). Fix, in two parts:
- `OrgOverviewPage.tsx` now contributes its own always-present "Overview" group (first, default-selected, preserving the old `sections[0]` fallback's practical effect) alongside whatever a module contributes — the whole page is one `ResourceMenu`-driven surface, nothing pinned above it. The stats row (`StatBar` + the "scoped, not full totals" caption) is that group's own content.
- `ResourceMenu.tsx` itself (not any one caller) now skips rendering its menu-strip chrome (`<nav>`/`<ul>` of group links) whenever `groups.length <= 1`, rendering `children` directly instead — a core, shared fix benefiting every `ResourceMenu` consumer with the same "sometimes there's only one group" shape, not an Organisation-Overview-specific one-off. Verified none of the app's other five `ResourceMenu` consumers (Org Admin, Project Admin, Server Admin, Preferences, Compliance Settings) ever pass exactly one group — all are fixed multi-group admin pages — so this is a strictly additive fix for them.

Both new patterns recorded in `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: project-like drill-down entities" (27b) and "Pattern: settings hierarchy" (27c) sections, next to the existing Phase 25b/25c/settings-hierarchy notes they extend.

**Verification.** `npx tsc -b`, `npm run lint` (targeted + full), clean. Storybook/Vitest: new/updated stories in `OrgOverviewPage.stories.tsx` (core stats render inside `.stat-bar`; "Overview" chrome hidden with zero module sections, shown with one, correctly defaulting to "Overview" rather than the module's own section) and `ResourceMenu.stories.tsx` (new 0-group/1-group/many-group stories covering the chrome-hide rule) all pass, plus the untouched `ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles.stories.tsx`/`OrgComplianceDashboard.stories.tsx`/`StatCard.stories.tsx`/`MetricTile.stories.tsx`/`ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx`/`StandardWorkspacePage.stories.tsx` re-run clean (confirms `StatCard`'s own consumers outside `OrgOverviewPage.tsx` are unaffected). Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image, then ran `org-overview.spec.ts` and `org-admin-modules.spec.ts` live against it (twice back-to-back, per this repo's idempotency rule) plus `org-compliance-view.spec.ts` and `module-contributed-roles.spec.ts` for regression coverage of the `ResourceMenu`/compliance-header changes — all pass. `org-overview.spec.ts` gained a new test exercising both the single-group (chrome hidden) and multi-group (chrome shown, "Overview" first and default-active) cases by toggling the Compliance module off/on for `orgAdminGamma` directly (no persona in the seed dataset has Compliance disabled — confirmed via `org-admin-modules.spec.ts`, which already documents it "entitled and enabled by default"), restoring the toggle afterward. Also visually confirmed via a live browser session (Playwright MCP, used sparingly per this repo's own guidance and only because this phase is specifically about a visual overlap/compactness defect): Alpha's 7-tile `StatBar` row (4 core + 3 compliance headline stats) renders with no overlap at both desktop and a 480px mobile viewport, stacking to a single column with top dividers below 720px.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 28: entity quick-switch pattern (chevron + popover)

Third human-review round, continued (compliance-module-plan.md Phases 27-30). **Decided by: User** — explicit ask for "a chevron next to the org name that, when clicked, brings up a list pop-up to allow you to switch directly," and explicitly requested as "a standard UX feature... applied to projects, standards, org management etc." rather than a one-off on Organisation Overview alone.

**New generic component: `EntitySwitcher` (`frontend/src/components/EntitySwitcher.tsx`).** A `ChevronDown` trigger + the existing `Popover` component (reused directly, not a second dropdown mechanism), parameterized only by the current entity's id and a `loadOptions` loader returning `{id, label, href}[]` — no module- or entity-specific logic inside it, matching this plan's own "build the generic mechanism once" habit (Phase 25b's `orgOverviewTiles`, Phase 23's expandable-nav-rail pattern). Renders nothing while the sibling list is loading, resolves empty, or the loader itself fails — a secondary navigation affordance disappearing quietly is preferable to it ever breaking or error-toasting the page it sits on (this also meant every pre-existing story for the five consuming pages, which don't mock the new sibling-list fetch, kept passing unmodified — the failed fetch is simply swallowed and the switcher renders nothing, exactly the same as a genuinely-empty list). Once the sibling list exceeds 8 entries, a filter input appears above it, reusing `UserAutocomplete`'s own lowercase/trim/substring-filter/cap idiom (not the component itself, which carries user/group-selection semantics this list doesn't need).

**Applied to all five call sites the phase spec named, in order:**
- **Organisation Overview** (`OrgOverviewPage.tsx`) — sibling list from `GET /orgs?mine=true`, filtered to active orgs.
- **Project Overview and Project Admin** (`ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`, `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`) — sibling list from `GET /projects?archived=false` (the same unfiltered fetch `ProjectListPage.tsx`'s own parent-project picker already uses), pointed at each page's own target path (`/projects/:id` vs. `/projects/:id/admin`).
- **Standard workspace** (`StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`) — sibling list via a new shared helper, `listStandardsAcrossMyOrgs` (`modules/compliance/api.ts`), extracted out of `StandardListPage.tsx`'s own pre-existing cross-org fan-out (`GET /orgs?mine=true` then `Promise.allSettled` over `listStandards(orgId)` per org, dropping a 404'd org silently — module disabled there) rather than duplicating that fan-out a second time. `StandardListPage.tsx` itself now calls the same helper instead of carrying its own copy of the logic.
- **Org Admin** (`OrgAdminPage.tsx`) — added to both of its *degraded* headers (a server admin hitting a disabled org, or one they aren't a member of) rather than its normal admin header, which renders its title through `ResourceMenu`'s own `title` prop and has no bespoke `<h1>` of its own to attach a chevron to. Framed here as a deliberate escape hatch off an otherwise dead-end page — a server admin stuck on one org's disabled/not-a-member view can jump straight to a different, working org via the same `?mine=true` list, rather than only "Enable"/"join as admin"/back-to-`/orgs`.

Two org-scoped loaders (`loadOrgSwitcherOptions`, `loadProjectSwitcherOptions`) live in a new shared `frontend/src/utils/entitySwitcherLoaders.ts` rather than duplicated across `OrgOverviewPage.tsx`/`OrgAdminPage.tsx`/`ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`/`ProjectAdminPage.tsx`, each parameterized by which target page ("overview" vs. "admin") to point sibling links at. The compliance standards loader stays inside `modules/compliance/` (not this shared core file) per this repo's Modular Feature System Boundary — a core file must never import from a module's own directory; `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx` builds its own loader locally, calling `complianceApi.listStandardsAcrossMyOrgs`.

**`docs/ux-style-guide.md`.** New "Pattern: entity quick-switch" section (after "Pattern: wayfinding"), plus a clarifying parenthetical appended directly to Principle 9 distinguishing this chevron from the tenant switcher that principle rejects — confirmed via direct search that no switcher of any kind existed anywhere in the codebase before this phase, and the distinction is that this chevron only ever appears on a page already scoped to one specific entity instance by its own URL (a navigation shortcut between sibling instances, not a global mode switch with ambient state), matching the phase spec's own explicit instruction to record this alongside Principle 9 rather than let a future reader see the new pattern as reversing it.

**Verification.** `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` on every changed/new file: clean. Storybook/Vitest: new `EntitySwitcher.stories.tsx` (no-siblings renders nothing; single sibling with no filter input; many-siblings filtering; selecting a sibling closes the popover) plus one new story per consuming page (`OrgOverviewPage.stories.tsx`, `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx`, `ProjectAdminPage.stories.tsx`, `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`, `StandardWorkspacePage.stories.tsx`) — 143 tests across all seven affected story files pass, including every pre-existing story on the five consuming pages (none needed updating, per the "fails quietly" design above). Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image, then ran the new `entity-quick-switch.spec.ts` E2E spec (org-admin-alpha-beta persona switches from Alpha's to Beta's Organisation Overview via the chevron popover) plus regression runs of `org-overview.spec.ts`, `project-admin-structural.spec.ts`, and `compliance-standards-management.spec.ts` — all pass.

Files changed — Frontend: `frontend/src/components/EntitySwitcher.tsx`/`.stories.tsx` (new), `frontend/src/utils/entitySwitcherLoaders.ts` (new), `frontend/src/pages/OrgOverviewPage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/ProjectOverviewPage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/ProjectAdminPage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/OrgAdminPage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/compliance/api.ts` (new `listStandardsAcrossMyOrgs`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardListPage.tsx` (now calls the shared helper), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`.

Files changed — Docs: `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/compliance-module-plan.md` (Status table), `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

Tests — Playwright: `tests/playwright/tests/e2e-workflows/entity-quick-switch.spec.ts` (new).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 29: Standard workspace Versions nav — auto-expand, version quick-switch, exact-match and chevron-styling fixes

Third human-review round, continued (compliance-module-plan.md Phases 27-30). Three confirmed defects in `StandardNavSection.tsx`'s expandable "Versions" group (Phase 23), each verified against the actual code before fixing, not assumed from the spec text alone.

**29a — auto-expand on a version's own route.** `StandardNavSection.tsx` now computes `routeForcesExpand` (`location.pathname.startsWith(`${versionsBase}/`)`) and ORs it into `effectiveExpanded` at render time only — it never writes through to the persisted `useUiPreference` value, so a route landing that forces the group open doesn't silently overwrite a user's own prior manual collapse choice the next time they open a different, non-version page. A second piece of local (non-persisted) state, `autoExpandSuppressed`, lets a manual click on the toggle actually collapse the group while its own route is still forcing it open — without this, OR-composition alone means the toggle can never visually collapse anything while `routeForcesExpand` stays true, which would have shipped a dead-looking button; found and fixed during implementation, before writing any test against it. Resets on every `location.pathname` change, so the next version page auto-expands fresh.

**29b — version quick-switch, depended on Phase 28.** `VersionWorkspace.tsx` renders `EntitySwitcher` ("Switch version") next to its own heading, sourced from the component's own existing `versions` prop (already fetched by `StandardNavSection`/`StandardVersionsSection` for the same standard) mapped to `{id, label, href}` — no new fetch, exactly as the phase spec called for.

**29c — exact-match highlight.** The "Versions" row's active check moved from the default `startsWith` (via plain `NavRailLink`) to an exact `location.pathname === versionsBase` comparison, computed directly in `StandardNavSection.tsx` since the row's own markup changed under 29d (below) and no longer delegates to `NavRailLink` when expandable. The non-expandable fallback path (rail collapsed, or no versions) still uses `NavRailLink` but now passes `exact` explicitly too, for the same reason Phase 25a already fixed this shape once for `ComplianceGlobalNavLink.tsx`.

**29d — chevron restyle.** New `.nav-link-row`/`.nav-link-row-link`/`.nav-link-row-toggle` classes in `theme.css` replace the toggle's old `.btn` styling. The background moves from the inner link to the wrapping row, so hovering anywhere in the row — including directly over the toggle — highlights the whole thing as one surface (a child element's box sits inside its parent's, so the parent's own `:hover` already fires without any extra JS or a `:has()` selector). The link and the toggle stay two separate, independently focusable/clickable elements (`<div>` wrapping a real `<Link>` plus a real `<button>`) — no `role="button"`-container rework needed, since neither element nests inside the other.

**`docs/ux-style-guide.md`.** "Pattern: expandable nav-rail group" gets four new bullets (the route-driven auto-expand rule, the exact-match rule, the shared-hover-surface toggle rule, and the "offer the quick-switch chevron on the child's own drill-down page too" rule) plus one existing bullet's wording correction (it previously described the toggle as "styled like every other nav-rail control," which Phase 29d's fix makes no longer accurate).

**Verification.** `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` on every changed file: clean. Storybook/Vitest: `StandardNavSection.stories.tsx` gained three new stories (`AutoExpandsOnDirectVersionRoute`, `ManualCollapseOverridesRouteForcedExpand`, `ToggleSharesRowSurfaceWithLink`); `VersionWorkspace.stories.tsx` gained two (`EntitySwitcherOffersSiblingVersion`, `NoSiblingVersionHidesSwitcher`) — all 4 existing stories in the first file kept passing unmodified (their accessible names for the toggle/link were left unchanged by the restyle). One real authoring bug found and fixed along the way: `StandardNavSection.stories.tsx`'s meta-level `withRouter` decorator combined with a second, story-level `withRouter` decorator (needed to land two of the new stories directly on a version's own route) nested two `<MemoryRouter>`s and threw — fixed by moving `withRouter` out of the shared `meta.decorators` and onto every individual story instead, matching `StandardWorkspacePage.stories.tsx`'s own established convention for this exact reason. Full Storybook suite (857 tests, 109 files): all pass. Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image, then ran the new `standard-version-nav.spec.ts` E2E spec (3 tests: auto-expand-on-direct-navigation, manual-collapse-overrides-route-force, version quick-switch) plus a regression pass of the full `tests/modules/compliance/` suite and `entity-quick-switch.spec.ts`/`org-overview.spec.ts` — all pass, after fixing one now-stale assertion this phase's own 29a fix broke: `compliance-standards-management.spec.ts`'s Phase 23 test navigated straight into a version's workspace via a stat tile and then tried to click a now-nonexistent "Expand versions" button (the group is now already expanded on arrival, by design) — updated to assert the group is already expanded instead of clicking to expand it.

Files changed — Frontend: `frontend/src/modules/compliance/StandardNavSection.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/compliance/VersionWorkspace.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`, `frontend/src/styles/theme.css`.

Files changed — Docs: `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, `docs/compliance-module-plan.md` (Status table), `docs/decisions.md` (this entry).

Files changed — Tests: `tests/playwright/tests/modules/compliance/standard-version-nav.spec.ts` (new), `tests/playwright/tests/modules/compliance/compliance-standards-management.spec.ts` (stale assertion fixed).

**Same-day follow-up (2026-09-09): drop the `.badge` chip from the expanded version rows.** **Decided by: User** — direct instruction that the status "badge" in the nav-rail's expanded version list read as visual noise on a small, indented sub-link row; replace it with plain parenthesised text (e.g. "v1.0 (Published)") instead of a separately-chip-styled `<span className="badge">`. `StandardNavSection.tsx`'s version row now renders `{version.version_label} ({STATUS_LABEL[version.status]})` as one plain text node. Two Storybook assertions in `StandardNavSection.stories.tsx`'s `ExpandingListsVersions` story relied on the old two-node structure (`getByText("Published")`/`getByText("Draft")`, which testing-library matches by exact full node text, not substring) — updated to assert the full combined accessible link name (`"v1.0 (Published)"`/`"v2.0 (Draft)"`) instead, which the two `toHaveAttribute("href", ...)` checks already needed anyway. No other test needed changing: every Playwright spec asserting this text (`compliance-standards-management.spec.ts`, `standard-version-nav.spec.ts`) uses Playwright's own `getByText`/`hasText`, which substring-matches by default, so "v1.0 (Published)" already satisfies a check for "Published". Verified: `tsc`/`eslint` clean; `StandardNavSection.stories.tsx` (7 tests) passes; rebuilt/recreated the `tests/container` frontend image and reran the full `tests/modules/compliance/` Playwright suite (12/12) twice — clean both times (one earlier run of just this file had one transient, unrelated flake on the quick-switch test that did not reproduce, consistent with this repo's known shared-persona/DB-timing flake family, not a regression from this change).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 30: group-based grants for module-contributed roles + Standards member-picker parity

Fourth and final phase of the third human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 27-30) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** at the plan level (this phase deliberately reverses Phase 2's own previously-settled "module-role inheritance through groups... V1 is direct grants only" scope decision — the user was explicit that the exclusion was never their own decision and asked for the full mechanism, not a UI-only workaround); implementation specifics below are this session's own judgment calls (**Decided by: Agent**) except where flagged otherwise.

**30a — the generic group-grant mechanism (core, not compliance-specific).** New model `GroupModuleRole` (`backend/app/models/module_role.py`) — structurally `UserModuleRole` with `org_group_id` (FK `org_groups.id`, CASCADE, indexed) in place of `user_id`, otherwise identical (`module_key`/`role_key`/`organization_id`/`project_id`/`scope_entity_id`/`granted_by`, same app-level dedup convention). `backend/app/services/rbac.py::_has_module_role_grant` gained a second branch: after finding no direct `UserModuleRole` match, it queries `GroupModuleRole` for the same `(module_key, role_key)` and scope filters, expands each granted `org_group_id` to include every group transitively nested inside it (`_descendant_org_group_ids` — the exact downward expansion `_direct_project_member_ids_base` already performs for `OrgGroupProjectRole`, reused rather than re-derived, per the phase's own spec), then checks `OrgGroupMember` for the acting user against that expanded set in one query. A new public `rbac.effective_org_group_member_ids(db, org_group_id)` factors out "every user a group transitively reaches" as a first-class core helper — compliance's own previously-narrow, single-purpose `service.py::_effective_org_group_member_ids` (Phase 22, whose docstring explicitly said "not a generalisation... per that phase's own boundary") is now a one-line delegate to it, since Phase 30 is exactly the reversal that docstring was written to flag as not-yet-done. Migration `backend/alembic/versions/0037_group_module_roles.py` creates `group_module_roles`, continuing the core Alembic chain from the Compliance module's own most recent migration (0036) — the same "core change, core chain, even though the revision number continues on from the module's own directory" situation 0034's own docstring already established for `scope_entity_id`.

**Compliance's own endpoints, on top of that core mechanism.** `POST/DELETE .../standards/{id}/group-roles(/{org_group_id}/{role_key})` (`router.py::assign_standard_group_role`/`revoke_standard_group_role`) — same `_require_standard_manage` gate, same cross-tenant `org_group_id`-must-belong-to-this-org check `assign_group_project_role` already applies one tier up, same idempotent-grant/silent-no-op-revoke conventions as the existing per-user endpoints. `GET .../standards/{id}/members` now also returns `group_members: ComplianceStandardGroupMemberOut[]` (`org_group_id`, `group_name`, `role_keys`, and a live-resolved `member_count`) alongside the existing `members` list.

**The manager floor now counts group coverage.** New `service.py::standard_manager_floor_covered_by_group_grants(db, standard_id, *, exclude_org_group_id=None)` — true if any `GroupModuleRole` `standards_manager` grant on the standard (other than `exclude_org_group_id`, when revoking that grant's own row) has a group with at least one effective member. Both `revoke_standard_member_role` (revoking a direct grant) and the new `revoke_standard_group_role` (revoking a group grant) now check this alongside the pre-existing `standard_manager_floor_covered_by_fallback` org-wide-fallback check before 400ing on "last manager" — a standard with a direct manager, a covering group grant, *or* fallback-group coverage is never falsely blocked, and removing the *only* remaining source of any of the three is still blocked exactly as before.

**30b — Standards member-picker frontend parity.** `StandardMembersSection.tsx`'s add-member flow rebuilt on `UserAutocomplete` (search-as-you-type, debounced server-side user search via `organizationId`, client-side org-group matching via `groups`/`onSelectGroup`) — replacing the flagged plain, unfiltered `<select>` — mirroring `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s own "manage users" add-flow wiring one level down (`addManageUsersGroupRole` → `POST .../group-roles`, same shape this phase's own backend endpoint above follows). `onSelectExternal` deliberately left unwired, per the phase's own explicit scope note — flagged here rather than silently built or silently assumed unnecessary. The roster (`DirectoryTable`) gained a second row kind for group grants, visually distinguished with the same `Users` icon + "Org group" badge `UserAutocomplete` already uses for a group match in its own dropdown, rather than expanding a group's row into its individual members — this stays a roster of the standard's own *direct* (user or group) grants, matching Phase 22's own original framing. The last-manager-checkbox client-side disable hint (a UX aid only; the backend re-checks authoritatively) was extended to count a group row's own `standards_manager` grant toward `managerCount` whenever that group's `member_count > 0`, mirroring the backend's own "zero-member group isn't real coverage" logic. `StandardWorkspacePage.tsx` now also fetches `orgGroups` (`GET .../orgs/{id}/groups`) alongside the existing `orgUsers` fetch, threaded down as a new required prop.

**Tests.** Backend: `tests/test_module_contributed_roles.py` gained three new tests against the *generic* mechanism (a fake fixture module, not Compliance) — an org-scoped `GroupModuleRole` grant is honoured for a group member and stops being honoured on removal from the group or grant revocation; the same but through a group nested inside the granted group (descendant expansion); the project-scoped equivalent. `app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_standard_scoped_rbac.py` gained eight new tests exercising the same mechanism through Compliance's own endpoints: group membership grants and revokes standard-manage access; leaving the group removes access; revoking the group's own role removes access; the roster correctly reports `group_members`/`member_count`; a `standards_contributor` is refused (403) on both new group-grant endpoints (RBAC boundary, mirroring Phase 22's own contributor-boundary test); the manager floor is satisfied by a covering group grant (a direct grant can then be safely removed) and is *not* satisfied once that group grant is the sole remaining coverage (its own removal 400s); grants are audit-logged (`entity_type="group_module_role"`). Full re-run: `test_schema_migrations_match_models.py` (model/migration parity), `test_module_contributed_roles.py`, `test_org_group_project_roles.py`, `test_org_group_nesting.py`, and the entire `app/modules/compliance/tests/` package — 230 tests, all pass, run as a single sequential `pytest` invocation per this repo's standing concurrent-pytest rule. `ruff` clean on every touched/new backend file.

Frontend: `StandardMembersSection.stories.tsx` rewritten for the new `UserAutocomplete`-based flow and the new group-grant row — 10 stories (existing roster/last-manager-disabled/last-manager-fallback-enabled cases, plus new: lists a group grant with its member count, last-manager checkbox enabled via group coverage, add-via-search for both a user and a group, and a no-groups-available case). `StandardWorkspacePage.stories.tsx`'s existing API mock updated to also serve `.../groups` (previously unmocked, now exercised by the new `orgGroups` fetch) — an omission the full Storybook suite run caught directly (8 unhandled-rejection errors) before it could reach a real deployment. `tsc -b`/`eslint` clean; full `vitest run --project=storybook` (109 files, 861 tests) passes clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx` "Load Error" story still logs its own already-expected unhandled-rejection warning, untouched by this change).

Playwright: `compliance-standard-scoped-rbac.spec.ts`'s existing test updated for the new search-based add flow (the old `selectOption("User", ...)` no longer has an element to select against); new second test, "granting standards_manager to an org group lets its member perform a manager-gated action" — creates a dynamically-named org group and adds `memberAlphaBeta` to it via direct API calls (mirroring `preferences-and-theme.spec.ts`'s own dynamic-group-fixture convention), grants the group `standards_manager` through the real UI search flow, then logs in as that member (who holds no direct grant of their own) and successfully archives the standard — a genuine manager-gated action. Both rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` backend+frontend images first (confirmed migration 0037 applied, head revision), then ran live: 2/2 pass. One bug found and fixed while writing the group test: `orgGroups` is fetched once, on standard-page mount — creating the group via the API *after* already landing on the standard's page (needed, since the standard has to exist first to scope the grant) left that in-memory list stale; fixed with an explicit `page.reload()` before opening "Add member", with a comment recording why. Full `tests/modules/compliance/` suite re-run live afterward: 12/13 pass, the one failure (`standard-version-nav.spec.ts`'s quick-switch test) reproducing only in the full-suite run and passing cleanly 3/3 in isolation — the same known shared-persona/DB-timing flake family Phase 29's own entry above already documented, not a regression from this change.

`docs/soc2/policies/access-control-policy.md`'s Authorization section (item 3's module-contributed-roles paragraph, item 6's module-owned-entity-scope paragraph, and the role-resolution diagram's own scope note) updated to record that module-contributed roles — including the module-owned entity scope Phase 22 added — are no longer direct-grant-only: a `GroupModuleRole` grant to an org group now also satisfies them, resolved the same transitive way `OrgGroupProjectRole` already resolves for core `ProjectRole` grants. The previously-accurate "explicitly *not* participating in group/hierarchy inheritance" language is corrected rather than left stale, since a SOC 2 policy document describing a boundary this phase deliberately removes would otherwise misstate the live authorization model to a future reader/auditor.
