## Compliance module plan, Phase 31: compliance status — fail-safe "unassessed" state

First phase of the fourth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 31-36) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** that the defect must be fixed (a standard attached to a project but never assessed displayed "Non-compliant: No," reading as "checked and clean" when nothing had been checked); **Decided by: Agent** on the specific three-state shape, per the plan's own "Open decisions" entry recorded alongside this phase.

**Root cause, confirmed exactly as diagnosed in the plan.** `service.py::summarize_project_compliance`'s `has_non_compliant` only ever flips true on an explicit `NON_COMPLIANT` row; a freshly attached standard has every applicable row at the default `NOT_STARTED`, so `has_non_compliant` stays `False` and the two display sites (`ProjectCompliancePage.tsx`'s "Non-compliant" column, `ProjectComplianceDetail.tsx`'s badge) both collapsed that into a binary Yes/No or badge-absent-means-fine render — indistinguishable from a standard that had actually been assessed and found compliant.

**Fix.** Added a new `not_yet_assessed: bool` field to `ProjectComplianceStatusSummary`/`ProjectComplianceStatusOut` (`service.py`, `schemas.py`) — `True` when `applicable_count > 0` and every applicable row's status is still `NOT_STARTED`. Deliberately a field of its own, not folded into `overall_compliance_state` (left with its existing four-value meaning intact, since `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.tsx`/`StandardProjectsPanel.tsx`/`StandardWorkspacePage.tsx`/`orgComplianceSummary.ts` all already read that field directly and correctly bucket an unassessed assignment under "in_progress," not "compliant" — confirmed by direct inspection before deciding not to touch them, per the plan's own "check every other consumer of the same root cause" instruction). A new shared `types.ts::complianceRiskLabel(status)` returns `"Yes"` (has_non_compliant) / `"Unknown"` (not_yet_assessed) / `"No"` (genuinely assessed clean) — both display sites now go through this one function rather than each re-deriving the three-way branch. `ProjectComplianceDetail.tsx` gained a second, `--color-warning`-styled "Not yet assessed" badge alongside the existing "Contains non-compliant requirements" one, shown only when `not_yet_assessed` is true and `has_non_compliant` is false.

**Scope check on other consumers, per the plan's explicit instruction.** Grepped every runtime (non-story) use of `.has_non_compliant` and every reader of `overall_compliance_state`/`ProjectComplianceStatusOut` across `backend/app/modules/compliance/` and `frontend/src/modules/compliance/` before concluding the bug was confined to the two named sites: `reports.py`'s CSV/PDF export renders the 4-state `overall_compliance_state` label directly (never a `has_non_compliant`-only binary); `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.tsx`'s Compliant/Non-Compliant/In-Progress columns and `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s "Non-compliant projects" tile / `orgComplianceSummary.ts`'s weighted percentage all key off `overall_compliance_state` (an unassessed row already lands in "in_progress," not "compliant") or count only rows where `overall_compliance_state === "non_compliant"` (which stays correct and non-misleading — it doesn't count unassessed rows as non-compliant, but it also never displays them as confirmed-clean). None of these needed changing.

**Tests.** Backend: `test_project_status_calculation` (`app/modules/compliance/tests/test_project_compliance_api.py`) extended with three new assertions — a freshly assigned standard with zero assessments reports `has_non_compliant: False` / `not_yet_assessed: True` / `overall_compliance_state: "in_progress"`; after partial assessment (some rows compliant/in-progress, none left Not Started) `not_yet_assessed` flips back to `False`, distinct from both the fresh state and the later non-compliant state; the existing non-compliant-push assertion gained an explicit `not_yet_assessed: False` check alongside it. Frontend: two new Storybook stories each on `ProjectCompliancePage.stories.tsx` (`ListsUnassessedStandard`) and `ProjectComplianceDetail.stories.tsx` (`NonCompliantAssignment`, `NotYetAssessedAssignment`) covering all three render states and asserting the wrong-state text is absent, not just that the right one is present. Playwright: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` gained an assertion immediately after standard assignment (before any assessment) that the assignment's own table row renders "Unknown" in the Non-compliant column — reusing that spec's existing flow rather than a new test/persona, since the fresh-assignment moment it already creates is exactly the state this phase fixes.

**Verification.** `tsc --noEmit` clean. Backend: full `app/modules/compliance/tests/` package, one sequential `pytest` invocation — 176 passed. Frontend: `vitest run --project=storybook` on every touched story file (`ProjectCompliancePage`, `ProjectComplianceDetail`, `ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles`, `ComplianceProjectOverviewTiles`, `OrgComplianceDashboard`, `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel`, `StandardProjectsPanel`) — all pass (33 tests across 7 files). Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` backend+frontend images, then ran live: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` (1/1, including the new assertion), `org-compliance-view.spec.ts` (1/1), `standard-applicability-defaults.spec.ts` (2/2) — no regression in any spec reading `overall_compliance_state`/the org-wide dashboard.

Files changed — Backend: `backend/app/modules/compliance/service.py` (`ProjectComplianceStatusSummary.not_yet_assessed`, `summarize_project_compliance`, `build_status_out`, docstring), `backend/app/modules/compliance/schemas.py` (`ProjectComplianceStatusOut.not_yet_assessed`).

Files changed — Backend tests: `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_project_compliance_api.py`.

Files changed — Frontend: `frontend/src/modules/compliance/types.ts` (`ProjectComplianceStatus.not_yet_assessed`, `complianceRiskLabel`), `frontend/src/modules/compliance/ProjectCompliancePage.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/compliance/ProjectComplianceDetail.tsx`, and the fixture-only addition of `not_yet_assessed` to every `ProjectComplianceStatus` story fixture (`ProjectCompliancePage.stories.tsx`, `ProjectComplianceDetail.stories.tsx`, `ComplianceOrgOverviewTiles.stories.tsx`, `ComplianceProjectOverviewTiles.stories.tsx`, `OrgComplianceDashboard.stories.tsx`, `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.stories.tsx`, `StandardProjectsPanel.stories.tsx`).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 32: searchable assignee picker parity

Second phase of the fourth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 31-36) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** on the need (a plain `<select>` assignee field "won't scale past a handful of users" and needs either an auto-complete text field or a search-in-dropdown); **Decided by: Agent** on reusing `UserAutocomplete` (Phase 30's established answer to this exact complaint shape) rather than adding search to the existing `<select>`s.

**Root cause, confirmed exactly as diagnosed in the plan.** Two independent, hand-rolled `<select>`s mapped an unfiltered `orgUsers` array to `<option>`s with no search: `RequirementAssessmentPanel.tsx` (compliance module, a required action's assignee, one instance per required action) and `RequirementDetailPage.tsx` (core, the "Create and link a new action" assignee field).

**Fix.** Both replaced with `UserAutocomplete`, wired with `organizationId` on both call sites (per the spec's own Phase-30-consistent instruction) so both now run debounced server-side search rather than filtering a fully-loaded client-side array. One addition beyond the spec's own bullets: `UserAutocomplete` alone has no notion of a *current* value — it is a search-and-pick control that resets its own query after every pick — so a new shared component, `frontend/src/components/AssigneePicker.tsx`, pairs it with the current-assignee display and an "Unassign" action (preserving the old `<select>`'s empty "Unassigned" option behaviour). This is a **core** component (`components/`, not `modules/compliance/`) specifically so both the core `RequirementDetailPage.tsx` and the compliance module's `RequirementAssessmentPanel.tsx` can use it without either importing from the other's territory — per `CLAUDE.md`'s "Modular Feature System Boundary," a core file must never import from a module's own directory, and this component lives on the correct (core) side of that line for a module to depend on. `UserAutocomplete.tsx` itself gained one small, backward-compatible prop, optional `ariaLabel` (falls back to `placeholder` when omitted) — needed because `RequirementAssessmentPanel.tsx` renders one instance per required action and each needs a distinct accessible name (`Assignee for <action name>`), the same way the old per-row `<select>`s did.

**Tests.** Frontend: new `AssigneePicker.stories.tsx` (6 stories — empty org/unassigned, few-users client-side search+assign, assigned-shows-Unassign-action, many-users server-side search) plus two new stories each on `RequirementAssessmentPanel.stories.tsx` (`RequiredActionAssigneeSearchAndAssign`, `RequiredActionUnassign`) and `RequirementDetailPage.stories.tsx` (`CreateActionAssigneeSearchAndAssign`, `CreateActionAssigneeUnassign`) — the latter two extending `mockRequirementDetailApis`'s existing mock helper to also serve `/orgs/{id}/users` and `/orgs/{id}/users/search`. Playwright: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` extended with a fixture action type + required action (needed so its requirement has an assignable required action at all) and a new sequence — search-narrow to an org member, assign, confirm the picker shows them, unassign, confirm it reads "Unassigned" again — run against the assessment panel's required-action field before the existing compliance-status/approval flow continues unchanged.

**Verification.** `tsc -b` and `eslint` clean on every touched/new file. Frontend: `vitest run --project=storybook` on `AssigneePicker.stories.tsx` (6/6), `RequirementAssessmentPanel.stories.tsx` (8/8, including the two new stories), `RequirementDetailPage.stories.tsx` (31/31, including the two new stories) and `UserAutocomplete.stories.tsx` (12/12, confirming the new optional `ariaLabel` prop is non-breaking) — no regressions. Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image, then ran live: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` alone (1/1) and the full `tests/modules/compliance/` suite (13/13) — no regression in any compliance spec. `requirement-actions.spec.ts` (the core `RequirementDetailPage.tsx` call site's own spec, otherwise unmodified by this phase) still passes its "create and link" step, which exercises the same assignee field this phase changed; a later, unrelated step in that same spec (unlinking an action, which depends on the Requirements list showing a just-created throwaway requirement) timed out on both a full-file and an isolated re-run. Traced to this long-running local `tests/container` stack's accumulated E2E fixture rows (30 requirements now exist on Alpha-1 alone after ~3 days of repeated local runs), not to this phase — neither the Requirements list nor the unlink flow were touched here, and confirmed against the DB directly rather than assumed. Flagged to the user as a pre-existing environment/test-data staleness issue rather than treated as in-scope to fix here.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 33: inline evidence upload from the assessment panel

Third phase of the fourth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 31-36) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** on the need (evidence could only be linked, not uploaded, while assessing a requirement, and it wasn't obvious how to upload evidence at all); **Decided by: Agent** on the specific UI composition below.

**Root cause, confirmed exactly as diagnosed in the plan.** `RequirementAssessmentPanel.tsx`'s Evidence section offered only a `<select aria-label="Link existing evidence">` over already-existing `Evidence` records — actual file upload only existed one level away, in the separate project-level Evidence library panel (`EvidencePanel.tsx`). A user assessing a requirement who needed new evidence had to leave the panel, create/upload it in the separate library, then return and manually link it.

**Fix.** Added an "Upload new evidence" button in the Evidence section, alongside the existing "link existing" control. It reuses `EvidencePanel.tsx`'s own evidence-creation form directly rather than a second, bespoke one — `EvidenceFormModal` (previously a private function in that file) is now exported and imported by `RequirementAssessmentPanel.tsx`. On save, the new flow (`createAndLinkEvidence`) calls `createEvidence` then immediately `linkEvidenceToRequirement` for the current assessment — no separate manual "link existing" step — then opens a small `Modal` scoped to the newly-created evidence, reusing `FileAttachmentList`/`ResourcePickerModal` exactly as `EvidencePanel.tsx`'s own Files section does (`uploadEvidenceAttachment`, `unlinkEvidenceFile`, `linkEvidenceOrgResource`, the same "Organisation shared resources" `ResourcePickerSource`). The existing "link existing evidence" select is untouched — this phase adds the missing upload path, it doesn't replace linking. No backend change was needed: all three calls (create, upload, link) already existed: this is pure frontend composition.

**Tests.** Backend: a new test in `test_compliance_evidence_api.py`, `test_inline_upload_from_assessment_panel_creates_uploads_and_links_like_the_library_flow`, pins that chaining create → upload file → link (the order the new frontend flow uses) produces the same `Evidence` record shape (`linked_requirement_ids`, `provided_by`/`provided_at`, `is_archived`) as creating one already linked via `project_compliance_requirement_ids` at creation time, and that the file and the link are both immediately visible from the requirement's own evidence listing. Frontend: a new `EvidenceLinkExistingAndUploadNew` story on `RequirementAssessmentPanel.stories.tsx` exercises both Evidence-section paths side by side in one flow — link an existing library item via the select, then create+auto-link+attach-a-file via "Upload new evidence" — with a dedicated `mockEvidenceApis` helper (distinct from the file's existing `mockApis`) tracking evidence state across the create/link/upload requests the way `EvidencePanel.stories.tsx`'s own `mockApis` already does for its create flow. Playwright: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` extended, immediately after its existing "link existing evidence" step, with the same sequence live — create a new evidence record via "Upload new evidence," attach a real file via the dialog's file input, confirm it's linked to the requirement (`Unlink <title>` visible) with no separate manual link step, then confirm it also appears in the project's own Evidence library tab.

**Verification.** `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on every touched file. Backend: full `app/modules/compliance/tests/` package, one clean sequential `pytest` invocation — 176 passed (a first attempt at this collided with an in-flight background run from earlier in the session and produced ~174 spurious errors from the standard-library "duplicate key on admin@example.com" DB-wedge pattern this repo has hit before; recovered by dropping and recreating the dedicated `reqtrack_pytest_test` schema and re-running alone — see `docs/decisions.md`'s standing guidance and this repo's own "never run concurrent pytest" rule, reconfirmed rather than a real regression). Frontend: `vitest run --project=storybook` on `RequirementAssessmentPanel.stories.tsx` (9/9, including the new story) and `EvidencePanel.stories.tsx` (6/6, confirming the `EvidenceFormModal` export change is non-breaking). Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` backend+frontend images, then ran live: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` alone (1/1, including the new inline-upload assertions) and the full `tests/modules/compliance/` suite (13/13) — no regression in any compliance spec.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 34: traceability links between core Requirements and ComplianceRequirements

Fourth phase of the fourth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 31-36) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** on the underlying report ("I can't add a traceability link between a standard requirement and a compliance standard requirement"); **Decided by: Agent** on the architecture below, per this plan's own "Cross-entity traceability links... owned and stored by the module, not by core" open decision (added alongside this phase's spec).

**Confirmed gap, exactly as diagnosed.** Core's `RequirementLink` (`backend/app/models/requirement.py`) only ever FKs `requirements.id` to `requirements.id`; nothing links a core `Requirement` to a `ComplianceRequirement` (`backend/app/modules/compliance/models.py`), a structurally comparable row belonging to a different table the compliance module owns.

**Fix.** A new table owned entirely by the compliance module, `ComplianceRequirementTraceabilityLink` (`compliance_requirement_traceability_links`, migration `0038_requirement_traceability_links.py`): `requirement_id` (FK to core's `requirements.id`, `ON DELETE CASCADE`), `compliance_requirement_id` (FK to this module's own `compliance_requirements.id`, `ON DELETE CASCADE`), `link_type_id` (FK to core's existing, org-scoped `requirement_link_type_definitions` — no second, compliance-only vocabulary table), `created_by`. Core gains zero new dependency on the compliance module: no FK, no import. Three new endpoints on `project_router.py` (`POST`/`GET`/`DELETE /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/modules/compliance/requirements/{requirement_id}/traceability-links`), gated for mutation by a new `_require_core_requirement_edit_role` mirroring `routers.requirements.CAN_EDIT_ROLES` exactly (as `routers/actions.py` already does) — the same permission that already gates every other edit to that core requirement's own links, not a new compliance-specific one — and for reads by the router's existing `require_project_module_enabled("compliance")`. `ComplianceRequirementTraceabilityLinkOut` denormalises the linked compliance requirement's reference/name and its owning standard/version (id, reference, name, version label), mirroring core's own `RequirementLinkOut`/`_link_to_out` "resolve everything server-side" convention; unlike a core-to-core link there is no source/target ambiguity, so `display_name` is always the link type's `forward_name`.

On the frontend, `TierAModuleDefinition` (`frontend/src/modules/types.ts`) gains `requirementDetailSections` — mirrors `projectOverviewTiles`'s exact "module hands the parent a render function, parent has no idea what's inside it" shape, gated the same way (the project's own `enabled-modules` list). `pages/RequirementDetailPage.tsx`'s existing Links card now renders every installed module's contribution generically (`useProjectEnabledModules` + `getInstalledModule(...).requirementDetailSections`), with zero knowledge of what a "compliance requirement" is. Compliance's own `RequirementTraceabilityLinksSection.tsx` implements the extension point: lists this requirement's existing compliance links and offers an "Add compliance link" `Popover` with three cascading selects (standard -> version -> requirement, reusing `RequirementMappingsModal.tsx`'s existing precedent — no cross-org compliance-requirement search endpoint exists) plus a core link-type select.

**Scope note, exactly as the plan flagged it as optional:** initiating a link from the compliance-requirement side (e.g. from within a Standard's own requirement browser, `RequirementTree.tsx`) is **not built in this phase** — the backend endpoints impose no such directional restriction, but no frontend picker exists yet on that side. Left as a reasonable, explicitly-deferred follow-up (mirroring Phase 30b's own precedent for saying so out loud rather than silently shipping half).

**A migration-numbering discovery, worth recording since it isn't obvious from this module's own migrations directory alone:** this codebase's Alembic revision ids are a single global sequence shared across `backend/alembic/versions/` (core) and every module's own `migrations/` directory, not independently numbered per directory — confirmed directly (attempting `0037` inside `compliance/migrations/` collided with core's own already-existing `alembic/versions/0037_group_module_roles.py`; compliance's own prior chain already skips numbers `0034`/core-claimed ones for the identical reason). The new migration is `0038`, with `down_revision` chained onto core's `0037` (the true, global prior head at the time), not compliance's own last file (`0036`).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 35: Standards list/tiles view toggle + entity quick-switch chevron chrome fix

Fifth phase of the fourth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 31-36) — implements exactly the spec recorded there: two small, independent UI fixes bundled into one phase since both are quick, confirmed, and unrelated to each other in cause. **Decided by: User** on both underlying reports (the Standards list lacking the tile/list toggle every other list page has; the quick-switch chevron reading as a separately bordered chip); **Decided by: Agent** on the specific implementation below.

**35a — Standards list view toggle.** `StandardListPage.tsx` rendered a single fixed `DirectoryTable` and never imported `ViewToggle`/`useViewMode`, unlike `ProjectListPage.tsx`'s own already-established tile/list split — a page that simply hadn't been brought into line with `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s existing "Pattern: view toggle" rule. Fixed by adding `useViewMode("standards")` + `<ViewToggle>`, plus a tiles-mode card render (name, reference, org when shown, issuing organisation, status) directly mirroring `ProjectListPage.tsx`'s own tile card — each card a `<Link>` to `/standards/:id`, not a `DirectoryTable` row. Defaults to tiles, per `useViewMode`'s own default (matching `ProjectListPage`/`FavouritesPage`). No style guide edit was needed — the spec's own diagnosis was that the generic rule already existed and just hadn't been applied here.

**This changed `/standards`'s default rendering from always-`DirectoryTable` to tiles-first**, which broke three existing Playwright specs that had encoded the old fixed-list shape into their own locators rather than the page's actual contract:
- `compliance-standards-management.spec.ts` and `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` each clicked `getByRole("link", { name: ORG_NAMES.alpha })` to reach `/standards/settings/:orgId` via the "Compliance settings" link row — a plain substring match that now also resolves to every standard's own tile card (whose accessible name contains the org name too). Fixed with `exact: true`, which only the settings link's own accessible name (the org name alone) satisfies.
- `standard-applicability-defaults.spec.ts` clicked `getByRole("button", { name: reference })` — correct against the pre-35a `DirectoryTable`-only render, whose `onRowClick` rows are real `<button>`s, but a tile-mode card is a `<Link>` (role `link`). Fixed by switching both occurrences to `getByRole("link", { name: new RegExp(reference) })`.

All three fixes are locator corrections in the test files themselves, not workarounds in the shipped feature — the tile view rendering standards as clickable cards is the intended Phase 35a behaviour. This is the same standing risk this plan's own Phase 27a/35b already call out for a shared-component fix (check every existing call site of the old shape before calling a defect closed) — here it applies to a page-level rendering-default change instead, and the fix was to sweep the whole `tests/modules/compliance/` directory for `/standards`-navigating specs rather than trust that only the page's own spec needed a look.

**35b — Entity quick-switch chevron chrome.** `EntitySwitcher.tsx`'s chevron trigger used the generic `.btn` class, giving it a separately bordered-chip appearance next to the entity name it sits beside — the same defect class Phase 29d already fixed once for `StandardNavSection.tsx`'s own disclosure toggle, but never applied to this shared component. Fixed at the source: a new `.entity-switcher-trigger` class in `theme.css` (borderless and transparent at rest, a background only on `:hover`/`:focus-visible`), replacing `.btn` on the trigger `<button>`. Unlike Phase 29d's `.nav-link-row` (which wraps both the link and its toggle in one row carrying a shared hover surface), this trigger has no wrapping row of its own to inherit one from — it sits directly beside a page's plain `<h1>` text, owned by each calling page, not by `EntitySwitcher.tsx` itself — so the "reads as part of the name" effect comes from being borderless at rest, not from a merged hover box. Fixing the shared component fixes every consuming page (Org Overview, Project Overview, Project Admin, the Standard workspace, Org Admin) in one change. Added a cross-reference note to `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: entity quick-switch" section pointing at Phase 29d's identical rule, per the spec's own documentation-governance instruction.

**Tests.** Frontend: `EntitySwitcher.stories.tsx` gained `ChevronChromeIsBorderless`, asserting the trigger carries `.entity-switcher-trigger` (not `.btn`) and has no border/background at rest. The spec's own "Tests" bullet asked for hover/active-state coverage too, but `getComputedStyle` after `userEvent.hover()` does not reliably observe a CSS-only `:hover`/`:focus-visible` pseudo-class change in this codebase's Vitest browser-mode test runner (confirmed directly — the assertion failed even though the rule is correct and visibly works in a real browser); no other story in this codebase snapshot-tests a CSS-only hover state either, so this was narrowed to the class/border assertion, which is still the real regression guard for the chrome defect itself. `StandardListPage.stories.tsx` gained `TogglesBetweenTilesAndListView`; its meta decorator switched from `withAuth` to `withStatefulAuth` (needed for `ViewToggle`'s `useUiPreference` writes to actually take effect in-story, the same reason `FavouritesPage.stories.tsx` already uses it). Playwright: a new test in `compliance-standards-management.spec.ts` confirms the toggle (tiles by default, switches to a real `<table>` in list mode), resetting back to tiles in a `finally` since `view_mode:standards` is a per-user preference shared across this shared `orgAdminAlphaBeta` persona's other runs — plus the three locator fixes above in the pre-existing specs.

**Verification.** `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on every touched file. Frontend: `vitest run --project=storybook` on `EntitySwitcher.stories.tsx` (7/7) and `StandardListPage.stories.tsx` (5/5) — no regressions. Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image (Compose doesn't bind-mount source), then ran live: the full `tests/modules/compliance/` suite (15/15) and `entity-quick-switch.spec.ts` (1/1) — no regression anywhere, including the three pre-existing specs whose locators needed the fixes described above.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 36: Org Compliance Dashboard layout rework

Sixth phase of the fourth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 31-36) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** that the current layout (uneven card heights, project lists embedded in stat tiles) is broken; **Decided by: Agent** on the specific redesign, since the user explicitly flagged their own suggestion as "only a first pass thought."

**Root cause, confirmed as diagnosed in the spec.** `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s top `.grid.grid-metrics` had several `StatCard`s rendering a variable-length `<ProjectList>` as `children` (Non-compliant projects, Projects with outstanding actions, Projects with expired evidence, Projects with evidence approaching expiry, Projects with overdue compliance reviews) — CSS Grid's `stretch` only equalises heights within a row, so a long embedded list still made that row taller than its neighbours. The second block of three "detail" cards used `alignItems: "flex-start"` on a flex row, opting out of equal-height stretching entirely.

**Fix, three parts, exactly as scoped:**
1. **Top grid cards are plain numbers again.** Every list-bearing `StatCard` became a `MetricTile` (the established "stat tile → click navigates to a filtered view" idiom) linking to a real, pre-filtered destination instead of embedding its own list. The now-dead `ProjectList` helper and its embedded renders were removed.
2. **Destinations reuse the two existing org-wide `ResourceMenu` groups rather than inventing a new page** ("Compliance by standard" for the standards-status-derived counts; "Outstanding compliance items" for the rest), each extended to read an initial filter off its own URL query string so the tile's click-through lands exactly on the condition it counted:
   - `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.tsx` gained a "Group by" pivot (`?groupBy=project`, in addition to the original standard-first shape) plus an initial `?state=` value for its existing compliance-state filter — the "way to view all projects for a compliance manager" the spec asked for, delivered by extending this tab rather than adding a fourth widget shape, per the spec's own explicit instruction. The pivot generalises the existing per-standard grouping/expand code (renamed `groupByStandard`→`groupRows`, `StandardGroup`→`Group`) rather than duplicating it; the expand/collapse control's accessible name text is unchanged for the default (group-by-standard) shape, so no existing locator broke.
   - `OrgComplianceOutstandingPanel.tsx` gained a "Category" filter (one of its five existing sections at a time, or all) and an "Evidence status" sub-filter (expired/expiring soon, since that one section covers two distinct tile conditions sharing one underlying list), both reading an initial value off `?category=`/`?validity=`.
   - "Assessments awaiting approval" — already a plain number pre-Phase-36 — was also given a `MetricTile` link into the Outstanding tab's Pending-approval section, for the same drill-down-everywhere consistency this file's own docstring already commits to (§23's "never a bare, unexplained number").
3. **Second block's height stretching fixed by removing `alignItems: "flex-start"`** (default `stretch` now applies) and bounding each card's own list length to a fixed 5 items ("Standards with the most outstanding issues" was already bounded to 5; "Recently changed compliance assessments"'s own fetch was narrowed from 10 to 5 items; "Upcoming compliance deadlines/reviews" was narrowed from a client-side `.slice(0, 8)` to `.slice(0, 5)`) rather than adding "see all" links to pages that don't exist for this data shape.

**Docs.** Added the "top-grid `StatCard`s must stay plain numbers" rule to `docs/ux-style-guide.md`, directly below the existing Phase 25c/27b grid-of-`StatCard` guidance it narrows further, per the spec's explicit instruction.

**Tests.** Frontend: `OrgComplianceDashboard.stories.tsx` gained `HeadlineTilesLinkToFilteredViews` (asserts each headline tile is a real link with the correct pre-filtered `href`, and that no project list is embedded inside the tile itself). `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.stories.tsx` gained `GroupedByProjectViaUrl` (the URL-driven pivot+filter). `OrgComplianceOutstandingPanel.stories.tsx` gained `CategoryFilteredViaUrl` (only the targeted section renders, narrowed by validity). Both panel story files had to move their `withRouter` decorator off `meta` and onto each individual story instead — a per-story `decorators` array in this Storybook setup *adds* to, rather than replaces, `meta`'s own decorators, so a story-level `withRouter` alongside a meta-level one double-wraps the component in two `MemoryRouter`s and throws; every existing story in both files needed its own explicit `withRouter(DEFAULT_PATH)` once the meta-level one was removed. Playwright: `org-compliance-view.spec.ts`'s "Non-compliant projects" assertion (previously read the project name straight out of the tile's own embedded list) now clicks the tile, asserts the resulting URL carries `?groupBy=project&state=non_compliant`, and drills into the expanded project row on the destination page — the flow was reordered so the pre-existing PDF-report-download step (which needs the Dashboard group's own "Export" button) re-selects "Compliance dashboard" first, since the tile click navigates away from it. That same spec's new assertion also had to scope its reference-text lookup to `getByRole("link", ...)` rather than a bare `getByText` — the Standards panel's own "Standard"/"Standard version" filter `<select>` options for this dynamically-created standard also contain the reference text, which a plain text lookup matched too (a strict-mode violation, not a real regression — the filter dropdowns pre-date this phase unchanged).

**Verification.** `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on every touched file. Frontend: `vitest run --project=storybook` on all three touched story files (17/17) plus `OrgOverviewPage.stories.tsx` (8/8, unaffected) — no regressions. Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image (Compose doesn't bind-mount source), then ran the full `tests/modules/compliance/` suite live (15/15) — no regression anywhere.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 37: Entity quick-switch applied to Org Settings

First phase of the fifth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 37-41) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User.**

**Confirmed gap, already flagged as deferred.** Phase 28's own completion notes recorded that `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s two degraded-state headers (a server admin hitting a disabled org, or one they aren't a member of) got the entity quick-switch chevron, but the page's normal admin header did not, because it renders its title through `ResourceMenu`'s own `title` prop rather than a bespoke `<h1>` of its own — there was no attachment point without either duplicating `ResourceMenu`'s title rendering or plumbing a new prop through it for one caller. Those notes explicitly deferred this "until a future review specifically asks for it" — this round is that ask. `ProjectAdminPage.tsx` was checked and needs no change: it already renders its own `<h1>` + `EntitySwitcher` above `ResourceMenu` and calls `ResourceMenu` itself with no `title` prop, so the gap is specific to `OrgAdminPage.tsx`, not a `ResourceMenu` consumer pattern in general.

**Fix.** Added a generic `titleAdornment?: ReactNode` prop to `ResourceMenu` (`components/ResourceMenu.tsx`), rendered in a flex row alongside its own `<h1>` — a component-level slot rather than an org-specific one, so any future `ResourceMenu` consumer with the same "chevron next to my title" need can reuse it without another plumbing change. Wired at `OrgAdminPage.tsx`'s normal-header `<ResourceMenu title={org.name} .../>` call site with `titleAdornment={orgId && <EntitySwitcher label="Switch organisation" currentId={orgId} loadOptions={() => loadOrgSwitcherOptions("admin")} />}` — the identical loader already used verbatim at the two degraded-header call sites, so no new loader, endpoint, or fetch was needed.

**Docs.** Added a "Attachment point when the page's title isn't a bespoke `<h1>`" addendum to `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: entity quick-switch" section, documenting the new `ResourceMenu.titleAdornment` slot as the attachment point for a `ResourceMenu`-driven header.

**Tests.** Frontend: `ResourceMenu.stories.tsx` gained `RendersTitleAdornment` (asserts the adornment renders alongside the `<h1>`; every other existing story in the file omits the prop, confirming it changes nothing when absent). `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx`'s shared `mockOrgAdminApis` helper gained an `orgs` override mocking `GET /api/v1/orgs?mine=true` (defaulted to `[]` rather than left unmocked, since this endpoint is now genuinely called on every render of the page's normal header, not just by a story that opts in) and a new `EntitySwitcherOffersOtherOrgs` story exercising the popover end-to-end, mirroring the existing `DisabledOrgEntitySwitcherOffersOtherOrgs` story's shape for the degraded-header case. Playwright: `entity-quick-switch.spec.ts` gained a second test, "switches organisations from Org Settings' admin header via the chevron popover," navigating via `/orgs` (the admin-target `OrgListPage`) rather than `/org-overview`, otherwise mirroring the existing Organisation Overview test exactly.

**Verification.** `tsc -b` and `eslint` clean on every touched file. Frontend: `vitest run --project=storybook` on `ResourceMenu.stories.tsx` (10/10) and `OrgAdminPage.stories.tsx` (69/69), then a full run of the whole Storybook suite (111 files, 886/886) — no regressions from the `ResourceMenu` markup change (the `<h1>` is now wrapped in an additional flex row alongside `titleAdornment`) at any other consumer (`OrgOverviewPage.tsx`, `ProjectAdminPage.tsx`, `PreferencesPage.tsx`, `ServerManagementPage.tsx`, `ComplianceSettingsPage.tsx`). Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend (and, incidentally, backend) images, then ran live: `entity-quick-switch.spec.ts` (2/2) plus a wider sweep of Org Admin-adjacent specs (`org-admin-manage-users-modal`, `org-admin-modules`, `org-admin-nav-link`, `org-admin-project-statuses-and-link-types`, `org-rename-and-test-email`, `org-overview` — 11/11) — no regressions.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 38: Org Compliance Dashboard — top-justify detail cards + full-width "Recently changed" row

Second phase of the fifth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 37-41) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User.**

**Root cause, confirmed directly.** `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`'s second block of three detail cards ("Standards with the most outstanding issues" / "Recently changed compliance assessments" / "Upcoming compliance deadlines/reviews") wraps them in a `<div className="row" style={{ gap: "1rem", flexWrap: "wrap" }}>` with no `alignItems` override. Phase 36's own notes claimed dropping the prior `alignItems: "flex-start"` would leave the row "defaulting to stretch" — but `.row` (`styles/theme.css`) itself sets `align-items: center`, not the browser's own flexbox default of `stretch`. So the three cards, which have different content heights, were rendering vertically centred relative to one another rather than top-aligned — Phase 36 changed the mechanism but achieved neither of the two outcomes it discussed, which is what read as "not top justified."

**Fix, confined to `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`.** The row now sets `alignItems: "flex-start"` explicitly rather than relying on `.row`'s own default. "Recently changed compliance assessments" was also pulled out of that row into its own full-width `<div className="card stack">` sibling below it, per direct user feedback that it should take up a full row on its own; the remaining two cards ("Standards with the most outstanding issues," "Upcoming compliance deadlines/reviews") stay paired in the original row.

**Docs.** Added a "Correction to the paragraph above" addendum immediately after `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s existing Phase 36 guidance on stat/detail card rows, recording that `.row`'s own `align-items: center` default is a trap for any row of cards with variable content length — a future row like this must always set `alignItems: "flex-start"` explicitly, never rely on `.row`'s own default expecting `stretch`.

**Tests.** Frontend: `OrgComplianceDashboard.stories.tsx` gained `DetailCardsTopAlignedAndRecentActivityFullWidth`, asserting the two remaining detail cards share one row with `style.alignItems === "flex-start"` and that "Recently changed compliance assessments" is no longer inside that row at all. No Playwright spec references this dashboard's detail cards by name, so none needed updating; live-verified instead (below) per the spec's own "visual/manual check" instruction.

**Verification.** `tsc -b` and `eslint` clean on `OrgComplianceDashboard.tsx`/`.stories.tsx`. Full `vitest run --project=storybook` (111 files, 887/887, one pre-existing unrelated unhandled-rejection warning from `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx`'s own intentional "Load Error" story) — no regressions. Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image, then checked live against the seeded demo org (Solstice Robotics, `demo.admin@example.com`): the two remaining detail cards ("Standards with the most outstanding issues," 2 items; "Upcoming compliance deadlines/reviews," 1 item) render top-aligned despite their different heights, and "Recently changed compliance assessments" renders as its own full-width card below them.

**Incidental fix found during that live check, same session (per `CLAUDE.md`'s fix-don't-defer rule).** The user spotted, from the live screenshot, that the top nine-card grid mixed two visually incompatible layouts: `StatCard` (`components/StatCard.tsx`, used for "Active compliance standards" and "Overall compliance") rendered label-above-value, left-aligned, while `MetricTile` (used for the other seven cards in the same `.grid.grid-metrics` row) renders value-above-label, centred — the two are used interchangeably in this grid, so the row read as inconsistent even though each component was internally correct on its own. Neither component's own isolated Storybook story could have caught this, since the mismatch only exists when both render side by side. Fixed `StatCard` to match `MetricTile`'s value-above-label, centred layout exactly (dropped the label's own explicit `fontSize`/`fontWeight` override too, so it now matches `MetricTile`'s label styling, not just its position). `StatCard.stories.tsx`'s `Default` story now asserts the value precedes the label in DOM order (`compareDocumentPosition`), not just that both are present. Re-verified live in the same demo-org screenshot: all nine cards in the top grid now render identically. Added a new style-guide principle ("Two components rendered interchangeably in the same grid must share the exact same internal layout") to `docs/ux-style-guide.md` for this failure mode generally.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 39: Compliance-by-standard panel — borderless expander, tree indentation, Standard → Version → Project grouping (2026-09-13)

Third phase of the fifth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 37-41) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** on all three of 39a/39c/39d; **Decided by: Agent** on 39a/39b's exact mechanism and 39d's nesting shape, per the spec's own framing.

**39a/39b.** `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.tsx`'s expand/collapse control used the shared `.btn` class (bordered chip) and literal `▾`/`▸` text glyphs. Reproduced 39b ("gradually moving further right") live per the spec's own instruction to confirm before treating it as fixed: it did not reproduce once 39a's fix was applied, confirming it was a symptom of the glyph's variable rendered width plus `.btn`'s own padding, not a separate defect. Fixed both together with a new `.disclosure-toggle` class (`theme.css`) — a borderless button that fills its own table cell (mirrors `.th-sort`'s "zero the cell's own padding, let the button re-add it" convention, but with a hover *background* rather than a text-colour change, since the whole row is the click target here) — plus fixed-size `ChevronDown`/`ChevronRight` icons (`lucide-react`), matching `StandardNavSection.tsx`'s own Phase 29d icon choice. Third instance of this "no bolted-on `.btn` chip on a disclosure control" fix, after `StandardNavSection.tsx` (Phase 29d) and `EntitySwitcher.tsx` (Phase 35b).

**39c.** The expanded child list rendered as a flush-left `<ul>`. Fixed by reusing `RequirementTree.tsx`'s own nested-list convention verbatim (`marginLeft: "1.75rem", borderLeft: "2px solid var(--color-border)", paddingLeft: "0.75rem"`) rather than inventing new spacing values.

**39d.** The default (group-by-standard) view's expanded row grouped every assigned project flatly regardless of which version of the standard it was on. Added a second client-side grouping pass (`groupByVersion`, mirroring the file's existing `groupRows` aggregation) inside the expanded row: one sub-heading per `standard_version_id`, that version's projects nested one indent level deeper underneath (Standard is the outer indent level, Version the middle, Project the innermost). Purely additive to the existing "Group by: Standard/Project" pivot — group-by-project's own expanded row is unchanged, since a project's own assignment of a standard has exactly one unambiguous version, nothing to group by.

**Live follow-up beyond the written spec, mid-implementation (Decided by: User).** Each version sub-group is itself collapsible when a standard has more than one version (default collapsed, its own `.disclosure-toggle`) — but when a standard has exactly one version, that sub-group renders pre-expanded with a plain `<h4>` heading and no toggle at all, since a lone version behind an already-explicit "expand this standard" click has nothing left to disambiguate.

**Incidental bug found and fixed, same session (per `CLAUDE.md`'s fix-don't-defer rule).** Live-reproducing 39d's own new Playwright test (expand a standard's row from `/org-overview`, click through to a project) surfaced a real, pre-existing, deterministic routing bug — not caused by this phase's UI changes, confirmed by reproducing it against an already-published standard/project fixture from an earlier, unrelated session. `useProjectEnabledModules.ts`'s Phase 13 fix for `App.tsx`'s wildcard-route redirect race only covered a *fresh page load* landing directly on a project-scoped URL. It missed the same race one render earlier: a client-side navigation from a project-less page straight into a project's own module route, for the first time in that page's lifetime. On that transition's first render, `projectId` had already changed but the `useEffect` that resets `loaded` hadn't run yet (effects fire after the render commits), so the hook still returned the *previous* `projectId`'s state — typically `loaded: true, modules: []` left over from the "no project" case. `App.tsx` then saw an apparently-already-loaded project with zero enabled modules and bounced straight to `/projects`, `replace`, before the real fetch ever started. Confirmed deterministic, not a timing race, via a 2-second artificial delay before the click (no effect on the outcome). Fixed by keying the hook's returned state to the `projectId` it was actually resolved for and resetting it synchronously during render when `projectId` changes — React's own documented "adjusting state when a prop changes" pattern — rather than relying solely on the effect, which is one render too late for this specific transition.

**Docs.** Added this phase's fix as a third cross-reference in `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: expandable nav-rail group" section (alongside Phase 29d/35b), and a new bullet documenting the tree-indent convention (`RequirementTree.tsx`'s margin/border/padding values) as reusable for any future tree-shaped nested list, not just this one.

**Tests.** Frontend: `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.stories.tsx` — `GroupedByStandard` now also asserts the toggle carries `disclosure-toggle` (not `btn`) and that the single-version case pre-expands with no separate toggle; new `GroupedByStandardWithMultipleVersions` story covers two versions of one standard each carrying a different project, asserting each version's sub-group lists only its own project. Playwright: `org-compliance-view.spec.ts` gained a new test — a standard published on two versions, each assigned to a different project, asserting both versions' sub-groups render with correct nesting and that a project link inside the nested structure still navigates; re-run twice back to back to confirm idempotency.

**Verification.** `tsc -b` and `eslint` clean. Full `vitest run --project=storybook` (111 files, 888/888, the same pre-existing unrelated `ProjectOverviewPage.stories.tsx` "Load Error" unhandled-rejection warning as Phase 38's own verification, no regression). `npm run build` clean. Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image twice (once per code change) and re-ran: the full `tests/modules/compliance/` Playwright suite (16/16), plus a sample of core cross-module navigation specs unrelated to Compliance (`entity-quick-switch`, `org-overview`, `module-contributed-roles`, `org-admin-modules`, 8/8) to confirm the `useProjectEnabledModules.ts` fix — which affects every project-scoped module route, not just Compliance's — introduced no regression elsewhere.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 40: Outstanding compliance items — side filter panel + Project/Standard/Version/Sub-section filters (2026-09-13)

Fourth phase of the fifth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 37-41) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** on the ask itself; **Decided by: Agent** on the scope boundaries and mechanism, per the spec's own framing.

**40a.** `OrgComplianceOutstandingPanel.tsx` passed `layout="top"` to its `FilterPanel` even though it renders a stack of card sections, not a table — `FilterPanel.tsx`'s own documented rule for `"top"` ("wide, many-column *directories*... where a 240px sidebar would otherwise eat into the table's available width") never actually applied to it. Fixed to the `layout="side"` default, wrapped in a `<div className="side-grid">` mirroring its sibling `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.tsx`'s own structure exactly.

**40b/40c.** Added `Project`/`Standard`/`Standard version` `FilterField`s to both the org-level and (new) project-level Outstanding panels, following `OrgComplianceStandardsPanel.tsx`'s own client-side-derived-options pattern (standard/version/project option sets built from a `useMemo` over whatever rows are already fetched, version options narrowed by the selected standard). This needed a real backend gap closed first: `NonCompliantRequirementOut`/`PendingApprovalOut`/`OutstandingRequiredActionOut` carried only display strings (`standard_reference`/`standard_name`/`version_label`), not stable ids — filtering by standard/version needs an id, not a reference string that only happens to be unique per org today. Added `standard_id`/`standard_version_id` to all three schemas and their single construction sites (`service.py::list_non_compliant_requirements_for_project`/`list_pending_approvals_for_project`/`list_outstanding_required_actions_for_project`), the same "resolve everything server-side, denormalize onto the response row" convention Phase 34 established for `RequirementLinkOut`.

**`ComplianceReviewOut` needed a different fix, since it already had a `standard_id` field — but the wrong one for this purpose.** It echoed the underlying `ComplianceReview.standard_id` model column verbatim: populated only for a *standard-level* review, always `null` for a *project-level* one (which instead carries `project_compliance_id`). That means a project-level review could never be filtered by standard at all under the old semantics. **Decided by: Agent, since the spec's own text ("carries `standard_id` but no reference/label at all") didn't anticipate this distinction explicitly.** `build_review_out` now resolves the owning standard through *either* path — directly for a standard-level review, through the assignment's own standard version for a project-level one — so `standard_id`/`standard_reference`/`standard_name` are populated for both kinds; `standard_version_id`/`version_label` stay `null` for a standard-level review specifically, since it isn't tied to one version. Confirmed no existing consumer read the old null-for-project-level value as a meaningful signal: `ReviewsPanel.tsx` is already project-scoped and never branched on it, and the sole backend test asserting `review["standard_id"]` is against a standard-level review fixture, unaffected by the change.

**40d.** "Sub-section" has no dedicated field in the data model — a standard's hierarchy is purely `parent_requirement_id`-based — so it means "top-level ancestor requirement." Added `api.ts::findTopLevelAncestor(requirementsById, requirementId)`, a small generic helper (walk `parent_requirement_id` up from a requirement until it's `null`, with a cycle guard) shared by both panels. Sub-section options and ancestor resolution come from fetching *every* version of the selected standard (`listStandardVersions` + `listRequirements` per version) as soon as a standard is picked — not derived from whatever rows happen to already be on screen — so switching the Standard-version filter afterward never needs a second fetch and the option list stays complete regardless of what Project/Category filters are currently hiding.

**40e.** `OutstandingPanel.tsx` (the Project Compliance page's "Outstanding" tab) had no filtering at all before this phase. Added the same `FilterPanel` (Standard/Standard version/Sub-section, no Project field since the page is already project-scoped), reusing 40c's ids and 40d's helper. Needed a new `orgId` prop threaded from `ProjectCompliancePage.tsx` (already resolves `project.organization_id` for its sibling panels), since the sub-section fetch's `listRequirements`/`listStandardVersions` calls are org-router endpoints.

**Scope boundary, Decided by: Agent.** The plan names four listing types needing `standard_id`/`standard_version_id` (`NonCompliantRequirement`/`PendingApproval`/`OutstandingRequiredAction`/`ComplianceReview`) but is silent on the fifth Outstanding section, Evidence (`OrgExpiringEvidence`/`ComplianceEvidence`) — which has no standard/version field anywhere in the data model at all (one evidence row can be linked to requirements across more than one standard, so it can't honestly carry a single owning standard). Evidence stays governed by Project + its own pre-existing Evidence-status filter only. Sub-section similarly only narrows the three per-requirement sections — Reviews are scoped to a standard/version as a whole, with no single requirement to resolve an ancestor from.

**Docs.** Added a corollary to `docs/ux-style-guide.md`'s "Pattern: filter panel placement — side vs. top" recording the 40a placement fix and the new tree-derived Sub-section filter shape as the precedent for the next filter that needs to key off a hierarchy with no flat/queryable field of its own.

**Tests.** Backend: `test_project_compliance_api.py`/`test_org_compliance_dashboard.py` gained `standard_id`/`standard_version_id` assertions on existing non-compliant/pending/outstanding-actions fixtures; `test_compliance_reviews_and_notifications.py`'s `test_reviews_due_listing_spans_project_and_standard_level` extended to assert the resolved standard identity on *both* a project-level and a standard-level review row, including the `standard_version_id`/`version_label` null-for-standard-level distinction. Full `app/modules/compliance/tests` suite: 183/183. Frontend: new Storybook stories on both panels exercising the Standard → Sub-section flow narrowing rows to "None." (`OutstandingPanel.stories.tsx::FilteredByStandardAndSubSection`, `OrgComplianceOutstandingPanel.stories.tsx::FilteredByProjectStandardAndSubSection`, the latter also covering the Project filter). Playwright: new tests in both `org-compliance-view.spec.ts` and `project-compliance-view.spec.ts` — each creates a standard with two top-level requirements (one with a child), assesses the child Non-Compliant, and confirms picking the *other* top-level requirement as the sub-section filter hides it while picking its real parent brings it back; the org-level test additionally asserts `.filter-panel-top` no longer renders at all (40a) and `.side-grid` does.

**Playwright quirk found and worked around while writing the new e2e tests (not an app bug).** `page.getByLabel(fieldLabel, { exact: true })` hung to a full timeout against every `FilterField`-wrapped `<select>` with any options at all (confirmed on "Standard," reproducible on any of this panel's other filters). Root cause: `FilterField` renders `<label><span>{label}</span>{children}</label>` — a label that *wraps* its control rather than pointing at it via `for`/`id` — and Playwright's `internal:label=` selector engine matches an exact label query against the label element's raw `textContent`, which for a wrapped `<select>` includes every one of its `<option>` elements' own text (unlike the browser's real accessible-name computation, which correctly excludes an embedded control's own value — confirmed this same markup resolves correctly via Testing Library's `getByLabelText` in this component's own Storybook stories). Since no existing Playwright spec had previously targeted a `FilterField` select with `exact: true`, this is the first time the gap surfaced. Not a product accessibility defect — worked around in the test layer only, the same way this directory's own `createStandardWithVersion` helper already works around a different label-ambiguity case: added `selectFilterOption(page, fieldLabel, optionLabel)` to `tests/modules/compliance/helpers.ts`, which locates the label's own `<span>` by exact text (nothing else nested inside it to pollute matching) and walks to the sibling `<select>` instead of trusting label association.

**Verification.** `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on every touched frontend file. `ruff check` clean on every touched backend file. Full backend `app/modules/compliance/tests` suite: 183 passed. Frontend: full `vitest run --project=storybook` on `src/modules/compliance/` (32 files, 196/196) plus a targeted run of the five files touched by this phase, including both new filter stories. Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` backend and frontend images, then ran live: the full `tests/modules/compliance/` Playwright suite (18/18, including both new tests), then re-ran just the two new tests a second time back to back to confirm idempotency.

Files changed — Backend tests: `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_project_compliance_api.py`, `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_org_compliance_dashboard.py`, `backend/app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_reviews_and_notifications.py`.

## Compliance module plan, Phase 41: Inline file attachment at evidence creation (2026-09-13)

Fifth and final phase of the fifth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 37-41) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** on the ask itself ("When evidence is created, I should be able to attach files on creation, not wait for creation and then add the file"); **Decided by: Agent** on the mechanism and the follow-up-modal skip behaviour below, per the spec's own framing.

**Confirmed directly.** `EvidenceFormModal`'s create form (`EvidencePanel.tsx`) collected only metadata — no file input — so both places that use it to create evidence (the top-level Evidence tab, and Phase 33's inline "Upload new evidence" flow from the requirement assessment panel) required a real, already-persisted `evidence.id` before any file could be attached, forcing a save-then-reopen or save-then-follow-up-modal detour.

**Fix.** `EvidenceFormModal`'s create mode (gated on `!initial`, same convention the modal already uses for its expiry-date field) now stages files locally as an in-memory `File[]` — not `FileAttachmentList`, which only knows how to drive already-uploaded `FileAsset[]` against a real evidence id. The staging UI reuses `FileUploadTrigger` plus the same row/remove-button shape `FileAttachmentList` itself uses (`Paperclip`/`Trash2` icons, `Remove {filename}` aria-label) for visual consistency, without pulling in `FileAttachmentList` itself since its data shape doesn't fit a pre-save file. `onSave`'s signature grew a second `files: File[]` parameter; both call sites now create the evidence record first, then upload each staged file via the existing `complianceApi.uploadEvidenceAttachment` in sequence, before closing/reloading — so creation and attachment complete as one user action.

**Follow-up-modal skip, Decided by: Agent.** Phase 33's `RequirementAssessmentPanel.tsx::createAndLinkEvidence` used to always open a second "Attach files to..." modal after create+link, specifically so the user could attach a file — that step is what this phase's create-time staging replaces. Rather than deleting the follow-up modal (the spec explicitly allowed keeping it as an "also add another file" convenience), `createAndLinkEvidence` now only opens it when zero files were staged at creation; if one or more were staged, they're uploaded immediately and the modal is skipped entirely, since asking the user to attach a file a second time when they already just did is exactly the "second detour" this phase exists to remove. A user who wants to add a further file after creation can still do so from the evidence's own `EvidencePanel.tsx` detail view, same as any other evidence record.

**Docs.** None required beyond this entry — this composes already-existing, already-documented mechanisms (`FileUploadTrigger`, `uploadEvidenceAttachment`) rather than introducing a new pattern, per the spec's own note.

**Tests.** Frontend: `EvidencePanel.stories.tsx::AddEvidenceWithFileAttachment` stages two files, removes one before save, and asserts only the kept file is uploaded (a single `postFile` call, to the newly-created evidence's own files endpoint) — proving the local staging/removal list, not just the upload call. `RequirementAssessmentPanel.stories.tsx::EvidenceUploadNewWithFileSkipsFollowUpModal` covers the skip behaviour: attaching a file in the create dialog itself uploads it and the old "Attach files to..." dialog never appears, distinct from the pre-existing `EvidenceLinkExistingAndUploadNew` story (no file staged) which still falls back to it. Playwright: `project-compliance-view.spec.ts`'s existing evidence-creation steps were extended rather than duplicated — the top-level "Add evidence" flow now attaches a file in the create dialog and confirms it's already present when the newly-created record is reopened (no separate upload step), and the Phase 33 inline "Upload new evidence" flow now attaches its file at creation time too, asserting the follow-up modal no longer appears and the file shows up in the project's Evidence library immediately.

**Verification.** `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on every touched frontend file. Frontend: full `vitest run --project=storybook` on `src/modules/compliance/` (32 files, 198/198, two new). Rebuilt and recreated the `tests/container` frontend image, then ran live: `tests/modules/compliance/project-compliance-view.spec.ts` (2/2, including the extended evidence-attachment assertions).

## Compliance module plan, Phase 42: Compliance report content — narrative requirement cell, title always shown (2026-09-13)

First phase of the sixth human-review round (`docs/compliance-module-plan.md` Phases 42-43) — implements exactly the spec recorded there. **Decided by: User** on both problems (a requirement's title going missing in the PDF, and the desired `docs/requirements.md`-style narrative-cell format, cited by name); **Decided by: Agent** on folding `description` in as a fourth bold-prefixed section and on leaving the CSV export's column-per-field shape alone, per the spec's own framing.

**Confirmed directly, two independent defects, both in `backend/app/modules/compliance/reports.py` (built Phase 15).** `_requirement_path()` built a report row's requirement label as a breadcrumb of `reference or name` for *every* ancestor including the leaf requirement itself, so a requirement's own `name` (its title) was silently dropped from the PDF's main table whenever it also had a `reference` — the normal case for any numbered standard clause. Separately, both the PDF's main table (`Standard/Requirement/Applicability/Status/Approval/Actions/Evidence/Justification/Notes`) and the org-level appendices laid every field out as its own column, rather than the "read this like a document" single-cell shape `docs/requirements.md`'s own table already uses for core requirements.

**Fix.** `ComplianceReportRequirementRow` gained four new fields (`ancestor_path`, `requirement_reasoning`, `requirement_description`, `requirement_clarification`), all defaulting to `""` so `_requirement_report_row_from_out` (the org report's non-compliant/pending-approval appendix adapter, built from a narrower response schema with no reasoning/description/clarification of its own) needed no changes to keep constructing the dataclass. `_requirement_path` was refactored to build on a new `_requirement_ancestor_breadcrumb` helper (ancestors only, excluding the leaf) plus the leaf's own `reference or name` — identical output to before, used unchanged by the CSV's "Requirement path" column. A new `_narrative_requirement_paragraph(row)` builds each requirement's PDF cell as one block: `ancestor_path` in italics as brief section context (if any), then the leaf's own `reference` + `name` as the always-shown title line (the actual bug fix — title is no longer conditional on the absence of a reference), then `<b>Reasoning:</b>`/`<b>Description:</b>`/`<b>Clarification:</b>`/`<b>Justification:</b>`/`<b>Notes:</b>` lines, each only when its source field is non-empty. Every interpolated value is passed through the existing `_safe()` escaper first — only the literal `<b>`/`<br/>`/`<i>` structural tags this function itself adds are ever unescaped, preserving the module's existing SSRF/markup-injection discipline.

The project report's main table now uses this narrative cell for its "Requirement" column and drops the now-redundant separate "Justification/Notes" column (widened Requirement column absorbs that width, total table width unchanged: `2.5/6.5/2.3/1.8/1.8/1.4/2.7 cm`). The org report's "Non-Compliant Requirements" and "Pending Approvals" PDF appendices were reformatted the same way for consistency between both report kinds — confirmed live (via the new tests, not just read) that `_requirement_report_row_from_out`'s flat `_requirement_label(reference, name)` was *not* actually hit by the ancestor-breadcrumb title-loss bug (it always includes the name), so only the visual reformatting applied there, not a second instance of the underlying bug.

**CSV, Decided by: Agent — left as one-column-per-field, per the spec's own reasoning.** The user's "join fields into one cell" instruction was framed around the PDF/document-reading experience (`docs/requirements.md`, a document, not a spreadsheet); a CSV cell has no rich-text/bold-prefix concept, and the CSV was never affected by the title-loss bug (it already carries `requirement_name` as its own column). Only change: that column's header was renamed "Requirement name" → "Requirement title" for clarity, since "Requirement path"/"Requirement reference"/"Requirement title" no longer leaves a reader guessing which column is the human-readable one.

**Docs.** `reports.py`'s own module docstring gained a new paragraph describing the narrative-cell convention, its `docs/requirements.md` precedent, and the bug it replaced. No `docs/ux-style-guide.md` change — this is generated-document layout, not interactive frontend UI, which is that guide's stated scope.

**Tests.** `app/modules/compliance/tests/test_compliance_reports.py` gained two new tests: `test_narrative_requirement_paragraph_always_shows_title_and_folds_in_free_text_fields` builds a requirement with a `reference` *and* `reasoning`/`description`/a post-publish clarification *and* an assessment `justification`/`notes`, calls `collect_project_compliance_report` directly (via a raw `SessionLocal()`, not through the HTTP-generated PDF bytes — this module's report generator has "no PDF-text-extraction dependency" by established convention, since ReportLab's default page compression makes raw-byte-search unreliable for text content, unlike the `/Subtype /Image` structural-marker search `test_report_images.py` uses), and asserts on the returned `Paragraph.text` that the title is present and every section appears in the stated order. `test_narrative_requirement_paragraph_omits_empty_sections` confirms a requirement with no reasoning/description/clarification renders no empty sections while a genuinely-present justification still shows. The existing CSV test gained an assertion pinning the "Requirement title" header rename. Full `app/modules/compliance/tests/` suite (185 tests, including these two) passed after rebuilding and recreating the `tests/container` backend image — this repo's Docker Compose services don't bind-mount source, so a stale image silently keeps running pre-edit code.
